adams-county/0.title: 2027 county budget development
adams-county/0.summary: Commissioners heard 2027 budget presentations from nearly every department in study sessions from late August into September. The County Manager's 2027 Proposed Budget came to the Oct. 13 hearing, followed by sessions on one-time budget items, sponsorships and changes from proposed to adopted budget. A third amendment to the 2026 budget was also on the agenda.

adams-county/1.title: North Broadway County Revitalization Plan
adams-county/1.summary: Commissioners sent the proposed North Broadway County Revitalization Plan to the Planning Commission on Sept. 29. The Planning Commission took it up in October for the roughly 263-acre area bounded by West 52nd Avenue on the south and the Union Pacific tracks on the west.
adams-county/1.where: North Broadway area, unincorporated Adams County (about 263 acres, north of West 52nd Avenue)

adams-county/2.title: Development Standards Overhaul
adams-county/2.summary: The county is comprehensively rewriting its Development Standards and Regulations, with zoning map amendments to align the official map with the new standards. It went to a commissioners' study session on Sept. 21 and to the Planning Commission on Oct. 22.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Study Session

adams-county/3.title: Balanced Housing Plan and affordable housing support
adams-county/3.summary: Commissioners and the Planning Commission reviewed the Adams County Balanced Housing Plan. The board also amended the 2026 fee schedule to rebate building permit fees for affordable housing. It assigned the county's 2026 private activity bond volume cap to Maiker Housing Partners and acknowledged a public hearing on refunding bonds for the Overlook at Thornton apartments.

adams-county/4.title: Homelessness response funding and Irondale Mobile Home Park acquisition
adams-county/4.summary: The county approved $95,000 for Brothers Redevelopment's Neighborhood Stability Project and agreements with Village Exchange Center for transformational homelessness response. Commissioners also scheduled study sessions on a possible acquisition of the Irondale Mobile Home Park.

adams-county/5.title: Battery storage, substation and solar facility permits
adams-county/5.summary: The Planning Commission heard conditional use permits for a battery energy storage facility and utility substation near 12500 Cavanaugh Road. It also heard permits for a major energy facility, utility transmission line and large-scale solar facility at 6301 Manilla Road.

adams-county/6.title: Zoning violation penalties and graduated fine schedule
adams-county/6.summary: Commissioners adopted a penalty payment process for zoning and building violations and a graduated fine schedule for civil infractions of the zoning and land use regulations. They took up an amended fine schedule on Oct. 27.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Public Hearing
Board of County Commissioners Public Hearing

adams-county/7.title: Oil and gas buffers and Water Master Plan
adams-county/7.summary: The Planning Commission got an update on buffers between new development and existing oil and gas facilities. It also considered a Comprehensive Plan amendment adding the Adams County Water Master Plan and a statutory water supply element.

adams-county/8.title: Park Central subdivision at 6030 Washington Street
adams-county/8.summary: A major subdivision preliminary plat to create four lots at 6030 Washington Street went to the Planning Commission on Sept. 24 and to commissioners on Oct. 13.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Public Hearing

adams-county/9.title: Water testing at the Old Shooting Range
adams-county/9.summary: Commissioners approved a $29,981.85 amendment to the agreement with Quantum Water & Environment for water testing and other services at the county's Old Shooting Range.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Public Hearing

adams-county/10.title: Strategic Growth Element of the Comprehensive Plan
adams-county/10.summary: The Planning Commission held a study session on the Strategic Growth Element on Sept. 24. Commissioners then reviewed compliance of the element with the Comprehensive Plan on Sept. 30.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Study Session

akron/0.title: Washington County Housing Authority housing project, water review and MOU
akron/0.summary: The Council reviewed a County Housing Authority request for a water review of a Title 13 subdivision, held special housing meetings in August and September, and discussed a proposed MOU with the Washington County Housing Authority (drafts dated 9/8 and 11/6). It was on the agenda again for negotiation on Nov. 2 and for possible action on the MOU on Nov. 9.

akron/1.title: Water system improvements and DWRF loan, DOLA grant application
akron/1.summary: A Drinking Water Revolving Fund public hearing covered the aging cast iron, PVC and asbestos cement distribution system and problems with arsenic, nitrate and uranium in well water. The estimated rate increase is $13 to $18 per month. Council also considered a new DOLA Energy Impact grant application of up to $1,000,000 recommended by GMS.

akron/2.title: Sanitary sewer collection system replacement and WPCRF loan
akron/2.summary: A public hearing described replacing failing sewer lines, including a severely corroded cast iron line under the railroad that would get a new crossing. A DOLA CDBG grant of about $700,000 is already awarded, with more from principal forgiveness and a CDPHE loan. The average monthly sewer bill would need to be about $55, a $13 increase.
akron/2.where: Townwide, sewer line under the railroad

akron/3.title: Town Manager settlement and DOLA-funded position succession plan
akron/3.summary: Council took up a possible settlement with the Town Manager in executive session on Aug. 18. In November, DOLA told the Council that Energy Impact grant no. 9540, which funds the town manager position, steps down from 75% to 50% to 25% and requires a plan to keep funding the job. Mayor Bowin said Council needs more time to review the contract and plan.

akron/4.title: Title 14 Planning and Zoning ordinance 614
akron/4.summary: Council took up Ordinance 614, adopting a new Title 14 Planning and Zoning, on first read Sept. 14 and second read Oct. 5.

akron/5.title: 2027 budget and employee compensation
akron/5.summary: Council reviewed the 2027 budget on Oct. 12 and discussed employee compensation on Nov. 2.

akron/6.title: Sheriff's contract and code enforcement for 2027
akron/6.summary: Council was to review and possibly act on the Sheriff's contract, with a final revised 2027 town contract for code enforcement, on Nov. 9.

akron/7.title: E-bike ordinance discussion
akron/7.summary: Council discussed a possible e-bike ordinance on Oct. 5.

akron/8.title: Scott hangar lease at the airport
akron/8.summary: Council considered Ordinance 613 approving a lease of a hangar to Scott, on second read Sept. 14.

arapahoe-county/0.title: Data center regulation and Land Development Code updates
arapahoe-county/0.summary: Commissioners got a data center overview on Sept. 22 ahead of a Sept. 25 tour, and a follow-up on Oct. 19 noted the county code does not define "data center." The board voted 5-0 for option 3, directing staff to set up a permitted and/or special use for data centers, with noise, air quality, water and Xcel energy costs among the concerns.

arapahoe-county/1.title: 2027 Recommended Budget and 1A Resident Advisory Committee
arapahoe-county/1.summary: The 2027 Recommended Budget was submitted Oct. 13 as structurally balanced, followed by a public hearing Oct. 27 and an Executive Budget Committee review Oct. 20. The 1A Resident Advisory Committee reviews it for alignment with ballot measure 1A. The Board of Health also took up its FY2027 budget in August.

arapahoe-county/2.title: County Water Supply Element of the Comprehensive Plan
arapahoe-county/2.summary: Staff are amending the 2018 Comprehensive Plan to add a water supply element required by state law (SB 24-174), building on the 2024 Water Supply Study. It went to the Planning Commission in September and is set for an Oct. 20 hearing, after commissioners reviewed it on Sept. 21.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Study Session

arapahoe-county/3.title: Gun Club Road widening and CORE transmission line relocation
arapahoe-county/3.summary: The county is to approve a relocation agreement with Rippey Commercial and Copperleaf Metro District for the CORE transmission line on the west side of South Gun Club Road between the E-470 ramps and East Belleview Avenue. Existing right-of-way is about 89 feet and 141 feet is needed. The agreement dedicates 32 feet of right-of-way and a public use easement, and the county pays design and construction costs. It was on the Oct. 27 consent agenda.
arapahoe-county/3.where: South Gun Club Road, between E-470 ramps and East Belleview Avenue

Board of County Commissioners Study Session

arapahoe-county/4.title: Proposed county rezonings (Dry Creek, Federal Enclave, Belleview, 4 Square Mile)
arapahoe-county/4.summary: The Planning Commission held a study session Aug. 18 on proposed county rezoning maps for several areas, including Dry Creek, which includes survey results and public comments. The documents give little detail on outcomes.
arapahoe-county/4.where: Dry Creek, Federal Enclave, 4 Square Mile and Belleview areas

arapahoe-county/5.title: Onsite wastewater cease and desist hearing at 23900 E. Ohio Ave.
arapahoe-county/5.summary: The Board of Health held a cease and desist hearing over an onsite wastewater system at 23900 E. Ohio Ave. The homeowner did not attend, and the board discussed options to gain compliance. An onsite wastewater update was set for September.

arapahoe-county/6.title: Proposition 123 affordable housing commitment 2027-2029
arapahoe-county/6.summary: The board voted 5-0 to authorize submitting the county's 2027-2029 Proposition 123 commitment. The formula yields a target of 231 affordable housing units.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Study Session

arapahoe-county/7.title: Payment Error Rate costs for human services
arapahoe-county/7.summary: Staff briefed commissioners on the state's 2026-27 Payment Error Rate. The state plans to cover 60% of the allocation reduction with counties covering the rest. Staff discussed how county Human Services could lower errors, and the issue is also on the county's legislative priorities.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Study Session
Board of County Commissioners Study Session

arapahoe-county/8.title: 2027 Open Space grants and High Line Canal leases
arapahoe-county/8.summary: Staff recommend keeping the 2027 Open Space grant total at $5.5 million and raising the maximum standard award from $600,000 to $750,000. Separately, the board reviewed extending High Line Canal recreation leases with local government partners.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Study Session
Board of County Commissioners Study Session

arapahoe-county/9.title: Ballot measures and state/federal legislative priorities
arapahoe-county/9.summary: Commissioners reviewed 2026 statewide measures including Propositions 136 and 137 and Amendments 81-87, covering taxes, natural gas, voter ID and immigration enforcement. They also adopted legislative priorities, with a push to add data center land use language.

arapahoe-county/10.title: Pipeline use by special review near Bennett
arapahoe-county/10.summary: Commissioners heard a request for a joint water pipeline, with route, CDOT and Colorado Parks and Wildlife referral questions. Bennett Watkins Fire noted future water infrastructure.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Business Meeting

arapahoe-county/11.title: Airpark/Monaghan Interchange agreement and avigation easement
arapahoe-county/11.summary: Commissioners got legal advice on an IGA for the Airpark/Monaghan Interchange Project and a proposed interchange impact fee. Separately, they considered a revised avigation easement form for development in airport influence areas.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Study Session
Board of County Commissioners Study Session

archuleta-county/0.title: Comprehensive Plan update and water supply/strategic growth review
archuleta-county/0.summary: Consultant HRGreen briefed the Planning Commission on the county's Comprehensive Plan update; commissioners asked about outreach (only one public meeting scoped) and state deadlines for water supply and strategic growth elements. A resident argued the plan should focus on growth and housing affordability, and commissioners were set to review the water supply and strategic growth elements on Nov 4.

archuleta-county/1.title: 2026 flood recovery and permit fee waivers
archuleta-county/1.summary: Commissioners planned to discuss waiving permit fees for flood recovery and a broader 2026 flood discussion, along with considering emergency gravel pits in the county.

archuleta-county/2.title: LPEA transmission line to Trujillo Substation
archuleta-county/2.summary: La Plata Electric Association applied for a Board Conditional Use Permit for about 2,700 feet of 115 kV double-circuit transmission line (initially run at 69 kV) with seven poles up to 75 feet tall at 2140 County Road 500, to power the approved Trujillo Substation. A public hearing was on the Nov 4 agenda.

archuleta-county/3.title: Housing Action Plan
archuleta-county/3.summary: The multijurisdictional housing coordinator was scheduled to brief officials on the Housing Action Plan on Sept 28.

archuleta-county/4.title: Cloman Blvd administrative rezoning
archuleta-county/4.summary: The Planning Commission heard the staff report on PLN-REZ-26-050, an administrative rezoning on Cloman Blvd.

archuleta-county/5.title: Draft 2027 budget and tourism/lodgers tax
archuleta-county/5.summary: The town drafted its 2027 budget for discussion, while commissioners were to review the Tourism Board budget and a lodgers tax update.

archuleta-county/6.title: Watershed and water presentations
archuleta-county/6.summary: The Upper San Juan Watershed Enhancement Partnership and San Juan Water Conservancy District were scheduled to brief commissioners on water issues.

archuleta-county/7.title: Secure transport services, capital asset sales and PIO position
archuleta-county/7.summary: Commissioners planned to discuss secure transport services, a request to sell capital assets, temporary land use approvals and whether to create a public information officer position.

archuleta-county/8.title: Transportation grant awards
archuleta-county/8.summary: A work session item covered transportation grant awards presented by staff.

arriba/0.title: Wastewater permit compliance and facility study
arriba/0.summary: Arriba is working with GMS Inc on an engineering study of its wastewater facility under new state permit rules, with half the costs covered by DOLA grants (a $16,428.06 reimbursement; $19,250 in invoices paid in July 2026). The facility has had BOD and ammonia violations, flooding and infiltration problems, and board members are looking at cheaper alternatives to evaporative ponds. In September 2026 CDPHE let the Town revert to its old permit compliance; the permit expires in 2027.
arriba/0.where: Town wastewater facility and sewer lines

arriba/1.title: RV park sewer and water rates
arriba/1.summary: Residents, notably Beverly Langley, have complained that campgrounds like Big Ben's RV Park use more water and sewer than they pay for. In January 2026 the board raised the monthly RV sewer rate per hookup (a $2 increase from $5 was moved after a $10 motion failed for lack of a second), and the RV park's heavy use has affected BOD levels at the wastewater pond. Residents asked again in August and September 2026 for a rate review.

arriba/2.title: Base water rate increase
arriba/2.summary: To stay in compliance with its drinking water loan covenant, the Town adopted a resolution raising the in-town and out-of-town base water rates by $5.50, to $55.00. It takes effect August 1, 2026.

arriba/3.title: Mandatory trash service ordinance and Rob's Trash Service contract
arriba/3.summary: The board negotiated a contract with Rob's Trash Service and adopted an ordinance requiring every occupied residential household to have trash service, with an option for residents to use their own approved 3-yard dumpster emptied monthly for $45. The contract can be renegotiated at the end of 2026.

arriba/4.title: 2026 budget and mill levy cut
arriba/4.summary: After a public hearing, the board adopted the 2026 budget and a 2025 supplemental sewer fund budget, which raised sewer spending from $116,940 to $229,440 for wastewater permit costs. The mill levy was certified at 14.509, down from 25.948, to stay under the property tax revenue limit.

arriba/5.title: Sales tax ballot question for 2026
arriba/5.summary: The board placed a question on the 2026 ballot asking voters to let the Town keep 2025 sales tax revenue above its estimate. The Town had estimated $14,000 but projected about $30,000. The 2026 election will be by mail ballot.

arriba/6.title: Wildfire Resiliency Code adoption (Ordinance 159)
arriba/6.summary: The state-required wildfire code was tabled for months over concerns about enforcement, with the Town Clerk as code official. In July 2026 the board adopted Ordinance 159 adopting the 2025 Wildfire Resiliency Code, after discussing its effect on residents' insurance rates and a state affidavit requirement.

arriba/7.title: Time capsule event and park improvements
arriba/7.summary: The Town held a July 4, 2026 time capsule event funded by a $7,500 grant and a $2,500 tourism grant, with a beer garden on the park basketball court. Volunteers painted the park building. A $2,500 donation from Big Ben's RV Park and Conservation Trust funds are earmarked for a park sprinkler system that staff and volunteers plan to install.

arriba/8.title: Pine Street drainage and speeding on College and Lincoln Avenues
arriba/8.summary: Resident Beverly Langley reported rainwater from Pine Street flooding her house, and the board agreed to a ditch on the west side of Pine Street. Residents also raised truck speeding, and the board discussed speed bumps on College Ave and Lincoln Ave, plus a missing stop sign at Grant and Lincoln.
arriba/8.where: Pine Street, College Ave, Lincoln Ave, Grant St

arriba/9.title: RV and manufactured home permits
arriba/9.summary: The board approved a manufactured home permit at 521 Lincoln Ave and an RV permit for Troy McCue at 214 Main Street. The board decided under the RV ordinance that no tap fee applies, only the permit fee and backhoe use.

arriba/10.title: Hooved animals ordinance (Ordinance 113)
arriba/10.summary: A request to allow hooved animals in Town or on lots over 5 acres was considered in July 2026. The board agreed not to change Ordinance 113, which bans them except by variance for 4-H.

arvada/0.title: Data center moratorium
arvada/0.summary: Council discussed a temporary moratorium on new data center applications, citing water, energy and land use concerns and moratoriums in neighboring jurisdictions. A first reading of CB26-029, a moratorium on applications for primary-use data centers, was scheduled with a public hearing set for October 6, 2026.

arvada/1.title: City water treatment plant annexation and rezoning at 6809 SH 93
arvada/1.summary: The city is annexing two parcels (17.885 and 9.016 acres) at 6809 SH 93 for its water treatment plant. The land would be rezoned from Jefferson County PUD to city Open Space and the Comprehensive Plan amended. The Planning Commission heard the case, and Council set an October 6 public hearing after first reading.

arvada/2.title: Hibernia Gold Strike Apartments, 240 units
arvada/2.summary: A conditional use permit is proposed for a five-story, 240-unit apartment building with about 1,000 sq ft of retail on 3.47 acres at 4800 W 60th Ave. The Planning Commission considered it, and about 20 residents attended the neighborhood meeting. Council first reading came October 20, with a hearing set for November 17.

arvada/3.title: 2027-2028 budget, mill levy and utility rates
arvada/3.summary: The City Manager proposed a 2027-2028 budget with a 2027 appropriation of $412,447,446, including a pay plan and 32 requested new positions. Council scheduled adoption of the 2027 budget, the 2026 mill levy certification, and new water, wastewater and stormwater rates for October 20.

arvada/4.title: Drought and dropped water surcharge ordinance
arvada/4.summary: Council declared a drought on March 24, 2026, and water use restrictions followed. Staff pulled ordinance CB26-018 on water surcharges and plan to bring surcharges back in spring 2027, possibly alongside a drought declaration extension.

arvada/5.title: Proposition 123 zoning changes and housing strategy
arvada/5.summary: The Planning Commission held a hearing on Land Development Code text amendments related to Proposition 123. Council was asked to commit to Prop 123 obligations for the 2027-2029 cycle, and a residential land use table ordinance (CB26-028) was introduced. The Housing Advisory Committee also worked on the city's housing strategic plan.

arvada/6.title: Olde Town paid parking
arvada/6.summary: Council held a study session on parking pressures in Olde Town, where studies since 2010 show demand outpacing supply. Staff reviewed options for a paid parking program called for in the Olde Town Strategic Reinvestment Plan, plus stakeholder feedback.

arvada/7.title: Residency restrictions for registered sex offenders
arvada/7.summary: Arvada has no ordinance on where registered sex offenders may live. Council members asked Legal to draft one, and staff sought direction on who it should cover, with Legal recommending no further than 1000 feet.

arvada/8.title: Wildfire early detection system
arvada/8.summary: The city approved up to $300,000 from the Urban Renewal Authority for cameras and chemical sensors to detect wildfires early in the Urban Renewal Area. Council later received an update after residents raised data ownership concerns at public comment.

arvada/9.title: Homelessness response and Navigation Center funding
arvada/9.summary: Council recognized faith leaders in the homeless response, considered an intergovernmental agreement on Navigation Center operating funding, and scheduled a Homelessness Action Plan update.

arvada/10.title: Parks, Trails and Open Space Master Plan update and Gold Strike Park
arvada/10.summary: Council reviewed the update to the 2016 Parks Master Plan, with a timeline and public engagement plan. A contract of up to $9,596,751.06 with Arrow-J Landscape and Design for redeveloping Gold Strike Park was also on the agenda.

arvada/11.title: Comprehensive Plan update
arvada/11.summary: The consultant Metta Urban Design finished Phase 1 of the Comprehensive Plan update, and Phase 2 begins next. Adoption is targeted for the third quarter of 2027, with a focus on housing attainability.

aspen/0.title: Connor Park performance stage and amplified music
aspen/0.summary: Residents and a church near Connor Park asked Council to reconsider the approved performance deck, worried that amplified music would harm the quiet park and the Armory Hall redevelopment. The park stage was scheduled for further Council discussion at the September 22 work session.

aspen/1.title: Entrance to Aspen / CO 82 reevaluation
aspen/1.summary: Council received updates on the refined preferred alternative for the CO 82 Entrance to Aspen. The Historic Preservation Commission discussed mitigation and reviewed CDOT historic resource survey materials.

aspen/2.title: Fee deferral program for qualified locals (Ordinance #11)
aspen/2.summary: P&Z reviewed a fee deferral program for qualified locals across two hearings and recommended on it. Council took up the continued ordinance at a public hearing on October 27.

aspen/3.title: Affordable housing fee-in-lieu five-year update
aspen/3.summary: Staff presented two phases of a fee-in-lieu study at a work session. P&Z then made a recommendation, and Ordinance #18 came to Council on first reading October 27.

aspen/4.title: 2027 city budget work sessions
aspen/4.summary: Council held four budget work sessions from October 5 to 26: kickoff and fund overviews, capital, supplemental requests and fees, and wrap-up of open items. Community Development fees were also reviewed, and ACRA and CORE presented their 2027 budgets.

aspen/5.title: Drought, Stage Three water restrictions and water supply
aspen/5.summary: With low flows and wildfires nearby, the city reported on a regional drought response using Ruedi Reservoir water and on continued Stage Three restrictions. Council also discussed buying Twin Lakes water right shares, water use at special events, and a water treatment bond question.

aspen/6.title: Water treatment facility improvements and ballot support
aspen/6.summary: Council considered an early work package amendment for the Water Treatment Facility project and a Holy Cross Electric contract for easements and conduit. It also considered resolutions supporting a water treatment plan bond question and county ballot issue 1A.

aspen/7.title: Home Rule Charter amendment on elections (Ordinances #17)
aspen/7.summary: Council moved two alternative charter amendment ordinances to public hearings on how the city's elections are decided. Staff outlined significant issues with a runoff in a memo, and Council discussed more outreach.

aspen/8.title: E-bike and e-moto rules
aspen/8.summary: A resident asked Council to align e-bike and e-moto rules up and down the valley, with licensing and a minimum age of 16. The mayor said other towns face the same issues and locals no longer feel comfortable on the Rio Grande Trail.

aspen/9.title: 121-123 East Hyman Avenue special review
aspen/9.summary: P&Z held a series of hearings, up to a third on October 21, on a special review for this property. Public comment from Good Thunder Condos was filed.

aspen/10.title: Armory Hall redevelopment
aspen/10.summary: Council approved a change order for Shaw Construction on the Armory Hall project and received an interior update at a work session.

aspen/11.title: Marolt housing and golf clubhouse master plans
aspen/11.summary: Council reviewed redevelopment concepts for Marolt housing in collaboration with AMFS and a master plan for the golf clubhouse area.

aspen/12.title: Short-term rental guideline amendments
aspen/12.summary: Staff reported forthcoming amendments to the short-term rental program guidelines.

aspen/13.title: 420 West Francis Street transferable development rights
aspen/13.summary: HPC recommended creating three TDR certificates for 420 W. Francis, and Ordinance #20 went to Council on first reading.

aurora/0.title: Data center moratorium and zoning standards
aurora/0.summary: Council took up a data center moratorium resolution (R2026-111) that would pause acceptance or processing of development applications with a data center as the primary use, with a waiver of reconsideration requested as time-sensitive. Council also held standards discussions and a public hearing on ordinance 2026-51, a Unified Development Ordinance text amendment to the permitted use table for data centers. An earlier agenda paired this with an evaporative cooling ordinance from Aurora Water.

aurora/1.title: 2027 city budget deliberations, fees and rates
aurora/1.summary: Council held a full-day budget session on Oct. 3 covering department budgets, the capital projects fund, proposed 2027 service fees, a 2026-2027 pay table, and 2027 budgets for several general improvement districts. On Oct. 12 it considered 2027 proposed rates and fees and a new fund to self-fund United Healthcare employee coverage.

aurora/2.title: Homeless services funding awards
aurora/2.summary: Council considered a series of Homeless Services Notice of Funding Opportunity applications, with recommendations including Advance Pathways and Aurora Housing Authority grants (Emergency Solutions Grant, HOME tenant-based rental assistance, marijuana funds). The items moved from the Oct. 12 study agenda to the Oct. 26 consent calendar.

aurora/3.title: Affordable housing: Mercy Housing ground lease and bond allocation
aurora/3.summary: Council considered a ground lease with Mercy Housing Mountain Plains for an affordable housing project (R2026-107), with an outside speaker listed. Council also considered assigning the city's 2026 private activity bond allocation to the Aurora Housing Authority.

aurora/4.title: Nine Mile Station and urban renewal redevelopment agreements
aurora/4.summary: The Aurora Urban Renewal Authority board considered amendments and agreements for The Point Crossing and Tempo at Nine Mile Station apartments in the Plaza 3 area, plus a restated finance agreement for Plaza 1. An IGA between the city and the Authority followed to council on Oct. 26.
aurora/4.where: Nine Mile Station, Plaza 1 and Plaza 3 urban renewal areas

aurora/5.title: Water restrictions on turf and ornamental water features
aurora/5.summary: Council finalized ordinances on new turf and ornamental water features, including one prohibiting certain permits, as part of Aurora Water conservation efforts. An evaporative cooling ordinance was also on an earlier agenda.

aurora/6.title: Water agreements: Lake County IGA and Westerly Creek storm sewer
aurora/6.summary: Council considered an amended and restated IGA with Lake County on water deliveries and storage, with a waiver of reconsideration requested to assist Lake County. It also took up an IGA for the Akron storm sewer and outfall to Westerly Creek for flood control improvements.

aurora/7.title: Regis Jesuit High comprehensive plan amendment
aurora/7.summary: Council held a public hearing on ordinance 2026-44 to amend the 2018 Comprehensive Plan placetype map for the Regis Jesuit High site, north of East Arapahoe Road and west of S. Olathe Street.
aurora/7.where: North of E. Arapahoe Road, west of S. Olathe St.

aurora/8.title: Fire and police labor contracts and public safety grants
aurora/8.summary: Council considered 2027-2028 collective bargaining agreements with IAFF Local and Fraternal Order of Police Lodge #49. It also considered police grant applications, including a state peace officer mental health program and a Department of Justice cybercrimes grant, plus mutual aid agreements with fire districts.

aurora/9.title: Industrial zoning and food truck rules
aurora/9.summary: Council considered a Unified Development Ordinance amendment for industrial zone districts and a text amendment to food truck standards and definitions.

aurora/10.title: Bethel Lutheran Church historic designation
aurora/10.summary: Council held a public hearing on ordinance 2026-52 designating Bethel Lutheran Church as a historic landmark.

avon/0.title: Flock license plate reader cameras
avon/0.summary: Residents repeatedly urged Council to end the Town's Flock Safety automated license plate reader program, citing privacy concerns and petitions with 1,544 to over 1,900 signatures. Town Manager Eric Heil said the Town has not renewed its Flock agreement and is reviewing contract terms and data security. Council is scheduled to discuss the program on October 6, 2026.

avon/1.title: Avon Whitewater Park and Bob the Bridge improvements
avon/1.summary: Residents asked Council to consider improving the Bob the Bridge area and redeveloping the Avon Whitewater Park, including a standing river wave. Speakers also asked for better river access amid low water this year and for skate park funding.
avon/1.where: Avon Whitewater Park / Bob the Bridge

avon/2.title: Piedmont Apartments trash and wildlife concerns
avon/2.summary: Residents raised property management and code enforcement concerns at the Piedmont Apartments, including trash drawing wildlife. Deputy Chief Cosper reported that police had received 27 calls about the trash.

avon/3.title: Community housing outreach
avon/3.summary: A resident asked for more opportunities for neighborhood participation and input on a recent community housing project. Town Manager Heil said the referenced meeting was not the final step and that further public comment would be available at future Town Council public hearings.

avon/4.title: Pedestrian crosswalk safety at Avon Road and Highway 6
avon/4.summary: A resident asked for flashing pedestrian beacons on both sides of Avon Road near Highway 6, after a near-miss involving his father in the crosswalk. He noted beacons exist on Highway 6 near Avon Road. Earlier, another resident said the Town had quickly made requested crosswalk improvements.

avon/5.title: Lot B (The Summit) redevelopment and tree removal
avon/5.summary: A resident asked about trees that could be removed during future redevelopment and site excavation of Lot B (The Summit). Town Manager Heil responded that trees would likely be removed as part of that work.

avon/6.title: Third 2026 budget amendment
avon/6.summary: Council's consent agenda on September 22 included a resolution for the Town's third budget amendment of 2026, renumbered as Resolution No. 26-14.

berthoud/0.title: Data center moratorium and land use rules
berthoud/0.summary: On Aug. 25 trustees asked for an agenda item on a possible moratorium on data center applications. On Sept. 22 they approved Emergency Ordinance 1391 temporarily suspending acceptance, processing and approval of large data center applications, with discussion of what size counts as large. A Sept. 29 work session began a Technical Criteria Guide and possible code amendments covering noise, heat and water, and a study session summary was set for Oct. 27.

berthoud/1.title: Legacy Park final plat and development agreement
berthoud/1.summary: Planning Commission held a hearing Sept. 10 on the Legacy Park final plat south of Mountain Avenue, and approved it. The Town Board held a hearing Sept. 8 on revised vesting and improvement guarantees in the development agreement. The silos on the site will be removed because of asbestos.
berthoud/1.where: South of Mountain Avenue, east of Meadowlark Drive, west of S. Berthoud Parkway

berthoud/2.title: Heron Lakes Marina neighborhood master plan
berthoud/2.summary: Planning Commission heard the Heron Lakes Marina Neighborhood Master Plan on Sept. 10 and sent a recommendation to the Town Board. The Board continued its public hearing on Resolution 2026-25 approving the plan to Oct. 27.

berthoud/3.title: Wildfire Resiliency Code and wildland-urban interface
berthoud/3.summary: The Town Board continued a hearing in September and on Oct. 13 approved Ordinance 1389 adopting the 2025 Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code, with a mapped wildland-urban interface boundary. A cooperative agreement with the Berthoud Fire Protection District for code administration was also considered.

berthoud/4.title: Chapter 30 land use code rewrite
berthoud/4.summary: Staff proposed amendments to Chapter 30 of the municipal code covering impact fees, annexation, zoning, flood mitigation and other sections. Planning Commission was to consider a repeal and replacement Oct. 22, with trustees hearing it Nov. 10. Also on the agenda was a discussion of Ordinance 1355 and a possible expansion of affordable housing.

berthoud/5.title: November 3 ballot measure and Mountain Vista Park bond
berthoud/5.summary: Trustees approved intergovernmental agreements with Larimer County for the Nov. 3 coordinated election and reviewed ballot language in Ordinance 1390. They worried it might not make clear that taxes would not increase. A resident spoke in favor of a bond to finance Mountain Vista Park.

berthoud/6.title: 2027 draft budget
berthoud/6.summary: Administrator Kirk introduced the preliminary draft 2027 budget on Oct. 13, and a public hearing was to be set. The Board also adopted a new supplies and equipment purchasing policy and reviewed purchase authorization limits.

berthoud/7.title: Boards and commissions ordinance 1388
berthoud/7.summary: Trustees adopted Ordinance 1388, consolidating rules for town boards and commissions into a new municipal code section 4.9. They asked each board to review it and update bylaws in October.

sources.body: Parks, Open Space, Recreation, and Trails Committee

berthoud/8.title: Welch Avenue and 9th Street road improvements
berthoud/8.summary: Trustees authorized a request for proposals for design of Welch Avenue roadway and drainage improvements. They also received an update on 9th Street crossing improvements.

berthoud/9.title: Water share purchases and Northern Water lease
berthoud/9.summary: Trustees approved contracts to buy Loveland Lake and Ditch water shares from Bebo and Hillside Commercial Group. A lease amendment with Northern Water for water was also on the agenda.

berthoud/10.title: Parks, open space and trail projects
berthoud/10.summary: The Board approved bids for Jaskowski Open Space construction, bike park improvements and a Mountain Vista Park design change order. A letter of support for the Eagle Vista/Front Range Trail grant was considered.
berthoud/10.where: Jaskowski Open Space, Mountain Vista Park, Eagle Vista Open Space

sources.body: Parks, Open Space, Recreation, and Trails Committee

berthoud/11.title: Urban forest and memorial tree program
berthoud/11.summary: A resident asked the Tree Advisory Committee and the Board about a program to buy memorial trees in Fickel Park. The committee also discussed grants and a fall planting plan.

berthoud/12.title: Historic preservation grants and survey
berthoud/12.summary: The Historic Preservation Advisory Commission reported funding for interpretive signage at the elevated water tank and worked on a survey plan grant from History Colorado. Residents asked the Board to support historic preservation.

berthoud/13.title: Regional housing discussion
berthoud/13.summary: Planning Commission held a work session Oct. 8 with the Northern Colorado regional housing director on housing.

black-hawk/0.title: Education Enhancement Tax and the proposed Gilpin County sales tax
black-hawk/0.summary: Black Hawk's 1.5% Education Enhancement Tax for the Gilpin school has raised about $16.9 million since 2009 and ends automatically if a countywide sales tax is adopted. Council discussed the County Commissioners' possible November 2026 sales tax and passed Resolution 17-2026 on March 25 reaffirming that the tax would terminate.

black-hawk/1.title: Water supply: Four Mile Gulch Well #6 and Army Corps reservoir permit
black-hawk/1.summary: The city is pursuing an Army Corps of Engineers permit for a reservoir and approved a reimbursement agreement (CB12) covering review costs. Residents of unincorporated Aspen Springs and Chalet Park spoke on Sept. 9 against drilling Well #6 near Dory Hill Road, saying it could harm neighbors' water, and asked the council to pause additional wells.
black-hawk/1.where: Four Mile Gulch / Dory Hill Road

black-hawk/2.title: Wildfire Resiliency Code adoption and fire restrictions
black-hawk/2.summary: Council adopted the 2025 Wildfire Resiliency Code into the municipal code on March 25 by a 5-1 vote. In July the city manager issued an administrative order imposing fire restrictions. The city also contracted Good People Tree Service for fire mitigation work.

black-hawk/3.title: City-owned land purchases and sales, including Resolution 48-2026
black-hawk/3.summary: Council approved a contract to buy land on Gregory Hill in June and accepted a property conveyance in July. A vacant land sale agreement (Resolution 48-2026) was repeatedly continued from August into September, with discussion of Central City's roadway permitting and traffic study.

black-hawk/4.title: Leadership turnover: new City Manager and Police Chief
black-hawk/4.summary: Police Chief Moriarty announced her retirement after 31 years, and the council met in executive session on City Manager matters. Lance Hillis's employment agreement as City Manager took effect May 2 (Resolution 22-2026), and Ely Reyes was introduced as the new Police Chief in July.

black-hawk/5.title: Capital projects: Bobtail Mine, Highway 119 culverts, Red Dolly electrical, Ballard House
black-hawk/5.summary: Council approved a $949,307 change order for Bobtail Mine Improvements Phase 2 and a $160,400 Bobtail wall excavation contract. It also approved relining two storm culverts under Highway 119 after a failure at Gregory Street, the Red Dolly Casino electrical relocation, storage sheds, and Ballard House renovation with a barn shed addition (Roche Constructors). Also streamlined the capital project approval process (CB10).

black-hawk/6.title: Historic preservation and Lace House designation
black-hawk/6.summary: The Historic Preservation Commission is working on the Lace House designation, a phased reconnaissance survey and an intensive survey property list. Council accepted the reconnaissance survey and the Five-Year HPC Work Plan in August to meet Certified Local Government requirements.

black-hawk/7.title: Rick Thomas Distillery trademark license and water fee waiver
black-hawk/7.summary: Council approved a trademark license agreement with Rick Thomas Distillery and extended a waiver of water fees for another year for its site on Lot 7 of the Black Hawk Park Subdivision.

black-hawk/8.title: Fee schedule update and 2025 audit
black-hawk/8.summary: Council accepted the 2025 audit and amended the fee schedule, aligning commercial electrical fees with state fees and moving SAFEbuilt's hourly rate to consultant fees, plus City Clerk fee changes.

black-hawk/9.title: Sanitation district agreement and ballot measure positions
black-hawk/9.summary: Council approved an amended and restated service agreement with the Black Hawk/Central City Sanitation District. The mayor also spoke against a County Commissioners property-tax measure (Initiative 1A) and proposed a resolution supporting Initiative 177 on natural gas purchases.

blue-river/0.title: Short-term rental caps, zones and new licensing rules
blue-river/0.summary: The Board held repeated work sessions on a revised short-term rental program. Direction covered a six-zone framework, cap percentages by zone, a possible nightly rental limit (about 150 nights per year), enforcement and a hearing officer, with a new ordinance planned for Jan. 1, 2027. Residents urged enforcement against unlicensed operators and consideration for owners hurt by the moratorium.

sources.body: Regular Meeting of the Board of Trustees
Regular Meeting of the Board of Trustees

blue-river/1.title: Exceptions to the STR moratorium and 2027 license processing (Ordinances 2026-10, 2026-11, 2026-12)
blue-river/1.summary: Ordinance 2026-10 would let a limited group of owners, including recent buyers who submitted nearly complete applications, apply for a short-term rental license despite the moratorium, with an application deadline of Nov. 1, 2026. Ordinance 2026-11 sets up processing of renewal applications and licenses effective May 1, 2027, and Ordinance 2026-12 amends the STR code processes. At the Oct. 20 meeting a resident asked for reinstatement of an expired license.

sources.body: Regular Meeting of the Board of Trustees

blue-river/2.title: Transition Zone District lot size and setback changes (Ordinances 2026-06 and 2026-07)
blue-river/2.summary: Ordinance 2026-06 sets minimum lot size, lot width and setbacks in the Transition Zone District. Ordinance 2026-07 would make the Development Code effective Oct. 1, 2026, conditioned on 2026-06 being in force. A resident commented on setbacks at the Sept. 15 hearing.

sources.body: Regular Meeting of the Board of Trustees
Regular Meeting of the Board of Trustees

blue-river/3.title: Proposed 2027 budget
blue-river/3.summary: The Board was scheduled to receive a presentation and discuss the proposed 2027 budget on Oct. 20. The August financial packet shows a mill levy of 10.459 after a temporary credit and about $930,583 in projected property tax revenue.

sources.body: Regular Meeting of the Board of Trustees
Regular Meeting of the Board of Trustees

blue-river/4.title: Sewer, septic and traffic concerns raised by residents
blue-river/4.summary: Residents raised aging septic systems and environmental concerns along Blue River Road and asked the Town to explore grants, financing and partnerships for future sewer infrastructure. Others raised neighboring construction and easements, and speeding on Indiana Creek Road with requests for traffic calming.
blue-river/4.where: Blue River Road and Indiana Creek Road

sources.body: Regular Meeting of the Board of Trustees

blue-river/5.title: Planning Commission review of 1253 Indiana Creek Road residence and other projects
blue-river/5.summary: The Commission held a work session on a proposed residence at 1253 Indiana Creek Road. It discussed the 35-foot height limit, recessed garage entrances, garage area limits, two separate living areas and possible restrictive covenants. A detached garage and variance at 0809 Blue River Rd, shed provisions in the land use code and wetland protection items are also on the agenda.
blue-river/5.where: 1253 Indiana Creek Road; 0809 Blue River Rd

blue-river/6.title: Goose Pasture Tarn boat dock rules repealed
blue-river/6.summary: The Board considered Resolution 2026-10, repealing Resolution 13-05 on rules and permits for private boat docks at Goose Pasture Tarn. The Town Attorney gave background and the Board moved to adopt it.

sources.body: Regular Meeting of the Board of Trustees
Regular Meeting of the Board of Trustees

blue-river/7.title: Summit School District mill levy override (Ballot Measure 4A)
blue-river/7.summary: Summit School District presented Ballot Measure 4A, a mill levy override that would raise up to $5.9 million a year, and the statewide Proposition NN. Funds would mainly support staff pay and retention amid turnover and cost of living.

sources.body: Regular Meeting of the Board of Trustees

blue-river/8.title: Summit County Hazard Mitigation Plan 2026
blue-river/8.summary: The Board was asked to adopt Resolution 2026-13 adopting the Summit County Hazard Mitigation Plan 2026.

sources.body: Regular Meeting of the Board of Trustees

boone/0.title: New water treatment facility startup, leaks and draws
boone/0.summary: Boone's new water treatment plant moved from operator training (March) toward startup in early May 2026, with periodic loan/grant draws and a 2-year warranty. By August the council said a leak in the GreenSands room and chlorine pump problems needed further investigation, and a bottled water advisory was lifted by the state health department in July.

boone/1.title: Water/sewer billing procedure ordinance and landlord-tenant section
boone/1.summary: The council spent months drafting an ordinance on water bill dates, late, reconnect and disconnect fees. The tenant/landlord responsibility section (Section 9) was repeatedly reworded, and the ordinance was approved and signed on Oct 14, 2026, with 30 days of posting before it takes effect. A new utility billing system with card and ACH payments was also approved.

boone/2.title: Water and sewer tap fee ordinance
boone/2.summary: A tap fee ordinance was in the works from January, read and accepted in June, and finalized, signed and posted by July 29, 2026. In October the council also discussed a sewer tap for a resident, who is responsible for issues up to the tap.

boone/3.title: Fire protection IGA with Edison Fire Protection District
boone/3.summary: Boone worked out an intergovernmental agreement and lease with the Edison fire district to cover fire service. Council accepted the IGA in April and adopted a resolution approving the IGA and contracts on May 7, 2026.

boone/4.title: Adopting Southern Colorado Building Department codes and amended IGA
boone/4.summary: The town worked with the Southern Colorado Building Department (SCBD/SOCOBD) attorney to update ordinances based on Pueblo regional codes for code enforcement. The ordinances were reviewed, finalized and posted Oct 14, 2026 (one was missed), while the amended IGA was tabled until Nov 18 so Rockvail can be added.

boone/5.title: Refuse rate increase
boone/5.summary: A 3% trash fee increase under the town's contract was discussed in June. Council approved a resolution for the refuse rate increase on July 29, and all members signed it Aug 19, 2026.

boone/6.title: Park playground equipment, mower and sprinklers
boone/6.summary: Council discussed the town park needing new playground equipment, and the Edison fire chief suggested USDA and GOCO grants. Eight sprinkler heads were replaced after mowing damage and council approved buying a new mower. A park memorial re-dedication for the 250th anniversary was also on the June agenda.

boone/7.title: Town administrator appointment and employee handbook
boone/7.summary: Council approved a resolution appointing a town administrator in August 2026, with a follow-up completed in September. An employee handbook workshop was set.

boone/8.title: Internet service change and 2026 budget
boone/8.summary: Council discussed switching the town from CenturyLink to Starlink at a $280 flat monthly fee. Separate budget meetings were held in March and April 2026.

boulder-county/0.title: 2027 Boulder County budget
boulder-county/0.summary: Commissioners held a town hall on the 2027 budget (Aug. 18), department presentations (Oct. 13-22), a public hearing on the recommended budget on Oct. 22, and a Nov. 5 work session. Adoption is scheduled for Dec. 8. Budgets for five county public improvement districts were also reviewed.

boulder-county/1.title: Land Use Code rules for data centers and detention centers
boulder-county/1.summary: The Planning Commission agenda for Oct. 21 includes text amendments defining data centers and detention centers as specific land uses. The amendments would set where and at what scale each may be permitted in unincorporated Boulder County.

boulder-county/2.title: Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan major update
boulder-county/2.summary: The Planning Commission and the commissioners conditionally approved the ten-year major update (BVCP-25-0001), including Rural Lands text amendments. The commissioners adopted the approving resolution on Oct. 13.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting
Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting

boulder-county/3.title: Amicus brief supporting Cook County assault-weapon ban
boulder-county/3.summary: The county asked commissioners to ratify its participation with other jurisdictions in a U.S. Supreme Court amicus brief in Viramontes v. Cook County. The brief supports Cook County's ban on certain semiautomatic firearms, including AR-15-style rifles.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting

boulder-county/4.title: Ballot measure to expand Board of Commissioners from 3 to 5
boulder-county/4.summary: Commissioners fixed ballot titles for a citizen initiative petition to increase the board from three to five members. It will appear on the Nov. 3, 2026 ballot. The board also considered taking positions on other 2026 ballot measures.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting
Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting

boulder-county/5.title: Eldorado Springs wastewater plant debt ballot question
boulder-county/5.summary: Sitting as the Eldorado Springs Public Improvement District board, commissioners referred a debt authorization question to the Nov. 3 ballot. The money would pay for wastewater treatment plant improvements required by the state health department.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting
Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting

boulder-county/6.title: Affordable housing funding and Housing Authority actions
boulder-county/6.summary: The county reviewed its Affordable and Attainable Housing Tax Innovation Fund and awarded $1,084,000 for Willoughby Corner Phases II and III in Lafayette. It assigned private activity bond volume cap to the Housing Authority and renewed a $956,189 rapid re-housing grant. The Housing Authority's 2027 Annual Plan and Moving to Work supplement were approved after a public hearing.
boulder-county/6.where: Countywide; Willoughby Corner, 928 Canterbury Drive, Lafayette

boulder-county/7.title: Longmont 1st & Main urban renewal tax increment agreement
boulder-county/7.summary: Boulder County considered a tax increment financing agreement with the Longmont Urban Renewal Authority for 1st & Main redevelopment. The project includes a regional transit center, environmental cleanup and public infrastructure.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting
Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting

boulder-county/8.title: Riverside Cabins Lodge special review revocation hearing
boulder-county/8.summary: Staff recommended revoking the Special Review approval (SU-23-0013) for violating conditions. Commissioners declined to revoke and continued the hearing to Jan. 7, 2027, to see if the conditions are met. A Lyons Fire Protection District representative spoke.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting

boulder-county/9.title: Energy Impact Offset Fund sunset and marijuana rules
boulder-county/9.summary: Commissioners approved Resolution 2026-070 after a hearing. It sunsets the fee on cultivators based on energy use and amends marijuana regulations, including extending license terms from one year to two.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting

boulder-county/10.title: Apahapa LLC Flagstaff Road boundary line appeal
boulder-county/10.summary: An appeal of a director's decision on a boundary line adjustment between parcels at 6808 and 7022 Flagstaff Road, which also denied recognition of 6808 Flagstaff as a parcel. Commissioners tabled it to Dec. 3 and will take public comment then.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting

boulder-county/11.title: Wildfire mitigation grants and fire restrictions
boulder-county/11.summary: The county funded fuels mitigation grants, including $191,350 for Superior grazing and $990,262.88 for the Conifer Hill work, and added $30K for the wildfire awareness campaign. Stage 1 fire restrictions in the mountain area were rescinded effective Oct. 15.
boulder-county/11.where: Superior, Conifer Hill and mountain areas

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting

boulder-county/12.title: Eldora Resort cell tower
boulder-county/12.summary: Commissioners conditionally approved a 100-foot Verizon macro-cell tower on a 46-acre forestry-zoned parcel at Eldora Resort. A resolution followed on Oct. 13.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting
Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting

boulder-county/13.title: Agricultural water share purchases
boulder-county/13.summary: Parks and Open Space proposed buying 20 shares of the Boulder and White Rock Ditch company for $450,000 and one James Ditch share for $120,000. The aim is better irrigation on county agricultural open space.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting
Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting

boulder-county/14.title: Tucker Complex interim management and zero waste plan
boulder-county/14.summary: A work session covered an interim management proposal for the Tucker Complex and a Zero Waste Plan update on fees and composting. Related grants fund construction and deconstruction material reuse policy.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting

boulder/0.title: Annexation of 1275 Cherryvale Rd. and 5995 McSorley Ln.
boulder/0.summary: Council took up a petition to annex about 5.43 acres at 1275 Cherryvale Rd. and 5995 McSorley Ln. with initial Residential – Rural 2 (RR-2) zoning. The item was removed from the Aug. 20 agenda and returned Oct. 1 with Ordinance 8764 on first reading and a public hearing date of Nov. 12, 2026.

boulder/1.title: 2027 city budget and special district budgets
boulder/1.summary: Council held a study session on the 2027 Recommended Budget on Sept. 10 and accepted its summary Oct. 1. On Oct. 15 it considered 2027 budgets and mill levies for the Central Area GID, University Hill GID, Boulder Municipal Property Authority and the Boulder Junction Access GID.

boulder/2.title: Wildfire resilience and home hardening hub
boulder/2.summary: Council is working on a priority project to build a Wildfire Home Hardening Implementation Hub and to assess current and planned city wildfire programs. It was discussed at study sessions on Aug. 27 and Oct. 22, and the summary was accepted Oct. 1.

boulder/3.title: Affordable housing bonds for Boulder Housing Partners, including Harvest34
boulder/3.summary: Council considered assigning $7,333,256 in 2026 private activity bonds to Boulder Housing Partners for permanently affordable rental housing. It also considered a public approval certificate for multifamily revenue bonds to finance the Harvest34 project.

boulder/4.title: Frasier and Naropa campus redevelopment proposals
boulder/4.summary: A Site Review Amendment would redevelop the Frasier campus into a joint campus, with a 55-foot, four-story independent living building holding 96 apartments and underground parking. A separate Site Review application to redevelop the Naropa campus was also on the Oct. 1 agenda.

boulder/5.title: Arapahoe Avenue rezoning and Marine Street right-of-way vacation
boulder/5.summary: Council took up first reading of Ordinance 8774, rezoning about 3.72 acres at 2106 and 2130 Arapahoe Ave. and adjacent land from RH-2 to RH-5. It also considered Ordinance 8775 vacating a portion of Marine Street right-of-way next to 2130 Arapahoe Ave.

boulder/6.title: Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan 10-year update
boulder/6.summary: Council considered on first reading Ordinance 8784 adopting the 2025 major 10-year update to the Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan.

boulder/7.title: Civic Area East Bookend development partnership RFP
boulder/7.summary: Council discussed a request for proposals for a development partnership on the Civic Area East Bookend at an Aug. 13 study session. The summary was accepted Sept. 17.

boulder/8.title: Xcel Energy facility expansion and power reliability forum
boulder/8.summary: A concept plan proposes expanding the Xcel Energy service and operations facility at 2655 N. 63rd Street. Council also held an Oct. 8 community forum on its priority project of power reliability and resilience.

boulder/9.title: Support for Boulder County ballot measure on commissioners
boulder/9.summary: Council discussed supporting the county ballot measure to change from 3 to 5 commissioners. On Sept. 17 it considered Resolution 1391 in support of the county's citizens' measure.

boulder/10.title: Restaurant and small business task force
boulder/10.summary: Council discussed on Sept. 3 whether to form a restaurant/small business task force.

boulder/11.title: Pedal cab licensing ordinance
boulder/11.summary: Ordinance 8757 would create licenses and fees for pedal cab agencies and drivers. It was introduced Aug. 20 and came up for second reading Sept. 3.

boulder/12.title: Marijuana code amendments (Ordinance 8770)
boulder/12.summary: Council considered amendments to the medical and recreational marijuana chapters, with first reading Sept. 3 and second reading Sept. 17.

breckenridge/0.title: Flock license plate cameras and the automated license plate reader program
breckenridge/0.summary: Residents told Council on Aug. 25 they are worried about Flock cameras capturing license plates and vehicle signals, with broad data-use rights and little oversight, and asked for better communication on camera placement and the contract renewal due March 2027. Council had an automated license plate reader program presentation on its Oct. 13 agenda.

breckenridge/1.title: 2027 budget, mill levy and capital improvement plan
breckenridge/1.summary: Council held a budget retreat on Oct. 13 covering the 2027 budget process and strategic goals, including housing and code enforcement. On Oct. 27 it was scheduled to take up the ordinance setting the 2027 mill levy (Council Bill 11) and a resolution adopting the 2027 budget and capital improvement plan. Open Space staff also presented a preliminary budget based on flat sales tax projections.

breckenridge/2.title: Housing Helps program and workforce housing density
breckenridge/2.summary: Residents thanked Council for the Housing Helps program, in which the Town buys homes and keeps them for locals, and urged continued robust funding. Planning Commission reviewed staff recommendations on workforce housing density for underutilized parcels, including 30 units per acre along Park Avenue, with concerns about views from Carter Park. Council also scheduled housing and accessory dwelling unit policy discussions.
breckenridge/2.where: Townwide; Carter Park and Park Avenue corridor

breckenridge/3.title: City Market fuel center redesign at 430 N. Park Avenue
breckenridge/3.summary: Planning Commission held repeated preliminary hearings on a new City Market fuel center, with a redesigned mountain-style look using stone veneer, faux wood shingles and metal roof, plus Park Avenue screening and tree removal at Airport Road. Commissioners praised the redesign and asked for a sample board at the final hearing; future demolition and remediation of the existing fuel center is included. No public comments were made at the hearing.

breckenridge/4.title: Mamba Trust retaining wall variance at 219 Glen Eagle Loop
breckenridge/4.summary: Planning Commission considered a variance to let part of an unpermitted retaining wall remain outside the platted disturbance envelope; staff said about 75 feet would need removal to comply. The owner's architect argued the wall's setting, and commissioners asked how disturbance envelopes are created.

breckenridge/5.title: Little Red Schoolhouse expansion
breckenridge/5.summary: The Town project to expand the Little Red Schoolhouse at 600 Reiling Road went through a Planning Commission work session on Sept. 15, a Commission hearing Oct. 6 and was on the Oct. 27 Council agenda for a hearing.

breckenridge/6.title: Trails at Berlin Placer water service and bond negotiations
breckenridge/6.summary: In executive session Sept. 8 Council received legal advice and discussed a town agreement for water service to the Trails at Berlin Placer development, and the Town Attorney was instructed to begin negotiations on bond money for it. A resident also asked on Aug. 25 about partnering with the Town for water service for housing units on Highway 9.

breckenridge/7.title: Lawsuit against MW Golden
breckenridge/7.summary: Council met in executive session on Aug. 11 to discuss negotiations and receive legal advice on the Town's litigation against MW Golden.

breckenridge/8.title: Support for school funding measures 4A, 1A and Proposition NN
breckenridge/8.summary: Council added and passed resolutions supporting Summit County's Strong Futures referred measure and the Summit School District mill levy override (Ballot Measure 4A), which would extend funding without new or increased taxes. It also scheduled a resolution backing statewide Proposition NN, which would raise public education funding 2% a year for 10 years. Council also held executive sessions on negotiations with Summit School District over real property.

breckenridge/9.title: Open space trails, Tiger Road Rec Path and downhill trail demand
breckenridge/9.summary: Open Space commission discussed a trails prioritization matrix, with Phase 1 of the Tiger Road Rec Path scoring well, and residents urged more hand-built downhill trails at Little Mountain. It approved trail names and discussed Little Daisy Open Space trail work and Quandary Trailhead improvements, with $400,000 in town matching funds pledged for a grant application.
breckenridge/9.where: Little Mountain, Tiger Road, Quandary Trailhead, Little Daisy Open Space

breckenridge/10.title: Aspen Alley seasonal shuttle and parking management
breckenridge/10.summary: Staff presented a seasonal plan for Aspen Alley with a free shuttle funded by a transit grant, police patrols and citations against illegal parking, and later reported strong compliance and plans to seek ongoing grant funding.

breckenridge/11.title: Wellington-Oro and French Gulch water treatment plant
breckenridge/11.summary: Staff are budgeting for engineering consultants to optimize treatment of cadmium and zinc, including pilot-testing an aeration pond, ahead of a critical 2029 Water Quality Control Commission hearing where the Town and County aim to show good-faith progress.

breckenridge/12.title: Worker and resident parking permits
breckenridge/12.summary: A resident told Council that permitted parking for workers and residents is hard to find and suggested gated permit lots, towing and expanding parking into South Gondola lots or the parking structure. Council also amended the delivery zone program on Sept. 8, updating fees and penalties.

brighton/0.title: 180-day data center moratorium
brighton/0.summary: Council took up an ordinance pausing acceptance, processing or approval of permits, licenses, zoning or other land use applications where a data center is a proposed use. It had initial consideration on Oct. 6 and an amended version came up for final consideration on Oct. 20.

brighton/1.title: Case Farms PUD rezoning (232 acres)
brighton/1.summary: Council held a public hearing and first reading on a zoning map amendment moving about 232 acres from Case Farms PUD to R-2 and open space and parks zoning. The Planning Commission had already acted on it (Resolution 26-09), and it returned on Sept. 1.

brighton/2.title: Bromley Park PUD 38th and 39th amendments
brighton/2.summary: Council heard the Bromley Park PUD 38th Amendment near the I-76 frontage road and North 60th Avenue on Sept. 15 and Oct. 6, with an ordinance on Oct. 20. A 39th Amendment covering about 5.92 acres on Bromley Business Parkway near the BNSF railroad also came up Oct. 20.
brighton/2.where: I-76 Frontage Road and North 60th Avenue; Bromley Business Parkway

brighton/3.title: 2027-2028 budget, mill levy and 2027 fees
brighton/3.summary: Council reviewed the proposed 2027 and 2028 budgets and a Q2 2026 financial update in August. A 2027 rate and fee proposal followed in September, and the 2027 budget, mill levy and fees were on the Oct. 20 agenda. A third 2026 budget amendment was heard Oct. 6.

brighton/4.title: Comprehensive Plan and land use code rewrite
brighton/4.summary: Council reviewed the 80% draft of the Comprehensive Plan, land use scenarios for city-owned property on Bridge Street, and amendments to Land Use and Development Code Articles 1, 10 and 11. Articles 1 and 11 went to public hearing Sept. 15 and Oct. 6. Floodplain amendments to Section 10.02 followed Oct. 20.

brighton/5.title: Water system: bond refunding, chemicals and well contamination lawsuit
brighton/5.summary: Council considered refunding the 2016 water revenue bonds with Series 2026 refunding bonds. It also awarded master price agreements for water treatment chemicals to Univar and PVS DX. On Oct. 6 it approved filing an amended complaint adding defendants in a case over contamination of a city drinking water well.

brighton/6.title: Lupton Meadows reservoir and Cherry Meadows pond work
brighton/6.summary: Council reviewed Cherry Meadows pond maintenance and the Lupton Meadows reservoir design in study session. It then considered Change Order No. 3 with Engineering Analytics for the Lupton Meadow Reservoir design project.

brighton/7.title: Police JAG grant and Flock
brighton/7.summary: Council considered accepting an Edward Byrne Memorial JAG grant and authorizing the police chief to sign it and other public safety grant agreements. Attached materials refer to Flock.

brighton/8.title: Board and commission appointment policy and Sustainability Board changes
brighton/8.summary: Council revised its policy on interviewing and appointing members of city boards and commissions. An ordinance amending Sustainability Board membership also moved forward in August and September.

brighton/9.title: South Brighton GID ballot content
brighton/9.summary: The South Brighton General Improvement District considered a resolution to certify ballot content for an election.

campo/0.title: 2055 Metropolitan Transportation Plan and Capital Blvd/US 1 North tolling
campo/0.summary: CAMPO held public hearings on the 2055 Metropolitan Transportation Plan, with the Board approving the draft in November 2025 and final adoption set for February. Staff recommended removing the U-5307 Capital Blvd/US 1 North project as a tolled project, reversing the Board's earlier action authorizing tolling to speed it up.
campo/0.where: Capital Boulevard / US 1 North, Wake County

campo/1.title: Triangle Bikeway East design alignment
campo/1.summary: The TCC and Executive Board were asked to endorse a technical alignment for the Triangle Bikeway East to carry forward to 30% design. A resident spoke against the project in November, citing mining regulations, zoning and active lawsuits on the property.

campo/2.title: FY 2027 Wake Transit Work Plan and Wake Bus Plan 2035
campo/2.summary: The draft and recommended FY 2027 Wake Transit Work Plan went through public hearings and TCC and Board approval in May and June. The Board also approved a Wake Bus Plan 2035 contract with Nelson\Nygaard in January, and a speaker in November backed the 2035 Wake Transit Plan.

campo/3.title: Regional Transit Technology Plan
campo/3.summary: The TCC and Executive Board approved the Regional Transit Technology Plan as a guiding document for future transit technology investment. It covers real-time passenger information, integrated payments, data standards and an open data portal, and an extra 30-day comment period drew no comments.

campo/4.title: Triangle Mobility Hub locally preferred alternative
campo/4.summary: GoTriangle sought approval of the Locally Preferred Alternative for the Triangle Mobility Hub. After a public hearing in June, where comments generally supported the project, the Executive Board moved to approve it. The Triangle West board approved it the day before.

campo/5.title: FFY 2027 LAPP projects and Crabtree Creek Greenway funding
campo/5.summary: CAMPO reviewed 19 submitted projects for FFY 2027 Locally Administered Projects Program funding and recommended the top roadway projects, including Rolesville at Riley Hill and Holly Springs Road. Raleigh also requested additional funding for the Crabtree Creek Greenway at Lassiter Mill, which requires a 50/50 match. The FFY 2028 target modal mix and call for projects are coming in August 2026.
campo/5.where: Wake County; Crabtree Creek Greenway at Lassiter Mill, Raleigh

campo/6.title: NC 540 bonus allocation projects and TIP amendments
campo/6.summary: CAMPO worked with NCDOT Division 5 to refine costs for 16 projects selected for the NC 540 bonus allocation, including a Neuse River bridge and Benson Road widening. They were included in TIP Amendment #3, approved after a May public hearing with no public comments received. The amendment also added an RDU interchange project at Aviation Boulevard and removed a Cary trail project. Amendment #4 is up for a public hearing in August.
campo/6.where: Johnston and Wake Counties; Aviation Blvd, RDU

campo/7.title: NCDOT cost estimate requirement and project delivery deadline
campo/7.summary: NCDOT is requiring cost estimates (CSCE) for prioritized projects, with all to be completed by September 30, 2027. CAMPO has 27 projects programmed that need plans to meet the deadline. TCC members questioned the status of projects such as the Western Boulevard Tunnel, and the Chair asked for more frequent updates.

campo/8.title: FAST Transit and Wake BRT corridor projects
campo/8.summary: Consultants presented FAST Transit concepts such as transit priority lanes on Blue Ridge Road and options on I-540 and I-40. The Wake BRT update noted that Raleigh has had difficulty getting bids on the New Bern Avenue project, which is under construction.
campo/8.where: New Bern Avenue, Blue Ridge Road, I-40, I-540

campo/9.title: NCDOT Division resurfacing and safety projects
campo/9.summary: NCDOT Division 5 and 6 staff briefed the TCC on resurfacing and safety projects, including the Angier Bypass, scheduled for April 2028. CAMPO staff asked whether FY 2028 resurfacing projects could be expanded to add intersection improvements through LAPP.

castle-pines/0.title: Annexation Policy and citizen-initiated charter amendment requiring voter approval of annexations
castle-pines/0.summary: Council adopted an Annexation Policy (Resolution 26-49) with a minor wording addition after continuing it from Aug. 11, and placed a citizen-initiated charter amendment on the ballot. It also passed Resolution 26-53 opposing the measure, which would require voter approval for certain large annexations. The Chamber of Commerce spoke against the ballot measure and a resident asked for a public-meeting timeline.

sources.body: City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting

castle-pines/1.title: Site Improvement Plan zoning amendment (Ordinance 26-06)
castle-pines/1.summary: Council took up Ordinance 26-06, which amends Section 27 (Site Improvement Plan) of the zoning ordinance, on first reading Aug. 11 and held a public hearing Aug. 25. A speaker wanted comprehensive plan elements left in and a holistic review; another said it gives a clear, predictable process. Council moved to adopt it after the hearing.

sources.body: City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting

castle-pines/2.title: Canyonside Preliminary Plan and replat approvals
castle-pines/2.summary: The Planning Commission held a hearing Sept. 24 and recommended approval of the Canyonside Preliminary Plan No. 1, 2nd Amendment (PFP-2026-001), presented by North Canyons Development. Council held a hearing Oct. 13 and moved to approve it (Resolution 26-62) with a condition on the Subdivision Improvement Agreement. A Filing No. 1, 3rd Amendment replat (Resolution 26-65) was on the Oct. 27 agenda.

sources.body: City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting
City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting

castle-pines/3.title: Happy Canyon Road/I-25 interchange agreements
castle-pines/3.summary: Council approved a series of agreements with the State and CDOT for the Happy Canyon Road/I-25 Interchange Project, including IGA amendments and an agreement on construction, maintenance and operations. A first amendment to estimating services was approved Oct. 13. The Oct. 27 agenda included further IGAs on BTE funds and CDOT maintenance and operations.

sources.body: City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting
City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting
City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting

castle-pines/4.title: Transfer of recreation properties and tracts from Castle Pines North district
castle-pines/4.summary: Ordinances 26-08 and 26-09 convey recreation properties and tracts of land under an intergovernmental agreement with the Castle Pines North district. They were introduced Sept. 22 and had a combined public hearing Oct. 13, after which motions were made to adopt both.

sources.body: City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting
City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting

castle-pines/5.title: Proposed 2027 city budget
castle-pines/5.summary: The City Manager presented the proposed 2027 budget on Oct. 20, with conservative revenue projections and 104 projected new home permits. Construction use tax is projected to fall 36% in 2027 and building permit and planning revenue to decline. Priorities include the Road Solutions Plan, a second Parks foreman, a Trails Master Plan update and research on lodging and admissions taxes.

castle-pines/6.title: Development notification and public input process
castle-pines/6.summary: Residents asked for a centralized online place for development information, more time than three minutes for comment, and notice to adjacent property owners. A Village at Castle Pines HOA resident asked that the HOA be included in development referrals.

sources.body: City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting

castle-pines/7.title: Trail signage, Coyote Ridge Park and Soaring Hawk Park
castle-pines/7.summary: The Parks board discussed signage for 35 trail segments (kiosks, directional signs and mile markers) with options at different costs and looks. It also reviewed the Coyote Ridge Park renovation and Soaring Hawk Park phasing, continued into October.

sources.body: Parks and Recreation Advisory Board Meeting
Parks and Recreation Advisory Board Meeting
Parks and Recreation Advisory Board Meeting

castle-pines/8.title: Affordable housing expedited review and Comprehensive Plan update
castle-pines/8.summary: The Planning Commission held a study session on an affordable housing expedited review and overlay project. It also had the kickoff of the 2026 Comprehensive Plan update with consultant feedback.

castle-pines/9.title: South Havana Street right-of-way vacation and council redistricting
castle-pines/9.summary: Ordinance 26-11 would vacate part of South Havana Street within a final plat. Ordinance 26-10, redrawing the boundaries of the city's three districts, passed first reading Oct. 13 and was set for second reading Oct. 27.

sources.body: City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting
City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting

centennial/0.title: Elevation Volleyball annexation, initial zoning and public hearing
centennial/0.summary: The council accepted an annexation petition in August, and the Planning Commission reviewed initial zoning for the Elevation Volleyball Annexation, moving from Arapahoe County mixed-use zoning. Annexation and zoning ordinances (2026-O-11 and O-12) were set for first reading on Sept. 15 and public hearings on Oct. 6.

centennial/1.title: Rezoning Fremont Avenue and Potomac Street site from PUD to light industry
centennial/1.summary: Ordinance 2026-O-14 would rezone property north of East Fremont Avenue and east of Potomac Street from Planned Unit Development to Employment Center – Light Industry 50. It went from the Planning Commission (Aug. 26) to first reading Sept. 1 and a council public hearing Sept. 15.
centennial/1.where: North of E. Fremont Ave and east of Potomac St

centennial/2.title: Legislative rezoning of Business Park land to Employment Center
centennial/2.summary: The city is pursuing legislative rezonings of Business Park (BP) land to Employment Center districts, with legal advice on regulating industrial and business park uses. Ordinances 2026-O-18 (south of E. Nichols Ave and east of S. Akron St) and 2026-O-19 (west of S. Chester St) were heard by the Planning Commission Nov. 4 and set for council hearings Nov. 17.
centennial/2.where: S. Akron St/E. Nichols Ave and S. Chester St areas

sources.body: Special Meeting of the Planning and Zoning Commission

centennial/3.title: 2027/2028 biennium budget
centennial/3.summary: Council and the Budget Committee reviewed revenues, fund balance and the City Manager's proposed 2027/2028 budget in September and October workshops.

centennial/4.title: Sales and use tax rate increase and November election
centennial/4.summary: In August, council considered resolutions on an intergovernmental agreement for the election and on authorizing a sales and use tax rate increase. A related ordinance (2026-O-21) amending tax provisions in the municipal code was set for hearing Nov. 17.

centennial/5.title: Opting out of the state graywater program
