centennial/5.summary: Ordinance 2026-O-15 would opt Centennial out of the state graywater program and prohibit graywater treatment works and graywater use. It had first reading Sept. 1 and a hearing Sept. 15.

centennial/6.title: Land Development Code amendments
centennial/6.summary: Staff presented proposed Land Development Code amendments to council and the Planning Commission in October. A Nov. 4 commission item covered possible code changes on utilities.

sources.body: Special Meeting of the Planning and Zoning Commission

centennial/7.title: Livable Streets residential collectors next phase
centennial/7.summary: Council discussed the next phase of the Livable Streets program for residential collector streets on Oct. 20.

centennial/8.title: Housing finance bond allocation and grant-funded budget amendment
centennial/8.summary: In August council considered assigning private activity bond ceiling to the Colorado Housing and Finance Authority, and amending the 2026 budget to accept an agreement for grant funding.

centennial/9.title: City manager contract and budget/investment committee changes
centennial/9.summary: Council took up a first amendment to the city manager's employment agreement and an ordinance changing the investment and budget committees, with a hearing set for Nov. 17.

chaffee-county/0.title: Corrigan Rezone in Garfield (Hwy 50)
chaffee-county/0.summary: A rezone of several parcels at 22420 and 22435 Hwy 50 in historic Garfield from Residential Rural to Mixed Use Rural would make them eligible for commercial lodging. The Planning Commission heard from neighbors who raised spot zoning, noise, unpermitted structures, fire and septic concerns, and the application went to the County Commissioners for a public hearing on Oct 20. The rezone is described as a remediation of a land use code violation.

chaffee-county/1.title: Regional Housing Needs Assessment and affordable housing efforts
chaffee-county/1.summary: Commissioners reviewed the final 2026 Regional Housing Needs Assessment, done with Buena Vista, Poncha Springs and Salida, and the Planning Commission held an affordable housing work session. The county also agreed to be fiscal host for a state asbestos-removal grant for River Village Mobile Home Park with Chaffee Housing Trust, and approved a $25,000 lodging-tax-funded fee reimbursement for the park.
chaffee-county/1.where: Countywide; River Village Mobile Home Park

sources.body: Board of Commissioners Work Session - 1st Monday
Board of Commissioners Work Session - 2nd Monday

chaffee-county/2.title: Airport land lease, development area and 2027 budget
chaffee-county/2.summary: The Airport Advisory Board discussed a new land lease at length, plans for a new development area, and the 2027 airport budget. Budget items include old fuel farm removal (about $48,000 eligible for reimbursement), a well for the development area, a master drainage plan and Taxiway A rehabilitation design. Residents Ray and Ann Plumb and Barry Cole commented.

chaffee-county/3.title: 2027 tourism marketing budget and Destination Management Council
chaffee-county/3.summary: The Destination Management Council worked on the 2027 tourism budget, marketing plan, a five-year strategic plan and a response memo to the Colorado Tourism Office about a perceived conflict of interest. Lodging tax revenue was reported up 18% in unincorporated areas, and commissioners were to discuss a recommendation on website and AI enhancements funding.

sources.body: Board of Commissioners Work Session - 1st Monday

chaffee-county/4.title: Retail food establishment fee schedule
chaffee-county/4.summary: Public Health proposed new fees and requirements for retail food establishments, discussed at the Oct 19 work session. Commissioners were asked to approve the updated Retail Food Fee Schedule on Oct 20.

sources.body: Board of Commissioners Work Session - 2nd Monday

chaffee-county/5.title: Post-event review of August concert at The Meadows
chaffee-county/5.summary: Commissioners scheduled a public hearing on Oct 20 to review the August concert at The Meadows, following vendor permit review by Public Health.

sources.body: Board of Commissioners Work Session - 2nd Monday

chaffee-county/6.title: Wildfire risk, grants and utility letter to the PUC
chaffee-county/6.summary: Commissioners ratified letters of support for several Forest Restoration and Wildfire Risk Mitigation grant applications (Chateau Chaparral, Colorado Firecamp, Fire Protection District, Salida Fire). They also planned to discuss a letter to the Public Utilities Commission asking Xcel and Black Hills Energy to address wildfire risk. Emergency officials reported dry conditions and the Willow fire.

sources.body: Board of Commissioners Work Session - 1st Monday

chaffee-county/7.title: EMS medical director, regional tactical agreement and 911 equipment
chaffee-county/7.summary: Commissioners approved a services agreement with Dr. Michael Mandrell as EMS Medical Director and an intergovernmental agreement with Buena Vista for regional tactical services. The 911 board discussed replacing aging Motorola consoles and amending the 2026 budget.

chaffee-county/8.title: County fleet EV study and budget hearings
chaffee-county/8.summary: A fellowship presentation on electric vehicles looked at fuel and maintenance cost comparisons, grants and replacement timing. Commissioners also held 2027 budget hearings, including the Sheriff's Office, and received the 2025 audit and a Human Services budget review.

sources.body: Board of Commissioners Work Session - 2nd Monday
Board of Commissioners Work Session - 2nd Monday
Board of Commissioners Work Session - 2nd Monday
Board of Commissioners Work Session - 1st Monday

chaffee-county/9.title: Chaffee County archery range ground lease with Colorado Parks & Wildlife
chaffee-county/9.summary: Commissioners approved entering a ground lease with CPW for operational management of the county archery range, with staff to finalize terms.

clear-creek-county/0.title: Lodging tax increase ballot question (Resolution R-26-55)
clear-creek-county/0.summary: Commissioners considered Resolution R-26-55 to send voters in unincorporated Clear Creek County and its towns (except Georgetown) a question to increase the county lodging tax. Proceeds would go to tourism-related road maintenance, public safety, childcare and housing. A tourism bureau website and messaging presentation was also on the agenda.

clear-creek-county/1.title: 2027 county budget and 2026 budget check-in
clear-creek-county/1.summary: The board held a 2026 budget check-in and 2027 budget process work session, followed by a 2027 proposed budget workshop on Oct. 20. A public hearing on the 2027 budget for the county, Emergency Services GID and Housing Authority was set for Nov. 3, along with a 2026 supplemental budget appropriation (R-26-61).

clear-creek-county/2.title: Short-term rental ordinance (Ordinance No. 21)
clear-creek-county/2.summary: Commissioners took up first reading of Ordinance No. 21, which would replace Ordinance 19 on short-term rentals. Community feedback was gathered in October 2026, and written public comments and a summary of changes were in the packet.

clear-creek-county/3.title: Open fire ban ordinance (Ordinance No. 20) and wildfire preparedness
clear-creek-county/3.summary: The board held a public hearing on second reading of Ordinance No. 20, which repeals and replaces Ordinance 16 on regulations for banning open fires. It also heard a Public Safety Power Shutoff presentation and reviewed the 2026 wildfire mitigation plan. A resolution rescinding R-01-83 had a hearing the same day.

clear-creek-county/4.title: Waldorf inholding purchase by Georgetown and open space funds
clear-creek-county/4.summary: The Open Space Commission discussed the Town of Georgetown buying Parcel 2091-034-00-645 (Waldorf inholding). The commissioners took up Resolution R-26-60 to contribute Open Space Trust Fund money toward the purchase.

clear-creek-county/5.title: Alvarado Open Space Park project and Glass Memorial
clear-creek-county/5.summary: The Open Space Commission and commissioners reviewed a concept for Alvarado Open Space Park and next steps on a Glass Memorial there. Parking on county roads to reach open space was also discussed.

clear-creek-county/6.title: Open Space Commission rules and gate on Sheep Mountain access road
clear-creek-county/6.summary: The commission started discussing an update of its rules and regulations, using Jeffco open space regulations as a model. It also sought legal advice on adding a gate to an access road for the Sheep area and on a public lands manager position.

clear-creek-county/7.title: Proposition 123 shared affordable housing credits and childcare support
clear-creek-county/7.summary: Commissioners considered an intergovernmental agreement on sharing Proposition 123 affordable housing credits. They also took up an amendment to an agreement supporting childcare in the county.

clear-creek-county/8.title: CDOT I-70 Floyd Hill and Condition 9 requirements
clear-creek-county/8.summary: The board held work sessions on CDOT reporting about the I-70 Floyd Hill project and CDOT requirements for Condition 9.

clear-creek-county/9.title: Emergency services, Fire Authority and ambulance
clear-creek-county/9.summary: The county considered a letter of support for an ambulance nomination and nominated Bruce Hohne to the Clear Creek Fire Authority board. Negotiations over amending the Fire Authority's 2024 intergovernmental agreement were also on the agenda.

clear-creek-county/10.title: County Annex building and courthouse basement restoration
clear-creek-county/10.summary: Commissioners held a work session on the County Annex building. They also considered final payment and a contract amendment for the courthouse basement restoration project (CP 26-01).

clear-creek-county/11.title: Road easements, drainage and striping projects
clear-creek-county/11.summary: The county considered accepting US Forest Service public road easements for several county roads, including Little Bear Creek, Raven Ridge and Sinton roads. It also considered a pavement marking contract and drainage improvements contract (RC 26-02D).

colorado-springs/0.title: Project Taurus data center appeal at 1565 High Tech Way
colorado-springs/0.summary: City Council held a special September 17, 2026 hearing on appeals of the administrative approval of a development plan modification for Corporate Ridge Filing No. 1 Lot 4, known as Project Taurus. Staff flagged acoustic (noise) impacts and a sound monitoring plan, and public comment was capped at 120 speakers. Planning staff said the project has operational similarities to a data center.

colorado-springs/1.title: Homelessness Response Action Plan and car-camping ban
colorado-springs/1.summary: Council received a briefing on the Homelessness Response Action Plan and the upcoming budget request for it. Police reported 335 vehicles dealt with since the ordinance banning sleeping in cars took effect, and staff described the Safe Parking program. Councilmember Donelson asked whether the Chief Housing and Homelessness Officer role should be split into two positions.

colorado-springs/2.title: 2027 city budget, tax levy and furlough day elimination
colorado-springs/2.summary: Council reviewed a financial report showing 2026 revenue above projections, including strong retail marijuana tax growth, and discussed police and fire turnover and funding for park restrooms. An ordinance would use extra revenue to eliminate the November furlough day. Budget work and markup sessions were set for October, along with a 2026 tax levy of 3.209 mills payable in 2027 and the 2027 salary schedule.

colorado-springs/3.title: Business license fee increases and code rewrite
colorado-springs/3.summary: Council moved ordinances 26-52, 26-53 and 26-54 repealing and reordaining the business licensing, sales of goods and services, and adult use business articles of city code. A 2027 fee schedule for general business licenses would raise fees toward full cost recovery by 2029, bringing in about $81,000 in year one, with CPI adjustments after that.

colorado-springs/4.title: 501 N Wahsatch Ave residential conversion adjustment
colorado-springs/4.summary: The Planning Commission heard a Development Standards Adjustment to convert a 9,800 sq ft commercial site with two buildings to residential use. Neighbors raised concerns about limited parking and the owner remodeling before seeking zoning relief, while staff said the request met all criteria and six parking spaces would be provided.

colorado-springs/5.title: Kettle Creek development: metro district, setbacks and road vacation
colorado-springs/5.summary: Council approved a service plan for the Kettle Creek Metropolitan District north of Old Ranch Road. The Planning Commission considered a seven-foot street-loaded garage setback adjustment for the Unit B housing product at 2060 Old Ranch Road, and an ordinance to vacate about 2.42 acres of Kettle Creek Road was set for second reading.

colorado-springs/6.title: Annexations and Banning Lewis Ranch rezonings
colorado-springs/6.summary: Council accepted annexation petitions for Peacock Ranch South, Sellers, Huber Road, Klein Nos. 1-3 and Crow Foot additions. It also took up the Banning Lewis Ranch Village B2 rezone, with a slate of 16 Banning Lewis Ranch items later approved unanimously.
colorado-springs/6.where: Banning Lewis Ranch and eastern city edge

colorado-springs/7.title: Height allowances for accessory dwelling units
colorado-springs/7.summary: A proposed ordinance amending the Unified Development Code would change height limits for accessory dwelling units. It moved through Planning Commission work sessions and hearings and was scheduled for a City Council work session on October 26.

colorado-springs/8.title: Sale of Meadows Park Community Center
colorado-springs/8.summary: Council went into closed session on August 24 to get legal advice and give instructions to negotiators about selling Meadows Park. The documents give no outcome.

colorado-springs/9.title: Parks master plans and park land
colorado-springs/9.summary: Staff presented a new Parks Master Plan, and Council was set to consider a resolution adopting the 2026 Park System Master Plan. Related items include rezoning gifted land to Public Park at 1179 Golden Hills Road, a partial parcel donation, and a closed session on a property interest in Wilson Ranch Park.

colorado-springs/10.title: Utilities bonds, electric rates and Garden Valley wastewater agreement
colorado-springs/10.summary: Council took up Colorado Springs Utilities revenue bond ordinances for improvements and refunding, plus a resolution setting electric rates. It also approved an agreement for regional wastewater treatment with the Garden Valley district.

colorado-springs/11.title: Downtown and special district budgets and mill levies
colorado-springs/11.summary: Council reviewed 2027 budgets and mill levies for the Downtown Development Authority, Briargate GID (4.409 mills), Marketplace at Austin Bluffs GID (50 mills) and several special improvement maintenance districts. It also considered dissolving the Barnes & Powers South Business Improvement District.

colorado-springs/12.title: Historic Preservation Board ordinance and schedule changes
colorado-springs/12.summary: The board discussed moving its meeting time earlier and the difficulty of advancing the Historic Resources Survey Plan because of sporadic attendance. Staff outlined possible changes to the preservation ordinance, from a clearer designation process to a full rewrite.

columbine-valley/0.title: E-bike and e-scooter ordinance
columbine-valley/0.summary: Trustees raised concerns about electric bikes in January, and in April the police chief described the department's approach to e-bikes and e-scooters. Trustees then directed staff to draft an ordinance. A resident spoke in support in June, and trustees later reported positive support.

columbine-valley/1.title: Platte Canyon Road sidewalk project
columbine-valley/1.summary: Trustees approved additional spending on the sidewalk in June. In August a required design change was discussed and trustees directed staff to proceed. In September staff said the sidewalk would not go ahead because the design had changed too much.

columbine-valley/2.title: Annexation of 8 Hunter Run
columbine-valley/2.summary: Trustees approved Resolution #14 on the annexation of 8 Hunter Run in August. The October agenda lists Trustee Bill #11 on the annexation with a public hearing. In May the town also discussed an HOA's interest in annexing.

columbine-valley/3.title: 2026 and 2027 town budgets
columbine-valley/3.summary: Trustees held a public hearing on the 2026 budget in November 2025 and adopted it in December along with the property valuation resolution. A first draft of the 2027 budget with special projects was presented in September, and a second draft and a November public hearing were scheduled. A long-range financial forecast was also presented in August.

columbine-valley/4.title: Housing Needs Assessment
columbine-valley/4.summary: The town is preparing a Housing Needs Assessment. A community survey is underway, and staff expect the response rate to exceed the 20% target. A first draft was scheduled for the October 20 meeting.

columbine-valley/5.title: Pickleball noise and recreational lighting
columbine-valley/5.summary: A resident at 7 Fairway raised pickleball noise in February and asked for proactive action before the Columbine Country Villas development. Pickleball came up again in May. A November study session was set on recreational lighting.

columbine-valley/6.title: Jake brake ordinance
columbine-valley/6.summary: Trustee Bill #8 on engine compression brakes (jake brakes) passed first reading in July and second reading in August.

columbine-valley/7.title: Building, fire and traffic code updates
columbine-valley/7.summary: Trustees adopted updated building codes in November 2025 and amended the Model Traffic Code. They adopted the 2024 Fire Code in June. An ordinance on the Building Commissioner was tabled indefinitely in March. A land use and zoning update (Trustee Bill #10) was on the October agenda.

columbine-valley/8.title: Smoking and vaping ban in Town Park
columbine-valley/8.summary: Trustee Bill #4 prohibiting smoking and vaping in the Town Park passed first reading in March and second reading in April.

columbine-valley/9.title: Town fee schedule and permit fees
columbine-valley/9.summary: Trustees approved Resolution #13 setting a town-wide fee schedule in August. Trustee Bill #9 on permit fees was on the October agenda.

commerce-city/0.title: Data center moratorium and study
commerce-city/0.summary: Council took up a request for a data center moratorium ordinance and a motion to schedule a data center study session. A resident later asked Council to extend the Data Center Moratorium and spoke on water restrictions. The Environmental Policy and Innovation Commission has been researching data centers and was set to make a recommendation in October.

commerce-city/1.title: Colorado Blvd traffic, jake brakes and Chambers Road/120th Ave road work
commerce-city/1.summary: Residents complained about truck traffic, speeding, drainage and poor road conditions on Colorado Blvd. Council directed the City Manager to find a way to prohibit jake brakes by ordinance by the end of Q1 2027, and moved to improve 120th Avenue between Sable Boulevard and Chambers Road, including the I-76 bridge, before winter. Council also awarded a Chambers Road and Heartland Drive contract and received a Chambers Road widening update.

commerce-city/2.title: 2027 city budget, tax levy and district mill levies
commerce-city/2.summary: Council held a 2027 budget workshop in September and a public hearing on November 2 on adopting the 2027 city budget and the tax levy. The Northern Infrastructure, E-470 Commercial and E-470 Residential general improvement districts and the Urban Renewal Authority each continued their budget and mill levy hearings to November 2. Parks and recreation fee increases for 2027 were also reviewed.

sources.body: E-470 Commercial Area General Improvement District
E-470 Residential Area General Improvement District
E-470 Commercial Area General Improvement District
E-470 Residential Area General Improvement District

commerce-city/3.title: Land Development Code and citywide legislative rezoning
commerce-city/3.summary: Council and the Planning Commission reviewed the legislative rezoning project and proposed zoning maps, with public comment attached. Ordinance 2795, other code amendments and Tier 2 amendments to the 2025 Land Development Code were also on agendas. Ordinance 2811 would repeal and reenact the official zoning map, with property owner feedback attached.

commerce-city/4.title: Annexations: Third Creek East, South Platte Crossing Phase 2, and surrounded enclaves
commerce-city/4.summary: Council found the Third Creek East annexation petition (AN26-0002) in substantial compliance and set an eligibility hearing. It did the same for South Platte Crossing Phase 2 (AN26-0004, 0.61 acres at 7110 Colorado Blvd), which went to Planning Commission with a zoning request. Council also discussed annexing surrounded enclaves.
commerce-city/4.where: 7110 Colorado Blvd and Third Creek East area

commerce-city/5.title: Reunion Filing 39 final plat and Hogan Property PUD amendment
commerce-city/5.summary: Oakwood Homes asked the Planning Commission to approve a final plat creating 84 lots in the Reunion PUD near Chambers Road and Heartland Drive; public comment and an applicant response were in the packet. Council adopted on second reading an amendment to the Hogan Property PUD covering 16.82 acres near 15955 E 101st Way, with written comment.
commerce-city/5.where: Reunion PUD near Chambers Rd and Heartland Dr; 15955 E 101st Way

commerce-city/6.title: Housing Action Plan and Commerce City Housing Authority
commerce-city/6.summary: Council discussed the Commerce City Housing Authority and its current and developed affordable projects. Council and Planning Commission were also scheduled to see a consultant presentation on a Housing Action Plan.

commerce-city/7.title: Crown Enterprises development plan at 10251 Newark Street
commerce-city/7.summary: Council considered a resolution approving a development plan amendment for the Crown Enterprises property at 10251 Newark Street. The item was continued to a later date set by staff.

commerce-city/8.title: Rezoning at East 52nd Avenue and Ivy Street to heavy industrial
commerce-city/8.summary: Council approved on first reading a rezoning of properties at the southwest corner of East 52nd Avenue and Ivy Street from I-2 to I-3 high intensity industrial.
commerce-city/8.where: SW corner of E 52nd Ave and Ivy St

commerce-city/9.title: Police mobile command unit and public safety items
commerce-city/9.summary: Council took up a budget amendment (Ordinance 2796) to buy a mobile command unit from the SACFD for the police department. It also considered an amendment to the Axon master services agreement and a presentation on municipal noise ordinance options.

commerce-city/10.title: Oil and gas development north of the city and Suncor
commerce-city/10.summary: A Chevron-hosted meeting reviewed proposed oil and gas development north of the city, mentioned at the parks commission. Council also requested a study session with Suncor.

commerce-city/11.title: Parks, trails and recreation projects
commerce-city/11.summary: The parks commission heard about trails and the Prairieways Action Plan, and impact fees and land dedication for new development. Council awarded the Pioneer Park renovation contract and ordered a feasibility study of pump tracks and bike parks.

cortez/0.title: Park Village on 7th affordable rental development and 7th Street property
cortez/0.summary: Council got an update on the 7th Street property on Aug. 25. On Oct. 13 it considered authorizing the Mayor to sign CHFA's notification form for Park Village on 7th, a proposed affordable rental development on city-owned land at the former high school property.

cortez/1.title: Lodger's Tax increase ballot question
cortez/1.summary: Council took up Ordinance No. 1375 to set the ballot title for a 4% increase in the city's Lodger's Tax. The question goes to voters at the Nov. 3, 2026 general election.

cortez/2.title: Historic designations: Garland Home and 209 West Main
cortez/2.summary: Council moved Ordinance 1376 to designate the Garland Home at 120 East North Street for the City Register of Historic Resources (first reading Sept. 8, second reading Sept. 22). Ordinance 1377 does the same for the building at 209 West Main (second reading Oct. 13). A state grant amendment adds $50,000 and the CLG grant was accepted. The Planning Commission also reviewed Land Use Code revisions for historic designation.
cortez/2.where: 120 East North Street; 209 West Main Street

cortez/3.title: Water System Master Plan and Comprehensive Plan update
cortez/3.summary: Council considered adopting the 2026 Water System Master Plan on Sept. 22 and toured the water treatment plant Aug. 11. On Oct. 13 it considered awarding the Comprehensive Plan update, covering strategic growth and water supply, to SE Group.

cortez/4.title: Cortez Municipal Airport contracts and FBO lease
cortez/4.summary: Council considered terminating the Fixed Base Operator lease and operations agreement. It also took up an asbestos abatement bid, extending the TSA terminal lease through June 2031, and a five-year engineering services contract starting Dec. 1, 2026. A youth seat on the Airport Advisory Committee was also considered.

cortez/5.title: Mobile food vendor licensing rules
cortez/5.summary: Council discussed and then considered Ordinance No. 1371, revising the city code on annual licensing for mobile food vendors.

cortez/6.title: Land Use Code changes
cortez/6.summary: Council considered Ordinance 1374 making changes to various sections of the Land Use Code, on first reading Aug. 25 and second reading Sept. 8. The Planning Commission also considered a recommendation to allow remote participation in its meetings.

cortez/7.title: Parks and Recreation Master Plan and ash tree beetle
cortez/7.summary: Council chose a representative for the Parks and Recreation Master Plan committee and held a community engagement update and listening session Oct. 27. Staff also briefed council on the green ash beetle's impact on park ash trees.

cortez/8.title: Montezuma-Sligo drainage improvements
cortez/8.summary: Council considered awarding Phase 2 of the Montezuma-Sligo Drainage Improvement Project to D&L Construction.

cortez/9.title: Site plan and permits at 127 N. Market and 1411 Montelores
cortez/9.summary: Council considered a site plan for 127 N. Market Street. The Planning Commission heard a conditional use permit and minor deviation for 1411 Montelores Avenue. Council on Sept. 22 heard a similar request for a carport encroaching into the setbacks of a single-family lot.

cortez/10.title: City spending authority and city attorney and judge contracts
cortez/10.summary: Council considered a resolution amending staff spending authority limits, replacing a 2001 resolution. It also considered a compensation increase for the city attorney and held executive sessions on the municipal judge's contract and the Fiber Express Line negotiations.

craig/0.title: Water and wastewater rate increase (Ordinance 1187)
craig/0.summary: The City Council was set to take up on first reading Ordinance No. 1187, which would raise water and wastewater rates in the Municipal Code so the Water and Wastewater Enterprise Funds keep a sufficient balance. Another ordinance (No. 1188) amending section 8.04.250 of the code was listed alongside it.

craig/1.title: 2027 city budget and property tax (Ordinance 1186)
craig/1.summary: Council scheduled introduction and first reading of Ordinance No. 1186, which adopts the 2027 budget, sets appropriations and fixes the property tax levy. The item was on the October 27 public hearing agenda.

craig/2.title: Meadows Apartments HUD and DOLA grant agreements
craig/2.summary: Council was asked to approve Resolution No. 34 (2026), covering subrecipient agreements for HUD and DOLA grant funding tied to the Meadows Apartments project.

craig/3.title: Craig Sports Complex bond counsel
craig/3.summary: The Parks and Recreation director recommended Butler Snow LLP as bond counsel for the Craig Sports Complex, which points to bond financing for the project. Council was to consider the selection on October 27.

craig/4.title: Craig Master Plan update awarded to SE Group
craig/4.summary: Council was asked to award the Craig Master Plan Update to SE Group for $195,000. The Planning Commission notes mention a master plan proposed to be completed by early 2028.

craig/5.title: Craig Business and Industrial Park sketch plan
craig/5.summary: The Planning and Zoning Commission reviewed a major subdivision sketch plan for the Craig Business and Industrial Park on West 1st Street. Commissioners raised concerns about vagueness, infrastructure capacity and sidewalks, and discussion pointed toward recommending approval to Council on the condition that sidewalks be added to meet the Land Use Code.

craig/6.title: Local Marketing District grants and business plan competition
craig/6.summary: On September 22 Council approved Economic Development Advisory Committee recommendations for Local Marketing District dissolution funds, including $15,000 for the Moffat County Balloon Festival, $4,000 for the Bear River Young Life car show and $15,000 for Powder Mountain Ventures. On October 13 the 2026 Business Plan Competition winners were announced.

craig/7.title: Site plan for hobby shop at 791 Industrial Avenue
craig/7.summary: Mike Thompson's site plan for a personal hobby shop in Green Tree Business Park went from the Planning Commission to Council. Council approved it on October 13.
craig/7.where: 791 Industrial Ave, Green Tree Business Park Lot 6, Block 1

craig/8.title: Tunatua RV Resort deferred amenities agreement
craig/8.summary: The Planning Commission was to consider recommending to Council a Deferred Recreational Amenities and Certificate of Occupancy Agreement for the Tunatua RV Resort.

craig/9.title: Timberg vacant land plan at Pine and East 12th
craig/9.summary: Bruce Timberg was scheduled to present a tentative plan for his vacant land east of Pine Street and East 12th Street to the Planning Commission. Staff also mentioned possible upcoming annexations.
craig/9.where: East of Pine Street and East 12th Street

crawford/0.title: Water rate overhaul and Water Rate Committee
crawford/0.summary: The town formed a committee to set a sustainable water rate structure. A consultant recommended about $125/month, and current rates of $35–$41 cover none of the required reserves. In June the committee presented a model with a fully funded operating need of $238,800, higher bulk water rates ($2–$3 per 100 gallons) and a higher tap fee. Sewer rate analysis was authorized in June, and water rates for the State Park and others were still on agendas in fall 2026.

crawford/1.title: Crawford State Park water and sewer rate structure
crawford/1.summary: The committee is reviewing how the State Park is charged. It has about 76–78 points of use, modeled as roughly 31 equivalent taps, and is billed as a rural commercial tap. Council noted the park has grown a lot since the 1990s and the issue appeared on the October and November 2026 agendas.

crawford/2.title: 2026 budget, water/sewer increases and fee schedule
crawford/2.summary: Council worked on the 2026 budget with a proposed $10/month water increase per meter, a sewer deficit of about $21,000 and a public hearing on Nov 24. Resolution 6-2025 updating the town fee schedule was discussed but deferred without final changes. Budget and fee-structure items, including address access and subdivision fees, returned on the fall 2026 agendas.

crawford/3.title: Spring water project, grant reimbursement and staff overtime
crawford/3.summary: The spring water project was substantially complete, with costs under $400,000 of a $537,000 grant. Staff logged about 150 overtime hours, and council debated comp time versus pay pending reimbursement guidance. Final reimbursement was received by June 2026.

crawford/4.title: Water storage tank replacement and system inspections
crawford/4.summary: The tank replacement project awaits state health department (CDPHE) approval of the final design before bidding, which was targeted for July. CDPHE requires full project review before splitting the potable tank bids. Tanks and the system passed inspections, and lagoon liner deterioration needs long-term planning for the 2027 budget.
crawford/4.where: Town water tanks and wastewater lagoon

crawford/5.title: Cemetery land plat and Grateful Flats Campground
crawford/5.summary: A final plat and boundary adjustment would let the Cemetery District buy more land, with a historic cattle-drive easement found abandoned. It was scheduled for June 22, 2026. Council also conditionally approved opening the in-town part of Grateful Flats Campground after county septic inspection and a public works review.

crawford/6.title: Fire-damaged properties and cleanup
crawford/6.summary: Council raised concerns about two properties on Dogwood and Elm left from earlier fires. Staff sent letters to the owners asking for cleanup plans.

crawford/7.title: Regional planning, broadband and campus master plan
crawford/7.summary: Region 10 presented regional economic development, fiber broadband links, small business help and Enterprise Zone credits. Council discussed a master plan for town-owned property and grants from DOLA and USDA.

crawford/8.title: Building permits, variances and property enforcement
crawford/8.summary: Council discussed formal variance procedures with applications, notice and fees. A resident asked for a permit renewal and raised inconsistent enforcement, and was allowed to renew for $50. Unauthorized excavation on town property on K Street is being pursued, and an A Street property closing needed a boundary adjustment.
crawford/8.where: K Street, A Street and townwide

crawford/9.title: 2026 town election and meeting access
crawford/9.summary: Three council seats were up for election, with petitions due January 26. Residents and a reporter asked for online access to agenda packets and water rate reports, and the clerk said she would work on providing them.

crawford/10.title: Town Hall conditions and office hours
crawford/10.summary: The Fire Department Auxiliary raised concerns about kitchen cleanliness, grease trap maintenance and bugs in Town Hall. Council also discussed Friday office hours and staffing costs.

crested-butte/0.title: Zoning code rewrite and new Chapter 16 land development code
crested-butte/0.summary: Council and BOZAR held joint work sessions from February to June 2026 on a full zoning and subdivision update covering residential, commercial and mixed-use districts, incentives, and PUDs. Ordinances 12-16 of 2026, including a new zoning map and Chapter 16 amendments, had second readings August 17; staff had proposed a September 1, 2026 effective date.

crested-butte/1.title: Non-primary home excise tax and long-range financial planning
crested-butte/1.summary: Facing structural budget pressures that rely heavily on sales tax, Council worked through 2026 financial planning sessions on new revenue, including an excise tax on vacant or underused homes and a longevity-based property tax rebate at $1.0M-$1.5M revenue levels. Draft ballot language was reviewed August 4, and a resolution calling a November 3, 2026 election was on the August 17 agenda. A 2027 Budget Advisory Committee was also discussed.

crested-butte/2.title: Five-year Housing Strategy and town housing purchases
crested-butte/2.summary: Council reviewed the town's affordable housing portfolio, then took up adoption of the 5-year Housing Strategy in May. The town also approved purchases of units and properties on Gothic Avenue (816, 818, 810, 806 #5A), 16 Ninth Street, sale of 16 Ninth Street #3A, and amended affordable housing guidelines.
crested-butte/2.where: Gothic Avenue and other town housing sites

crested-butte/3.title: Red Lady Avenue and Sixth Street roundabout
crested-butte/3.summary: The town is designing a roundabout at Red Lady Avenue and Sixth Street on Highway 135, where the intersection operates at LOS E in peak hours, below CDOT standards. In June 2026 Council considered a cost-sharing request from the Gunnison Watershed School District, a partner in design cost sharing.
crested-butte/3.where: Red Lady Avenue and Sixth Street (Highway 135)

crested-butte/4.title: Gunnison to Mt. Crested Butte Corridor Plan
crested-butte/4.summary: Council has been working out its values and priorities for the Corridor Plan and Transportation Strategy led with Gunnison County, including an MOU, county presentations and a listening session on August 4.
crested-butte/4.where: Gunnison to Mt. Crested Butte corridor

crested-butte/5.title: Drought water restrictions and water/sewer penalties
crested-butte/5.summary: Council considered changes to water restrictions to address drought conditions in June, then passed Emergency Ordinance No. 10 in July amending violations and penalties for water and sewer regulations. Council ratified it July 20.

crested-butte/6.title: PROST Plan for parks, recreation, open space and trails
crested-butte/6.summary: Council reviewed the Parks, Recreation, Open Space and Trails plan through work sessions on open space definitions, success measures, cost recovery philosophy, and a parks decision-making framework and survey, and scheduled plan adoption for May 4, 2026.

crested-butte/7.title: Community Spaces Strategy and Lower Verzuh proposal
crested-butte/7.summary: The 5-year Community Spaces Strategy, one of three Community Plan implementation items, was reviewed in December and brought for adoption in May. Council also considered a referral letter on an amended Lower Verzuh proposal.

crested-butte/8.title: Wildfire code and hazard planning
crested-butte/8.summary: Council discussed the Wildfire Ready Action Plan update, adopted the Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code as Chapter 18, Article 6.5 and adopted the Gunnison County Hazard Mitigation Plan.

crested-butte/9.title: Special event policy, food trucks and sanitation bin fees
crested-butte/9.summary: Council reviewed special event permitting changes, single-use plastic reduction for events, extended the suspension of food truck rules, and discussed Save-As-You-Throw bin fees for 2026-2027 to fund sanitation.

de-beque/0.title: Temporary moratorium on data center development
de-beque/0.summary: The Council was set to discuss and give direction on a temporary moratorium on data center development within the town. The agenda does not state an outcome.

de-beque/1.title: Pivot Energy solar farm in unincorporated Mesa County
de-beque/1.summary: The Council continued discussing a proposed Pivot Energy solar farm in unincorporated Mesa County that borders the town. It also planned further discussion and direction on the development.
de-beque/1.where: Unincorporated Mesa County bordering De Beque

de-beque/2.title: CDBG housing abatement and demolition grant application
de-beque/2.summary: The Board of Trustees held a public hearing on a Community Development Block Grant application to the state Division of Housing for a housing abatement and demolition program. It also considered Resolution 2026-32 authorizing staff to apply.

de-beque/3.title: Automated license plate readers
de-beque/3.summary: The Council scheduled a discussion on using automated license plate readers. No decision is recorded in the agenda.

de-beque/4.title: Updated 2027 preliminary budget
de-beque/4.summary: Staff submitted an updated 2027 preliminary budget for the board's review.

de-beque/5.title: Sanitary sewer agreement and dedication/acceptance resolution
de-beque/5.summary: The Council was to consider Resolution 2026-34 on the dedication and acceptance of infrastructure tied to a sanitary sewer agreement between the Town of De Beque and another party. It also considered Resolution 2026-33 directing staff to enter a contract.

de-beque/6.title: DOLA Local Capacity Grant and timelines
de-beque/6.summary: The Council received a presentation on the DOLA Local Capacity Grant and its timelines.

del-norte/0.title: Outdoor Entertainment Overlay District (Ordinance 789)
del-norte/0.summary: The Town set a public hearing and considered Ordinance No. 789, which would create an Outdoor Entertainment Overlay District, define its boundaries and amend the Use Chart (Table 16-4A) of the municipal code. Hearings were noticed for Sept. 9 and Oct. 14, 2026, and the ordinance came back on the Oct. 14 agenda.

del-norte/1.title: Moratorium on Flock Safety cameras
del-norte/1.summary: Council discussed a temporary moratorium on Flock Safety license-plate cameras on Sept. 9, and Resolution 13-2026 for a moratorium on Flock cameras was on the Oct. 14 agenda.

del-norte/2.title: Police Department policy manual
del-norte/2.summary: Council discussed adopting Police Department policy and procedure, and Resolution 12-2026 to adopt the Police Department Manual as a stand-alone policy was on the Oct. 14 agenda.

del-norte/3.title: 2027 Town budget
del-norte/3.summary: The proposed 2027 budget was to be accepted on Oct. 14 and a work session set. A public hearing on the budget was scheduled for Nov. 5 (a Nov. 11 date was also floated), with a budget work session set for Nov. 18, 2026.

del-norte/4.title: Lookout Mountain annexation and GOCO grant
del-norte/4.summary: Gary Blakley addressed council on Sept. 9 about annexing the Lookout Mountain property and about GOCO grant funding.

del-norte/5.title: South Water Well expense and water treatment plant property
del-norte/5.summary: Council was to consider allocating Water Fund balance for the South Water Well expense. Aaron Woodke also raised use of the town's water treatment plant property on County Road 14.

del-norte/6.title: Master Print web design contract
del-norte/6.summary: Council weighed signing a contract with Master Print with defined expectations on price and deliverables, or issuing an RFP to find another firm for print and web design work.

del-norte/7.title: River Park changing stall request
del-norte/7.summary: Patti Kelly of D Mountain Recreation presented to council on Sept. 9 about a changing stall at River Park.

del-norte/8.title: Nuisance violations and civil abatement process
del-norte/8.summary: Council discussed the town's handling of nuisance violations and the civil abatement process on Sept. 9.

del-norte/9.title: Rio Grande County Comprehensive Plan outreach
del-norte/9.summary: The town and county planned an open house on the county comprehensive plan on Oct. 27 and a town board stakeholder meeting on Nov. 4, 2026.

del-norte/10.title: Funding requests: library computers and Rio Grande Museum
del-norte/10.summary: The Del Norte Library asked for funding for computers, and the Rio Grande Museum requested a donation from the town.

delta-county/0.title: Clear Water Enterprises rezone (PLN26-022) for 378.5 acres
delta-county/0.summary: Peter Edwards/Clear Water Enterprises LLC asked to rezone about 378.5 acres from A-35 to RES-1 for future residential subdivision. A water attorney's opinion says the water rights and augmentation plan (Golden Eagle Water Company, Shea Pump and Pipeline, Blue Mesa releases) can supply it. The Planning Commission heard it Aug. 12 and the commissioners held a hearing Sept. 15.

delta-county/1.title: Land Use Code amendments: battery storage, natural medicine, and general cleanup
delta-county/1.summary: The county reworked its Land Use Code, with hearings on Sept. 1 and Sept. 15. The changes cover battery energy storage systems (BESS) and natural medicine businesses, ending earlier moratoriums, plus setbacks, site plans, temporary special events and intensive agricultural setbacks. The Planning Commission heard public comment in October, and the commissioners were set to consider adopting a resolution on Nov. 3.

delta-county/2.title: Concentrated animal feeding operation (CAFO) regulations working group
delta-county/2.summary: Commissioners considered forming a working group to evaluate, review and draft amendments to the county's land use rules for CAFOs.

delta-county/3.title: Proposed 2027 county budget
delta-county/3.summary: The commissioners held a special meeting on Oct. 13 for a presentation of the proposed 2027 Delta County budget. Related items include updated mileage and per diem rates starting Jan. 1, 2027, which had not risen since 2008, and a county property assessment study.

delta-county/4.title: Fire Mountain speed limit change
delta-county/4.summary: Commissioners were to consider a speed analysis and a resolution changing the speed limit on Fire Mountain. They also looked at a driveway spacing variance (PLN26-013) off 3260 Road near Highway 92, where the standard requires 200 feet from the arterial.

delta-county/5.title: Hotchkiss skate park request at the fairgrounds
delta-county/5.summary: Hotchkiss resident Tanner Wilson asked commissioners to consider a skate park at the county fairgrounds, saying families now drive to other towns. He offered to fundraise and pointed to the fairgrounds master plan.

delta-county/6.title: Comment letter on the 2001 Roadless Rule and Forest Service road agreement
delta-county/6.summary: Commissioners discussed a county comment letter on the federal 2001 Roadless Rule on Sept. 15. On Oct. 6 they discussed a road agreement with the U.S. Forest Service.

delta-county/7.title: Portable chemical toilets policy and septic variance
delta-county/7.summary: The Board of Health scheduled a discussion of public health policy on portable chemical toilets and an onsite wastewater (OWTS) variance request.

delta-county/8.title: Resolution supporting Amendment 83
delta-county/8.summary: Commissioners were to consider a resolution in support of Amendment 83, a constitutional rights ballot measure.

denver/0.title: Mayor's Proposed 2027 Budget and council amendments
denver/0.summary: Council held the public hearing on the Mayor's Proposed 2027 Budget on Oct. 19 and took up a series of council member amendments on Nov. 2 and Nov. 9. The Finance committee also advanced the 2027 appropriation ordinance, a rescission of $16.1 million in unused capital funds, and 2027 plans for business improvement districts.

denver/1.title: Data center moratorium update
denver/1.summary: The Community Planning and Housing committee heard an update on Denver's data center moratorium on Aug. 18. The documents give no details on its terms or next steps.

denver/2.title: Homelessness shelters and rapid rehousing contracts
denver/2.summary: Council approved a stream of contracts for rapid resolution and rapid rehousing services, including Salvation Army, Volunteers of America, St. Francis Center, Delores Project and Colorado Coalition for the Homeless. It also approved temporary pallet and micro-community shelter licenses with Colorado Village Collaborative at 3815 N Steele St. and The Gathering Place at 1375 N. Elati St., plus an emergency shelter scope change at the Sand & Sage/Westerner Motel on East Colfax.

denver/3.title: Citibot and Slalom contract amendments fail
denver/3.summary: Council called out and voted down amendments to the city's contracts with Citibot ($3.89 million added) and Slalom ($5 million added) on Oct. 13 after they had cleared committee. Council had earlier postponed other contract items, such as a $500,000 addition to the Wheeler Trigg O'Donnell legal contract.

denver/4.title: Airport use and lease agreements and DEN projects
denver/4.summary: Council approved a block of three-year use and lease agreements with airlines at Denver International Airport, including Air Canada, Air France, Alaska, Lufthansa, Turkish and WestJet. One item (COPA) was called out. Council also approved large DEN construction contracts and airport bond note plans.

denver/5.title: Affordable housing loans and DHA agreement
denver/5.summary: Council advanced an amended agreement with the Denver Housing Authority, a loan to 1600 Pearl LLLP for housing in North Capitol Hill, and a loan for a 118-unit income-restricted building. It also approved state funding for middle-income row homes at Loretto Heights and an amended loan involving 3755 Tennyson St.

denver/6.title: Rezonings and landmark designation
denver/6.summary: Committees advanced map amendments including 3418 W. 14th Ave. and 1371 N. Julian St. (G-RH-3 to G-MU-5), North Mariposa Street properties, 500 West Tennessee Ave., and a zone change near 76 North Hazel Court that had a required public hearing. A landmark designation for 740 N. Washington St. also moved ahead.

denver/7.title: Caring for Denver, preschool and college tax spending limits
denver/7.summary: A committee advanced ordinances barring Caring for Denver, Denver Preschool Program and college affordability tax revenue from being spent on alcohol and other administrative items, and the Caring for Denver ones also bar spending on staff wellness programs. Council also handled the Denver Health sales tax spending update and contract.

denver/8.title: Downtown Development Authority boundaries and funding agreements
denver/8.summary: Council approved changes to the Denver Downtown Development Authority boundaries and advanced DDDA funding agreements for the Midland Condominiums unit at 444 17th St., the University Building at 900-918 16th St., and 101 W. Colfax Ave., where the city also approved a lease for about 64,654 square feet.

denver/9.title: Broadway Station pedestrian bridge and stadium site
denver/9.summary: Committee advanced an amended 2025 stadium site intergovernmental agreement with the Broadway Station Metropolitan District and a state grant for a pedestrian bridge over the railroad and RTD tracks. The bridge links the Broadway RTD station to the NWSL soccer stadium and Santa Fe Yards.

denver/10.title: Automated vehicle identification (AVIS) ordinance
denver/10.summary: The Health and Safety committee and council advanced an ordinance amending Chapter 54 on automated vehicle identification systems. The documents do not describe the specific changes.

denver/11.title: Proclamations opposing Amendments 81 and 82
denver/11.summary: Council took up a proclamation opposing Colorado Amendment 81 (law enforcement) and a measure on Amendment 82, the proposed right to purchase and sell natural gas.

denver/12.title: Minority and women-owned business contracting ordinance
denver/12.summary: Council passed a bill revising Chapter 28 of the city code to advance access to public contracting for minority-owned, women-owned and small businesses. It also advanced an amendment to the competitive selection process for certain contracts.

denver/13.title: District 6 police facility and Civic Center projects
denver/13.summary: Council approved design and construction contracts for a new Denver Police District 6 station and garage at 1566 N. Washington St., and added $1.63 million for Studio Gang on Civic Center Park. It also approved a Cuernavaca Park facility amendment of $8.1 million and an East Colfax CD8 sidewalk land acquisition ordinance.
denver/13.where: 1566 N. Washington St.; Civic Center Park; Cuernavaca Park

dolores/0.title: Broc's Development PUD and rezoning of 206 and 207 South Third Street
dolores/0.summary: The board reviewed a PUD concept plan from KKV Development/Broc Smith in May, with neighbors raising concerns about parking, three-story buildings, infrastructure and density. Ordinance 592, rezoning 206 and 207 S. Third Street from Downtown Mixed Use, had its first reading in August and was moved for approval on second reading on Sept. 14.

dolores/1.title: Phase 2 water project and water main replacement funding
dolores/1.summary: The town is funding Phase 2 of its water infrastructure project, with about $700,000 from DOLA and a DWRF loan agreement (Resolutions 700 and 719). Construction is expected to start in spring 2027, and the water main replacement continues. Staff also got consensus to hire a water law attorney on town water rights and to meter Riverside Park.

dolores/2.title: Fee schedule update and Ordinance 591
dolores/2.summary: The town rewrote its fee schedule and adopted Ordinance 591, which lets fees be set by resolution and sets renewal, late-fee and enforcement procedures. The board set the business license fee at $30 with a $50 late fee, and short-term rental permit fees were questioned. A business owner contested her late fee.

dolores/3.title: 2027 budget
dolores/3.summary: Staff presented the preliminary 2027 budget in October. The board held a budget workshop on Oct. 26 and reviewed the whole budget notebook. Residents urged making park improvements a priority, and Community Center funding was to be handled in the budget.

dolores/4.title: Sheriff's Office contract
dolores/4.summary: The board scheduled a workshop on the Sheriff's contract. In August it reviewed a draft and discussed metrics for judging the level and value of law enforcement service.

dolores/5.title: Comprehensive Plan update
dolores/5.summary: The town is updating its comprehensive plan with a consultant. Public outreach ended July 10 and comments closed July 31, and a draft is expected in October. Residents were urged to complete the questionnaire.

dolores/6.title: Public comment rules and board meeting procedures
dolores/6.summary: The board discussed limiting personal attacks on staff during public comment and planned signage on expectations. A speaker argued this raises First Amendment concerns. The board also discussed adding a public comment period before workshops and changing the meeting schedule.

dolores/7.title: Town attorney resignation and new legal services
dolores/7.summary: Town Attorney Ethan Sumrall announced his resignation, and in October the board accepted it (Resolution 723). It approved a legal services agreement with Holligan Westendorff, PLLC.

dolores/8.title: Dog licensing ordinance changes
dolores/8.summary: Ordinance 589 changing dog licensure requirements passed first reading in March and had a second reading hearing in April. Staff also discussed feral cats later.

dolores/9.title: Dolores Community Center funding and direction
dolores/9.summary: The Community Center Advisory Board asked for direction on the center, including a boundary issue and parking lot. The board directed staff to move on the boundary issue and to review funding in the budget process.

dolores/10.title: 2024 International Codes and wildfire resiliency code
dolores/10.summary: Ordinance 594 adopting the 2024 International Codes passed first reading in October. A resident thanked the board for not adopting the Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code. Fire hazard mitigation along the escarpment was also underway.

dolores/11.title: Hemp and THC beverage policy
dolores/11.summary: In April the board considered Resolution 698 setting a policy on hemp-derived and THC beverages. HB 26-1409's effect on marijuana tax distributions was also discussed in September.

douglas-county/0.title: Ballot measure to expand the Board of County Commissioners from 3 to 5
douglas-county/0.summary: In late August the commissioners fixed the ballot title for expanding the board from three to five members and then referred a measure to preserve voters' rights to vote on it. About 26 residents spoke on Aug. 31, and the board approved an amended referral resolution (R-026-062). Ballot title protest administrative hearings were scheduled for Sept. 3 and 4.

douglas-county/1.title: Flexential business personal property tax incentive agreement
douglas-county/1.summary: The board took up a business personal property tax incentive agreement between Douglas County and Flexential Corp (project ED2025-002). The item was pulled from the consent agenda, five residents spoke, and Vice Chair Van Winkle moved approval on Aug. 11. Flexential is a data center operator, but the documents don't describe the facility.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Business Meeting

douglas-county/2.title: Private activity bonds for Ponderosa Pines
douglas-county/2.summary: A $50 million private activity bond authorization for Ponderosa Pines was continued in August. A $37 million bond authorizing resolution (R-026-070) was approved on Sept. 22 on the consent agenda; the documents don't confirm it is the same project.

douglas-county/3.title: Zoning rules for nonfunctional turf and artificial turf
douglas-county/3.summary: A proposed zoning amendment (DR2026-001) would regulate nonfunctional turf and artificial turf. It went to a Planning Commission work session on Sept. 14 and a hearing on Sept. 28, and then to commissioner hearings on Oct. 27 and Nov. 3.

douglas-county/4.title: Zoning rules for training and exercising non-owned animals
douglas-county/4.summary: A zoning amendment (DR2026-004) would regulate training lessons and exercise sessions for animals not owned by the property owner. It moved from a Planning Commission work session to hearings before the Planning Commission and the commissioners in late September through early November.

Board of County Commissioners Land Use Meeting/Public Hearing

douglas-county/5.title: Use by Special Review requests at 6685 S. Highway 83 and 2485 S. Russellville Road
douglas-county/5.summary: Two special-use requests, US2023-011 at 6685 S. State Highway 83 and US2025-010 at 2485 S. Russellville Road, went to the Planning Commission in October. They are scheduled for commissioner hearings on Oct. 27 and Nov. 3. The documents don't state the proposed uses.

douglas-county/6.title: Metropolitan district service plans: Castle Pines North and Roxborough Village
douglas-county/6.summary: The Castle Pines North Metropolitan District service plan (and a second amendment) and the Roxborough Village Metropolitan District service plan amendment were scheduled for review in October and November.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Business Meeting

douglas-county/7.title: Sterling Ranch Filing 6A, 2nd Amendment
douglas-county/7.summary: Commissioners approved the minor development amendment (SB2026-014) on Sept. 22 with 2 conditions. Two people spoke during public comment.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Land Use Meeting/Public Hearing

douglas-county/8.title: Pine View Circle road vacation
douglas-county/8.summary: The Planning Commission reviewed and commissioners approved vacating Pine View Circle on Aug. 25 with 2 conditions (SB2026-017). No one spoke.

douglas-county/9.title: Road and bridge projects
douglas-county/9.summary: The county approved several road contracts. These include Woodmoor drainage and road repair ($106,463), the Dakan Road bridge replacement, a University Blvd and Post Office traffic signal, Waterton Road improvements ($2.15 million) and a transportation safety action plan. It is also pursuing $2.875 million in district funding for the County Line Road and Inverness Parkway intersection.

douglas-county/10.title: Regional parks, open space and Rueter-Hess
douglas-county/10.summary: The county approved a Mark Weston Open Space Memorial renaming with up to $30k in open space funds. It also backed a GOCO grant for Wildcat Regional Park and approved a Macanta Regional Park pedestrian bridge contract. The Rueter-Hess Advisory Board discussed budget updates and Incline Trailhead improvements.

douglas-county/11.title: Homelessness and older adult grants and human services funding
douglas-county/11.summary: The county applied for a $125,000 Homelessness Resolution Program grant, gave Older Adult Initiative grant checks, and amended TANF and Colorado Works contracts ($2.4 million). The Homeless Initiative and Board of Health also met, with a 2027 health department budget on the Board of Health agenda.

dove-creek/0.title: Sewer usage fee ordinance replacing Section 24-85
dove-creek/0.summary: On Oct. 27 the council scheduled a public hearing and first reading of an ordinance replacing Section 24-85 of the Dove Creek Code of Ordinances on sewer usage fees. Residents could comment for or against. The same agenda lists a Sinclair sewer item.

dove-creek/1.title: Town Manager hiring and contract
dove-creek/1.summary: In August the council reviewed applications for town manager, then on Aug. 25 held an executive session on the manager's contract and offer, with possible action afterward.

dove-creek/2.title: Town Clerk/Treasurer recruitment and contract
dove-creek/2.summary: The council took up a contract for the treasurer on Sept. 29, reviewed Town Clerk/Treasurer applications on Oct. 13, and planned discussion and possible action on the selection on Oct. 27.

dove-creek/3.title: Town Attorney legal services RFP
dove-creek/3.summary: The council is reviewing responses to a request for proposals for town attorney legal services and planned to schedule interviews with candidates.

dove-creek/4.title: Foundational ordinance draft and proposed ordinance changes
dove-creek/4.summary: On Sept. 22 the board was to review a foundational ordinance draft and approve its public release. In October the council held an ordinance overview, presentations, discussion and proposed changes.

dove-creek/5.title: Preliminary budget, capital plan and DOLA meter grant
dove-creek/5.summary: The council began with a preliminary budget on Oct. 13. The Oct. 27 agenda lists a DOLA meter grant and a capital improvement plan.

dove-creek/6.title: Enforcement order project update and trench box purchase
dove-creek/6.summary: The council received a project update on an enforcement order on Aug. 25 and on Sept. 22 considered buying a trench box for worker safety.

durango/0.title: 2027 city budget and appropriations
durango/0.summary: Council is taking up the City Manager's proposed 2027 budget, with a public hearing and introduction of the operating and capital appropriation ordinances. It also considers amending the 2026 capital budget and the city's investment policy, and a budget reconciliation session is scheduled.

durango/1.title: Water and sewer rate changes
durango/1.summary: An ordinance was introduced to amend water charges (Sec. 25-30) and sewer service rates (Sec. 25-114) in the city code. Council also has a study session on Water Efficiency Plan and Water Shortage Response Plan updates.

durango/2.title: Lake Nighthorse water pipeline agreement
durango/2.summary: Council is asked to authorize the City Manager to sign a four-party agreement for design and construction of a 200-foot pipeline conveying Lake Nighthorse water.

durango/3.title: City Hall/Police Station site plan
durango/3.summary: The Community Development Commission is getting early design guidance on the major site plan for the new City Hall/Police Station (PR-26-52).

durango/4.title: Noise rules in the Land Use and Development Code
durango/4.summary: A public hearing is scheduled on text amendments to the Land Use and Development Code regarding noise (PR-26-68).

durango/5.title: Regional housing and child care support for 2027
durango/5.summary: Council hears presentations from the Regional Housing Alliance of La Plata County on 2027 and beyond, and an update on the Child Care Investment Fund city grant with a 2027 support proposal.

durango/6.title: Remote parking code change and parking wayfinding
durango/6.summary: Council gives final reading to a Land Use and Development Code ordinance on remote parking. A study session covers the Parking Wayfinding Project.

durango/7.title: Animas Air Park and La Posta economic discussion
durango/7.summary: Council has a staff presentation at a study session on Animas Air Park and La Posta economic matters.

durango/8.title: Camino Crossing underpass and drone deliveries
durango/8.summary: The Community Development Commission hears a presentation on the Camino Crossing underpass and discusses drone deliveries, proposed by the Chair.

eagle/0.title: Proposed pickleball courts at Town Park
eagle/0.summary: Neighbors near Town Park, including residents 68 feet from the proposed courts, spoke against new pickleball courts over noise, park space, cost and upkeep. Council held an August 25 open house and online survey and heard the results September 8. At the September 22 meeting residents asked that courts not go within 500 feet of homes, while others backed amenities that draw visitors.

eagle/1.title: 2026 supplemental and 2027 town budget and capital plan
eagle/1.summary: Staff presented a 2027 draft with a General Fund operating surplus of $466,340 before transfers and $350,000 in assumed vacancy savings. Council held work sessions on operating and capital priorities (Sept 15 and 29), and a public hearing on the 2026/2027 budget was set for October 27. Capital projects include Nogal Park updates, Brush Creek Road extension right-of-way purchases and Grand Ave. Grill demolition and parking.

eagle/2.title: Eagle River Park funding and river park engineering
eagle/2.summary: The Eagle River Park Coalition asked Council to fund maintenance and an engineering project for the river park in the 2027 budget. Residents asked that the Coalition rather than a third-party contractor be involved and asked about the rapid blocks. Council scheduled a site visit to the river park at 200 Fairgrounds Rd.

eagle/3.title: Bike Park maintenance funding for 2027
eagle/3.summary: The Town owns the Eagle Bike Park, which the Vail Valley Mountain Trails Alliance operates under a 2023 license that sets no Town cash contribution. Council approved $44,500 for 2026 maintenance from the Sales Tax Capital Improvement Fund. Council asked how much the Town and the Alliance should each pay in 2027.

eagle/4.title: Variance and appeal rules in the Land Use Code
eagle/4.summary: Council amended Ordinance 13, Series 2026 on variances (Chapters 4.17 and 4.20), deleting the subsection that prohibited the call-up procedure. Council directed staff to draft language letting neighbors who took part in hearings submit call-ups, and letting the Community Development Director refer administrative decisions to Planning and Zoning. The commission was to review the appeal, referral and call-up changes October 20.

eagle/5.title: Capitol Flats rezoning at 123 and 137 Howard Street
eagle/5.summary: A request to rezone two properties on Howard Street was scheduled for the Planning and Zoning Commission, with a request to continue the hearing to November 17, 2026.

eagle/6.title: Red Mountain Ranch Metropolitan District service plan
eagle/6.summary: Council held a public hearing on Resolution 52 to approve the consolidated service plan for Red Mountain Ranch Metropolitan Districts 1 and 2. Council discussed financial risks and utility ownership and maintenance responsibilities.

eagle/7.title: Downtown Development Authority expansion and Capitol Street area
eagle/7.summary: The DDA approved Resolution 05 to include 212 E. Third Street in the district and discussed outreach to owners of 214 Capitol Street and the Big Bear building. Council also took up Ordinance 16 adding a vacated alley in Block 13, and Council had earlier considered buying 215 Capitol Street. The DDA reviewed its 2027 budget draft, including a commercial activation rebate program and a downtown parking assessment.

eagle/8.title: Parking in the public right-of-way
eagle/8.summary: Police Chief Buhlman told Council that Town Code does not specifically prohibit parking in the right-of-way, though vehicles left 24 hours or more can be tagged as abandoned and other violations apply. Council held work sessions on code and enforcement options. A resident also asked for a flashing sign at a crosswalk near Eagle Ranch Road.

eagle/9.title: Event funding and merger of Economic Vitality and Marketing committees
eagle/9.summary: The Marketing and Events Advisory Committee reviewed 45 event-funding requests totaling $246,000 and discussed funding tiers. The Economic Vitality Committee discussed merging with MEAC, a joint pilot project, and tourism tied to the Aspen Airport closure.

eagle/10.title: Haymaker Trailhead restroom and open space projects
eagle/10.summary: The Open Space committee reviewed the Haymaker Trailhead restroom, whose budget rose from $90,000 to about $160,000 against a single bid of about $380,000, and considered a vault toilet as an interim option. It also reviewed trail signs, bear-resistant trash cans and the Open Space Fund budget.

eagle/11.title: Council support for school ballot issue SB
eagle/11.summary: Council passed Resolution 61 supporting Eagle County School District Ballot Issue SB on the November 3, 2026 ballot after several residents and teachers urged support. Council agreed to revisit a policy on when to take positions on outside matters, discussed in a November 3 work session.

eagle/12.title: Automated license plate readers
eagle/12.summary: An Avon resident asked Council to avoid automated license plate readers and later thanked Council for not considering them.

eagle/13.title: Climate and water conservation requests
eagle/13.summary: A resident proposed an ordinance banning collection of grass clippings and leaves, and rainwater collection, to conserve water and cut temperatures. Council reviewed climate group memberships and net-zero and carbon sequestration targets, and heard about the Beyond Lawn program and heat pump funding.

edgewater/0.title: Zoning Code Update and rewrite (RLI, RMLI, RMHI districts)
edgewater/0.summary: The city is rewriting its zoning code with a Technical Focus Group. The group's June 8, 2026 meeting reviewed proposed residential districts (RLI, RMLI, RMHI), rear-lot intensification, building heights and floor area limits, balancing more housing against Edgewater's cottage-scale character. The code update is also tied to HB24 state housing requirements and the Edgewater 2040 Comprehensive Plan.

edgewater/1.title: Transit-Oriented Communities housing study (HB 24-1313)
edgewater/1.summary: Consultant Matrix Design Group is running a Transit-Oriented Communities planning project and presented existing conditions, housing market and economic feasibility findings to Planning and Zoning on Aug. 12, 2026. The work is meant to shape Edgewater's response to HB 24-1313 housing capacity requirements and to guide housing, land use and transportation strategies.

edgewater/2.title: Proposition 123 affordable housing fast-track review policy
edgewater/2.summary: Staff proposed a resolution adopting an expedited review policy for qualifying affordable housing, with a 90-day review period. Adopting it by June 30, 2026 makes Edgewater eligible for about $45,000 in state incentive funding, which staff would use for affordable housing tools in the zoning code update.

edgewater/3.title: Sheridan Boulevard safety improvements with CDOT
edgewater/3.summary: Planning and Zoning was briefed on the updated Sheridan Corridor Multimodal Plan, coordinated with CDOT, for Sheridan Boulevard between 17th and 26th Avenues, a high-injury corridor. The design adds ADA improvements and signal timing changes, and construction is expected to begin in late 2026.

edgewater/4.title: 2026 budget, tax levy and audit findings
edgewater/4.summary: Council reviewed department budget presentations, set the 2025 tax levy, and scheduled adoption of the annual budget in December. The City Manager called next year's budget very tight. The 2024 audit presentation prompted talk of water, sewer and trash losses, segregation of duties and rate increases.

edgewater/5.title: Local minimum wage ordinance 2025-23
edgewater/5.summary: Council took up an ordinance amending the local minimum wage and tip provisions of the municipal code, effective January 1. First reading was Nov. 25, 2025 and second reading was scheduled Dec. 16.

edgewater/6.title: Right-of-way funding sales tax ballot measure
edgewater/6.summary: A sales tax ballot measure for right-of-way funding was presented to city boards, including the HARP board and the Board of Adjustment, in August and September 2026.

edgewater/7.title: Rezonings at 2525 Harlan St. and 2403 Fenton St.
edgewater/7.summary: Planning and Zoning held public hearings and recommended approval to City Council of a rezoning of 2525 Harlan Street to Residential 2, and of 2403 Fenton Street from R-1 and R-3.

edgewater/8.title: Accessory dwelling unit ordinance and home rule dispute
edgewater/8.summary: Planning and Zoning recommended an ordinance amending Chapter 16 on accessory dwelling units, driven by state legislation. Resident Larry Welshon objected, citing home rule authority. Council tabled Resolution 2025-14 affirming home rule authority.

edgewater/9.title: Foothills Animal Shelter intergovernmental agreement
edgewater/9.summary: Council considered Resolution 2026-02 approving an amended intergovernmental agreement with Jefferson County, Arvada and others on animal sheltering, licensing and funding for the Foothills Animal Shelter.

edgewater/10.title: Accessory structure height variance
edgewater/10.summary: The Board of Adjustment heard a variance request for a 20'2" accessory structure, over the 15-foot limit. It also approved a variance allowing rear-lot parking access closer than five feet to the side lot line.

el-paso-county/0.title: Triple H Ranch preliminary plan (244 lots)
el-paso-county/0.summary: The commissioners' land use hearing on Oct. 22 covers a request by P760 Land, LLC for a 752.68-acre preliminary plan creating 244 single-family lots in the RR-2.5 zone. The plan includes 40.57 acres of tracts and 67.92 acres of right-of-way.

el-paso-county/1.title: Weed, rubbish and unsafe structure ordinances (HB 26-1239)
el-paso-county/1.summary: First readings of Ordinances 26-02, 26-03 and 26-04 update county rules and enforcement procedures on weeds and brush, rubbish accumulation, and unsafe structures to comply with Colorado House Bill 26-1239.

el-paso-county/2.title: 2027 budget hearings and Q3 budget report
el-paso-county/2.summary: The commissioners held 2027 Budget Hearing #3 with department critical-needs presentations on Oct. 27, and the Regional Building Department's 2027 budget was up for approval Oct. 13. A third-quarter 2026 budget report is scheduled for Nov. 3.

el-paso-county/3.title: Sugarbowl Urban Renewal tax increment agreement
el-paso-county/3.summary: The commissioners were asked to approve a Tax Increment Revenue Agreement with the Colorado Springs Urban Renewal Authority for the Sugarbowl Urban Renewal Plan.
el-paso-county/3.where: Sugarbowl urban renewal area, Colorado Springs

el-paso-county/4.title: Mesa Ridge Parkway condemnation and road projects
el-paso-county/4.summary: The commissioners considered condemning property for the Mesa Ridge Parkway Improvements Project (Powers Blvd to Marksheffel Rd). Other road items include a CDOT agreement for US-24 and Judge Orr Road, Commerce Road Bridge easements, and North Calhan Highway design work.
el-paso-county/4.where: Mesa Ridge Parkway, Powers Blvd to Marksheffel Rd; US-24 & Judge Orr Road; Commerce Road

el-paso-county/5.title: Courthouse construction contract
el-paso-county/5.summary: The commissioners were asked to approve a $3,633,791 trade contractor agreement with Adolfson and Peterson Construction for the courthouse construction project.

el-paso-county/6.title: Paint Mines Interpretive Park grant
el-paso-county/6.summary: The county is to accept a $200,000 grant from Lyda Hill Philanthropies for Paint Mines Interpretive Park and appropriate it to the Parks Department 2026 budget.

el-paso-county/7.title: Bent Grass Commercial Metropolitan District service plan
el-paso-county/7.summary: The commissioners set a Nov. 17, 2026 hearing to consider the Bent Grass Commercial Metropolitan District service plan.

el-paso-county/8.title: Federal and state grants for Sheriff, emergency management and wetland bank
el-paso-county/8.summary: The county is to accept a $500,000 DOJ Byrne grant for the Sheriff's Office, a $56,139 FEMA emergency management grant, and $2,980,440 in federal revenue for the Akers wetland bank project.

elizabeth/0.title: Gold Creek Commons Sketch Plan (Resolution 26R28)
elizabeth/0.summary: The Planning Commission held a quasi-judicial public hearing on the Gold Creek Commons Sketch Plan on Sept. 15 and considered recommending Resolution 26R28 to the Board of Trustees. The Trustees took up a public hearing and possible action on the same resolution on Oct. 13. Applicant is Alexandra Cramer.

elizabeth/1.title: 2027 Town budget and budget workshops
elizabeth/1.summary: The Board of Trustees held budget workshops on Sept. 26 and Oct. 17 and reviewed the 2027 draft budget on Oct. 13. A discussion of 2027 budget modifications is set for the Oct. 27 meeting.

elizabeth/2.title: Extending town water restrictions
elizabeth/2.summary: On Oct. 13 the Trustees were to discuss and possibly act on extending the town's water restrictions, with a presentation by Travis Scurlock.

elizabeth/3.title: E86 Annexation Agreement (Resolution 26R29)
elizabeth/3.summary: The Board of Trustees had the E86 Annexation Agreement, Resolution 26R29, on its Oct. 13 agenda.

elizabeth/4.title: Metropolitan district discussion
elizabeth/4.summary: Corey Hoffmann is scheduled to lead a discussion of metropolitan districts at the Oct. 27 Trustees workshop.

elizabeth/5.title: Town fire regulations
elizabeth/5.summary: Fire Chiefs TJ Steck and Jeff Engel are to discuss town fire regulations with the Trustees on Oct. 27.

elizabeth/6.title: Housing planning grant for Comprehensive Plan elements (Resolution 26R32)
elizabeth/6.summary: The Trustees are to consider a Colorado Department of Local Affairs Housing Planning Grant (HPLN-H26084) for the Elizabeth Comprehensive Plan Elements Project on Oct. 27.

elizabeth/7.title: Main Street Station site plan agreement extension (Resolution 26R31)
elizabeth/7.summary: The Trustees are to consider a first amendment to the site plan agreement with Main Street Station Elizabeth, LLC, extending it, on Oct. 27.

elizabeth/8.title: Road and paving contracts: NexCivil and Hillside Village
elizabeth/8.summary: On Oct. 27 the Trustees are to consider Resolutions 26R33 and 26R34, amending trade contractor agreements including NexCivil Engineering and Construction. They will also discuss a change of scope on the Hillside Village paving project.

elizabeth/9.title: Main Street events, Friday Night Markets and communication plan
elizabeth/9.summary: The Main Street Board discussed recent events on Main Street and a possible communication plan. The Trustees heard a 2026 recap of the Friday Night Markets from Tony Briggs of Elizabeth Brewing Company.

elizabeth/10.title: Depot parking lot restrooms and town facilities
elizabeth/10.summary: The Trustees are to discuss the Depot Parking lot restrooms on Oct. 27. That meeting is also a workshop on town facilities.

erie/0.title: Sale and lease of Town mineral rights near the Draco drilling pad (SM Energy)
erie/0.summary: Council approved Ordinance 26-028 on June 23 to sell Town-owned mineral rights to SM Energy. SM Energy terminated the contract Aug. 19 and Council repealed the ordinance Aug. 25. On Sept. 1 staff asked for direction on a lease offer (a $12,000 per net mineral acre bonus, about $1.36M) and on the state ECMC drilling and spacing process.

erie/1.title: 2027 Town budget and revenue shortfall
