erie/1.summary: Staff said sales tax growth is below 2% and use tax and building permits are down over 40%, so the 2027 budget limits new staff to health and safety needs. Council held study sessions Aug. 18 and Oct. 6 and saw the proposed budget on first reading Oct. 27. Advisory boards were asked to trim their own 2027 budgets, for example the Tree board from $5,000 to $4,750 and Sustainability to $9,928.

sources.body: Open Space and Trails Advisory Board

erie/2.title: Tree removal for new water meters and water line work
erie/2.summary: Several residents spoke at the Sept. 8 Council meeting against the Town digging up trees to make way for new water meters. Council later approved temporary water meter standards for water line transitions tied to the end of automatic fire sprinkler requirements in homes.

erie/3.title: Comprehensive Plan amendments and Proposition 123 affordable housing
erie/3.summary: Residents spoke against any changes to the Comp Plan on Sept. 8, citing water shortage and traffic on Alpine and Primrose. The Planning Commission discussed Prop 123 resolutions; staff said Erie is asking to reduce its Prop 123 unit requirement to 30 units. A comp plan amendment creating a medium-low density designation was reported approved in early November.

sources.body: Open Space and Trails Advisory Board

erie/4.title: Oil and gas regulations update (Title 10, Chapter 12)
erie/4.summary: Planning Commission reviewed proposed changes including doubling inspection fees, per-well fees, notification periods, legacy wells, noise and air quality. A resident commented, and staff and outside counsel noted constitutional limits on what the Town can do.

erie/5.title: Vista Ridge golf course Planned Development Amendment No. 9
erie/5.summary: Planning Commission held a hearing on recommending the amendment for the golf course, and Council held a public hearing Oct. 13 with a presentation from Gauge Land Development and the golf course manager.

erie/6.title: Short-term rental rules and permit fee
erie/6.summary: Planning Commission considered a new Chapter 16 of the Unified Development Code on short-term rentals on Oct. 7, and Council was set to consider a fee for short-term rental permit applications on Oct. 27.

erie/7.title: Colliers Hill urban renewal tax increment changes
erie/7.summary: The Urban Renewal Authority and Council approved agreements on tax increment for the Colliers Hill plan area. A Weld County amendment, approved Sept. 2, removes the requirement that revenue between $10M and $14M go to Weld County Road 5 and allows parks and recreation facilities.
erie/7.where: Colliers Hill Urban Renewal Plan area

erie/8.title: Downtown infrastructure and 150 Briggs redevelopment
erie/8.summary: The URA is paying for downtown infrastructure, including a $30K design contract amendment for a bridge project with Felsburg Holt & Ullevig. It also considered a disposition, development and reimbursement agreement for 150 Briggs Street. Council approved a downtown alleyway consultant amendment and several right-of-way encroachment licenses on Briggs Street.

erie/9.title: Erie airport fees, hangar leases and noise complaints
erie/9.summary: A resident asked for more regulation of early-morning touch-and-go flights. The board discussed residential through-the-fence fees (a council proposal in December), commercial fees, and a possible ballot question allowing land leases longer than 20 years for hangar development. A hangar presentation to Council is set for Oct. 13.

erie/10.title: Protecting open space and the Page property
erie/10.summary: OSTAB and Planning Commission met to discuss open space zoning, the Reserved Open Space zoning district and the voter approval needed to sell or rezone open space. Council discussion of the Page property was scheduled for Nov. 10, with the rezoning process explained to the board.
erie/10.where: Page property and town open space

sources.body: Open Space and Trails Advisory Board
Open Space and Trails Advisory Board
Open Space and Trails Advisory Board

erie/11.title: New Town Manager appointment
erie/11.summary: Council scheduled a vote Oct. 20 to appoint Kelli Johnson as Town Manager effective Jan. 4, 2027, with an employment agreement, after interviews and executive sessions.

erie/12.title: Compass Park and safe sidewalks
erie/12.summary: Residents spoke in favor of Compass Park and safe sidewalks at the Oct. 6 Council meeting.

erie/13.title: Flock Safety technology and security arrangements
erie/13.summary: Council planned an executive session Sept. 15 on security arrangements and mitigation strategies, including Flock Safety technology. No details were released.

estes-park/0.title: Housing definitions, density bonuses and parking in the draft Development Code
estes-park/0.summary: The Town Board reviewed the 50% draft Development Code's housing definitions, base densities, density and height bonuses, and lower parking minimums for qualifying projects. The Estes Park Housing Authority said 1.2 to 1.4 spaces per unit would work for its properties, while some board members worried about going below two cars per unit. Related housing needs were also raised in public comment and the Housing Assessment and Action Plan.

estes-park/1.title: Fall River Village II PUD and subdivision plats
estes-park/1.summary: Resolutions 87-26, 88-26 and 89-26 on the Fall River Village II PUD and subdivision plats were continued from July 28, and the public hearing was re-opened on August 11. Staff noted the Development Code and state statute require action within 30 days or the application is deemed approved.

estes-park/2.title: Annexation of Fawn Valley and Highway 7 enclaves
estes-park/2.summary: Staff reported costs and benefits of annexing two enclaves, including a $50,000 consultant cost for the map and legal description, about $12,750 a year in added sales tax and $1,900 in property tax. Neighbors surveyed on Highway 7 responded four against and one in favor. Staff will research who owns an unannexed gap parcel that would first need to be annexed.
estes-park/2.where: Fawn Valley and Highway 7 enclaves, including Chalet Ridge Court

estes-park/3.title: Parking license plate recognition policy
estes-park/3.summary: Staff presented a draft policy for license plate recognition at Town-owned paid parking, with data kept one day unless tied to a citation. Prohibited uses include enforcing federal immigration law and monitoring First Amendment activity. The Board asked for the policy to come back for consideration and discussed limiting private LPR use.

estes-park/4.title: Parks and Open Space Master Plan
estes-park/4.summary: The final draft plan covers 11 parks, 2 natural areas and 2 town parcels, and found 76% of households are within a 15-minute walk of a park. About 890 people gave feedback, including students. Board members asked for an urban forestry element and more dog parks, and staff said implementation depends on funding.

estes-park/5.title: Dark Sky lighting ordinance and certification
estes-park/5.summary: Visit Estes Park presented on pursuing International DarkSky Community Certification and a draft Lighting Ordinance. Board members questioned requiring residential properties to comply with Dark Sky fixtures within ten years and how Rocky Mountain National Park's status affects certification.

estes-park/6.title: Water administrative penalties, Windy Gap units and Colorado-Big Thompson subcontract
estes-park/6.summary: Water staff proposed administrative fines to enforce repair of leaking surface lines. The Board declined its right of first refusal to buy Windy Gap water units from Platte River Power Authority, which would have cost nearly $10 million for two units. A Colorado-Big Thompson subcontract extension with the YMCA of the Rockies and Northern Water was pulled for discussion of incorporating Town water customers into the district.

estes-park/7.title: Rezoning review criteria amendments
estes-park/7.summary: Staff proposed amending Development Code Section 3.3 so rezonings must be consistent with the Future Land Use Plan of the Estes Forward Comprehensive Plan, replacing the 'change in conditions' criterion, along with a second new criterion.

estes-park/8.title: Feather flag temporary sign rules
estes-park/8.summary: The Board reviewed Ordinance 15-25, which temporarily allowed feather flags without permit or fee, limited to one per lot up to 12 feet tall, and not in residential zones or downtown. Members were split on whether to charge a fee and require a permit or make the rules permanent.

estes-park/9.title: Youth tobacco and vaping policy request
estes-park/9.summary: A speaker urged the Town to consider policies on tobacco and vape products to protect youth, citing Larimer County's survey results and concerns about Estes Park schools.

estes-park/10.title: Utility purchasing policy non-compliance
estes-park/10.summary: An audit found Power and Communications and Water divisions accepted competitive quotes for inventory purchases instead of following the $30,000 bid process. Staff said this will be addressed in the ongoing revision of purchasing policies.

estes-park/11.title: Events Center storage building contract
estes-park/11.summary: The Board approved a $424,350 contract with Kinley Built to design and build a new storage building at the Events Center Complex, and accepted a $100,000 state DOLA grant toward design of a project.

fairplay/0.title: Gemenskap development sewer dispute and lawsuit
fairplay/0.summary: The Board has repeatedly gone into executive session on the sewer system at the Gemenskap development in Park County, including mediation with the developer on July 27, 2026, a joint session with the Park County commissioners on Sept. 15, and by November a lawsuit the developer filed against the Town. The documents also mention settling Sallie Williard's potential claim; no outcome is stated.

fairplay/1.title: Park County use of Fairplay water for landfill-area wells
fairplay/1.summary: The Board discussed Park County's use of Town water for wells contaminated by the landfill, and in November took up fees for Park County's use of Town water on parcels outside Town limits.
fairplay/1.where: Outside-of-town parcels near Park County landfill

fairplay/2.title: Land swap with Park County (Ordinance 5)
fairplay/2.summary: The Board held first reading of Ordinance No. 5, 2026, authorizing a land swap in which the Town conveys Park County Parcel No. 32670 to Park County in exchange for county property.

fairplay/3.title: 2026 amended and 2027 budget
fairplay/3.summary: Staff presented preliminary 2027 staffing, salaries, police and events budgets. The proposed FY2026 amended and FY2027 budgets were submitted Oct. 19, with a first budget hearing Nov. 2.

fairplay/4.title: Police Department matters: station assessment and personnel review
fairplay/4.summary: The Board reviewed the proposed 2027 police budget and paid for a structural assessment of the police station. Executive sessions covered legal advice and personnel matters involving Chief Jeff Worley and an officer in an investigation.

fairplay/5.title: Water conservation, source water protection and capital planning
fairplay/5.summary: The Board discussed a water conservation plan, heard a Colorado Rural Water Association presentation on the Source Water Protection Plan, and held a work session on Town water rights and the utilities capital improvement plan. Wastewater lagoon liner and new lagoon projects are underway.

fairplay/6.title: Property Improvement Incentive Program (PIIP) agreements
fairplay/6.summary: The Town considered incentive agreements for exterior and window projects at 711 Front Street (Andrew Schofield, with a Certificate of Appropriateness), 305 4th Street and 402 Hathaway Street (Greg Johnson).

fairplay/7.title: Funding requests from nonprofits and community groups
fairplay/7.summary: The Board weighed funding requests from the Park County Senior Coalition, Rocky Mountain Rural Health, the Boys & Girls Club of the High Rockies and others, and donated $1,000 to a South Park High School football fundraiser. It also picked a Mardi Gras fundraiser beneficiary and considered Burro Days and Halloween event requests.

fairplay/8.title: Automated vehicle identification system ordinance
fairplay/8.summary: First reading of Ordinance No. 6 to repeal and re-enact rules on the Town's automated vehicle identification system.

fairplay/9.title: Fee schedule changes and records request policy
fairplay/9.summary: Resolutions amend the Town's schedule of fees; the November version adds a policy on responding to Colorado Open Records Act and criminal justice records requests.

fairplay/10.title: Fireworks show and special events
fairplay/10.summary: The Board discussed whether to hold a 2026 fireworks show, and staff reviewed 2027 events budget items including a tire recycling fee grant.

federal-heights/0.title: 2027 fee schedule and automated vehicle identification (Verra Mobility) agreement
federal-heights/0.summary: Council agenda included Resolution 26-27 adopting the 2027 fee schedule and an item amending the service fee schedule tied to the Verra Mobility services agreement for automated vehicle identification systems. The documents do not state the outcome.

federal-heights/1.title: Public safety tax discussion and 2027 draft budget changes
federal-heights/1.summary: A council work session item covered a possible public safety tax and changes to the 2027 draft budget. Details and decisions are not given in the documents.

federal-heights/2.title: Hyland Hills intergovernmental agreement for surveying
federal-heights/2.summary: Resolution 26-28 would approve an intergovernmental agreement between Federal Heights and the Hyland Hills Park and Recreation District for surveying.

federal-heights/3.title: Local natural hazard mitigation plan agreement with Thornton and other jurisdictions
federal-heights/3.summary: Resolution 26-29 would approve an intergovernmental agreement for a local natural hazard mitigation plan between Federal Heights, Thornton and other partners.

federal-heights/4.title: 2027 Motorola VESTA NXT project
federal-heights/4.summary: Council considered a decision item on the 2027 Motorola VESTA NXT project. VESTA is a 911 call-handling system, though the documents give no further details.

federal-heights/5.title: Resident Ted May's complaints about city documents and First Amendment rights
federal-heights/5.summary: During public comment, Ted May questioned the validity of certain city documents and said his First Amendment rights had been violated. He said his attorney had copies of related records.

federal-heights/6.title: Ward II council appointment and audit services contract
federal-heights/6.summary: Minutes show a Ward II council appointment and a contract with John Cutler & Associates for audit services at $13,500 per year.

firestone/0.title: Comprehensive Plan update
firestone/0.summary: The Planning and Zoning Commission is scheduled to hold a public hearing on Oct. 1, 2026 on Resolution PC-26-03, which would approve an update to Firestone's Comprehensive Plan. The agenda shows the hearing but not the outcome.

firestone/1.title: Barefoot Lakes Filing 5, 2nd Amendment preliminary plat
firestone/1.summary: The Planning and Zoning Commission held a hearing on July 16, 2026 on Resolution PC-26-02, recommending approval of the Barefoot Lakes Filing 5, 2nd Amendment preliminary plat. Resident Steve Trunk raised concerns about impacts on neighboring properties, including views and buffering.

firestone/2.title: Parks, trails and 2027 budget recommendations
firestone/2.summary: The Parks, Trails, Recreation and Open Space Commission is reviewing a proposed projects list and making 2027 budget recommendations. Ideas raised include trail connections to St. Vrain Park via the Legacy trail, trail work at Birch and Firestone Blvd., Cotton Hollow and Sable, and Pinecone and Frontier, repairs to rotting bridge boards south of Gateway Park, and possibly adding pickleball courts. The commission also discussed Arts in Public Places.
firestone/2.where: Townwide, including Gateway Park and St. Vrain Park

sources.body: Parks, Trails, Recreation and Open Space Commission

firestone/3.title: Summer Hours Pilot Program discussion
firestone/3.summary: The Board of Trustees has a discussion item on Oct. 14, 2026 about a Summer Hours Pilot Program. The agenda gives no details on what it would involve.

fort-collins/0.title: Downtown paid-parking pilot and Old Town parking fees
fort-collins/0.summary: At an Aug. 11 work session, Council discussed piloting paid parking at the Oak & Remington surface lot, possibly with on-street paid parking, and asked staff to return with revised pilot options and downtown employee parking ideas. A code update is planned ahead of an on-street pilot. A resident later spoke on messaging about downtown parking fees.
fort-collins/0.where: Downtown / Old Town Fort Collins; Oak & Remington lot

fort-collins/1.title: ELCO wholesale water agreement for Montava development
fort-collins/1.summary: Council reviewed a proposed wholesale water deal with East Larimer County Water District (ELCO) to supply Montava, a 4,000+ unit mixed-use development in northeast Fort Collins. Councilmembers voiced support. Questions covered development fees, utility revenue, long-term supply under climate change and a non-potable system, with a roughly $2.5M capital project noted.

fort-collins/2.title: City joins Northern Integrated Supply Project (Glade Reservoir) instead of Halligan expansion
fort-collins/2.summary: The Water Utility Enterprise board considered agreements for the city to participate in NISP and store some of its own water rights in Glade Reservoir. The city would notify the Army Corps and withdraw its Clean Water Act permit application for the Halligan Reservoir enlargement, citing permitting uncertainty and lower projected rate increases. The resolution was adopted 6-1, with Nelsen opposed.

fort-collins/3.title: 2027-2028 biennial city budget
fort-collins/3.summary: Council held a series of work sessions on the City Manager's Recommended 2027-2028 Budget, the first under a new priority-based budgeting approach after a gap between ongoing revenue and expenses and an exercise to identify 8% cost reductions. A third session on Oct. 13 sought direction on additions and offsets, including use of the Parks & Recreation 2050 tax. Residents objected to higher cost recovery and rental rates at the Lincoln Center and other city facilities.

fort-collins/4.title: North College Urban Renewal area: property purchases, Bristlecone Affordable loan and community charter
fort-collins/4.summary: The Urban Renewal Authority has been working on North College redevelopment: executive sessions on property acquisition including possible eminent domain, a $250,000 supplemental budget to acquire 1630 North College, and a proposed $2 million loan for Bristlecone Affordable, a 112-unit income-restricted housing project. It also discussed a coalition charter with 15 voting seats for community-led redevelopment starting with 1636 North College, and plan finances before tax increment collection ends. Board approval of the charter is planned for December 2026.
fort-collins/4.where: North College Avenue, 1630 and 1636 North College

fort-collins/5.title: 1505 North College façade and food-systems grant
fort-collins/5.summary: The Urban Renewal Authority considered a redevelopment and reimbursement agreement and supplemental budget for property improvements at 1505 North College Ave., near the Bike Co-op and Budget Host Motel. The project is about $1 million, with a one-time storefront grant and a performance-based programming grant supporting local food systems, aimed at preventing blight from returning.

fort-collins/6.title: College and Drake urban renewal plan amendment
fort-collins/6.summary: The Authority considered funding an existing-conditions study around the Drake and College intersection to amend the College and Drake Urban Renewal Plan, because changing conditions mean the original plan no longer works. The study would evaluate adding properties.

fort-collins/7.title: Housing Action Plan and safe parking pilot
fort-collins/7.summary: Council reviewed draft strategies in a new Housing Action Plan that would replace the 2021 Housing Strategic Plan, covering supply, affordability, preservation, stabilization and funding, with a six-year implementation plan. Council also discussed a Safe Parking Pilot Program with mixed input on whether to pursue an ordinance, and a homelessness response system and funding session.

fort-collins/8.title: Affordable housing land and funding decisions (314 N. Howes St., EcoThrift site)
fort-collins/8.summary: Council took up an ordinance to convey city-owned property at 314 North Howes Street for affordable housing; a speaker called it a large giveaway. Residents also raised the Housing Catalyst project at the EcoThrift site lacking funding, which Councilmember Nelsen attributed to competitive subsidies. Council also appropriated remaining CCIP sales tax reserves and moved ARPA funds toward the affordable housing program.

fort-collins/9.title: Land Use Code Ordinance 118 and RP3 parking permit charge
fort-collins/9.summary: Council considered Ordinance No. 118, amending the Land Use Code, on first reading, with speakers supporting adoption. Separately, a resident opposed an RP3 change charging for the first vehicle parked in front of a home; a councilmember said she had requested a pause on the new rates.

fort-collins/10.title: Platte River Power Authority rollback of 2030 non-carbon goal
fort-collins/10.summary: Several residents spoke against the Platte River Power Authority board's discussion of rolling back its goal of 100% non-carbon electricity by 2030.

fort-collins/11.title: Pedestrian and intersection safety projects (Vision Zero)
fort-collins/11.summary: Council appropriated $1,003,544 for the Pedestrian Intersection Improvements project at five locations, for a total of $2,460,856, to improve safety on the High Injury Network. It also funded property acquisition and a replacement signal for the Lemay and Drake intersection ($1,549,760). A resident urged pedestrian safety improvements downtown.
fort-collins/11.where: Five intersections; Lemay Ave and Drake Rd

fort-collins/12.title: Election code changes and campaign finance rules
fort-collins/12.summary: The Election Code Committee reviewed proposed code changes, including letting the clerk issue fines directly for late campaign finance reports, precinct boundary changes, and long-term ideas such as public campaign funding. It also reviewed the 2025 election, which cost about $176,300.

fort-collins/13.title: Economic Development Investment Program
fort-collins/13.summary: Council gave broad support to a proposed Economic Development Investment Program, favoring community vitality and micro-business support over jobs or sales tax goals. Members were uneasy about ongoing annual commitments and discussed staffing and an after-the-fact review role. Council plans to adopt the 2027/28 budget in November 2026.

fort-lupton/0.title: Comprehensive Plan update, Housing Action Plan and Strategic Growth Element
fort-lupton/0.summary: The city is updating its Comprehensive Plan with consultant Ayres Associates, including a new Water Supply Element added by contract amendment on Sept 1. In late October the Planning Commission and Council reviewed the draft Housing Action Plan, Strategic Growth Element and proposed Future Land Use Categories. The city also backed a DOLA Local Planning Capacity Grant application.

fort-lupton/1.title: Western Midstream buried gas pipeline special use permit
fort-lupton/1.summary: The Planning Commission heard Western Midstream's request for a special use permit for buried gas gathering pipelines through I-2 industrial parcels near the Basalite plant, mining and agricultural land. Nearby property owners, including residents of S Denver Ave and County Road 10, asked about pipe size, property access and effects. The commission's recommendation goes to City Council.
fort-lupton/1.where: Industrial parcels near County Road 10 and S Denver Ave

fort-lupton/2.title: Water and sewer plant investment fee changes and water system projects
fort-lupton/2.summary: Council approved a resolution revising the water and sewer infrastructure investment (tap) fee schedule effective December 1, 2026, after staff surveyed regional tap fees; METRO Water Recovery is raising its fee to $6,290 per single family home. Council also took up 2027 plant investment fee changes, the 2027 Colorado-Big Thompson assessment (up to $191,000.70), and ongoing water tower construction with a Murray Farms easement and change orders.

fort-lupton/3.title: Ewing Annexation Agreement amendment
fort-lupton/3.summary: Council considered and adopted an ordinance accepting the first amendment to the Ewing Annexation Agreement originally approved April 16, 2024, with a second reading on Sept 29.

fort-lupton/4.title: Street reconstruction projects funded by CR 12 UPRR money
fort-lupton/4.summary: Council awarded design contracts for added street projects: JVA for 5th Street and Broadway Avenue (up to $143,095) and IMEG for Homestead Drive and Columbine Avenue, with funds from the CR 12 UPRR project. HKS was proposed for 3rd and 5th Streets, and a JVA contract amendment came up in October. The 9th and Northrup/9th Street Extension project was also discussed.
fort-lupton/4.where: 5th St & Broadway Ave; Homestead Dr & Columbine Ave; 3rd St; 9th & Northrup

fort-lupton/5.title: Koshio Park renovation
fort-lupton/5.summary: The park renovation has involved a temporary irrigation change order, Change Order No. 2, an update and a gazebo discussion in October. FLURA noted a groundbreaking and the park is next to the school area.

fort-lupton/6.title: Metropolitan district service plans: Lancaster Crossing and 277
fort-lupton/6.summary: Council reviewed the resubmitted Lancaster Crossing Metropolitan District Nos. 1-5 service plan and a separate 277 Metropolitan District service plan on Sept 29. The documents list no outcome.

fort-lupton/7.title: 2027 budget and property tax limit exclusion
fort-lupton/7.summary: Council received the 2027 requested budget on Sept 29 and applied for exclusion from the 5.5% limit on assessed valuation growth. A budget retreat was held October 17 and the Urban Renewal Authority reviewed its own 2027 draft budget.

fort-lupton/8.title: Urban Renewal Authority grants and TIF reimbursements
fort-lupton/8.summary: FLURA discussed a six-month grant extension requested by El Rey Del Taco, a 50% reimbursement to the city for survey and engineering of a $86,820 project, and TIF reimbursements for Vincent's and the Rec Center. A planned Odd Fellows historic project may seek FLURA grant help.

fort-lupton/9.title: Odd Fellows building historic preservation review
fort-lupton/9.summary: The Historic Preservation Board gave final approval to the Independent Order of Odd Fellows application for work needing replacement of historic elements, which is expected to seek a FLURA grant. The board also discussed Certified Local Government benefits.

fort-lupton/10.title: Energy and infrastructure feasibility studies and Xcel access
fort-lupton/10.summary: Council approved an MOU with Performance Services, Inc. for feasibility studies on solar, water, wastewater and infrastructure improvements. It also approved a Public Service Company temporary access agreement for boring and testing on the city parcel east of the South Platte River, north of the Fort site.
fort-lupton/10.where: City parcel east of South Platte River, north of the Fort

fort-lupton/11.title: Proposition 123 affordable housing commitment
fort-lupton/11.summary: Council scheduled consideration of the city's Proposition 123 commitment for affordable housing for 2027-2029.

fort-lupton/12.title: Data center ordinance legal work
fort-lupton/12.summary: A city payment in October covered legislative work on a data center ordinance, suggesting rules are being drafted; the documents give no details.

foxfield/0.title: Wildfire Resiliency Code adoption (Ordinance 2026-03)
foxfield/0.summary: The Board worked through the State-required Wildfire Resiliency Code from spring to summer 2026, with insurance implications and enforcement through building and fire officials discussed. Ordinance 2026-03 was approved after an Aug. 6 public hearing with no public comments. Trustees also pushed wildfire education with South Metro Fire, including grass height rules and a fire prevention meeting.

foxfield/1.title: Land Use Code update (Ordinance 2026-02)
foxfield/1.summary: The Board held a public hearing on rewriting Articles 1-6 of Chapter 16, continued it several times and postponed it, partly using an AI (Copilot) review of the code. It passed unanimously on Aug. 6, 2026 after a hearing with no public comments.

foxfield/2.title: Speeding data and radar speed signs
foxfield/2.summary: Trustees debated speed data, monitor placement and traffic calming after resident concerns. In July they moved to buy four solar radar signs with tracking software for Hindsdale and Waco. The roughly $22,373 purchase (Resolution 2026-08) was reconsidered in September, with a majority favoring a resident speeding-report tool on the website instead. Trustee Pakanati asked to bring it back when all Trustees could attend.

foxfield/3.title: Road maintenance: crack seal and pavement program
foxfield/3.summary: The Board approved the 2026 SEH engineering fee estimate and pavement repair program. In October it considered a Vance Brothers bid of $11,800 for additional crack seal, an added $6,300, after the first 2 tons did not cover all roads. It was approved in November after SEH explained the estimating shortfall. Emergency repairs on Arapahoe Road with Terracare were also ratified.

foxfield/4.title: Waco Street drainage, erosion and culvert repairs
foxfield/4.summary: Staff presented engineering recommendations on erosion and roadway deterioration near Waco Street and Arapahoe Road. The Board debated riprap versus seeding. In September it approved a revised Terracare quote that dropped the culvert cleanout, with work scheduled for fall.

foxfield/5.title: Home rule charter process
foxfield/5.summary: After a presentation from Town Attorney Corey Hoffmann, Trustees debated whether to start the home rule process, with some feeling it was being rushed. Staff laid out a timeline with a possible special election to form a charter commission in 2026 and a charter vote in 2027. Home rule authority and land use also came up in July.

foxfield/6.title: 2026 and 2027 budgets, taxes and falling sales tax
foxfield/6.summary: The 2026 budget, with general fund spending up about 25% mainly for speed-related items, was adopted after a hearing with no public attendance, and the property tax levy was approved (mill levy 4.982). Trustee Hodge noted sales tax has dropped significantly over four years and vacancies at Foxfield Village Center. A 2027 budget study session was set for November.

foxfield/7.title: Law enforcement (ACSO) and code enforcement contracts
foxfield/7.summary: The Board approved the 2026 Arapahoe County Sheriff's law enforcement agreement and a new SafeBUILT code enforcement agreement with revised rates. A 2027 ACSO agreement was on the November agenda.

foxfield/8.title: Street and tunnel lighting repairs
foxfield/8.summary: Trustees pursued repairs to non-working streetlights and tunnel lights, including S Lewiston Way and Parker Road. In August the Board approved a CLI Services proposal to replace three fixtures and a fuse kit.

foxfield/9.title: Short-term rental litigation
foxfield/9.summary: In July the Board discussed a Summary Judgment ruling in the town's short-term rental lawsuit and future steps.

foxfield/10.title: AI use policy for town staff
foxfield/10.summary: Staff proposed a policy governing AI use by employees and contractors, noting AI chats can be requested under the open records law (CORA).

frederick/0.title: Roads & Routes transportation tax and debt ballot measures
frederick/0.summary: The Board of Trustees took up a Roads & Routes Taskforce update and ordinances setting ballot language for a 1% sales and use tax for transportation infrastructure (Ord. 1422) and for issuing debt for transportation projects (Ord. 1423). A Resolution 26-R-46 in support of the road tax followed on Oct. 7, and staff produced video, FAQ and signage for the campaign.

frederick/1.title: Land Use Code bi-annual amendments (Ordinance 1425)
frederick/1.summary: The Planning Commission reviewed Resolution PCR 2026-08 recommending amendments to Articles 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9 and 13 of the Land Use Code. Changes include creating a marijuana retail sales use and prohibiting it in all zoning districts, changing permitted animals in A and AOS zones, and clarifying parking and loading rules. The Board of Trustees scheduled a public hearing on Ordinance 1425 for Oct. 21.

frederick/2.title: Town budget, budget amendment and public hearings
frederick/2.summary: The Board held a finance quarterly update and budget introduction, a budget work session, Ordinance 1424 for a budget amendment, and a first budget public hearing on Nov. 4. Action on the budget is expected after a second public hearing on Dec. 2, 2026.

frederick/3.title: Water rights, leases and water costs
frederick/3.summary: Water staff arranged a water lease with the Wyndham Hill Metropolitan District, filed a Statement of Opposition in water court case 2026CW3081, and submitted the annual water audit. Bills include $198,000 and $132,000 to Central Weld County Water District for tap fees and a $278,640.88 Northern Water Class B assessment, plus Lower Boulder change-of-use consulting.

frederick/4.title: Public Works & Parks Campus / Municipal Service Center construction
frederick/4.summary: Phase 1 (Building A and site work) is nearly complete on the new Public Works & Parks Campus, and Phase 2 (Fleet Shop and Warehouse) began with concrete footings. Construction pay application #19 was among large payments in the fall bills.

frederick/5.title: Parks water, urban forestry and golf course management plans
frederick/5.summary: The PROST commission heard final updates on the Parks Water Management Plan, Urban Forestry Management Plan and Golf Course Management Plan, which are heading toward adoption this fall. The Planning Commission also held a work session on parks, open space and trails design standards.

sources.body: Parks, Recreation, Open Space & Trails Commission (PROST)
Parks, Recreation, Open Space & Trails Commission (PROST)

frederick/6.title: Engineering Building mural and public art
frederick/6.summary: The Arts Committee is pursuing a mural on the Engineering Building and approved an RFP with a $19,000 budget covering all costs. It also approved placing new wood carvings in Centennial Park and Crist Park and discussed hiring a balloon artist for Frights on Fifth.
frederick/6.where: Engineering Building; Centennial Park and Crist Park

frederick/7.title: Historic preservation plan, grants and Miners' Museum
frederick/7.summary: The Historic Preservation Committee works on its Historic Preservation Plan goals, state historic fund grants, and the Town's application to become a Certified Local Government. It also discussed Miners' Museum hours and cleaning and plaques for founding families; a resident spoke during public comment on Oct. 13.

frederick/8.title: Del Camino South tract conveyance to KO Industrial and Wheatlands plat extension
frederick/8.summary: The Board considered Ordinance 1421 to convey Tract B of Del Camino South Replat of Outlot A to KO Industrial, LLC with vacation of drainage, utility and access easements. It also considered Resolution 26-R-43 extending the Wheatlands preliminary plat expiration date.

frederick/9.title: Town community grants and Youth Commission funding
frederick/9.summary: A community grant application seeks funds for a rent and utility assistance program, and the Board agreed with the St. Vrain Education Foundation on Resolution 26-R-47. The Youth Commission reported grant funding failed and plans to seek sponsors and present to Erie, Firestone and Dacono boards, with Youth Day postponed over budget limits.

frederick/10.title: Algae control permit for reservoir
frederick/10.summary: The Town received a discharge permit effective Sept. 1, 2026 allowing phosphorus inactivation treatments to curb algae blooms and improve water quality in a reservoir.

fremont-county/0.title: Cañon Dolomite Quarry truck traffic permit amendment
fremont-county/0.summary: Amrize asked the commissioners to amend Section K of Conditional Use Permit 11-001 for the Cañon Dolomite Quarry so the truck traffic limit uses "Annual Average Daily Traffic" wording, matching the original CDOT approval. The quarry operates only a day or two a month and wants room for sales surges on those days, not more operating days.

fremont-county/1.title: 152-lot Planned Unit Development at 1337 County Road 3A
fremont-county/1.summary: A Planned Unit Development with 152 lots at a minimum lot size was on the October 13 agenda for a hearing. It is at 1337 County Road 3A, Cañon City.

fremont-county/2.title: Outside consultant review fees billed to an applicant
fremont-county/2.summary: Planning & Zoning asked the commissioners to bill an applicant for review costs beyond the application fee. The excess came from an outside consultant hired after the applicant alleged staff bias. The request relies on Section 306 of the county resolution.

fremont-county/3.title: 2027 Fremont County budget
fremont-county/3.summary: A public hearing on the proposed 2027 county budget was scheduled for the October 27 meeting. The agenda also lists a 2027 MotivHealth employee health plan proposal and a bid award for the DHS building roof replacement.

fremont-county/4.title: Resolutions on state ballot measures (Amendment 83, Amendment 87, Proposition NN)
fremont-county/4.summary: The commissioners were to consider resolutions supporting Amendment 83 and opposing Amendment 87 (graduated income tax) and Proposition NN. Titles are partly cut off in the agenda.

fremont-county/5.title: Aspen Acres Fire and evacuation planning for veterans center
fremont-county/5.summary: Public Health reported on the Aspen Acres Fire, which came close to the Bruce McCandless Veterans Community Living Center before firefighters controlled the north side. Staff have planned and practiced evacuation since the 24 Fire. Fire danger in the county remains extreme, and DOT stopped mowing to avoid sparks.
fremont-county/5.where: Bruce McCandless Veterans Community Living Center

fremont-county/6.title: Colorado River shortage and water rights
fremont-county/6.summary: Commissioner McFall reported on Colorado Counties Inc. discussions about Colorado River negotiations. The Bureau of Reclamation decided the Lower Basin must cut use by 1.25 million acre-feet because the states could not agree.

fremont-county/7.title: Rezoning from Business to Residential (R1)
fremont-county/7.summary: A property owner asked for a zone change from commercial to Residential One so they can add a full bathroom to a unit for personal use. A public hearing was held August 25.

fremont-county/8.title: New liquor license for restaurant, bar and mercantile and CDOT highway access
fremont-county/8.summary: The commissioners considered a new malt, vinous and spirits-light license for a restaurant, bar and mercantile in a building with 134-person occupancy. The site's existing CDOT access permit allowed only 20 trips a day, so a traffic study was needed for a new permit using the West gate off Grant Street. The motion to approve was made.

fremont-county/9.title: RV roof repair business development hearing
fremont-county/9.summary: A hearing was scheduled for a proposed business that maintains and repairs RV roofs inside a building. Details are limited in the documents.

frisco/0.title: Fast-track affordable housing review (Proposition 123) and Unified Development Code changes
frisco/0.summary: The Planning Commission held public hearings on Aug 20 on code amendments, including a fast-tracked review process for affordable housing to meet Proposition 123 state requirements. Council took up Ordinances 26-17 and 26-18 on first reading Sept 8 and second reading Sept 22.

frisco/1.title: Short-term rental cap and licensing changes
frisco/1.summary: Staff asked Council on Oct 13 whether to draft an ordinance changing how the short-term rental cap is calculated, including whether income-restricted units like the Scout rental development count toward the total of residential units. Ordinance 26-14 amending STR licensing was on the Oct 27 agenda for first reading.

frisco/2.title: 2027 budget, mill levy and investment review
frisco/2.summary: Council held a 2027 budget discussion Sept 8, with a review of the town's investment portfolio (about $21.2 million market value). In October it considered the budget appropriation and mill levy ordinances (26-22, 26-23) and a resolution adopting the 2027 budget and 2027-2031 plan.

frisco/3.title: Residential uses in Light Industrial district and ADU incentives
frisco/3.summary: The Planning Commission scheduled hearings on Nov 5 on code amendments to permit residential uses in the Light Industrial District and one and two dwelling units in mixed-use. It also heard amendments to allow incentives for accessory dwelling units.

frisco/4.title: Ballot measures: Summit County Strong Future mill levy and school district 4A
frisco/4.summary: Council considered resolutions of support for Summit County's referred Strong Future mill levy reauthorization (a continuation, not an increase) and for Summit School District ballot measure 4A, a mill levy override for teacher and staff pay. The Summit County Education Association and school district presented to Council.

frisco/5.title: 207 Granite Street eight-townhome project
frisco/5.summary: The Planning Commission reviewed a sketch plan for eight new townhomes at 207 Granite Street. Issues included stepbacks along 2nd Avenue, a single access needing a waiver, a dumpster access waiver, a possible Granite Street sidewalk, and compatibility with the historic park across the street.

frisco/6.title: Sixth Degree Townhomes mixed-use at 121 E Main Street
frisco/6.summary: The Planning Commission conducted a final major site plan review of six residential and two commercial units. Discussion centered on parking lifts without a covenant, an unlocated water line and easement, and compliance with the town's new lighting rules.

frisco/7.title: Telecommunication facility at 101 W Main Street
frisco/7.summary: The Planning Commission was to consider a special use permit for a new freestanding telecommunication facility, applicant BMF Development LLC.

frisco/8.title: Right-of-way vacation near Pioneer Park
frisco/8.summary: The Planning Commission was to consider a request to vacate a portion of town right-of-way adjacent to Pioneer Park, north of 99 N. Council also had a closed session on right-of-way vacation and a potential property purchase.

frisco/9.title: Geothermal thermal energy network test bore at Town Hall
frisco/9.summary: Council considered Resolution 26-23, a revocable license and right of entry for a utility thermal energy network test bore on the Town Hall property, tied to the town's geothermal partnership with Xcel.

frisco/10.title: Council strategic plan retreat and water system update
frisco/10.summary: Council held a retreat Aug 25 to review the strategic plan, covering infrastructure, water rates set for five years, housing, wildfire trail work, and Dark Skies certification. A water systems update and strategic plan briefing followed Oct 27.

frisco/11.title: Downtown winter parking and Unsheltered in Summit license
frisco/11.summary: Council received a downtown winter parking update Sept 22 and considered a revocable license agreement with Unsheltered in Summit on Oct 13.

fruita/0.title: 2027 city budget and the J Road / Fremont Street to 18½ Road spending
fruita/0.summary: The City Manager's recommended 2027 budget has fewer, smaller capital projects, with about $2 million for building J Road from Wildcat Avenue to Skiff Road, and the city is seeking grants. Resident Paul Schultz asked Council on Oct. 20 to halt the roughly $2.2 million Fremont Street to 18½ Road expenditure, citing past eminent domain use and cost overruns on 19 Road.
fruita/0.where: J Road, Fremont Street and 18½ Road

fruita/1.title: State-mandated Water Supply and Strategic Growth elements of the comprehensive plan
fruita/1.summary: Colorado requires cities with comprehensive plans to adopt Water Supply and Strategic Growth Elements by Dec. 31, 2026. Planning Commission and Council discussed a community engagement strategy and a draft water survey. Council noted it is an unfunded mandate and staff is seeking a grant to hire a consultant.

fruita/2.title: 1925 J Road annexation and rezone
fruita/2.summary: The Planning Commission was set to hear a request to annex about 36.14 acres at 1925 J Road and rezone it to Community Residential (CR).

fruita/3.title: Raptor Crossing PUD amendment
fruita/3.summary: A major amendment to the Raptor Crossing PUD guide would allow certain residential and other uses. It went to Planning Commission in August, and Council introduced Ordinance 2026-17 on first reading, with a public hearing set for Sept. 15.

fruita/4.title: Fruita Co-op annexation and industrial rezone
fruita/4.summary: The Planning Commission was scheduled to consider annexing about 40.16 acres for the Fruita Co-op and rezoning it to Industrial.

fruita/5.title: CDOT US 6 West / SH 139 Access Control Plan amendment
fruita/5.summary: CDOT presented an amendment to the access control plan for the future Highway 6 widening from 18 Road to 22 Road. It includes right-in/right-out intersections with dedicated U-turns and changes to access for private properties and businesses. An updated intergovernmental agreement is expected in January 2027.

fruita/6.title: Metropolitan districts ordinance (Title 18)
fruita/6.summary: Ordinance 2026-20 would enact a new Title 18 of the municipal code on metropolitan districts, with a public hearing set for Nov. 17. A resident asked Council to pull it from the consent agenda.

fruita/7.title: Park conditions, Farmers Market location and recreation feedback
fruita/7.summary: The Parks and Recreation Commission discussed worn grass at Civic Center Park and possibly moving the Farmers Market to Reed Park or alternating sites. Salt Wash soccer fields are drying out because of drought water cuts, and residents asked for more lap lanes at the Community Center. The commission also discussed e-scooter and off-road vehicle rules and possible homeless camps near the LAUNCH project.
fruita/7.where: Civic Center Park, Reed Park, Salt Wash fields

fruita/8.title: Public art sculpture selections
fruita/8.summary: The Arts and Culture Board reviewed artist applications for sculptures at sites including South Mesa Street and the Dinosaur Journey parking lot. Members visited the pieces on Aug. 17 and planned to notify selected artists.
fruita/8.where: South Mesa Street, Dinosaur Journey lot, FARM

fruita/9.title: Bee City USA proposal
fruita/9.summary: Council heard a proposal to make Fruita Mesa County's first Bee City, which requires a $200 annual fee and a Council resolution. Staff suggested the Livability or Parks and Recreation commission take responsibility for the application.

fruita/10.title: Municipal judge ordinances and judge appointment
fruita/10.summary: Council introduced ordinances amending municipal code sections on municipal judges' powers and another section, with hearings set for Sept. 15. In executive session on Sept. 22 it interviewed candidates and recommended the City Manager negotiate a contract with its choice for Municipal Court Judge.

garden-city/0.title: Town Administrator/Clerk transition and Cheryl Campbell's resignation
garden-city/0.summary: On July 21, 2026 the Board accepted Town Administrator Cheryl Campbell's resignation and discussed handing the position over once Linda Blackston starts. An employment agreement and an alternate town attorney option were also on the agenda.

garden-city/1.title: New Police Department building construction
garden-city/1.summary: The Board repeatedly approved Mark Young Construction change orders and invoices for the Police Department project, including a $301,598.32 November 2025 invoice and a June 2026 invoice. The police chief also noted the PD floor will be entirely replaced and grants were submitted.

garden-city/2.title: 2026 budget, property tax levy and employee raises
garden-city/2.summary: After a public hearing, the Board in December 2025 considered adopting the 2026 budget, appropriating funds and setting the general property tax levy. It also considered a 4% cost-of-living raise and a larger health insurance stipend for employees.

garden-city/3.title: Electric and solar ready building code (Ordinance 11-2025)
garden-city/3.summary: The Board introduced Ordinance 11-2025 adopting by reference the 2023 International electric and solar ready codes and the Colorado Wildfire Resiliency code, then held a public hearing on December 9, 2025.

garden-city/4.title: Award Alliance incentive
garden-city/4.summary: Paul Hlad of Award Alliance presented to the Board in November 2025, and in December the Board considered Resolution 13-2025 granting an incentive to Award Alliance.

garden-city/5.title: Marijuana license applications and renewals
garden-city/5.summary: The Board considered several retail marijuana store, cultivation and manufacturer licenses in November 2025, including Nature's Herbs and Wellness Center and High Plainz Strains II. In July 2026 it took up a Star Buds license at 2502 8th Ave.
garden-city/5.where: 2502 8th Ave and other Garden City locations

garden-city/6.title: Use by special review and Northern Colorado Driveline
garden-city/6.summary: In July 2026 the Board adopted Resolution 10-2026 granting a use by special review and separately discussed Northern Colorado Driveline. The documents give no further details.

garden-city/7.title: Weld County CDBG agreement and coordinated election
garden-city/7.summary: The Board approved an intergovernmental agreement for the Community Development Block Grant program in Weld County and a memorandum for a coordinated election, and discussed the election.

garden-city/8.title: El Rodeo Night Club commercial revitalization grant
garden-city/8.summary: The Board reviewed final approval of a Commercial Revitalization Grant for El Rodeo Night Club LLC in November 2025.

garfield-county/0.title: 2027 county budget hearings and workforce analysis
garfield-county/0.summary: The commissioners held 2027 budget hearings in October, with department and elected office presentations, plus Budget Supplement #4 and a $234,039 supplemental request. They also heard an MGT workforce analysis, and the Early Childhood District and Forest Improvement District presented. Unfreezing two Human Services positions and a sheriff's office early retirement plan were also on the agendas.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners - Work Session
Board of County Commissioners - Budget Hearings

garfield-county/1.title: Affordable housing: USDA programs, Housing Authority funding and Cavern Springs
garfield-county/1.summary: Commissioners heard from USDA Rural Development on affordable housing programs and from the Garfield County Housing Authority, which asked for $90,000 in 2027 funding. They were also asked for a letter of support for the Cavern Springs Mobile Home Park request, and to sign an amendment to the Oak Meadows Ranch Filing 4B affordable housing plan involving Habitat for Humanity.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners - Work Session

garfield-county/2.title: Mitchell Creek Community PUD rezoning and sketch plan
garfield-county/2.summary: The Planning Commission held a public hearing on rezoning from Rural to PUD and a major subdivision sketch plan for the Mitchell Creek Community PUD at 50235 Highway 6/24 near Glenwood Springs. The owner is AMICHAUX Limited Partnership LLLP.

garfield-county/3.title: Lake Springs Ranch PUD amendment and rezoning
garfield-county/3.summary: The Planning Commission was to hear a substantial PUD amendment, a preliminary plan and rezoning of land being removed from the Lake Springs Ranch PUD, about 3.5 miles southeast of Glenwood Springs off County Road 114.

garfield-county/4.title: McClure River Ranch PUD amendment and 12-lot preliminary plan
garfield-county/4.summary: Commissioners were asked to sign resolutions approving a substantial amendment to the 98-acre McClure River Ranch PUD and a preliminary plan dividing 48.96 acres into 12 lots and 2 tracts, about 4 miles east of Carbondale. The applicant is Aspen Polo Partners. A resolution for the Hogback View Estates major subdivision preliminary plan east of New Castle was also up for signature.

garfield-county/5.title: Xcel Hopkins to Basalt transmission line rebuild
garfield-county/5.summary: The Planning Commission reviewed the location and extent of Xcel Energy's rebuild of the Hopkins to Basalt transmission line 9256, starting near Red Canyon Road and Fisher Cemetery Road east of Carbondale. Xcel also gave the commissioners a presentation.

garfield-county/6.title: Library district tax extension on November ballot
garfield-county/6.summary: The Garfield County Public Library District asked commissioners to place a ballot issue on the Nov. 3, 2026 election ballot asking voters to extend a portion of the district's property tax levy.

garfield-county/7.title: Parachute funding requests: 1st Street/US 6 reconstruction and transit
garfield-county/7.summary: The Town of Parachute asked for $600,000 for the Parachute MOVES 1st Street/US 6 reconstruction project. It also asked for disbursement of $200,000 in 2026 funding for the Parachute Area Transit System and for a 2027 funding request.

garfield-county/8.title: Slaughterhouse Gulch mudslide landfill fee waiver
garfield-county/8.summary: A request asked commissioners to waive landfill tipping fees because of the Slaughterhouse Gulch mudslide. Rifle also asked for half-price landfill fees for its 18th annual fall cleanup.

garfield-county/9.title: LoVa Trail letter of support for federal funding
garfield-county/9.summary: Commissioners were asked for a letter of support for Glenwood Springs' Federal Lands Access Program application to fund the LoVa Trail through South Canyon. A letter of support for a Roaring Fork Outdoor Volunteers trail planning grant was also requested.

garfield-county/10.title: Madison AI assistant purchase
garfield-county/10.summary: Commissioners were asked to approve a $43,200 supplemental appropriation and a Carahsoft contract for a 12-month Madison AI subscription, with a countywide assistant and one for Community Development.

garfield-county/11.title: Garfield Clean Energy 2027 funding and Colorado River District update
garfield-county/11.summary: Garfield Clean Energy requested $150,000 for 2027 membership. The Colorado River District also gave an annual update, including the Shoshone Water Rights Preservation project.

gilpin-county/0.title: Rollinsville area fire-protection cisterns
gilpin-county/0.summary: The commissioners took up Resolution 26-085 to develop a community cistern for fire protection in the Rollinsville area, choosing between the East/Gold Dirt and West/Public Works cistern projects. By Sept. 8 the resolution covered coordinated procurement of both projects.

gilpin-county/1.title: Short-term rental regulations (Ordinance 26-01)
gilpin-county/1.summary: Ordinance 26-01 on rental regulations had a first reading on Aug. 25 and a second reading at a public hearing on Sept. 22. Community Development and the County Attorney presented it.

gilpin-county/2.title: Roadway design manual, road classification and county road inventory
gilpin-county/2.summary: The county reviewed a Roadway Design and Construction Manual and County Road Inventory. On Aug. 25 a public hearing covered Resolution 26-084, designating and classifying county roads, and Resolution 26-088, adopting the roadway manual.

gilpin-county/3.title: 2027 budget, employee benefits and compensation
gilpin-county/3.summary: A draft 2027 budget was presented on Sept. 22. Commissioners also considered the 2026 Compensation Plan (Resolution 26-089) and the 2027 employee benefits renewal (Resolution 26-097).

gilpin-county/4.title: Wildfire mitigation grants and fire restrictions
gilpin-county/4.summary: The county committed $51,000 over three years to the Clear Creek Watershed & Forest Health Partnership's grant application for forest restoration and wildfire risk mitigation. It also coordinated a Community Wildfire Defense Grant and supported fuels reduction projects. Stage 2 fire restrictions were lowered to Stage 1 on Sept. 8, and Resolution 26-099 removed the remaining restrictions in late October.

gilpin-county/5.title: Ballot issue referred to Gilpin County voters
gilpin-county/5.summary: Resolution 26-077 refers a ballot issue to county voters. It appeared on the Aug. 11 and Aug. 25 agendas. Upcoming ballot propositions were discussed on Sept. 8, and a November election resolution was also on the Aug. 25 agenda.

gilpin-county/6.title: Affordable housing: Proposition 123 credits and commitment
gilpin-county/6.summary: The county considered an intergovernmental agreement on Proposition 123 affordable housing unit credits (Resolution 26-086). It also considered Resolution 26-098 authorizing an affordable housing commitment filing.

gilpin-county/7.title: Parks and Recreation fees, equipment and youth programs
gilpin-county/7.summary: Commissioners discussed a fee structure and equipment purchase plan for Parks and Recreation. A youth programs status update followed in October. The county's comprehensive fee schedule was also updated (Resolution 26-093).

gilpin-county/8.title: Code enforcement policy and public records (CORA) process
gilpin-county/8.summary: A draft code enforcement policy was discussed on Aug. 18. The county amended its public records request policy (Resolution 26-090) and heard an update on the CORA process and fees.

gilpin-county/9.title: COMBA bike trail outside I-70 project
gilpin-county/9.summary: A bike trail project with COMBA outside the I-70 corridor was on the Aug. 18 agenda for discussion.

glenwood-springs/0.title: Short-term and accessory tourist rental rules
glenwood-springs/0.summary: Planning and Zoning reviewed a code amendment requiring permit holders to actually rent and remit lodging tax in order to renew short-term rental and accessory tourist rental permits. Council took up Ordinance 2026-22 on Sept. 17, with an amendment to a minimum of 20 nights and $150 in sales tax remitted over two years, and it returned on the Oct. 1 consent agenda.

glenwood-springs/1.title: Xcel transmission line rebuild (6584 line)
glenwood-springs/1.summary: Xcel Energy is replacing aging wood poles on the 6584 transmission line with steel monopoles and widening easements to reduce wildfire risk. Planning and Zoning considered the Location and Extent permit and a 1041 recommendation, and the 1041 application went to City Council on Nov. 5.
glenwood-springs/1.where: Glenwood Springs portion of the 6584 transmission line

glenwood-springs/2.title: Canyon Vista affordable housing at 51993 Hwy 6 & 24
glenwood-springs/2.summary: The 80-unit affordable multifamily project on about 4 acres between Highway 6 and Donegan Road needed a preliminary plat to merge three parcels into one lot. Planning and Zoning reviewed it with six recommended conditions, then Council took up the plat and a right-of-way encroachment license on Oct. 15. Revised water service agreements followed on Nov. 5.
glenwood-springs/2.where: 51993 Hwy 6 & 24, between Highway 6 and Donegan Road

glenwood-springs/3.title: 130 Midland affordable homeownership funding request
glenwood-springs/3.summary: Council considered a funding request for the 130 Midland affordable homeownership project on Oct. 1 and continued it on Oct. 15. A tour of the Habitat project, The Confluence at 8th and Midland, was planned for Nov. 5.
glenwood-springs/3.where: 130 Midland Avenue / The Confluence at 8th and Midland

glenwood-springs/4.title: Bennett Avenue parking and 1600 Bennett fee-in-lieu request
glenwood-springs/4.summary: Five residents spoke at the Sept. 3 council meeting about parking on Bennett Avenue. Council later had a parking fee-in-lieu request for 1600 Bennett on its Oct. 1 agenda.

glenwood-springs/5.title: 2027 city budget and fees
glenwood-springs/5.summary: Council received the 2027 budget presentation on Oct. 1, held a public budget hearing on Oct. 15, and had a resolution approving the 2027 budget on the Nov. 5 agenda. Related items included a 2026 appropriation amendment, the 2027 Tourism Promotion Fund budget, 2027 landfill fees and the 2027 parks and recreation fee schedule.

glenwood-springs/6.title: Fire tax ballot issue and coordinated election
glenwood-springs/6.summary: Council took up a resolution certifying a ballot issue and setting its ballot title, and held public comment. It also approved an intergovernmental agreement with Garfield County for the 2026 coordinated election. The mayor spoke in support of the fire tax.

glenwood-springs/7.title: Pay as You Throw trash contract and haul route weight limits
glenwood-springs/7.summary: Council discussed and then scheduled action on a Pay as You Throw contract with Mountain Waste and Recycling. A councilor also asked for support to study street weight limits and designated haul routes.

glenwood-springs/8.title: Ride Glenwood on-demand pricing and transportation planning
glenwood-springs/8.summary: Council scheduled action on pricing for the Ride Glenwood on-demand service on Oct. 15, alongside a comprehensive transportation discussion. A joint work session with the Transportation Commission was set for Oct. 1.

glenwood-springs/9.title: Electric vehicle charging regulations
glenwood-springs/9.summary: Council considered Ordinance 2026-18 amending the municipal code on regulating and permitting electric vehicle charging projects. It later appeared on the Sept. 3 consent agenda.

glenwood-springs/10.title: Water litigation and Hot Springs Pool raw water contract
glenwood-springs/10.summary: Council went into executive session on litigation involving the Mitchell-Cooper Ditch and Pipeline Company and JG Housing Solutions, LLC. Another executive session concerned negotiations on the Hot Springs Pool raw water delivery contract.

golden/0.title: City Manager separation and interim appointment
golden/0.summary: After an executive session on Charter, Code and the City Manager's contract, Council moved to negotiate a separation agreement and appointed Carly Lorenz as Interim City Manager on Aug. 11. Resolutions on an Acting City Manager agreement and a City Manager Separation Agreement were on the Aug. 25 agenda, and an outside investigation was mentioned. Residents submitted public comment.

golden/1.title: Fire Department incident and community response
golden/1.summary: Council, the REDI Task Force and the public have been dealing with an incident at the Golden Fire Department. Community members raised concerns about racial profiling, and Council noted an outside investigation and an active legal case. The REDI group discussed how to move forward and hold space for staff and residents.

golden/2.title: The Junction urban renewal area and tax increment financing
golden/2.summary: GURA is weighing a new urban renewal plan for The Junction, a 51-acre light industrial business park west of Highway 93. The developer seeks 100% tax increment financing to cover about $59 million in public improvements, including a Highway 93 roundabout and a pedestrian bridge to North Table Mountain Park. Staff is negotiating revenue sharing with the county (an 88% proposal) and other taxing entities, and the subcommittee recommended explicitly excluding data centers from the plan.
golden/2.where: West side of State Highway 93 near North Table Mountain Park

golden/3.title: Nazarene affordable housing project and TIF agreement at 17455 West 16th Avenue
golden/3.summary: The Nazarene Plan Area was adopted by Council on July 14, and the developer secured key grant financing. GURA is reviewing a draft TIF agreement, with a focus on making the affordable housing commitments survive any sale and raising the income cap from 30% to 35% of area median income.

golden/4.title: Clayworks development: gas amendment, parking and mobility
golden/4.summary: Clayworks developers asked to amend their Official Development Plan to allow limited natural gas for pool and spa heating, fireplaces and grills. Sustainability advisers and a Sustainable Golden member urged keeping the original all-electric commitments. The Mobility board has repeatedly discussed Clayworks parking, its travel demand plan and a traffic memo. The amendment must still go to Planning Commission and Council.

golden/5.title: Flock license plate camera contract
golden/5.summary: Council held a study session on Flock technology and how Golden Police use it. Councilors Knecht and Kurzinski proposed reconsidering the Flock contract, and it would go to a vote if three or more councilors support it.

sources.body: City Council Study Session 5pm-Regular Business Meeting 7:00pm

golden/6.title: 2027-2028 biennial budget and revenue outlook
golden/6.summary: The city is drafting its first two-year budget for 2027-28 under revenue constraints. Council reviewed the proposed 2027 budget in October, and a budget appropriation ordinance was set for hearing Nov. 10. The citizens' budget committee also reviewed the proposed budget and discussed shifting marijuana tax money toward rent assistance and food insecurity. Sales tax is up 2.87% year to date but use tax is down.

sources.body: City Council Study Session & Regular Business Meeting
City Council Study Session 5pm-Regular Business Meeting 7:00pm

golden/7.title: Alley spur and historic home at 2122 Jackson Street
golden/7.summary: Council called up Planning Commission review of three Form Zone site plans at 2122 Jackson Street, mainly to examine how an alley spur is defined. Neighbors, including Natalie Palmer, said the alley is narrow and raised concerns about trash, parking, lights and green space, and the plan would keep a historic home as a feature.

golden/8.title: Historic preservation cases: demolitions and new construction in East Street district
golden/8.summary: The Historic Preservation Board approved a rear cottage at 2024 Ford Street, and considered demolition requests for 612 10th Street (Schall Residence) and 1735 and 622 Water Street (Barnes-Peery Residence). It also considered additions at 403 18th Street and a revised facade at 2211B Ford Street, with Resolution HPB 26-06 for 403 18th Street approved with conditions.
golden/8.where: 2024 Ford St, 612 10th St, 403 18th St, 2211B Ford St, 622 Water St

golden/9.title: Special events impacts and grants
golden/9.summary: A resident asked the events committee to review the cumulative parking and traffic impact of events on the west end of 10th Street. The committee also handled a new Golden Skull Marathon application, shuttle and parking plans, and the special events grant program, with about $33,657 of the $40,000 budget approved for 2026.

golden/10.title: Visit Golden marketing contract and vendor fee funding
golden/10.summary: The Community Marketing Board reviewed its 2027 strategic plan, a 17 million visitor figure it may revise or remove, and the 2027-28 budget. Council considered a contract with DVA Advertising. The board also discussed the sales tax vendor fee credit that funds the program.

golden/11.title: Lions Park playground redesign, GOCO grant and public art
golden/11.summary: Council backed a Great Outdoors Colorado grant for the Lions Park Nature Play and outdoor project. The Arts and Culture Commission selected 'Pollinators at Play' by Alexander Bond for the playground after reviewing 29 entries.

sources.body: Lion's Park Art Selection Panel Meeting - No Recording
Parks and Recreation Advisory Board Meeting
ACC Lion's Park Art Selection Panel Meeting - No Recording

golden/12.title: Drought response and water conservation
golden/12.summary: Staff reported on 2026 water conservation and drought response, including a new weather-normalization model, increased June use and turf damage in parks. Council scheduled an after-action review of the drought response, and an ordinance amending water and wastewater regulations and administrative citations was set for a Nov. 10 hearing.

sources.body: City Council Study Session & Regular Business Meeting

golden/13.title: Commercial energy benchmarking and universal recycling ordinance
golden/13.summary: The sustainability board discussed a proposed commercial energy benchmarking program, with public comment urging clear goals and a voluntary pilot. Staff is developing a universal recycling ordinance, possibly starting with hauler licensing, and the board backed raising the 2027 rebate request to $200,000.

golden/14.title: Heritage Road and Kimball Avenue roundabout landscaping
golden/14.summary: Neighbors asked Parks and Recreation to add the roundabout statue landscaping to its watering rotation after the volunteer who watered it died. The city has no maintenance agreement for the landscaping, and options included a watering truck or extending the sprinkler line.
golden/14.where: Heritage Road and Kimball Avenue roundabout

sources.body: Parks and Recreation Advisory Board Meeting

golden/15.title: 2027 recreation service fees
golden/15.summary: Parks staff proposed 2027 fee changes for athletic fields, the Community Center, Splash, Fossil Trace Golf Club, the RV park and pavilions. In early 2027 users paying by card would be charged a processing fee of up to 3%, and the full city fee schedule goes to Council in early December.

sources.body: Parks and Recreation Advisory Board Study Session

granby/0.title: Town Manager separation and recruitment of an interim manager
granby/0.summary: The Board met in executive session on the Town Manager's employment, then took up ratifying a Town Manager separation agreement on Sept. 8. In October it discussed interim manager and permanent recruitment, and a transition. The documents do not state the terms or outcome.

granby/1.title: Data center workshop
granby/1.summary: The Board held a data center workshop led by the Town Manager on Aug. 25. The agenda does not say whether a specific facility or new rules are proposed.

granby/2.title: Zoning code rewrite and new zoning map (Ordinance 1041)
granby/2.summary: The Board held a public hearing on Aug. 25 and again on Sept. 22 on comprehensive amendments to Chapter 16 (zoning regulations) and a legislative update to the official zoning map.

granby/3.title: Ten Mile Crossing planned development plan
granby/3.summary: The Planning Commission held a hearing on Oct. 5 on the preliminary plat and plan for the Ten Mile Crossing Planned Development Overlay District, with conditions. The Board held a hearing on the preliminary plan on Oct. 13.

granby/4.title: Nuche Village apartments agreement, funding and contract
granby/4.summary: The Board dealt repeatedly with the Nuche Village apartments. It considered an agreement extension on Sept. 8, funding on Oct. 13, and the contract on Oct. 27. Hearing board appointments for Nuche Village also came up in August and September.

granby/5.title: Annexation proceedings and the GRCO annexation
granby/5.summary: On Sept. 22 the Board considered a resolution initiating annexation proceedings and setting a hearing on the eligibility of certain lands. On Oct. 27 it took up annexation consideration for GRCO.

granby/6.title: Grand Elk Ranch GID property conveyance and 2027 budget
granby/6.summary: The Grand Elk Ranch General Improvement District reviewed its 2027 budget on Oct. 13. On Oct. 27 it took up Ordinance 81 authorizing conveyance of real property related to the Village at Buckhorn.
granby/6.where: Grand Elk Ranch / Village at Buckhorn

granby/7.title: 2027 Town of Granby budget
granby/7.summary: The Finance Director presented the 2027 town budget for discussion on Oct. 13.

granby/8.title: Wildfire resiliency code workshop
granby/8.summary: The Board held a workshop on a wildfire resiliency code on Aug. 11.

granby/9.title: Peddler, mobile vendor and solicitor rules (Ordinance 1040)
granby/9.summary: The Board considered an ordinance amending Chapter 5.05 and adding Chapter 5.06 of the municipal code to regulate peddlers, mobile vendors, solicitors and canvassers.

granby/10.title: Granby Trails revegetation and parks planning
granby/10.summary: A resident and the Middle Park Conservation District presented revegetation and tree planting at Granby Trails using CSFS grants, with an update on Aug. 25. The Board also discussed Bark Park pond, parks planning and a parks and rec position in October.

granby/11.title: Police Chief contract and new Tahoes
granby/11.summary: The Board considered buying two Chevy Tahoes for the police department in August. A police chief contract was on the Sept. 22 agenda, and an oath of office for the police chief on Oct. 13.

granby/12.title: Alley traffic concerns
granby/12.summary: The Board discussed alley traffic concerns on Sept. 8.

grand-junction/0.title: Temporary moratorium on large data centers
grand-junction/0.summary: Council discussed on Sept. 14 a temporary moratorium on large data centers because the code does not address them and they could use significant power and water; no applications are pending. An ordinance for a moratorium lasting until code amendments or 365 days was introduced Oct. 7 with a hearing set for Oct. 21.

grand-junction/1.title: 2027 city budget and structural deficit
grand-junction/1.summary: Staff reported a $6 million General Fund structural gap. The recommended 2027 budget is $317.4 million ($120.8 million General Fund), with about $2 million in personnel cuts, reduced Lincoln Park Pool hours, and $2.7 million for public safety including six police officers and three fire battalion chiefs. It also includes utility rate and golf fee increases and a $93.5 million capital program; a regional fire district is being explored. Appropriation hearings are set for November.

grand-junction/2.title: Significant Tree Ordinance removed from Development Code
grand-junction/2.summary: At the Housing Affordability Code Task Force's request, Council considered removing the significant tree protections from the Zoning and Development Code. The Forestry Board later reported Council voted to remove them despite strong public support for keeping them. A consultant review of the code may bring an alternative.

grand-junction/3.title: Housing Affordability Code Task Force and code simplification
grand-junction/3.summary: The task force is working with consultant KLJ to find code and TEDS requirements that raise housing costs, aiming to finish recommendations including hearings in early 2027. It discusses cost analysis, incentives versus mandates, and a final report.

grand-junction/4.title: Juniper Grove affordable homeownership at the Salt Flats
grand-junction/4.summary: Council considered selling about 3.3 acres of the city-owned Salt Flats at 450 28 Road to Grand Junction Homes for 48 for-sale units serving households under 100% AMI. The city would also cover $593,340 in water and sewer fees; the hearing was continued to Sept. 16, with completion expected winter 2027.

grand-junction/5.title: Housing Action Plan update
grand-junction/5.summary: Consultant Root Policy presented a revised Housing Action Plan that drops the proposed Housing Advisory Board and pushes exploration of new housing revenue to years four to six. Council supported moving forward; DOLA review, public comment and a Council adoption hearing follow.

grand-junction/6.title: Galley Meadows rezone at 2590 Galley Lane and 675 26 Road
grand-junction/6.summary: Neighbors raised concerns about traffic, lighting, construction and density on the 13.04-acre rezone to RL-4. The Planning Commission recommended approval, and Council approved Ordinance 5341 on Sept. 16.

grand-junction/7.title: Lincoln Park Barn and Certified Local Government
grand-junction/7.summary: The Historic Preservation Board is weighing the city's pursuit of Certified Local Government status and its effect on design review in historic districts. Residents asked the board to nominate the Lincoln Park Barn for designation, and members asked for a special meeting.

grand-junction/8.title: I-70B corridor improvements and historic resources
grand-junction/8.summary: The Historic Preservation Board reviewed CDOT's request for comments on I-70B improvements, including impacts on the former Union Carbide building, possible buried streetcar tracks and Emerson Park, and chose to send feedback.

grand-junction/9.title: Water supply element and water conservation
grand-junction/9.summary: Staff presented the Water Supply Element required by SB 24-174 for the Comprehensive Plan, saying supplies are sufficient for current and projected needs. Separately, the Forestry Board discussed how turf conversion affects mature trees, and Council reviewed the Juniata Ditch piping grant, which addresses about 1,400 acre-feet of annual loss.

grand-junction/10.title: Matchett Park bike park future
grand-junction/10.summary: A survey showed strong support for keeping the Matchett bike park. Given budget limits and the Lunch Loop project, the Parks board moved to hold off on further development.

grand-junction/11.title: Parks capital plan and impact fee decline
grand-junction/11.summary: The 2027 parks capital plan includes a second greenhouse, parking repairs and playground work, while impact-fee revenue is projected to fall from about $1.2 million to $758,000. Columbine and Hawthorne parks get a $500,000 Safe Streets grant for lighting, and a facility naming policy was approved.

grand-junction/12.title: 2911 D 1/2 Road annexation and mixed-use zoning
grand-junction/12.summary: Anthony Properties petitioned to annex 14.88 acres at 2911 D 1/2 Road. The Planning Commission was to consider a Comprehensive Plan amendment, MU-2 zoning and a Circulation Plan amendment, with a Council hearing set for Dec. 16.

grand-junction/13.title: Rezone of 2324 Hwy 6 & 50 to commercial
grand-junction/13.summary: RAMS 1 Ho LLC requested rezoning 2.88 acres from I-1 to CG for new retail and office; the Planning Commission recommended approval, noting the loss of industrial land. Council set a hearing for Oct. 21.

grand-junction/14.title: Materials Recovery Facility financing
grand-junction/14.summary: Council approved Ordinance 5338 authorizing an additional $9.3 million in Certificates of Participation to finish acquisition and improvements for the city's Materials Recovery Facility. No public comment was given.

grand-junction/15.title: Persigo sewer budget and lift station
grand-junction/15.summary: The 2027 Persigo wastewater budget totals $69.9 million, about $49.7 million of it capital, with $4.5 million in unplanned needs. Council also authorized buying 354 Bonny Street for a new sewer lift station.

grand-lake/0.title: Land Use Code overhaul: definitions, shoreline rules and development review (Ordinances 13-2026 to 27-2026)
