grand-lake/0.summary: The Planning Commission reviewed amendments (Resolutions 08-2026 and 10-2026) to Chapter 12 of the town code. They move definitions out of several sections, drop the certified-mail notice requirement, create a new Certifications section and clarify development review thresholds and procedures. The Board of Trustees scheduled a public hearing and first reading of Ordinances 13-2026 through 27-2026 for Nov. 9.

grand-lake/1.title: 2027 town budget and public hearing
grand-lake/1.summary: The Board held workshops on Sept. 28 and Oct. 8 and reviewed the draft 2027 budget on Oct. 12 and 26, including wages and benefits compared with other municipalities. The preliminary budget shows $7.51M of General Fund revenue, of which $2.87M is grant money tied to four specific projects. A public hearing on the FY 2027 budget was set for Nov. 9, with final approval planned for Nov. 23.

grand-lake/2.title: Major subdivision at 120 County Road 663
grand-lake/2.summary: The Planning Commission held a public hearing on the final development application and final plat for a major subdivision on property annexed in 2025. Staff flagged concerns about fire and emergency access, the road improvements needed, protecting the water main under County Road 663 that supplies all of Grand Lake, and stormwater and flood risk after the post-fire flooding.

grand-lake/3.title: Shoreline and side/front yard setback variances
grand-lake/3.summary: The Board of Adjustment heard variance requests for 536 Cairns Avenue, including a side yard setback for a separate staircase, which neighbors spoke in support of, and a front yard setback for an elevator. A shoreline setback variance (Resolution 08-2026) had a notice error naming the wrong hearing body, since shoreline variances go to the Planning Commission. The Trustees were set to hear a shoreline variance (Resolution 87-2026) for a property on Mad.

grand-lake/4.title: Boots, Bass & Big Air downtown winter event
grand-lake/4.summary: Trustees discussed a proposed downtown winter event on Saturday, January 30, 2027, with a working budget of $40,000 and a snowmobile jump on a closed Grand Avenue. Staff raised concerns about public safety and liability, street closures, parking and staff time on the same weekend as skijoring. No action was requested, only Board direction.

grand-lake/5.title: Town Council retreat agenda: marketing, housing, parking and governance
grand-lake/5.summary: Multi-day Board sessions covered the What Makes Us Grand marketing campaign, events policy (fee waivers, food trucks, mobile stage), Mary Drive next steps and workforce housing, downtown property acquisition and parking direction. They also covered home rule versus statutory town, the Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code, reserves policy and a five-year capital plan.

grand-lake/6.title: $175,000 promissory note for Space to Create Grand Lake
grand-lake/6.summary: Trustees were asked to approve Resolution 91-2026, a $175,000 promissory note with The Grand Foundation for the Space to Create Grand Lake project.

grand-lake/7.title: Little Columbine Creek restoration and fire mitigation contracts
grand-lake/7.summary: The Board considered a construction contract with Frontier Environmental Services for Little Columbine Creek restoration (Stormwater Plan Phase 2). It also considered a fire mitigation contract for the Mathews Property at 195 County Road.

grand-lake/8.title: Public comment and meeting recording policy
grand-lake/8.summary: Trustees considered Resolution 94-2026 adopting a public comment and meeting recording policy.

grand-lake/9.title: Town Square Park marquee sign
grand-lake/9.summary: The Board considered a revised proposal from SALT Workshop and MetalMorphic Methods for the Town Square Park marquee sign. A sign code waiver (Resolution 92-2026) was also on the Nov. 9 agenda.

greeley/0.title: Sales tax ballot question 2F for West Greeley and Civic Campus projects
greeley/0.summary: Council moved to put a 0.60% sales and use tax increase (Jan 1, 2027 through Dec 31, 2067) to fund capital projects on the Nov. 3, 2026 ballot as Question 2F, and later passed a resolution of support. Dozens of residents spoke Aug. 18 against combining the contentious Catalyst/West Greeley project with the civic campus, or against new taxes; a few supported a sales tax. Council also took legal advice in executive session and held first and second readings of Certificates of Participation financing for the Civic Campus.

sources.body: West Greeley Project Citizen Oversight Committee

greeley/1.title: 2027 city budget, reductions and museum/culture cuts
greeley/1.summary: The City Manager's recommended 2027 budget was released Sept. 4, reviewed at a Sept. 11 council retreat, and brought to first reading Oct. 20. Sales tax is down, reserves are tight, 67.75 positions were cut through voluntary separations, and departments face reduction targets. The Museum Board, Historic Preservation Commission and residents objected to museum cuts, and CPRD identified $2.9 million in reductions including UCCC fee increases.

sources.body: Union Colony Civic Center Advisory Board

greeley/2.title: GlobalAI pre-annexation agreement and interim water service for data center campus
greeley/2.summary: Global AI (Colorado) LLC bought about 438 acres near Highway 257 and Eastman Park Drive (former Kodak/Carestream campus) and is evaluating a data center campus. A pre-annexation agreement requires annexation by March 31, 2028, and the Water and Sewer Board considered an interim water service agreement tied to it, bridging the existing agreement that expires March 31, 2027.
greeley/2.where: East of State Highway 257, south of Eastman Park Drive

greeley/3.title: Flock license plate readers and police drones
greeley/3.summary: Residents urged Council to end the Flock Safety contract for automated license plate readers, citing costs, lack of a public vote, Fourth Amendment concerns and misuse. Council held a Sept. 8 work session on ALPRs and Drones as First Responder; police use 17 Flock cameras with 30-day data retention.

greeley/4.title: Great Western Industrial Park annexations and Windsor's reconsideration motion
greeley/4.summary: Council went into executive session Sept. 22 for legal advice on the Great Western Industrial Park annexations 1-15 and a Motion for Reconsideration from the Town of Windsor, and the consent agenda included a GWIP reconsideration motion.

greeley/5.title: Arroyos del Sol annexation
greeley/5.summary: Planning Commission heard annexation of about 999.72 acres northwest of Highway 257 Spur, west of WCR 19 and south of the Cache la Poudre River, with C-D conservation zoning. Much of the land is under a conservation easement, with a master plan focused on public recreation.
greeley/5.where: Northwest of State Highway 257 Spur, south of the Cache la Poudre River

greeley/6.title: Civic Campus and Judicial Center redevelopment
greeley/6.summary: Planning Commission reviewed preliminary subdivisions for the Judicial Center and the Civic Campus (4 lots) downtown, with phased redevelopment by Richmark including a temporary juror parking lot for the new City Hall. Council also considered an alley vacation near 10th Avenue and 9th-10th Streets.
greeley/6.where: Downtown Greeley, 10th Avenue to 11th Avenue, 9th to 10th Streets

greeley/7.title: MERGE highway project and transportation updates
greeley/7.summary: The MERGE project (underpasses at 35th and 47th Avenues, roundabouts, property impacts) has over $50 million in federal grants plus state funds but still needs a substantial local share. Advisory boards also discussed US 34/WCR 17 crashes, 16th Street safety, the Safe Streets for All plan and a 13th Street quiet zone with eminent domain acquisitions; the Art Commission weighed up to $400,000 for MERGE public art.

greeley/8.title: Water and sewer rates, master plans and water supply
greeley/8.summary: Staff proposed 4.5% water and 3.0% sewer rate increases for 2027, delaying the F Street Operations Facility to limit impacts. The board reviewed treatment plant and solids master plans and leases, and Council authorized legal action over the Halligan Water Supply Project Clean Water Act 401 certification. Parks cut watering at 13 sites after the Greeley-Loveland Ditch shut off early.

greeley/9.title: Housing needs assessment, Prop 123 and housing funding
greeley/9.summary: Council considered a Housing Needs Assessment contract with Interval, LLC and an affordable housing commitment under Proposition 123. The Housing for All Advisory Board reviewed CDBG and HOME funding after the first cycle, and the Housing Authority handled voucher consolidation, waiting lists and 2027 plans.

greeley/10.title: Urban renewal (GURA) and TIF
greeley/10.summary: Council and GURA discussed urban renewal law, tax increment financing, expanded board rules under HB 1348 and bonding authority. GURA reviewed its 2027 budget and projects including Mobility Hub and Western Sugar connectivity.

greeley/11.title: Historic preservation: Savig House, museum awning and Hawes Building
greeley/11.summary: Historic Preservation Commission designated the Savig House, reviewed awning rehabilitation at the Greeley History Museum (714 8th Street) and scheduled review of the Hawes Building facade at 810-12 8th Street.

green-mountain-falls/0.title: Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code ordinance (Ordinance 2026-05)
green-mountain-falls/0.summary: The town introduced Ordinance 2026-05 to adopt the state-mandated Wildfire Resiliency Code, which must be in effect by July 1, 2026. A public hearing was held April 23, the board approved it May 5 with a correction, and in August it approved changing WUI references to the Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code. A resident questioned the penalties.

green-mountain-falls/1.title: Sales tax increase ballot question for capital projects
green-mountain-falls/1.summary: Staff presented a "Closing the Gap" plan for a sales tax increase to fund sidewalks, culverts, sewage, and pool and park updates. On April 7 the mayor moved to put a 0.05% sales tax increase for four years on the ballot for the Capital Improvement Fund, and ballot and TABOR resolutions followed in May. The board called the general election in August.

green-mountain-falls/2.title: Town-owned open space: land sales, rezoning to park, and enclave annexation
green-mountain-falls/2.summary: The board has debated selling town land, including an appraisal for the El Paso trail property. A resident urged rezoning open space to park, or an ordinance giving sales the same legal requirements as parkland. In June the board sent annexation of enclaves to the Planning Commission and notified owners. Enclave annexation (Resolution 2026-15) and updating the 1997 annexation plan are on fall agendas.

green-mountain-falls/3.title: 2027 budget, fee schedule and mill levy
green-mountain-falls/3.summary: In December 2025 the council handled the 2026 fee schedule, mill levy certification and 2026 budget adoption. A 2026 fee schedule resolution was approved in May. Work on the 2027 draft budget, work sessions and the 2027 fee schedule was scheduled for fall 2026.

green-mountain-falls/4.title: Short-term rental tax and rules
green-mountain-falls/4.summary: In December 2025 the council took up Ordinance 2025-06 on a short-term rental tax and Ordinance 2025-09 amending short-term rental rules.

green-mountain-falls/5.title: Comprehensive Plan addendum and 3-mile plan update
green-mountain-falls/5.summary: The town manager is updating the 1997 3-mile plan. A 2026 Comprehensive Plan addendum was on several agendas, with a work session set for August 18 and further review scheduled in the fall. A resident urged the board to follow the plan's goals.

green-mountain-falls/6.title: Downtown parking, paving and drainage
green-mountain-falls/6.summary: The town planned a roughly $96,000 paving contract focused on parking near the Blue Moose and Lake Street, and a Maple Street parking survey. By June the new paving was complete, giving 78 downtown parking spots. Trailhead parking and 2026 drainage improvements also came up.
green-mountain-falls/6.where: Downtown, Lake Street and Maple Street

green-mountain-falls/7.title: Wastewater, septic and water rights
green-mountain-falls/7.summary: The town manager said pumping septic for the Marshal's building and park would cost about $16,000. The board tabled hiring a water attorney for water rights until creek flows are measured. A wastewater feasibility study was announced in April, and a resident thanked staff for work on a water and cesspool issue.

green-mountain-falls/8.title: Municipal election date change and planning commission role
green-mountain-falls/8.summary: Ordinance 2026-03 moved the town election from the first Tuesday of April. A resident asked that the Planning Commission be involved in more decisions, and the board considered ordinances changing Planning Commission and board responsibilities, with one tabled in March.

green-mountain-falls/9.title: Marshal's office pay and equipment
green-mountain-falls/9.summary: The board approved a budget amendment for a Marshal's office wage increase, added another speed camera near the pool park, and the town manager applied for a grant to replace a patrol car.

green-mountain-falls/10.title: Trash contract and bear reduction grant
green-mountain-falls/10.summary: The November agenda includes a trash RFP and a grant for human-bear conflict reduction.

green-mountain-falls/11.title: Pool, park restrooms and events
green-mountain-falls/11.summary: The board approved Bronc Day fee waivers, the 4th of July event with a $600 fee and Green Box pool use at $1,200. Park restrooms were due in March, the pool opening was discussed, and Lake Street bathrooms were on a September agenda.

greenwood-village/0.title: Emergency permit parking districts near Cherry Creek High School
greenwood-village/0.summary: On Aug. 3, 2026 Council passed emergency ordinances 08-26 and 09-26 expanding the permit district in Cherry Creek Village North and creating one in Village on the Lake, ahead of a student parking shortage from the Cherry Creek High School rebuild. By October police reported 88 warnings, 18 citations and permits for about 125 households, and Council held a study session on the districts Oct. 5.
greenwood-village/0.where: Cherry Creek Village North and Village on the Lake neighborhoods

greenwood-village/1.title: 2027 city budget and mill levy
greenwood-village/1.summary: Council held the first-reading hearing on the 2027 budget, Capital Improvement Program and mill levy ordinances (12-26 and 13-26) on Oct. 19, following a Sept. 28 budget workshop. An amended budget added $164,000 for a citywide access control system, and the second reading was placed on the Nov. 2 consent agenda.

greenwood-village/2.title: Grace Chapel reuse of building and parking lot at 8500 E Orchard Road
greenwood-village/2.summary: Council held a quasi-judicial hearing on a Special Use Permit and Site Development Plan to repurpose an existing building and parking lot for Grace Chapel, with 250 parking spaces proposed. Staff found all approval criteria met and the Planning and Zoning Commission recommended approval.

greenwood-village/3.title: Drone delivery regulations
greenwood-village/3.summary: Council was scheduled to discuss how to regulate commercial drone delivery on Nov. 2. Staff compared approaches of other Colorado cities, including moratoriums in Castle Rock and Parker and special use permits in Northglenn, and looked at buffers around schools and parks.

greenwood-village/4.title: Electric vehicle charging station rules
greenwood-village/4.summary: Staff presented options for adding EV charging standards to the Land Development Code, including screening of equipment, citing the lack of current code language and state law deadlines under House Bill 24-1173. A separate Planning Commission item concerned expanding EV chargers from two to four at 7600 E Orchard Road.

greenwood-village/5.title: High Line Canal irrigation phase two and park water use
greenwood-village/5.summary: Council considered a license agreement with Arapahoe County for the second phase of High Line Canal irrigation, running from Long Rd to Steele to Garden Ln to connect to well water. Councilmembers asked about switching Curtis Park, which uses Denver Water, to well water, which would need a large booster pump.

greenwood-village/6.title: Carson Park sculpture installation
greenwood-village/6.summary: Parks staff and the Arts and Humanities Council asked Council to approve fabrication and installation of three sculptures by Kevin Shaffer in Carson Park, tied to the park improvements and the City's 75th anniversary. A public input meeting was held Aug. 26, 2026.

greenwood-village/7.title: Side-yard setback variances at Monaco Heights and other homes
greenwood-village/7.summary: The Board of Adjustments and Appeals heard a variance to build a garage addition 15 feet from the side lot line in the 20-foot Monaco Heights PUD setback; staff said hardship criteria were not met. Another side-yard variance heard Sept. 24 drew an opposed neighbor, and a Radcliff Ave fence variance was approved Oct. 22.
greenwood-village/7.where: Monaco Heights PUD; 9150 E Radcliff Ave

greenwood-village/8.title: Brinkerhoff Landmark Restaurant site plan at 5390 Greenwood Plaza
greenwood-village/8.summary: Council's Sept. 14 agenda included a public hearing on the Site Development Plan for the Brinkerhoff Landmark Restaurant and a related development improvement agreement.

greenwood-village/9.title: City use of artificial intelligence
greenwood-village/9.summary: Council discussed the city's evaluation of AI for municipal operations, focusing on protecting sensitive information before any broader adoption.

gypsum/0.title: Automated license plate reader cameras and security camera program
gypsum/0.summary: A resident asked for an independent investigation into the Town's license plate reader cameras and possible legal claims. Staff gave a detailed presentation on the Town's camera technology on Sept. 8, and council held a dedicated public comment period on cameras and the Sheriff's Office contract on Sept. 22. A records request about the cameras was raised again on Oct. 13.

gypsum/1.title: Tower Center PUD amendment, Filing No. 2 final plat and improvement agreements
gypsum/1.summary: Council approved Ordinance 10 amending the Tower Center PUD guide on Aug. 11 after a public hearing. Resolution 22 on the Filing No. 2 final plat and subdivision improvement agreements was tabled, then approved Aug. 25. On Sept. 8 council approved Resolution 25 assigning the improvement agreement.

gypsum/2.title: Town lodging tax ballot question
gypsum/2.summary: Council approved Resolution 23 calling a special coordinated election on a Town lodging tax that would replace the existing county tax rather than add a new one. A resident letter asked about the ballot measure, and council discussed the ballot language.

gypsum/3.title: State collection of town sales tax (Ordinance 11)
gypsum/3.summary: Council repealed and reenacted Chapter 3.02 of the sales tax code to comply with state statutes and let the State collect the Town's sales tax. It passed first reading Aug. 11 and second reading Aug. 25 after a public hearing.

gypsum/4.title: 2027 budget, audit and financial advisor
gypsum/4.summary: Staff are developing the draft 2027 budget. Council accepted the 2025 audit presentation and approved a financial advisor contract with UMB Financial Services for up to $50,000. A resident asked that the camera issue be considered in budget talks.

gypsum/5.title: Public comment policy changes
gypsum/5.summary: After legal and historical background from the town attorney, council decided to move to a general public comment period at the start of each meeting. The mayor explained the changes on Oct. 13.

gypsum/6.title: Proposed settlement with JPJG over Siena Lake project
gypsum/6.summary: A Denver resident asked council to consider a proposed settlement between the Town and JPJG related to the Siena Lake project during public comment on Oct. 13. The documents show no decision.

gypsum/7.title: I-70 Eagle Airport Interchange grant application
gypsum/7.summary: Council authorized an application to the FHWA PROTECT competitive grant program for planning and design of the I-70 Eagle Airport Interchange project.

gypsum/8.title: Clubhouse restoration change orders
gypsum/8.summary: Council approved Change Order 2 for $241,269.06 with A.J. Construction in August and Change Order 3 in September. The project is complete apart from a final punch list.

gypsum/9.title: Fire restrictions and wildfire planning
gypsum/9.summary: Council confirmed moving from Stage 2 to Stage 1 fire restrictions on Sept. 8 and confirmed another order on Oct. 13. Eagle Valley Wildland is scheduled to give a fall update and 2027 plan on Oct. 27.

gypsum/10.title: Water system projects: Cooley Mesa generator and Mosher plant
gypsum/10.summary: Council awarded the Cooley Mesa Road pump station backup generator contract to Pinnacle Electric for $131,183.68. A lightning strike at the Mosher water plant was reported. Water use was reported down 20 percent compared to last year.
gypsum/10.where: Cooley Mesa Road pump station; Mosher water plant

gypsum/11.title: Amazon facility public improvements dedication
gypsum/11.summary: Council's Oct. 27 agenda includes Resolution 30 accepting dedication of public improvements for the Amazon facility.

gypsum/12.title: Street chipseal and recycling center contracts
gypsum/12.summary: Council approved Change Order 2 of $14,570.63 with A-1 Chipseal for the 2025/2026 street renovations. It also approved Change Orders 1-3 totaling $28,598.27 for the Gypsum Recycling Center, with Eagle County sharing the cost.

haxtun/0.title: 2026 town budget adopted
haxtun/0.summary: After a public hearing on Dec. 1, 2025 with no public comment, the Council adopted the 2026 budget and appropriation resolutions (2025-9 and 2025-10). The general property tax levy brings in $189,144, and the final property assessment set the mill levy slightly above the estimate. Staff also raised a crack-filling machine for streets and a supplemental fund tied to the generator project.

hayden/0.title: Data center moratorium study and citizen advisory committee
hayden/0.summary: Council is running a study tied to a data center moratorium. A citizen committee was to be announced shortly, and the Data Center Citizen Advisory Committee appointment was on the Nov. 5 agenda. Council also asked staff to draft letters to state and federal representatives about data center bills.

hayden/1.title: 2027-2029 draft budget, COLA and proposed 32-hour work week
hayden/1.summary: The Town Council, the Northwest Colorado GID and the Housing Authority held their budget discussions in tandem. Staff presented the draft 2027-2029 budget and asked for direction on an additional COLA increase and a proposed 32-hour work week. The property tax sheets show a general fund mill levy of 25.067 and a debt service levy of 3.990, with about $1.54 million in budgeted property tax revenue.

hayden/2.title: Council endorsements of 2026 ballot measures (fire district, schools, CMC, regional transit)
hayden/2.summary: Council considered Resolution 2026-14 endorsing ballot measures 6A (West Routt Fire mill levy override), 4B (Hayden schools joining Colorado Mountain College district), 7A (half-percent sales tax for the Yampa Valley Regional Transportation Authority) and 4A (Hayden RE-1 mill levy override). Councilmember Haight objected to the language on the transportation authority and moved to remove it. Resolution 2026-16 separately endorsed referral of Measure 7A.

hayden/3.title: Business park road to Highway 40 and new hotel lot
hayden/3.summary: The Northwest Colorado GID heard that design is starting for a new road from the business park to Highway 40. The GID is also closing on another business park lot that will be used for a hotel.

hayden/4.title: Colorado Main Street program presentation
hayden/4.summary: Council received a Main Street 101 presentation from the Colorado Main Street team on joining the program. It covers mini-grants, façade and building improvements, and a Main Street manager for downtown Hayden.

hayden/5.title: Outdoor pickleball court and 3rd Street Park
hayden/5.summary: The Parks & Recreation board discussed building an outdoor pickleball court, possibly splitting the court, with a cost near $260,000. Staff are looking for grants, and a pickleball co-op was suggested. The board also received 3rd Street Park updates at each meeting, and one project has a $5,000 grant.

hayden/6.title: Parks & Recreation board bylaws on members who move
hayden/6.summary: The board discussed amending its bylaws on members who move away during their term. The bylaw discussion was also placed on the Nov. 5 Council agenda.

hayden/7.title: Animal ordinance 752 and emergency fee schedule change
hayden/7.summary: Council held a second reading and public hearing on Ordinance 752, a new ordinance on animals within the town. No one commented. Council also considered Resolution 2026-15 adopting an emergency fee schedule change.

hayden/8.title: Routt County Hazard Mitigation Plan adoption
hayden/8.summary: Council considered Resolution 2026-17 adopting the 2026 Routt County Hazard Mitigation Plan.

hayden/9.title: Parks & Rec revenue ideas and events planning
hayden/9.summary: The Parks & Rec board reviewed ways to generate revenue and planned events, including a farmers market with pumpkins in October and vendor fees. Other items were food trucks, drink service and volunteer incentives. The board also reviewed budget work that takes effect January 2027.

hooper/0.title: 2026 budget, property tax levy and attorney contract
hooper/0.summary: At the December 3, 2025 meeting the Town held a public hearing on the 2026 budget. Trustees were also set to consider Resolutions 6, 7 and 8-2025 to adopt the budget, levy property taxes and appropriate funds. The agenda also listed an attorney contract rate increase and a legal services contract (Resolution 5-2025).

hooper/1.title: Town park safety concerns and 2026 park improvements
hooper/1.summary: Ramona Smith presented park safety concerns in December 2025. In March 2026 the Board planned to discuss a 2026 park grant led by Trustee Mimi Dolan, hiring a park and town maintenance employee, and placing a library box in the town park.

hooper/2.title: Public nuisance and ground fowl ordinances
hooper/2.summary: The March 18, 2026 agenda included Ordinance 1-2026 amending public nuisance provisions and Ordinance 2-2026 amending standards for ground fowl in the municipal code.

hooper/3.title: 2026 regular town election
hooper/3.summary: Resolution 4-2025 on the December 2025 agenda called the town's regular election.

hotchkiss/0.title: Drought restrictions, water moratorium and bulk water standpipe
hotchkiss/0.summary: In February the board passed an emergency ordinance (2026-01) pausing new out-of-town water taps and limiting sales from the town standpipe. In April and May it discussed drought restrictions, Resolution 2026-04, and raising bulk water rates to $12 per thousand gallons outside the 81419 ZIP code. Water rates and the standpipe were sent to a separate work session.

hotchkiss/1.title: Hiring a permanent Town Administrator and new Town Attorney
hotchkiss/1.summary: The board worked with KRW Associates on a search for a permanent Town Administrator, with executive sessions in May and June. Kimberly States was in the job by July, and Ordinance 2026-04 set out the office's powers. The board also sought proposals for a new town attorney and had the contract reviewed. Sarah Ross was serving as attorney by July.

hotchkiss/2.title: Proposed park on Bridge Street lots and skate park request
hotchkiss/2.summary: Don Foster proposed a park on the empty lots at 171 and 191 E Bridge Street, and the board agreed to form a working group in August. Resident Larry Wilkening opposed it and said the land should host a revenue-generating business. Tanner Wilson asked the town to consider a skate park, and the town offered a letter of support.

hotchkiss/3.title: Ordinance 2026-07 on demonstrations and special events in public rights-of-way
hotchkiss/3.summary: The board took up an ordinance setting content-neutral safety, access and permit requirements for demonstrations and special events on public rights-of-way. Residents commented, and the board approved it on August 27. In September the parade permit process had to change, and the board waived the permit for the North Fork Miners homecoming parade.

hotchkiss/4.title: Staff wage study and benefits
hotchkiss/4.summary: Graves Consulting presented a wage compensation study, with implementation proposed for June 1, 2026 and no increase to the 2026 budget. Staff also proposed more vacation time and insurance improvements costing $3,000 to $5,000. Trustee Sven Edstrom said there was too much information to decide on that night.

hotchkiss/5.title: Wildland-Urban Interface Code and wildfire planning
hotchkiss/5.summary: Ordinance 2026-03 adopting a Wildland-Urban Interface Code came to a public hearing in July, with a fire-risk map covering the whole town. The Western Slope Conservation Center presented a Wildfire Ready Action Plan in December. Staff also noted a wildfire near the town's water source could cut off supply, and talks are underway to fund a study.

hotchkiss/6.title: Variance requests: drive-thru lot and parking, sheds and fences
hotchkiss/6.summary: In November the board tabled a variance for a nonconforming lot at 6th Street for a drive-thru, sending the applicant back for a documented parking agreement with City Market. Neighbors raised parking concerns. In June it considered variances for a shed at 159 E Orchard, an 8-foot fence at 791 Barrow Mesa Road, and a 6-foot fence at 319 Knob Hill Circle Drive.
hotchkiss/6.where: 6th Street; 159 E Orchard; 791 Barrow Mesa Road; 319 Knob Hill Circle Drive

hotchkiss/7.title: Master Plan and housing
hotchkiss/7.summary: The town worked with Urban Rural Continuum on a new Master Plan, and the Planning Commission approved the final plan in April. Trustees also discussed the difficulty of finding housing in town.

hotchkiss/8.title: Sidewalk repair funding
hotchkiss/8.summary: A resident said no progress had been made on sidewalk repairs since a 2022 rating of sidewalks. He suggested a utility bill fee that would need voter approval.

hotchkiss/9.title: Police vehicles and Police Department policies
hotchkiss/9.summary: The board discussed transferring police vehicles in exchange for tuition at Technical College of the Rockies. It directed the chief to seek a contract amendment so the town avoids extra tuition costs. In September the board approved revisions to the Police Department vehicle use policy.

hotchkiss/10.title: Trustee compensation ordinance
hotchkiss/10.summary: After a work session discussion, the board passed Emergency Ordinance 2026-02 on trustee pay in March. It was set to take effect before the next election, with pay aligned with other valley towns.

hotchkiss/11.title: DMEA broadband franchise and telecom purchase
hotchkiss/11.summary: A franchise agreement with DMEA concerning broadband was planned for January. In July the board considered Ordinance 2026-05, a franchise agreement for the purchase of Delta County Tele-Com.

hudson/0.title: Prestige Builder Group settlement for Canterbury Meadows (Ravenna Street and Stow Road)
hudson/0.summary: Council held a public hearing on Resolution 26-118, settling litigation and a multi-million-dollar takings claim with Prestige Builder Group over a 32-lot development on about 94.56 acres. Neighbors raised drainage, high water table and precedent concerns and questioned why Council, not the Planning Commission, is deciding. The Planning Commission also discussed the agreement and asked for separate legal counsel.

hudson/1.title: Clinton Crossing downtown redevelopment
hudson/1.summary: Council and the Planning Commission reviewed the Clinton Crossing concept site plan, including a market hall, a residential component, parking studies and the nearby railroad tracks. Council heard about public finance tools such as TIF, new community authorities and special improvement districts. A Planning Commission concept plan hearing was set for Nov. 9.
hudson/1.where: Clinton Street and Morse Road, downtown

hudson/2.title: Low-speed vehicle rules (Ordinance 26-113)
hudson/2.summary: Council amended Chapter 478 on low-speed vehicles such as golf carts, with readings in August. Residents objected to the ban on 35 MPH roads and asked why lights are required if the vehicles cannot be operated at night.

hudson/3.title: Hudson Innovation Park and Hines Hill Road salt barn
hudson/3.summary: Staff updated Council on the Innovation Park at 996 Hines Hill Road, covering salt barn relocation, excess soil, tax abatement options and Hines Hill Road improvements. A reimbursement agreement for excess soils was on the October agenda, and the Planning Commission set a Nov. 9 site plan hearing for the salt barn.

hudson/4.title: 2027 budget, five-year capital plan and unfunded projects
hudson/4.summary: Council reviewed the 2027-2031 five-year capital plan, covering streets, stormwater, sidewalks, trails and debt service. Council also discussed which unfunded projects to fund, including Fiber-to-the-Home, stormwater and the Barlow Road sidewalk, amid income tax changes. It also accepted the county budget commission's property tax rates.

hudson/5.title: Short-term rental rules (Ordinance 26-78)
hudson/5.summary: Council has worked on amendments to Chapter 876 on short-term rentals since March. The ordinance was postponed to Nov. 10, with a new amendment from Councilor Goetz.

hudson/6.title: Utility construction rules and Velocity Broadband fiber (Ordinance 26-115)
hudson/6.summary: A proposed ordinance sets requirements for horizontal directional drilling, vacuum excavation and field checklists. Council debated its time and cost effects on the Velocity Broadband schedule. A motion to pass it without three readings failed.

hudson/7.title: Historic district reviews: 88 N. Main door appeal and Owen Brown Street townhomes
hudson/7.summary: The BZBA heard an appeal over a door installed without a permit at 88 N. Main Street, with the appellant's attorney challenging an executive session. A townhome project at Clinton and Morse, reduced from 22 to 18 units, went through historic board review and was appealed to the BZBA after a denial.
hudson/7.where: 88 N. Main Street; 86 Owen Brown Street

hudson/8.title: Brandywine Creek watershed study and stormwater projects
hudson/8.summary: Council reviewed the Brandywine Creek Watershed Study and a ranked list of capital projects. It also took up a stormwater project at Ellsworth Meadows Golf Course and pond retaining wall work.
hudson/8.where: Brandywine Creek; Ellsworth Meadows Golf Course

hudson/9.title: Maple Grove Park lease termination with Summit Metro Parks
hudson/9.summary: Council moved toward a settlement and lease termination agreement with Summit Metro Parks over Maple Grove Park. A resolution was on the Oct. 20 agenda.

hudson/10.title: Downtown Phase II property financing on Owen Brown Street
hudson/10.summary: Council considered $740,000 and $925,000 in note issues to refinance and finance former Windstream properties at 94 and 100 Owen Brown Street.

hudson/11.title: Road, rail and intersection projects: Barlow Road crossing exemption, SR 303 and Hayden Parkway, truck restrictions
hudson/11.summary: Council agreed to seek a PUCO exemption for the W. Barlow Road railroad tracks. It also considered an ordinance for the SR 303 and N. Hayden Parkway intersection, truck restrictions near SR 91 and SR 303, and annual road programs.
hudson/11.where: W. Barlow Road; SR 303 and N. Hayden Parkway

huerfano-county/0.title: GroAway LLC conditional use permit (LU-26-000154)
huerfano-county/0.summary: The Planning Commission held a hearing Sept. 10, continued it twice to Oct. 8 and Oct. 22, and weighed late public comment and a Colorado Parks and Wildlife letter. On Nov. 3 the commissioners moved to deny the conditional use permit after residents voiced concerns, including about a proposed cat sanctuary.

huerfano-county/1.title: Affordable housing, pre-approved home plans and land banking
huerfano-county/1.summary: The county worked on pre-approved house plans (tiny home, barndominium and ranch designs), Prop 123 down payment assistance, an affordable housing revolving loan fund with Impact Development, a codified Housing Authority and a land banking policy. Resolutions 26-43 to 26-45 were on the Sept. 29 agenda and a resident asked how the program and application would work.

huerfano-county/2.title: County camping ordinance (Ordinance 26-04)
huerfano-county/2.summary: Commissioners approved a county ordinance regulating camping on first reading in August, with a second reading on Sept. 1. Discussion at the first reading touched on camping rights.

huerfano-county/3.title: 2027 county budget and employee pay
huerfano-county/3.summary: Administrator Carl Young presented a preliminary 2027 budget with a 3.6% cost of living raise and market-rate adjustments for Human Services and Road and Bridge, capped at $4,000. He warned that County General needs cuts, inflation and fuel costs are straining the budget, and jail housing costs are a drain.

huerfano-county/4.title: Recreation and cultural mill levy and voter survey
huerfano-county/4.summary: Magellan Strategies presented a county voter survey that touched on parks and rec and jail renovation projects. Commissioners then approved Resolution 26-34 on a recreation and cultural mill levy, and Commissioner Wardell explained the projects it focuses on.

huerfano-county/5.title: Water augmentation lease-purchases and bulk water permits
huerfano-county/5.summary: Commissioners approved lease-purchase financing for eight acre-feet of augmentation water for the Gardner Public Improvement District and three acre-feet for Road and Bridge. Bulk water permits came up at nearly every meeting, and a Gardner sewer project bid was reviewed.

huerfano-county/6.title: Fox Theater loan guaranty in Walsenburg
huerfano-county/6.summary: The county considered guaranteeing a First Southwest Bank loan for the Fox Theater (Resolution 26-41, approved in October), tied to proceeds from tax credit sales. A second guaranty resolution (26-48) and a McKinstry change order for the Fox were also approved.

huerfano-county/7.title: Gardner Main Street and Rio Cucharas revitalization plans
huerfano-county/7.summary: The County Revitalization Authority discussed outreach to taxing entities and plan adoption. Commissioners approved the Gardner Main Street Revitalization Plan and the Rio Cucharas plan on Sept. 1.

huerfano-county/8.title: Wildfire protection plans, grants and fire restrictions
huerfano-county/8.summary: Commissioners moved the county from Stage 2 to Stage 1 fire restrictions, then lifted Stage 1. They approved the 2026 Community Wildfire Protection Plan, an amended Community Wildfire Defense Grant agreement, and letters of support for forest restoration grants including Blackhawk Ranch and the Ember Shield Coalition.

huerfano-county/9.title: Cuchara Mountain Park ski pond dam and special event liquor license
huerfano-county/9.summary: Commissioners approved a $10,600 geotechnical services agreement for the Cuchara Mountain Park ski pond dam. They accepted the Liquor License Authority's recommendation not to approve a special event liquor license for the park, and the Tourism Board noted snowmaking and pipe upgrades there.

huerfano-county/10.title: Spanish Peaks Regional Airport budget, taxiway and capital plan
huerfano-county/10.summary: The airport advisory board is working on a turnaround taxiway project, a 2027-2036 capital improvement plan, FAA-advised land acquisition, and an operating budget that is in the red. Members are frustrated with commercial tax assessments.
huerfano-county/10.where: Spanish Peaks Regional Airport, County Road 101

huerfano-county/11.title: Tourism Board marketing, 2027 budget and EV chargers
huerfano-county/11.summary: The Tourism Board manages lodging tax funds, approved a 2027 budget and paid for an Enchanted Outpost winter ad ($3,560.75). It also discussed EV charger location posters and Dark Sky efforts. Lodging tax is down about 2%, and the board appointed Meg Rutter as Director of Tourism.

huerfano-county/12.title: Marijuana license hearings
huerfano-county/12.summary: Commissioners held a public hearing on the ISO99, LLC marijuana license, where a citizen asked about water use during drought. They also acted on licenses for TKJ Investments and Focus Buds LLC.

huerfano-county/13.title: School Creek Gravel Pit conditional use permit
huerfano-county/13.summary: The Planning Commission held a long public hearing on the School Creek Gravel Pit conditional use permit (LU-26-000122) on Aug. 13. It approved a recommendation to send the application to the Board of County Commissioners.

huerfano-county/14.title: Trash and illegal dumping
huerfano-county/14.summary: The Sheriff and Administrator Carl Young discussed illegal trash dumping, what the current ordinance says and what a future ordinance could add. A resident asked whether residents could request dumpsters.

hugo/0.title: Water restrictions and water supply shortfall
hugo/0.summary: Hugo went under Level One water restrictions to stay within its water allocations after LAWMA explained the town owns only common shares. Council replaced the restrictions ordinance (Ordinance 300) and passed emergency Ordinance 302 changing watering days and hours after a resident objected to watering three days in a row. The town leased two preferred shares, and restrictions lifted October 1.

hugo/1.title: Water and sewer system improvements, loans and grants
hugo/1.summary: Hugo is financing water system work with a Colorado Water Resources and Power Development Authority loan of up to $5,395,767, plus a CDBG grant and WPCRF projects handled by GMS. Water tank repair and well pump replacements moved ahead. Sewer loans, including one up to $1,559,900 and a principal forgiveness loan, were on the November agenda.

hugo/2.title: Water and sewer rate study and 2027 fee schedule
hugo/2.summary: Colorado Rural Water Association is preparing a rate study, and the council is considering resolutions to change water, wastewater and refuse rates and the fee schedule effective January 1, 2027. A backflow prevention program review found many businesses were not inventoried.

hugo/3.title: Sales tax ballot question for pool, culture and recreation
hugo/3.summary: The town held a community meeting on a possible additional 1% sales tax for the pool, culture and recreation, and Ballot Issue #2 was on the January agenda.

hugo/4.title: Roundhouse Estates infrastructure and impact fees
hugo/4.summary: GMS was approved to study Roundhouse Estates and a tap fee study. The infrastructure was reported as improperly built, mostly sewer, roads and drainage, and a lift station was ordered. Impact fees per lot were suggested for new development.

hugo/5.title: Photo radar and automated vehicle identification
hugo/5.summary: Council approved Ordinance 296 establishing an automated vehicle identification system and an agreement with DacraTech in March. In November it was to consider repealing that resolution and approving a new DacraTech agreement.

hugo/6.title: New Hugo Fire Protection District firehouse
hugo/6.summary: Fire district representatives presented plans for a new firehouse. Council denied adding the fire department driveway to the CDOT sidewalk project, disconnected district land from town via Ordinance 301, and waived one water and one sewer tap at 5th Street and 9th Avenue.

hugo/7.title: Hugo Main Street program and Main Street Live
hugo/7.summary: The town is working toward becoming an official Colorado Main Street community, forming a board and steering committee and passing a support resolution. A geotech and survey for the Main Street Live project is underway, dependent on a Colorado Historical grant outcome.

hugo/8.title: Trash, junk and abandoned property ordinance updates
hugo/8.summary: Staff are revising the trash ordinance, reviewing tire and junk rules, and applying for a DOLA Local Planning Capacity Grant to update the abandoned and deteriorated property ordinance. Council authorized code enforcement and approved a Willdan code enforcement agreement.

hugo/9.title: Wildfire Resiliency Code (Ordinance 295)
hugo/9.summary: Council tabled Ordinance 295, which would adopt the 2025 Wildfire Resiliency Code by reference.

hugo/10.title: Affordable housing and Hugo Housing Authority
hugo/10.summary: Council adopted expedited review policies for affordable housing projects. The Housing Authority reported plumbing repair needs and compliance work, and may seek a grant partnership with the town.

hugo/11.title: Street maintenance and parks
hugo/11.summary: Council approved a pothole repair proposal and discussed pavement testing for a street maintenance plan. It also approved a playground equipment proposal from BYO Recreation and discussed safety of kids on a hard football field.

idaho-springs/0.title: Roberts Brothers Garage redevelopment and arts center fee waivers
idaho-springs/0.summary: The Clear Creek Center for Arts & Education won a $1.538 million state grant that needs a 1:1 match and has about $700,000 in hand. It asked the city for in-kind help, fee waivers and other contributions worth up to $729,307 to redevelop the Roberts Brothers Garage at 121 15th Avenue. Council took up Resolution #27 on the fee waivers, Ordinance #20 on designating the property, a parking fee-in-lieu request, and parking arrangements with Four Bairs Inc.

idaho-springs/1.title: Recreational occupation tax on outdoor recreation providers
idaho-springs/1.summary: Council referred a ballot issue to create a new occupation tax on outdoor recreation providers such as rafting companies, per Ordinance #19. The measure would allow a per-customer fee of up to $5, with revenue dedicated to the impacts of those activities on streets, parking, public safety, water and parks. Rafting businesses have made requests about the tax.

idaho-springs/2.title: Parking: private paid parking moratorium, parking study and managed parking
idaho-springs/2.summary: Council considered Ordinance #18, a temporary moratorium on permits and licenses for private paid parking facilities. The city is also reviewing parking study results and parking requirements, and a Libertarian Party representative asked that Disabled Veteran plates get free parking in the managed parking program. Council also took up library parking and renamed and rescoped the parking, transportation and mobility enterprise.

idaho-springs/3.title: 2027 city budget
idaho-springs/3.summary: The proposed 2027 budget was described as extremely difficult to prepare, with the General Fund tightly constrained. Measures included moving community promotion costs to the Parking Fund and pausing some employee benefits. The city's share of property tax is projected to fall from $282,237 to $267,546 at the same 6.310 mill levy. The Business & Community Promotions Board recommended a $211,109 baseline budget, and council also took up a fee schedule update.

idaho-springs/4.title: Affordable and senior housing efforts
idaho-springs/4.summary: Council applied to the state Division of Housing for predevelopment funding for the Idaho Springs Affordable Senior Housing Project. It also discussed affordable housing incentives, its Proposition 123 commitment for 2027-2029, and updated Chapter 21 for housing for people with disabilities under the Fair Housing Act (Ordinance #17). The Miner Street Apartments multifamily plan was also in the packet.

idaho-springs/5.title: Two-way traffic on downtown Miner Street
idaho-springs/5.summary: Council was asked to approve two-way vehicle traffic on downtown Miner Street. The street has been closed for the Miner Street Market and Halloween events, and was set to reopen to traffic November 5.

idaho-springs/6.title: 2026 Comprehensive Plan adoption
idaho-springs/6.summary: The Planning Commission held a hearing on a resolution approving the 2026 Comprehensive Plan and recommending adoption. Council then took up Resolution #31 to approve it, after a September update on next steps.

idaho-springs/7.title: Noise ordinance with decibel limits
idaho-springs/7.summary: Staff proposed adding objective decibel limits to the noise ordinance, as the code has no maximum level. The police chief wants a professional meter to enforce limits that vary by zone and time of day.

idaho-springs/8.title: Lots 1-12, Block 75 minor subdivision and new Golddigger Park
idaho-springs/8.summary: The Planning Commission held a hearing on SUBD26-002, a minor subdivision of Lots 1-12, Block 75 and vacated Sixth Avenue that creates a fourth lot. Council took up the plat approval in September. Council also took up Resolution #29 accepting Lot 3 of the former Golddigger Field subdivision as Golddigger Park, along with a park conveyance by Fieldhouse Development.

idaho-springs/9.title: Development standards, water use and public concerns at Planning Commission
idaho-springs/9.summary: Residents asked for clearer zoning rules for new developments, including buffer zones, lot lines and parking, with fines for violations. Another resident asked the city to follow residential water restrictions and use native landscaping, citing the waterfall and sprinklers on city property.

idaho-springs/10.title: I-70 Floyd Hill project and Exit 240 agreement
idaho-springs/10.summary: Council received an I-70 Floyd Hill project update. It also took up Resolution #18 on an agreement for the project near Exit 240 and a related RAISE planning grant for downtown.

idaho-springs/11.title: Ameresco facility assessment, mobility planning grant and council vacancy
idaho-springs/11.summary: Council considered a preliminary facility assessment agreement with Ameresco, and a $78,750 proposal from The Antero Group for the CAMP e-mobility planning grant. It also weighed applicants for a council vacancy and a Clear Creek Fire Authority board seat.

jefferson-county/0.title: 2027 Proposed Budget
jefferson-county/0.summary: The commissioners received the 2027 Proposed Budget presentation and budget book on October 27, 2026. Earlier, the board passed the August and September 2026 supplementary budget and appropriation resolutions and held a closed session on budget practices.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Special Meeting

jefferson-county/1.title: Proposition 123 affordable housing agreements and Jeffco housing plans
jefferson-county/1.summary: The county worked on Prop 123 unit-sharing agreements, including a JeffCo-Denver-Arvada agreement tied to a 2026 private activity bond allocation for the Belveron project. It also reviewed its 15-year affordable housing plan and a funding request for the Prop 123 expedited review incentive bonus.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions
Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions
Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions

jefferson-county/2.title: Lakewood Navigation Center operating costs agreement
jefferson-county/2.summary: The board approved an intergovernmental agreement and memorandum of understanding with Arvada, Edgewater, Golden, Lakewood, Westminster and Wheat Ridge on operating costs for the Lakewood Navigation Center. The commissioners reviewed it on September 29 and approved it on October 13, 2026.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions

jefferson-county/3.title: 143-unit planned development rezoning (Case 25-122535RZ)
jefferson-county/3.summary: The commissioners approved, by majority vote, rezoning land from Agricultural-Two and Commercial-One to Planned Development to allow up to 143 dwelling units. The Planning Commission heard it on August 12, and the Board approved it on September 1 after public testimony.

jefferson-county/4.title: Special district service plan (Case 25-124167SV)
jefferson-county/4.summary: After staff and applicant presentations and public testimony, the Board unanimously approved a resolution on a special district service plan. The hearing was continued from July 28, 2026.

jefferson-county/5.title: Preliminary and final plat (Case 24-114721PFP)
jefferson-county/5.summary: Staff pulled this plat from the hearing consent agenda at the request of the public. After testimony, the Board unanimously approved Resolution CC26-266 on September 29, 2026.

jefferson-county/6.title: Red Rocks Amphitheatre transportation hub
jefferson-county/6.summary: The Planning Commission was scheduled to consider a site approval to build a transportation hub with 397 parking spaces and roadway improvements serving Red Rocks Amphitheatre.
jefferson-county/6.where: 17355 Jurassic Road and 17900 Trading Post Rd, Golden

jefferson-county/7.title: Rocky Mountain Metropolitan Airport leases and taxiway project
jefferson-county/7.summary: The county approved a contract with Amrize West Central for the Taxiway D Phase II reconstruction. It also approved hangar ground leases (Winston Air and Premier Hangar Group) and a new airport lease agreement policy.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions
Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions

jefferson-county/8.title: Junction Urban Renewal Plan tax increment revenue sharing
jefferson-county/8.summary: The commissioners held closed-session and briefing discussions on negotiating how tax increment financing revenue would be shared under the Junction Urban Renewal Plan.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions
Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions

jefferson-county/9.title: North Table Mountain Park improvements and parks contracts
jefferson-county/9.summary: The county approved a purchase order of up to $3,224,336 with American West Construction for North Table Mountain Park improvements. It also handled the Meyer Ranch Park forestry contract, Hildebrand Ranch Park diversion work, and utility easements and agreements at several parks.
jefferson-county/9.where: North Table Mountain Park and other county open space

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions
Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions

jefferson-county/10.title: Water supply briefing and Denver Water property purchase
jefferson-county/10.summary: Commissioners received a water supply overview. The board also approved a purchase and sale agreement with Denver Water, and in August toured the Clear Creek watershed, which supplies drinking water to more than 450,000 people.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions
Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions

jefferson-county/11.title: Hazard mitigation plan, wildfire and fire codes
jefferson-county/11.summary: Commissioners were briefed on the 2026 Hazard Mitigation Plan before adoption. They also approved the 2024 fire codes adopted by the Conifer and Elk Creek fire protection districts and hosted a statewide pine beetle task force.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions

jefferson-county/12.title: Head Start program funding and expansion
jefferson-county/12.summary: The county approved Head Start policy updates and a continuation grant application. It also commented on proposed federal changes to the Head Start performance standards, and noted an expansion in Lakewood.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions
Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions

jefferson-county/13.title: County manager and county attorney employment agreements
jefferson-county/13.summary: The board appointed a county manager and approved her employment agreement. It later approved a second amendment to the county attorney's contract.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions

jefferson-county/14.title: Positions on 2026 ballot measures
jefferson-county/14.summary: The board adopted positions on ballot measures. It supported Amendment 87 (graduated income tax) and Front Range Passenger Rail Measure 7A, and opposed Amendment 84 on mail ballot voter ID.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Special Meeting

jefferson-county/15.title: 80th Avenue Church Ditch culvert replacement
jefferson-county/15.summary: The board approved a purchase order of up to $1,038,725 with American West Construction for the culvert replacement. The Vision Zero Safety Action Plan, funded through a Safe Streets and Roads for All grant, was also discussed.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions

johnstown/0.title: Permanent property tax mill levy cut of 8 mills (Ordinance 2026-299)
johnstown/0.summary: Council considered an ordinance permanently reducing the town's property tax mill levy by 8.000 mills in four annual steps of 2.000 mills. Any future increase would need new voter approval, and staff are directed to handle general fund impacts without restoring mills. It follows the FY2027 budget work, where staff recommended keeping the 23.947-mill levy because property tax revenue has declined.

johnstown/1.title: FY 2027 budget
johnstown/1.summary: Council held a preliminary FY2027 budget work session on Sept. 28, acknowledged receipt of the preliminary budget, and held a public hearing on the 2027 proposed budget on Nov. 2. A resident asked for trees at Clearview Park in the budget.

johnstown/2.title: Senior Center construction
johnstown/2.summary: Council discussed continuing the Senior Center project in August, with a resident speaking in support. On Oct. 5 it considered awarding the construction contract to Fransen Pittman Construction Co., Inc.

johnstown/3.title: Power outages and future AI centers
johnstown/3.summary: Residents raised repeated power outages in Centerra and elsewhere in Johnstown, and one asked about plans for future AI centers and what happens with them.

johnstown/4.title: I-25 East Frontage Road devolution from CDOT
johnstown/4.summary: Council held a public hearing on Ordinance 2026-297, accepting a portion of the I-25 East Frontage Road between mile markers 253.2 and 257.1 and approving an intergovernmental agreement with CDOT. It returned for further action on Sept. 9.

johnstown/5.title: Downtown Development Authority plan and DDA Fund
johnstown/5.summary: The Planning Commission reviewed the DDA Plan of Development and Council held a public hearing on it in August. Council later took up Ordinance 2026-298 establishing a DDA Fund, and a new DDA executive director was introduced.

johnstown/6.title: Water supply, rates and water projects
johnstown/6.summary: Council approved a $326,400 J-U-B Engineers contract to update the Water System Master Plan. It also dealt with the Raw Water Transmission Project, the Northern Integrated Supply Project agreement, CBT units and a Little Thompson Water District agreement. A resident raised water use at town facilities and water rates.

johnstown/7.title: State-required housing needs assessment and comprehensive plan updates
johnstown/7.summary: Under state Senate Bill 24-174, the town is drafting a Housing Needs Assessment plus Strategic Growth and Water Supply plan elements with consultant ECOnorthwest. Planning Commission review is set for Nov. 18 and Council adoption for Dec. 2, with a Housing Action Plan in mid-2027.

johnstown/8.title: New Town Attorney selection
johnstown/8.summary: Council interviewed firms for Town Attorney, including Hoffmann Parker Wilson & Carberry. On Oct. 5 it considered a legal services agreement with Wilson Williams Fellman Dittman.

johnstown/9.title: Development approvals: Whitehall rezone, Lucky Star Monopine, Diamond Ridge Metro District
johnstown/9.summary: The Planning Commission heard the Whitehall Filing No. 2 rezone and preliminary plat and a special review for a wireless tower (Lucky Star Monopine) northeast of County Road 42 and Colorado Blvd. Council took up Resolution 2026-40 on the tower and the Diamond Ridge Metropolitan District service plan.
johnstown/9.where: County Road 42 and Colorado Blvd; Whitehall; Diamond Ridge

johnstown/10.title: Property deals: Quality Liquid Feeds and Gillam Development
johnstown/10.summary: Council considered a purchase and sale agreement with Quality Liquid Feeds, Inc. (Resolution 2026-42) and another with Gillam Development Corporation, along with executive sessions on real property.

johnstown/11.title: YMCA facility management agreement and settlement
johnstown/11.summary: Council took up an amended and restated facility management agreement with the YMCA of Northern Colorado, tied to a settlement and release agreement and a reimbursement.

kersey/0.title: Property tax ballot issue 2B: ten-year extension of 17.205-mill levy
kersey/0.summary: The October 13 agenda includes an ordinance referring a ballot issue to voters and a resolution supporting Ballot Issue 2B, which would extend the Town's existing 17.205-mill property tax levy for ten years (2028 through 2037) without raising the rate. A related ordinance (2026-0012) refers a measure fixing the rate at 12.000 mills. The documents don't state outcomes.

sources.url: https://www.kerseygov.com/October 13, 2026 Regular Meeting Agenda and Packet.pdf?t=202610092015300

kersey/1.title: Water Blueprint Plan and long-term water supply
kersey/1.summary: The Board began the first of three working sessions with Brendle Group on a $50,000 Water Blueprint. Kersey isn't facing an immediate water emergency, but buy-and-dry pressure and Northern Water's native-supply requirement for new development may make its Colorado-Big Thompson water insufficient for growth. The plan is funded by a $37,500 DOLA grant, $10,000 from Northern Water and a $2,500 town match. A November work session is expected to cover it again.

sources.url: https://www.kerseygov.com/September 22, 2026 Work Session Agenda and Packet.pdf?t=202609221902470

kersey/2.title: Clark Street Storm Sewer Project contract
kersey/2.summary: The Board awarded the Clark Street Storm Sewer construction contract to Mountain Constructors, Inc., the second-lowest of 13 bidders, after staff raised concerns about the lowest bidder. The bid came in well below the engineer's estimate, and the company agreed to hold its pricing for 180 days while the Town awaits FEMA funding. Other project costs will be incurred separately.

kersey/3.title: Adopting the 2024 International Fire Code
kersey/3.summary: Ordinance 2026-0010 adopts the 2024 International Fire Code, moving the Platte Valley Fire Protection District from the 2018 code and aligning it with the Town's already adopted 2024 building codes. It had first reading August 11 and a public hearing September 8, where no public comment was recorded. The new code addresses issues like energy storage systems.

kersey/4.title: Renaming duplicate street names in Berryman Farms
kersey/4.summary: Staff asked the Board to authorize renaming streets east of 1st Street in the Berryman Farms subdivision because their names duplicate or resemble other Kersey streets, which could confuse police, fire and EMS dispatch. Staff would coordinate with residents, Weld County and emergency agencies and bring formal action back to the Board. Residents would need to update their addresses.
kersey/4.where: Berryman Farms subdivision, east of 1st Street

sources.url: https://www.kerseygov.com/08.25.2026 Work Session Agenda and Packet.pdf?t=202608211214270

kersey/5.title: 2027 budget review
kersey/5.summary: The Board has a 2027 budget introduction and review at a September 22 work session and a preliminary budget presentation on October 13.

sources.url: https://www.kerseygov.com/October 13, 2026 Regular Meeting Agenda and Packet.pdf?t=202610092015300
https://www.kerseygov.com/September 22, 2026 Work Session Agenda and Packet.pdf?t=202609221902470

kersey/6.title: Kersey holiday event changes
kersey/6.summary: Staff sought Board feedback on changes to the Kersey Holiday event, citing community feedback from the RTAP workshop that showed a high priority on it.

sources.url: https://www.kerseygov.com/08.25.2026 Work Session Agenda and Packet.pdf?t=202608211214270

kiowa/0.title: New 2026 Zoning Code replacing Chapter 16
kiowa/0.summary: The Planning Commission was asked to approve the 2026 Zoning Code Update as the town's official zoning ordinance (Resolution 2026-PC-01). On Oct. 13 the Board of Trustees holds a public hearing on Ordinance 2026-08, which would repeal and replace Chapter 16 and adopt a new zoning code.

kiowa/1.title: Proposed 2027 budget for the town and water authority
kiowa/1.summary: The Board of Trustees and the Kiowa Water and Wastewater Authority both have the proposed 2027 budget on their Oct. 13 agendas for discussion. The documents give no figures.

kiowa/2.title: Affordable housing commitment filing
kiowa/2.summary: Resolution 2026-19 would authorize the Town Administrator to file an affordable housing commitment with a state or other agency. The agenda excerpt does not name the agency.

kiowa/3.title: Floodplain permit fee
kiowa/3.summary: The Trustees have the town's floodplain permit fee, set by Resolution 2026-18, on their Oct. 13 agenda for discussion.

kiowa/4.title: Water authority contract with Gen-Tech, LLC
kiowa/4.summary: The Kiowa Water and Wastewater Authority is considering an agreement for professional services with Gen-Tech, LLC at its Oct. 13 meeting.

kiowa/5.title: Real property purchase discussions in executive session
kiowa/5.summary: The Trustees plan a closed session on Oct. 13 about the town's possible purchase or acquisition of real property, including negotiation strategy.

kit-carson-county/0.title: 2027 county budget public hearing
kit-carson-county/0.summary: The Board of County Commissioners scheduled a 1:30 PM public hearing on the 2027 draft budget on October 28, 2026. The documents do not state the outcome.

kit-carson-county/1.title: Engie Resources conceptual site plan and setback variance
kit-carson-county/1.summary: The Planning Commission's October 20 agenda included a conceptual site plan for Engie Resources and a request for a setback variance. The documents give no details on the project type or any decision.

kit-carson-county/2.title: Letter to Colorado Parks and Wildlife on prairie dogs on public lands
kit-carson-county/2.summary: The commissioners considered sending a letter to the Colorado Parks and Wildlife Commission about prairie dogs on public lands.

kit-carson-county/3.title: Landfill leachate pump bids
kit-carson-county/3.summary: The commissioners reviewed bids for a leachate pump and its installation at the county landfill.

kit-carson-county/4.title: Axon contract renewal and dispatch equipment purchases
kit-carson-county/4.summary: The commissioners met with Travis Belden on renewing the Axon contract. They also considered a $60,760.60 Russ Bassett sales agreement for console desks for dispatch.

kit-carson-county/5.title: Albertsons opioid settlement agreement
kit-carson-county/5.summary: The commissioners took up the county's agreement under the Albertsons opioid settlement on November 4, 2026.

kit-carson-county/6.title: 2027 rodeo contracts and applications
kit-carson-county/6.summary: The county considered 2027 rodeo items: two bullfighter contracts at $2,400 each, a $1,300 PRCA application and a $150 WPRA application.

kit-carson-county/7.title: Road & Bridge pickups and other 2027 purchases
kit-carson-county/7.summary: The county took bids for 2027 Road & Bridge pickups and for Clerk & Recorder office furniture. It also considered a $4,352.45/month copier and printer rental and a $23,850 Catalis subscription paid by an ERTB grant.

la-junta/0.title: 2027 city budget, mill levy and utility rates
la-junta/0.summary: Finance Director Aliza Libby presented the 2027 budget on Sept. 8, and a public budget hearing was set. On Oct. 19 council adopted Resolution R-14-2026 approving the proposed budget and passed the mill levy and annual appropriation ordinances on first reading, with second readings on the Nov. 2 agenda. The Board of Utilities was also set to consider 2027 electric, water, wastewater and sanitation rate resolutions on Oct. 13. The mayor noted that people say La Junta has the highest utility rates in Colorado.

la-junta/1.title: Residents' complaints over police handling of a assault case
la-junta/1.summary: On Oct. 19 family members spoke at council about an assault case that was reportedly dismissed without notifying the family. They described a city/county jurisdiction disconnect, unanswered requests for updates, and alleged unprofessionalism and a double standard in the police department. They also raised the mayor's endorsement of a sheriff candidate. Earlier council notes referenced transparency and accountability with the police department.

la-junta/2.title: Pueblo sewage spill and Arkansas River safety
la-junta/2.summary: Water Utilities Director Tom Seaba briefed council and the Utilities Board on a major raw sewage spill in Pueblo that reached the river. Residents were told not to use river water or untreated shallow well water for cooking or bathing. Local drinking water was stated to be safe, and reservoir releases were increased to help flush the river.

la-junta/3.title: Urban Renewal Authority grants and Chestnut Apartments
la-junta/3.summary: The URA tabled the Sangre de Cristo Community Care Spark Grant for a sign at 207 Colorado Ave. because the work was done before approval, and later said it would not be awarded. It approved a roof grant for Arkansas Valley CASA, and La Junta Associated Charities has an application on the Oct. 22 agenda. The Chestnut Apartments project is behind its 180-day contract, and the board tabled the 2027 URA budget for a work session. A resident asked whether the TIF district would expand.

la-junta/4.title: New Economic Development Board ordinance
la-junta/4.summary: Council passed an ordinance on first reading on Sept. 21 and second reading on Oct. 5 creating a city Economic Development Board. It would be an arm of the city rather than a nonprofit, partly because of an IRS issue. The clerk will call for letters of interest for board vacancies.

la-junta/5.title: Water system improvements and state loan
la-junta/5.summary: The utilities department is extending the water system on 24th Street between Carson and Belleview to improve flow and fire protection. A Nov. 2 first-reading ordinance would authorize a loan from the Colorado Water Resources and Power Development Authority for distribution system improvements. Water grant applications for new meters and storage tank rehabilitation are also underway.

la-junta/6.title: Low-speed vehicles allowed during temporary events
la-junta/6.summary: Council passed on first and second reading a temporary event ordinance allowing side-by-sides and other low-speed vehicles during events. It grew out of a tour with Main Street and Urban Renewal and the electric department, with Tarantula Fest and Early Settlers Day mentioned.

la-junta/7.title: Street flooding and drainage at Lewis Avenue and 2nd Street
la-junta/7.summary: A resident said recent rainstorms flood the road and send water into basements and businesses at Lewis Avenue and 2nd Street, where there are only two drains.

la-junta/8.title: Naming field for Jim Sullivan at Potter Park
la-junta/8.summary: Residents asked to name the field Jim Sullivan Field at Potter Park, without renaming the park, under the city's naming procedure.

la-junta/9.title: Arkansas Valley Emergency communications authority agreement
la-junta/9.summary: Council approved an intergovernmental agreement establishing the Arkansas Valley Emergency authority among area towns and agencies, tied to the phone fee used for emergency services.

la-junta/10.title: City-owned junk property cleanup under Copper Grant
la-junta/10.summary: Council discussed a resolution on a city-owned blighted property that is part of a larger brownfield-type 'Copper Grant', and asked about plans for four properties and abatement costs.

lake-city/0.title: Elk Fire local disaster emergency
lake-city/0.summary: The Town Manager declared a local disaster on August 7, 2026 due to the Elk Fire on the border of Lake City, and Council ratified it on August 12 with Resolution 2026-10. Council approved an emergency agreement with the USDA Forest Service for potable water and grey water disposal at $0.03 per gallon. Backup generators were borrowed from Estes Park and Windsor, and on October 21 Council discussed Resolution 2026-13 terminating the emergency.
lake-city/0.where: Lake City and unincorporated Hinsdale County

lake-city/1.title: Hinsdale County & Lake City Phase 1 housing plan implementation
lake-city/1.summary: Council accepted a Phase 1 Housing Plan Implementation grant agreement and sought proposals for a consultant. It first selected Collegiate Peaks Law & Mediation, but by October 21 it was discussing a notice of award to Western Space(s) LLC, and a professional services agreement with Western Spaces was on the November 4 agenda. The work supports a comprehensive county and town housing plan.

lake-city/2.title: ADU grant and pre-approved ADU plans
lake-city/2.summary: Council discussed DOLA ADU Supportive Jurisdiction certification and approved a grant application of $107,000 with a 13% match of $13,910. The money would fund pre-approved accessory dwelling unit designs and ADU financial assistance.

lake-city/3.title: 2027 budget, water and sewer rates, and capital projects
lake-city/3.summary: Council reviewed the 2027 draft budget, 2027 water and sewer rates, capital improvement projects, alternate health insurance plans versus the current CEBT plan, and limited funds for donations. The Town Manager was appointed budget officer. A 2026 audit RFP and an engagement letter with Green & Associates were also discussed.

lake-city/4.title: Armory apartment rent and applicant criteria
lake-city/4.summary: Council discussed rent, use and applicant criteria for the apartment at the Armory building on October 7 and again on October 21.

lake-city/5.title: Dark Sky Community designation
lake-city/5.summary: Council reviewed the certification requirements for becoming an International Dark Sky Community and discussed the designation application on September 16.

lake-city/6.title: Colorado Ride 2027 tent camping in Memorial Park
lake-city/6.summary: Summit Cycle Solutions asked to use Memorial Park for tent camping for about 70 participants from August 11 to 13, 2027. Council approved Resolution 2026-12 permitting it on October 7.

lake-city/7.title: Wildfire resiliency code and stormwater concerns
lake-city/7.summary: Council discussed CML and DOLA responses on adoption of the Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code and future grant funding. A resident also raised concerns about loss of containment of stormwater and its depth and velocity.

lake-city/8.title: Pickleball courts public engagement
lake-city/8.summary: Council discussed holding public engagement on pickleball courts in spring or summer 2027.

lakewood/0.title: Ballot Issue 2G: 0.5% sales tax increase for public safety
lakewood/0.summary: Council referred Ballot Issue 2G to the November 3, 2026 ballot (Resolution 2026-58, Aug. 24) and then passed a resolution of support on Oct. 12. It would raise the sales and use tax rate by one-half percent, with revenue dedicated to public safety and traffic safety improvements, including crime prevention and homelessness response.

lakewood/1.title: Automated license plate readers and proposed AVIS
lakewood/1.summary: Police presented Lakewood's use of 17 fixed Flock Safety license plate cameras, in use in various forms since 2010 and originally funded by a federal JAG grant. Council is reviewing whether more safeguards are needed and how the city's proposed Automated Vehicle Identification System relates to the existing cameras.

lakewood/2.title: Rezonings on S. Kipling, W. Mansfield and W. Duquesne
lakewood/2.summary: Council took up a series of rezoning ordinances: 2555 S. Kipling St. and 7201 W. Mansfield Ave. (first reading Oct. 26, second reading Nov. 9), and 7801 W. Duquesne and 2501 S. Kipling St. (first reading Nov. 9).
lakewood/2.where: 2555 and 2501 S. Kipling St.; 7201 W. Mansfield Ave.; 7801 W. Duquesne

lakewood/3.title: Natural Grocers headquarters public benefit agreement
lakewood/3.summary: Council considered a performance-based incentive agreement to keep Natural Grocers' national headquarters in Lakewood, tied to a building remodel, 50 new jobs and average wages at or above the Jefferson County average. The company must repay the incentive if it moves its headquarters out during the retention period. A 2023 agreement for a larger project at 12612 W. Alameda Parkway never moved forward.

lakewood/4.title: Purchase of 1081 Vance Street for open space and park
lakewood/4.summary: Council considered an ordinance authorizing the city to buy the property at 1081 Vance Street for municipal open space and park purposes. It was on first reading Sept. 28 and second reading with a public hearing Oct. 12.

lakewood/5.title: 2025 Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code adoption
lakewood/5.summary: Council adopted the 2025 Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code with local deletions and amendments, with first reading Aug. 24 and second reading with a public hearing Sept. 28.

lakewood/6.title: Revised 2026 and proposed 2027 city and LRA budgets
lakewood/6.summary: Council and the Lakewood Reinvestment Authority heard presentations of the revised 2026 and proposed 2027 budgets on Sept. 14. Staff plans to seek approval of the LRA budget at the Oct. 19 meeting. Council also approved 2027 budgets for the Alameda Corridor and West Colfax business improvement districts.

lakewood/7.title: Permanent police committee
lakewood/7.summary: Council amended its earlier resolution (R-2026-6) on establishing a permanent police committee and appointed a member to the ad-hoc committee working toward it.

lakewood/8.title: City Manager contract
lakewood/8.summary: Council had a city manager contract item on its Aug. 24 agenda. The documents give no details of terms or outcome.

lakewood/9.title: Neighborhood Participation Program and capital project funding
lakewood/9.summary: Council considered setting 2026 capital improvement project funding levels, including projects recommended under the Neighborhood Participation Program, which funds small neighborhood-proposed projects such as playgrounds, public art and community gardens. A related item concerned increasing the city's affordable housing stock by 3%.

lamar/0.title: Data center moratorium and development standards
lamar/0.summary: Council discussed data centers in September, then heard residents' concerns in October and November. It also debated a proposed 24-month moratorium so the city has time to write community benefit and responsible development standards. The mayor said no agreement or NDA has been signed and that a company contacted the city first.

lamar/1.title: Main Café brownfield cleanup
