lamar/1.summary: The city held a pre-bid walk-through for the EPA-funded cleanup and awarded Bid 46-002 for $483,299 to Rockies Environmental on Oct. 12. The contract has since been signed, and staff are starting a third assessment grant and closing out the second.

lamar/2.title: 2027 city budget adoption
lamar/2.summary: Staff began budget meetings with directors in August and held a council work session on revenue projections on Aug. 24. Council approved Ordinance No. 1290 adopting the 2027 budget on Nov. 9.

lamar/3.title: Ward I council vacancy filled
lamar/3.summary: Robert Seay was the only applicant for the vacant Ward I seat. He was interviewed in open session and appointed to serve until November 2027.

lamar/4.title: Subdivision regulations rewrite (Ordinance 1287)
lamar/4.summary: Council approved on second reading Ordinance No. 1287 amending Chapter 22, Subdivisions, of the municipal code.

lamar/5.title: Land Use Board seat and outside counsel review
lamar/5.summary: The administrator said an appointment to the Land Use Board seat will wait until outside counsel completes a document and internal review it was engaged to do.

lamar/6.title: Parks and recreation upgrades
lamar/6.summary: Escondido Field was topsoiled, reseeded and treated for weeds and fungus. Council members discussed replacing the community building carpet and looking for grants for ADA-accessible playground equipment. Kolby Brubacher was made permanent Park, Cemetery & Recreation Director.

lamar/7.title: Willow Valley water line project
lamar/7.summary: A councilmember reported the water line project should be finalized within weeks. The Street Department will then make street repairs.

lamar/8.title: Resident complaints on law enforcement response and affordable housing
lamar/8.summary: At the Nov. 9 meeting Donna Smith said law enforcement keeps refusing to respond to her calls and submitted a formal written request. Another resident asked about affordable housing.

lamar/9.title: Donated Colorado State Patrol Taser equipment
lamar/9.summary: Council accepted Taser X26P units and equipment donated by the Colorado State Patrol, worth about $50,000.

lamar/10.title: Tyler software system rollout
lamar/10.summary: The city is moving sales tax, court, utility billing, parks and recreation, accounts receivable and cemetery functions into the Tyler system. Most modules are close to done, with sales tax and cemetery still pending in November.

limon/0.title: 2026 budget, property tax levy and appropriations
limon/0.summary: Council held a budget workshop on Nov. 18, 2025, then a public hearing on Dec. 10 to adopt the 2026 budget (Resolution 25-12-20), set the property tax levy (25-12-21) and appropriate funds (Ordinance 648). A 2025 budget supplement and supplemental appropriations were heard Dec. 29.

limon/1.title: Water and sewer projects
limon/1.summary: Council received a GMS report and recommendations for water and sewer projects in April 2026, followed by project reports and discussions in August and November 2026.

limon/2.title: Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code adoption
limon/2.summary: Council held a public hearing in March 2026 on adopting the 2025 Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code (Ordinance 649). The ordinance appeared again on the April agenda.

limon/3.title: Municipal code changes on driver licensing and penalties
limon/3.summary: Council took up ordinances to enforce state vehicle rules (Ordinance 650), require a valid license or permit when driving (651), and amend municipal penalties (652).

limon/4.title: Affordable housing project review policies
limon/4.summary: In June 2026 council considered Resolution 26-06-12 establishing review policies for affordable housing projects. A Housing Authority board appointment followed in August.

limon/5.title: Limon Municipal Airport
limon/5.summary: Council considered Resolution 26-04-07 on transferring airport entitlements to Archuleta County in April 2026, and received a presentation on the airport in August.

limon/6.title: Chip sealing of city streets
limon/6.summary: Council considered a proposal from A-1 Chipseal to chip seal designated streets (Resolution 26-05-10).

limon/7.title: Tamarack Golf Club user rates
limon/7.summary: Council set user rates for Tamarack Golf Club through Resolution 26-03-06.

littleton/0.title: Temporary moratorium on data centers
littleton/0.summary: Council took up Ordinance 22-2026, which would pause acceptance, processing and approval of data center applications while staff study and recommend land use regulations. It was on first reading Oct. 20 and second reading Nov. 3.

littleton/1.title: South Platte Renew wastewater plant governance
littleton/1.summary: Council reviewed governance model options for South Platte Renew, the wastewater treatment facility Littleton owns jointly with Englewood. Resolution 81-2026 on Nov. 3 expresses support for forming a public authority to operate it and directs staff on next steps.
littleton/1.where: South Platte Renew wastewater treatment facility

littleton/2.title: Geneva Village site redevelopment
littleton/2.summary: Council discussed process options for redeveloping the Geneva Village site in August and received the Redevelopment Advisory Team's recommendation on Oct. 27.

littleton/3.title: 2027 budget and tax levies
littleton/3.summary: On first reading Nov. 3, council considered the 2027 annual budget appropriations, enterprise fund budgets and amendments to the 2026 budget. It also considered the tax levies, including one for the Downtown Development Authority. Council also approved 2027 operating plans and budgets for the Aspen Grove and Mineral Business Improvement Districts.

littleton/4.title: Utility rate study
littleton/4.summary: Council heard Part 2 of the utility rate study results on Aug. 11. The documents do not state any decisions.

littleton/5.title: Economic partnership incentives for Mineral/Scheels retail
littleton/5.summary: Council took up an amended Economic Partnership Incentives Policy (Resolution 61-2026). It also considered an amendment to the sales tax share-back agreement with RIG Mineral LLC and a new incentive agreement involving RIG Mineral and Scheels.

littleton/6.title: Safer streets: 25 mph speed limit and street safety
littleton/6.summary: Ordinance 17-2026 would set a maximum lawful speed limit of 25 mph. It was on first reading Aug. 18 and second reading Sept. 1. Council also received a Safer Streets update on Sept. 8. A Transportation Master Plan update contract was on the Oct. 20 agenda.

littleton/7.title: E-bike and e-motor safety ordinance
littleton/7.summary: Council discussed a draft ordinance on e-bike and e-motor safety on Aug. 25.

littleton/8.title: Hauler licensing, waste diversion and equal space ordinance
littleton/8.summary: Council discussed a proposal for trash hauler licensing and an equal space ordinance in August. Ordinance 19-2026, amending Title 3 and tied to the South Metro Waste Diversion Plan, went to first reading Oct. 20 and second reading Nov. 3.

littleton/9.title: Main Street sign variances at 2450 W Main Street
littleton/9.summary: The Appeals & Adjustment Commission was to hear seven variance requests for signs at 2450 W Main Street. They covered a marquee sign projecting 6 ft where 4 ft is allowed, a 30 ft clearance where 25 ft is allowed, exposed bulb lighting, and two window signs.

littleton/10.title: Historic review of facade remodel at 2589 W Main Street
littleton/10.summary: The Historical Preservation Commission held a public hearing on a certificate of appropriateness for a facade remodel of an existing restaurant at 2589 W Main Street. A second certificate (HPC Resolution 04-2026) was also on the agenda.

littleton/11.title: Bear Valley Bible Institute master plan
littleton/11.summary: The Planning Commission considered a conceptual master development plan for Bear Valley Bible Institute at 7926 S. Platte Canyon Road.

littleton/12.title: Main Street investment, Elati corridor and land use code update
littleton/12.summary: Council reviewed Main Street investment strategies and an Elati Street corridor study update. The Planning Commission previewed a Unified Land Use Code update and joint study session topics.

logan-county/0.title: Sage Pointe wastewater plant violations and rental unit costs
logan-county/0.summary: The Sage Pointe metropolitan district reported about 170 violations for discharging to groundwater, a cease-and-desist order, and a temporary rented treatment unit that began around $28,000 per month. The district is working on rates, lender and state loan hurdles, and payment plans with unpaid vendors, and commissioners asked about those unpaid costs.

logan-county/1.title: Sterling sales tax ballot question for road repair
logan-county/1.summary: The City of Sterling is asking voters to raise its sales tax from 3% to 4% for five years, with all money dedicated to city road maintenance. A similar measure failed last year. The commissioners can't spend public money on it but discussed passing a resolution encouraging a vote and asked about sewer drainage study questions.

logan-county/2.title: Prairie dog rules and Parks and Wildlife Commission petition
logan-county/2.summary: Commissioners discussed a petition before the Colorado Parks and Wildlife Commission about prairie dogs, with the topic on the November CPW agenda. Commissioners urged residents with prairie dog problems to submit written comments through Engagecpw.com. Speakers raised concerns about compensation for landowners and local voices being heard.

logan-county/3.title: Rural Health Transformation grant for EMS interfacility transports
logan-county/3.summary: Sterling Fire and county EMS leaders pursued a Rural Health Transformation Program grant contract to fund interfacility ambulance transports. The signing deadline moved to Oct 28, requiring a special meeting. Gaps in wellness funding and audit requirements were being reviewed by the county attorney and city.

logan-county/4.title: 2027 EMS and ambulance budget
logan-county/4.summary: EMS leaders sought guidance on the 2027 budget, including moving a $14,000 RETAC training grant into 2027 and a capital fund for ambulance grants. They plan to pursue a CDPHE grant with a roughly $40,000 county match on a $337,000 ambulance, and are splitting shared costs between county and city budgets. The city also wants a 3% cost-of-living raise included.

logan-county/5.title: CR 26 bridge and off-system bridge grants
logan-county/5.summary: The board decided not to pursue a bridge planning grant for the CR 26 bridge and instead keep it open, and agreed to hold a public meeting on the bridge's future. They also discussed hiring an engineer experienced with diversion structures and a narrow old bridge near Proctor/Crook.

logan-county/6.title: Underground fire water tank at County Roads 70 and 11
logan-county/6.summary: The Centennial Soil Conservation District won a $30,000 state resiliency grant to bury a 10,000-gallon fire suppression tank in the northwest part of the county, where water hauls are long. The board agreed to maintain and plow the section of County Road 11 to the site.

logan-county/7.title: Wind and battery storage projects and county comprehensive plan
logan-county/7.summary: The board reviewed a Niyol wind blade replacement requiring temporary sign removal at County Roads 67 and 24, and a right-of-way agreement with Genesis Wind. A DOLA manager noted the county comprehensive plan dates to 2013 and a possible $50,000 housing planning grant with Sterling would require a county match. Commissioners toured a battery storage facility and discussed solar regulations.

logan-county/8.title: Fairgrounds master plan and Fair Board 2027 budget
logan-county/8.summary: The fairgrounds director asked the board for direction on capital spending from last year's master plan as he prepares next year's budget. The Fair Board is also considering ticket prices and fees, gate cameras, and bids for radio, coolers, bull riding and demo derby contracts. A corrected Public Service easement for fairgrounds transformers was also handled.

logan-county/9.title: Permit Gateway online oversize and overweight permits
logan-county/9.summary: Road and Bridge staff presented Permit Gateway, a free system for the county that automates oversize and overweight transport permits and routes trucks around restricted bridges. Carriers pay a service fee, and the board indicated support for moving forward.

logan-county/10.title: County employee health insurance rates
logan-county/10.summary: The county health pool rates came in lower than expected, with the employee-only plan down $11 and the family plan down $26, and dental moved to Ameritas. Staff asked about separate family tier rates and a stipend for older employees.

logan-county/11.title: Viaero fiber optic line along Highway 14
logan-county/11.summary: Viaero Fiber Optic is installing fiber internet along Colorado Highway 14 to its Sterling store and discussed serving city and county buildings.
logan-county/11.where: Colorado Highway 14 and Main Street, Sterling

logan-county/12.title: Human Services 2027 budget, child care agreements and federal cost share
logan-county/12.summary: The Human Services Board reviewed the 2027 department budget, approved child care assistance agreements with Baca and Washington counties, and discussed a 60/40 state-county cost share tied to error-rate penalties.

lone-tree/0.title: Fidelity Office Building site improvement plan (SP26-0017)
lone-tree/0.summary: The Planning Commission held a public hearing on Oct. 27 on the Fidelity Office Building site improvement plan. The City Council opened its Nov. 3 hearing only to continue it to Nov. 17, with no discussion or testimony that night.

lone-tree/1.title: Colorado Transportation and Housing Investment Zone application
lone-tree/1.summary: Council considered an engagement letter with Beck Rivera LLP for legal and advocacy services on the city's 2027 Colorado Transportation and Housing Zone application. A program update was also on the Nov. 3 study session.

lone-tree/2.title: Hillcamp Drive/Cabela Drive extension and water booster pump station
lone-tree/2.summary: Council scheduled public hearings on the Hillcamp Trail Filing No. 1 final plat for the Hillcamp Drive/Cabela Drive extension and on the Hillcamp Water Pump Booster Station permits. Both were continued, with testimony set for the Nov. 17 hearing.

lone-tree/3.title: Southwest Village plan and parks master plan amendments
lone-tree/3.summary: The Planning Commission held a public hearing on Oct. 27 on amendments to the Southwest Village Preliminary Plan (RG26-0003) and the Southwest Village Parks Master Plan (RG26-0002).

lone-tree/4.title: Unified Development Code overview
lone-tree/4.summary: City Council had a strategy session on Oct. 26 for an overview and preliminary discussion of a Unified Development Code. No votes or public comment were taken at the session.

lone-tree/5.title: 2027 business improvement district budgets
lone-tree/5.summary: Council took up resolutions 26-47 and 26-48 approving the 2027 operating plans and budgets for the Park Meadows and Lone Tree Business Improvement Districts.
lone-tree/5.where: Park Meadows and Lone Tree business districts

lone-tree/6.title: Council strategy session on staffing, police and capital plans
lone-tree/6.summary: On Oct. 5 council discussed compensation and a five-year staffing plan, the police department, the five-year capital projects plan and community development. No votes or public comment were taken at the session.

lone-tree/7.title: Parks, Open Space and Trails Master Plan and park projects
lone-tree/7.summary: The Recreation Advisory Committee worked on the Parks, Open Space, and Trails Master Plan, the Entertainment District Park, High Note Park and the South Suburban strategic plan.

longmont/0.title: 1st and Main urban renewal plan, transit center and parking garage
longmont/0.summary: Council took up an ordinance approving the 1st and Main Urban Renewal Plan and finding the area blighted, plus lease-purchase financing for a parking garage. The Urban Renewal Authority took up tax increment revenue agreements with the city, Boulder County, Northern Water, St. Vrain Valley School District and the Downtown Development Authority. Council also considered a development agreement with Main Street Tebo, LLC for the 1st and Main Transit Center and a transit-oriented project.

sources.body: City Council Joint Meeting with Boulder County Commissioners

longmont/1.title: November 2026 ballot: public safety tax increase and charter amendments
longmont/1.summary: Council worked on ballot language for a city sales/use tax increase and property tax increases (up to 4.06, 3.25 and 2.44 mills options) for public safety, including police, dispatchers and firefighters. Charter amendments would require voter approval to sell open space, and would also cover ranked choice voting and council elections. Council also considered resolutions urging voters to vote yes on several of these measures and on a Boulder County property tax question, and called the special election.

longmont/2.title: 2027 city budget and capital improvement program
longmont/2.summary: Council received the 2027 proposed budget and the 2027-2031 Capital Improvement Program, with two public hearings and final council direction. The budget ordinance and the Downtown Development District tax levy were set for adoption in October. Other items involved the Longmont Housing Authority 2027 budget.

sources.body: Longmont Housing Authority Board of Commissioners Meeting

longmont/3.title: Annexations: Dry Creek, 8513 St. Vrain Road, Longmont Gateway Northwest, 8979 Nelson Road
longmont/3.summary: Council considered several annexation petitions: Dry Creek (Airport Road and Clover Basin Drive, zoned R-MN), 8513 St. Vrain Road (east of Airport Road, north of 9th Avenue) and Longmont Gateway Northwest (U.S. 287 and Park Ridge Avenue, with a comprehensive plan amendment). A neighborhood meeting notice also covered a 0.88-acre church property at 8979 Nelson Road.
longmont/3.where: Airport Road, St. Vrain Road, U.S. 287 and Park Ridge Ave, 8979 Nelson Road

longmont/4.title: Composting subsidy and sanitation rate structure
longmont/4.summary: Council discussed a possible subsidy for composting services and compost rate proposals, and asked the Sustainability Advisory Board for feedback on the sanitation rate structure. Staff are also looking at solid waste collection problems in alleys.

longmont/5.title: Water supply, drought and extraterritorial service
longmont/5.summary: The Water Board reviewed a one-year exchange of 148.8 acre-feet with the St. Vrain and Left Hand Water Conservancy District amid limited 2026 supplies. It also reviewed Ralph Price Reservoir water rights and conveyance plats. Council considered extraterritorial water taps for Hygiene Fire Protection District's fire house and fire suppression system, and the Water Board planned a Dry Creek Fire presentation.
longmont/5.where: Ralph Price Reservoir (Button Rock) and Hygiene

longmont/6.title: Airport future, vision and monitoring systems
longmont/6.summary: Council held an airport vision session on facilities, governance models and building trust with the community. A study session covered options to implement airport monitoring systems.

longmont/7.title: Longmont Housing Authority and affordable housing
longmont/7.summary: The Housing Authority board discussed Briarwood Apartments, resignation of the property manager at Zinnia, multifamily revenue bonds and the 2026 voucher administrative plan. Council also assigned the city's 2026 private activity bond allocation to the authority. Boards reviewed the inclusionary housing fee-in-lieu (12% affordable units or a fee) and the countywide affordable-attainable housing tax review.

sources.body: Longmont Housing Authority Board of Commissioners Meeting
City Council Joint Meeting with Boulder County Commissioners
Longmont Housing Authority Board of Commissioners
Housing and Human Service Advisory Board

longmont/8.title: Human services funding hearings
longmont/8.summary: The Housing and Human Services Advisory Board set a two-tier scoring system, with a minimum of 3.25 per question for funding consideration. It then held a series of agency funding hearings through October.

longmont/9.title: Platte River Power Authority noncarbon energy plan
longmont/9.summary: Platte River staff briefed the Sustainability Advisory Board on its noncarbon goals and the next Integrated Resource Plan, due January 2028. It cannot reach 100% noncarbon by 2030, and a federal emergency order kept Craig Unit 1 from retiring. Council also appointed Longmont's electric services director to the Platte River board.

longmont/10.title: Avis car rental at 206 S. Main Street
longmont/10.summary: Avis proposes a rental car operation at the rear of 206 S. Main, storing vehicles in the back parking area. It needs conditional use review by City Council because the site is adjacent to a greenway.

longmont/11.title: Short-term rental at 607 Emery Street
longmont/11.summary: An owner seeks conditional use to operate 607 Emery Street as an intermittent short-term rental. A rental already exists at 619 Emery, and the code allows only one per street segment without conditional use approval.

longmont/12.title: Contractor's shops in MU-E zone (citizen-initiated code change)
longmont/12.summary: A citizen request would allow contractor's shops as a permitted use in the MU-E zone. The Planning and Zoning Commission hearing could be continued to November 18, 2026, and staff are still analyzing compatibility concerns.

louisville/0.title: Inclusionary housing ordinance update (Ordinance 1936)
louisville/0.summary: Council took up Ordinance No. 1936, amending the city's inclusionary housing rules, with a second-reading public hearing on Aug 18 and another hearing on Sept 15. Strong Towns Louisville and residents wrote in, urging zoning reform first, by-right incentives and an exemption for small projects of 10 to 12 units, and warning about costs to builders.

louisville/1.title: 2027-2028 city budget, mill levy and capital plan
louisville/1.summary: Staff and council worked through a budget with an operating deficit, a General Fund gap and a six-year 2027-2032 capital plan. The City Manager's initial budget came Sept 1, a public hearing on the final budget was set for Oct 20, and adoption with the mill levy was scheduled Nov 2. The northeast water loop was pulled from the budget after rate discussions.

louisville/2.title: Sustainability funding, bag tax and climate action
louisville/2.summary: The Sustainability Advisory Board met with Council Aug 11 on funding ideas, including a possible dedicated tax or fee, expanding the bag tax, renegotiating the Xcel franchise and water conservation. Residents asked for a climate impact fee, urban heat island work and more bag tax transparency. The board is also pursuing electrification rebates and heat pumps.

louisville/3.title: Centennial Valley development plan amendment and open space/trails plan
louisville/3.summary: The Open Space Advisory Board and Parks board held hearings on a Centennial Valley General Development Plan amendment for future residential development and parks. A resident said the housing would grow Louisville's units by 12% and the parks are too small, and the open space group LOSA wrote with critiques of the draft PROS Guidebook and trails plan, including Trail 18 and City Charter references. The draft PROS Guidebook also went to Council.

louisville/4.title: Development Code update and Comprehensive Plan
louisville/4.summary: The city is moving to a development code update, with a DOLA grant accepted and a contract agreement on Council's Oct 6 agenda. Planning Commission reviewed the Comprehensive Plan on Oct 8; residents raised worries about projected growth, traffic, water, wildfire evacuation routes and community character.

louisville/5.title: Sale of city property at 1501 Empire Road and part of 1303 Empire Road
louisville/5.summary: Council considered a purchase contract to sell the industrial-zoned city property at 1501 Empire Road and the east part of 1303 Empire Road to Ripple Creek Properties LLC. Council later considered an amendment extending the buyer's examination period from 60 to 100 days.

louisville/6.title: Golf course and recreation fees for 2027
louisville/6.summary: The Recreation Advisory Board reviewed golf fee models showing green fees alone cannot close the Golf Fund shortfall, and recommended 2027 golf fees. It also backed 3% resident and 7% non-resident increases for Recreation and Senior Center admission. Fees were set in Council's Nov 2 resolution.
louisville/6.where: Coal Creek Golf Course and Recreation/Senior Center

louisville/7.title: Grain Elevator and Grain Yard revitalization grants
louisville/7.summary: The Revitalization Commission handled a Grain Elevator tax increment financing agreement and a conditional grant assignment for the elevator at 540 County Road. It also weighed Grain Yard facade and property improvement funding, with $73,467 and $87,705 left in the two programs afterward, and a $344,400 budget reallocation. Concern was raised about Front Street construction effects on Street Fair and businesses.

louisville/8.title: Business assistance agreements for Arsenal Health, Infleqtion Quantum and Louisville Cyclery
louisville/8.summary: Council considered incentives: $208,400 for Arsenal Health, an enhanced agreement up to $281,114 for Infleqtion Quantum, and an amendment to Louisville Cyclery's 2021 sales tax rebate agreement (max $58,000). Staff fixed a termination clause for consumer-use-tax rebates in the Infleqtion deal.

louisville/9.title: Historic preservation: grants, landmarks and a preservation tax
louisville/9.summary: Historic Preservation Commission handled a $15,000 Focused grant for the Mudrock House at 613 Grant Ave, a landmark request for the Methodist Church at 741 Jefferson Ave, and the Giorzelli House designation. Council also took up a 2026 election resolution on a Historic Preservation Tax, and an architect submitted ideas to broaden preservation.

louisville/10.title: Affordable housing: Centennial Drive senior housing and expedited review
louisville/10.summary: Council reviewed a concept plan for Centennial Drive affordable senior housing and a Housing Strategic Framework from Trestle Strategy Group. Resolutions would set expedited review for affordable housing projects and support a state affordable housing commitment filing.

louisville/11.title: E-bike and e-moto regulations
louisville/11.summary: Council scheduled a discussion on Oct 27 of e-bike and e-moto rules, with a police presentation on responding to concerns and future traffic safety strategies.

louisville/12.title: Utility and refuse rates and sewer backup policy
louisville/12.summary: Council considered a policy on payments for cleanup after sewer backups or water meter failures, prompted by a November 2025 backup affecting a business. It also considered new refuse, recycling and compost fees effective Sept 1 and revised 2027 utility rates, whose discussion was postponed.

louisville/13.title: Bocce courts and park improvements
louisville/13.summary: Residents asked for better maintenance and capital improvements to bocce courts at Memory Square and Community Parks, but staff said Council and staff have no interest in adding them to the capital plan. The Parks board also discussed Community Park shade structures, the Bee City program and weed management.

manzanola/0.title: 112 S. Canal brownfield cleanup and demolition
manzanola/0.summary: CDPHE awarded a Targeted Brownfields Assessment for 112 S. Canal, and the town later applied for grants. By spring 2026 the demolition was out for bid, and Earth Services & Abatement was named contractor, with the grant contract still to be awarded.

manzanola/1.title: Water plant storage study, Well #2 testing and water system mapping
manzanola/1.summary: Engineers GMS (Tom McClernan) have been working on a water plant storage study, which moved to a PER with flow and chemical tests on Well #2. The town is also considering a $15/month Diamond Maps system from Colorado Rural Water to map valves, meters and hydrants. A report noted 84% water loss in April 2026.

manzanola/2.title: MMOF/CDOT sidewalk grant of $474,041
manzanola/2.summary: The town received a $474,041 CDOT MMOF grant for sidewalks. The contract is budgeted for Colorado's 2029 budget year, and a related council resolution was held until the grant amount was known.

manzanola/3.title: Southeastern Water Conservancy District Conduit vault at water plant
manzanola/3.summary: The council asked Congress for support of the Conduit and heard from SECWCD's Hunter Willits on placing a conduit vault at the water plant, for Valley water. It remained on agendas through October 2026.

manzanola/4.title: Drought water restrictions and project water release
manzanola/4.summary: The council took up Resolution 2026-02 on drought water restrictions in April 2026. In July it discussed a 100 acre-foot project water release on 6/30/2026.

manzanola/5.title: Second Street repair and chip seal
manzanola/5.summary: Otero County was to repair Second Street for about $1,000 in mid-2026. A chip and seal of the street is planned for 2027 at about $10,000.

manzanola/6.title: Solar tax credit refund
manzanola/6.summary: The IRS sent a November 3 letter saying a tax credit refund is coming on the town's solar project.

manzanola/7.title: Federal procurement and grant compliance policies
manzanola/7.summary: In March 2026 the council took up a package of procurement policies, including 2 CFR 200 compliance and requirements for federally funded projects.

manzanola/8.title: Budget approval and insurance renewal
manzanola/8.summary: The council approved the budget and its resolutions in December 2025. It also considered the Gallagher insurance renewal at $36,216.

manzanola/9.title: Weed and tree removal ordinance, senior housing parking lot, and surplus vehicles
manzanola/9.summary: The council considered Ordinance 2026-05 on emergent weed and tree removal. It also discussed paving the Park Street Senior Housing parking lot and whether to sell or scrap a 2012 Dodge police car and a jetter truck.
manzanola/9.where: Park Street Senior Housing and Townwide

manzanola/10.title: Charter franchise agreement
manzanola/10.summary: A Charter franchise agreement was on the February 2026 agenda.

mead/0.title: New Mead Police Facility: site plan, financing and groundbreaking
mead/0.summary: The town is building a 19,000 sq ft police facility at the Municipal campus in Liberty Ranch on Chaparral Street. The Urban Renewal Authority heard a DOLA grant presentation and financing options from Piper Sandler and reviewed a cooperation agreement with the Town. The Board approved the site plan by Ordinance 1118, held a special meeting on Oct. 29 on construction and funding, and a groundbreaking was scheduled for Oct. 19.

mead/1.title: Twelve-month moratorium on data centers
mead/1.summary: The Town Board adopted a twelve-month moratorium on data centers at its Aug. 31 meeting. Planning staff said the town has not yet received any data center proposals.

mead/2.title: 2027 town budget and GID budgets
mead/2.summary: The 2027 proposed budget was presented on Sept. 28, with questions taken on Oct. 12 and a public hearing and adoption resolution on Oct. 26. The Urban Renewal Authority and the Highway 66/I-25 and Elevation 25 General Improvement Districts also held 2027 budget presentations and hearings that set mill levies. The Board also amended the 2026 Municipal Facilities Impact Fee Fund budget.

mead/3.title: Reconsideration of Ordinance 1121 (Public Facilities zoning) and possible CUP
mead/3.summary: The Board approved a zoning map amendment placing Public Facilities (PF) zoning on certain town-owned properties, including the Valdez annexation property, after Planning Commission review. A special meeting on Oct. 29 listed options to reconsider Ordinance 1121 or pursue a conditional use permit application.

mead/4.title: Waterfront Filing No. 2 preliminary plat
mead/4.summary: The Planning Commission recommended conditional approval of the Waterfront Filing No. 2 preliminary plat for a mixed-use development. Commissioners focused on traffic capacity, road improvements and trail connections, and called for broader coordination of transportation improvements among nearby developments.

mead/5.title: Ariet's Grove Filing No. 1 preliminary plat
mead/5.summary: The Planning Commission reviewed the Ariet's Grove Filing No. 1 preliminary plat and recommended conditional approval. The Board of Trustees held a public hearing on conditional approval on Oct. 26.

mead/6.title: 1785 Weld County Road 32 annexation and Valdez annexation zoning
mead/6.summary: The Planning Commission recommended approval of initial zoning for the 1785 Weld County Road 32 annexation and for the town-owned Valdez annexation property, which gets Public Facilities zoning.

mead/7.title: Urban Renewal Authority tax increment incentive policy
mead/7.summary: Counsel proposed a formal policy for evaluating requests for tax increment financing reimbursement of public improvements, with eligibility thresholds, three evaluation criteria and a small project track. A resolution approving the policy was on the Oct. 26 consent agenda.

mead/8.title: I-25 sewer relocation and wastewater projects
mead/8.summary: The Board awarded the bid to SMH West LLC for the I-25 Sewer Relocation Project and approved a common use agreement with CDOT. It also approved contracts for sewer and culvert cleaning, headworks rehabilitation at the wastewater plant, and on-call engineering.

mead/9.title: United Power electricity franchise agreement
mead/9.summary: The Board extended the letter agreement with United Power month-to-month through Jan. 31, 2027, and Ordinance 1122 granting a new franchise to use town rights-of-way was on the Nov. 9 agenda.

mead/10.title: High Plains Boulevard and Safe Routes to School
mead/10.summary: Construction of two miles of High Plains Boulevard between WCR 32 and WCR 36, with two roundabouts, bike lanes and a detached sidewalk, is nearly complete, with a celebration planned. The Board also awarded a Safe Routes to School contract to Colorado Paving.
mead/10.where: High Plains Blvd, WCR 32 to WCR 36

mead/11.title: New Mead Library
mead/11.summary: The Board granted conditional acceptance of public improvements for the High Plains Library District Mead Library, and a community opening event was scheduled for Oct. 3.

meeker/0.title: Short-term rental conditional use permit for Chase Rule
meeker/0.summary: The City Council held a public hearing on Feb. 23, 2026 on a conditional use permit for Chase Rule to operate a short-term rental. The agenda excerpt does not give the full address or the outcome.

meeker/1.title: Setback variance requests (891 3rd Street and 325 Curtis Creek Drive)
meeker/1.summary: On Feb. 23, 2026 the Council heard two variance requests. The Dawsons asked for a side yard setback of about 6 feet at 891 3rd Street. Renninger Investments, LLC asked for a 0-foot front yard setback at 325 Curtis Creek Drive. The outcomes are not in the documents.

meeker/2.title: Variance for Training Grounds, LLC at 390 Market Street
meeker/2.summary: The Council scheduled a July 13, 2026 public hearing on a request for a reduced side yard setback at 390 Market Street. The documents do not state the outcome.

meeker/3.title: Home occupation and right-of-way encroachment requests
meeker/3.summary: The July 13, 2026 agenda included a conditional use request from Tevin Pelloni for a home occupation at 440 Garfield Street. It also included an encroachment request from Rebekah and Justin Grant to access the town right-of-way at Sanderson Hills Subdivision.

meeker/4.title: Oversized sign and 8-foot fence variances
meeker/4.summary: The Aug. 3, 2026 hearings covered two variance requests. David Bradfield asked for a sign larger than the maximum at 43904 Highway 13. Jessica and Matt Franks asked to build an eight-foot fence at 172 Water Street.

meeker/5.title: Fairfield Apartments update and mayor appointment process
meeker/5.summary: The Nov. 3, 2026 agenda includes an update from Commissioner Scritchfield on the Fairfield Apartments. It also includes a resolution setting the process for appointing a mayor.

mesa-county/0.title: Temporary moratorium on data center applications
mesa-county/0.summary: On Sept. 29 the commissioners were set to consider a temporary moratorium on accepting, processing and approving land use applications for data center facilities in unincorporated Mesa County. It would also suspend negotiation of county inducements for such facilities.

mesa-county/1.title: 32 1/2 Road Phase II roadway improvement project
mesa-county/1.summary: The county moved to award a $4,606,193.95 contract to Mountain Valley Contracting for the project. Related agreements include a stormwater detention facility with Housing Resources of Western Colorado, an MOU with Clifton Water District, and a property purchase for right-of-way.

mesa-county/2.title: Grand Junction Regional Airport FAA grants and runway replacement
mesa-county/2.summary: The county accepted and ratified several FAA Airport Improvement Program grants as co-sponsor with the Airport Authority. They include $13,265,445 for the runway replacement transition and taxiway conversion, plus terminal improvements.

mesa-county/3.title: Flock license plate camera presentation
mesa-county/3.summary: The Sheriff's Office gave the commissioners a presentation on Flock cameras on Aug. 18.

mesa-county/4.title: 2027 county budget and supplemental budget
mesa-county/4.summary: Staff briefed the commissioners on the proposed 2027 budget for the county and its improvement and pest districts. A supplemental budget resolution was also considered in September and again in November.

mesa-county/5.title: Board of Public Health budget and legal counsel
mesa-county/5.summary: The Board of Public Health took up its 2027 budget and held special meetings on hiring legal counsel. It also discussed an intergovernmental agreement with Mesa County and considered engaging conflict counsel.

sources.body: Board of Public Health Work Session
Board of Public Health Special Meeting

mesa-county/6.title: Appeal of short-term rental approval at 123 Mesa Vista Road
mesa-county/6.summary: Commissioners heard an appeal by Parentice of the administrative approval of a residential planning clearance for a short-term rental at 123 Mesa Vista Road, owned by Passion Project, LLC.

sources.body: Board of Commissioners Land Use Hearing

mesa-county/7.title: Land use rezones and plan changes
mesa-county/7.summary: Commissioners considered the Serrano Estates rezone of a 4.1-acre parcel at 825 26 Road and the Bailey rezone of 7 acres at 1083 20 Road. They also heard an Experius Community PUD amendment seeking a five-year extension to 2031, an easement vacation at 223 Elberta Drive, and the Smith vacation of Loma rights-of-way.

sources.body: Board of Commissioners Land Use Hearing
Board of Commissioners Land Use Hearing
Board of Commissioners Land Use Hearing

mesa-county/8.title: North Avenue Enhanced Transit Corridor funding
mesa-county/8.summary: The county considered an agreement of up to $1.25 million with the City of Grand Junction for improvements consistent with the North Avenue Enhanced Transit Corridor plan.

mesa-county/9.title: Justice Center rooftop unit replacement and north addition
mesa-county/9.summary: The county considered a $2,223,684 contract with Comfort Air for replacing rooftop HVAC units at the Justice Center. A $15,000 change order for design of the Justice Center North Addition was also on the agenda.

mesa-county/10.title: Stormwater Management Manual update
mesa-county/10.summary: The county considered change orders with Wright Water Engineers, including $87,214 and a second one for cost-impact analysis, outreach, training and technical updates to the manual.

mesa-county/11.title: Wildfire mitigation and trails grant applications
mesa-county/11.summary: The county considered an $840,000 Forest Restoration and Wildfire Risk Mitigation grant application for the Mesa Creek Cross-Boundary project and a Colorado Parks and Wildlife Trails Stewardship grant application. It also considered letters supporting federal forest health and water bills.

milliken/0.title: Water bills, new smart meters and rate increases
milliken/0.summary: Residents complained at several meetings about high water bills, a roughly 30-35% rate increase, tiered rates, and the new Metron smart meters (about $1.25 million project). Some questioned the meter bid and asked for records via CORA requests. Staff said 2027 rates come from a five-year cost-of-service study and are usually adopted in December.

milliken/1.title: Proposed paving of County Road 44 in 2027 budget
milliken/1.summary: Residents along CR 44 near Meadow Farms spoke for and against paving, with some asking that it be removed from the 2027 budget over cost, traffic and speed concerns, and another describing severe road deterioration east of WCR 19. A Meadow Farms IGA and service plan were cited as relevant to paving responsibility.

milliken/2.title: 2027 town budget retreats and hearings
milliken/2.summary: The Board held budget retreat work sessions and continued discussions of the proposed 2027 budget in August through October. The first public budget hearing was set for October 14, with final adoption at the November public hearing.

milliken/3.title: Town Hall rental program fees and hybrid model
milliken/3.summary: After the August 12 discussion, staff proposed a hybrid model with higher hourly rental rates. It keeps tiers with reduced rates for residents and nonprofits, higher rates for non-residents, and clearer rental agreement rules, to recover costs of staffing and utilities.

milliken/4.title: New Town Administrator Greg Brinck
milliken/4.summary: The Board approved an employment agreement offering the Town Administrator job to Greg Brinck, and a resolution appointing him was on the September 9 agenda. He later gave the Board updates as Town Administrator.

milliken/5.title: Strategic Growth Plan / Strategic Growth Element
milliken/5.summary: The Board discussed a draft Strategic Growth Element of the comprehensive plan covering growth policies, infill and redevelopment, and greenfield development, considering water availability and infrastructure. Staff also began a Water Supply Element update to the Comprehensive Plan.

milliken/6.title: Sunfield Filing 3 preliminary plat
milliken/6.summary: The Planning Commission held a public hearing on the Sunfield Filing 3 preliminary plat on November 4, and the Board of Trustees scheduled a public hearing on it November 9.

milliken/7.title: Milliken Store-N-Go self-storage permit
milliken/7.summary: The Planning Commission recommended approval of a conditional use permit for a fully enclosed self-storage facility in the C-4 zone, with seven buildings totaling over 52,000 sq ft, no outdoor storage, and surveillance. Any highway access improvements would require CDOT approval.

milliken/8.title: Milliken Sidewalk and ADA Project contract
milliken/8.summary: Staff asked the Board to award a $1,018,200 construction contract (total not to exceed $1,170,930) to Gold Star Concrete. The grant-funded project has a funding shortfall, and the Board discussed scope cuts, delays and cost-sharing with the school district.

milliken/9.title: Town-wide rate and fee study with Willdan
milliken/9.summary: The Board was asked to approve a professional services agreement with Willdan Financial Services for a town-wide rate and fee study.

milliken/10.title: Milliken Housing Authority budget and Dove Valley property
milliken/10.summary: The Housing Authority drafted and approved its 2027 budget, questioned Dove Valley operating costs and a water bill with possible sprinkler damage, and worked on a strategic plan and Prop 123 meetings. It planned a November presentation to the Board of Trustees.

milliken/11.title: Food Truck Park and student home construction partnership
milliken/11.summary: The Board scheduled discussions on a food truck park and on a student home construction partnership at 1398 Irene.

milliken/12.title: Highway 257 noise complaint
milliken/12.summary: The Board discussed and gave direction on a noise complaint about Highway 257.

milliken/13.title: Social media and communications policy
milliken/13.summary: The Board discussed updating the town social media and communications policy across several meetings.

minturn/0.title: Police services contract with Eagle County Sheriff's Office
minturn/0.summary: Council appointed an ad-hoc committee to negotiate a Sheriff's Office police services contract starting in 2027, covering service levels, costs, terms and community concerns about automated license plate readers. The proposed terms will return to the full Council; the contract was on the Oct. 21 and Nov. 4 agendas.

minturn/1.title: Minturn shooting range grant and Forest Service permit
minturn/1.summary: Minturn won a $225,000 Colorado Parks and Wildlife grant to improve the town shooting range and address long-standing issues. The town is seeking in-kind help from Eagle County, such as road grading, and aims to have a USFS special use permit by spring 2027. A status update was on the Oct. 21 agenda, and a councilmember asked to continue the related item on Oct. 7.

minturn/2.title: Speed bumps and traffic calming, Main Street speed camera study
minturn/2.summary: Residents in the Boulder and Pine Street area asked for more speed bumps and tables, and at the Oct. 7 meeting a resident raised a 2023 petition and speed concerns. Staff is studying a Main Street speed camera and evaluating FY 2027 funding for speed bumps and radar feedback signs.
minturn/2.where: Main Street; Boulder and Pine Street area

minturn/3.title: FY 2027 town budget
minturn/3.summary: The FY 2027 budget was the subject of a public hearing on Nov. 4. Items in line for consideration include traffic calming, Beach Park retaining wall work and other capital projects.

minturn/4.title: Water moratorium ordinance, water tank design and downtown water funds
minturn/4.summary: Council considered on second reading Ordinance No. 11 amending the water moratorium, and Resolution No. 50 to repurpose CDS funds for downtown water improvements. An update from S.E.H. on water tank evaluations and design progress on Bellm Bridge was scheduled for Nov. 4.

minturn/5.title: Electric outages and Xcel Energy reliability
minturn/5.summary: Town staff met with the Colorado Energy Office and Xcel Energy about outages and reliability. At Xcel's recommendation the town sent formal correspondence requesting improvements and is monitoring Xcel's response and timelines.

minturn/6.title: ERWSD Main Street siphon rehabilitation
minturn/6.summary: Eagle River Water & Sanitation District's siphon rehabilitation is underway, with sewer bypass pumping expected to begin by Aug. 14. Traffic control remains in place on US 24/Main Street during construction.

minturn/7.title: Historic Preservation Plan update
minturn/7.summary: The Historic Preservation Commission worked on the final 2026 Historic Preservation Plan, with amendments to goals on objects and cultural resources. Members discussed asking Council about a historic district and a budget line item, and elected Ken Halliday chair and Dan Brown vice chair. The Meyer's Barn project was also updated.

minturn/8.title: Joint meeting with Eagle County on housing and e-bikes
minturn/8.summary: At a joint meeting, Minturn and the County discussed a Regional Housing Authority, with concerns about unoccupied homes, business costs and employee housing, and the need for a clear plan after past ballot measures. They also discussed e-bike rules, confusion over e-bike classes and youth riders.

minturn/9.title: Land development code definitions and Bolts Lake zoning
minturn/9.summary: The Planning Commission reviewed new definitions for the land use code, including pervious surfaces, bulk plane and affordable housing terms. Staff explained the settlement agreement and the use table for the Bolts Lake zone districts.

minturn/10.title: Silver Star Trail changes to approved plans
minturn/10.summary: Requests to change approved plans at 0024 and 0018 Silver Star Trail went to the Planning Commission on Oct. 14 and Council on Oct. 21. The 0018 item was continued to Nov. 4.

minturn/11.title: DDA investment and incentive policy
minturn/11.summary: The Downtown Development Authority board considered Resolution No. 02 adopting an Investment and Incentive Policy. It covers a small project matching grant program, large redevelopment projects and strategic property acquisition.

minturn/12.title: Highlands parcels listing strategy and conservation options
minturn/12.summary: Council planned a discussion on a strategy for listing the Highlands parcels and conservation options, with negotiations possibly handled privately.

moffat-county/0.title: Data center moratorium and regulations
moffat-county/0.summary: Residents, Yampa Valley Electric and Pure-Green Colorado spoke on a possible data center moratorium (Resolution 2026-103) tied to the Trapper Reborn project. The Planning & Zoning Commission took up rule-making and held public and expert panel meetings in early October. On Oct 13 the commissioners called for a motion to adopt the moratorium, got no response, and the motion died.

moffat-county/1.title: Term limits referendum on the November ballot
moffat-county/1.summary: Commissioners approved Resolution 2026-100 for a referendum on term limits and an intergovernmental agreement with the Clerk's Office to place it on the November ballot. Both passed 3-0.

moffat-county/2.title: Proposed 2027 county budget hearing
moffat-county/2.summary: A public hearing was held on Oct 13 to present the proposed 2027 county budget for adoption. The documents shown do not state the outcome.

moffat-county/3.title: Loudy-Simpson Park Master Plan
moffat-county/3.summary: Staff presented a proposal from Logan Simpson to develop a master plan for Loudy-Simpson Park. The related contract was on the Sept 22 consent agenda.

moffat-county/4.title: Craig skatepark funding and design
moffat-county/4.summary: The Craig Skatepark Alliance and county staff won approval to apply for $25,000 grants each from the Laura Jane Musser Fund and El Pomar Foundation. The group plans a GOCO application in January. A services agreement with Grindline Skateparks was approved Oct 13.

moffat-county/5.title: Echo Park Road (CR 156) closure
moffat-county/5.summary: Commissioners approved Resolution 2026-120 temporarily closing County Road 156 in Dinosaur National Monument because flash-flood erosion made it unsafe. The Park Service must investigate archaeological concerns before repairs.
moffat-county/5.where: County Road 156 (Echo Park Road), Dinosaur National Monument

moffat-county/6.title: Road and Bridge snow bank payment policy
moffat-county/6.summary: Road and Bridge employee George Miner asked commissioners to examine inconsistencies in the snow bank payment policy and followed up on Sept 8 on his earlier request.

moffat-county/7.title: Employee Health Insurance Advisory Board reinstated
moffat-county/7.summary: Commissioners were asked to reinstate the Employee Health Insurance Advisory Board and appointed five employee-elected members to recommend plan improvements. On Oct 13 they also named Mountain West Insurance, a local firm, as agent of record.

moffat-county/8.title: Contract monitoring policy
moffat-county/8.summary: Commissioners adopted Resolution 2026-111, setting a standard for monitoring contracts, grants, subawards and intergovernmental agreements.

moffat-county/9.title: Welba Peak mineral lease and Browns Park property sale
moffat-county/9.summary: Commissioners approved Resolution 2026-96, the Welba Peak mineral lease. On Oct 13 they amended Resolution 2026-39 on the sale of county real property to the Browns Park Alumni.

montrose-county/0.title: Non-native wildlife ordinance and CPW lead ammo and prairie dog resolutions
montrose-county/0.summary: On Oct. 28 commissioners were set to hold a public hearing on proposed Ordinance 2026-01, which would prohibit intentionally introducing or releasing non-native wildlife in unincorporated Montrose County. They also were to consider resolutions opposing a citizen petition to ban lead ammunition for hunting and opposing proposed Colorado Parks and Wildlife prairie dog rule changes, to be sent to CPW as county comment. Proposed CPW changes were also a work session topic on Oct. 26.

sources.body: Special Meeting - Board of County Commissioners - NO VIDEO RECORDING

montrose-county/1.title: 2027 proposed county budget
montrose-county/1.summary: The 2027 proposed budget was presented to the commissioners at a public hearing at a special meeting on Oct. 14, 2026. A budget packet and presentation were posted.

sources.body: Special Meeting - Board of County Commissioners

montrose-county/2.title: Emergency $75,000 for West End Family Link
montrose-county/2.summary: At a special meeting in Nucla on Sept. 17, the commissioners heard a presentation and public comment on an emergency funding request from West End Family Link. Commissioner Pond moved to fund it at $75,000.

sources.body: Special Meeting - Board of County Commissioners - NO VIDEO RECORDING

montrose-county/3.title: Gold Mountain Fire FEMA support and Wildfire Resiliency Code
montrose-county/3.summary: The commissioners ratified a letter asking for federal FEMA support after the 2026 Gold Mountain Fire. They also approved an agreement with Norwood Fire Protection District to share administration and enforcement of the county's Wildfire Resiliency Code.

sources.body: Regular Meeting - Board of County Commissioners

montrose-county/4.title: Housing needs assessment grant and private activity bonds
montrose-county/4.summary: Planning staff discussed a grant application for a housing needs assessment tied to state law SB24-174. The commissioners also assigned $1,573,936 of the county's 2026 private activity bond allocation to the Colorado Housing and Finance Authority.

sources.body: Regular Meeting - Board of County Commissioners - NO VIDEO RECORDING

montrose-county/5.title: Iron Will Dog Lodge special use permit and subdivision plats
montrose-county/5.summary: Commissioners were to consider a resolution on the Iron Will Dog Lodge special use permit (SU26-002) with a related waiver request. Earlier they took up the Coal Creek Estates III preliminary plat and a Sunshine Road minor subdivision item.

sources.body: Regular Meeting - Board of County Commissioners
Regular Meeting - Board of County Commissioners

montrose-county/6.title: County road maintenance, Kinikin Road and road education
montrose-county/6.summary: Work sessions covered Kinikin Road updates and county road education. The commissioners were also to accept county maintenance of 5465 Court and of 6785 Lane and Uriah Court in Thornburgh Estates. A bridge rail replacement contract of $487,333 and an Olathe asphalt overlay agreement were also on the agendas.

sources.body: Regular Meeting - Board of County Commissioners
Regular Meeting - Board of County Commissioners
Regular Meeting - Board of County Commissioners

montrose-county/7.title: Montrose Regional Airport projects and permits
montrose-county/7.summary: Airport items included an apron and taxilane reconstruction geotechnical amendment, a law enforcement reimbursement of $54,750, and a baggage claim delivery permit for Lonely Luggage replacing Love's Delivery. The commissioners also took up bus and hotel courtesy vehicle agreements.

sources.body: Regular Meeting - Board of County Commissioners
Regular Meeting - Board of County Commissioners
Regular Meeting - Board of County Commissioners
Regular Meeting - Board of County Commissioners - NO VIDEO RECORDING

montrose-county/8.title: Safe sleep incentive program and Headwaters to Home
montrose-county/8.summary: A work session on Oct. 5 covered a Rocky Mountain Health Plans safe sleep incentive program services agreement and the Headwaters to Home program.

montrose-county/9.title: Montrose and Ouray county line discussion
montrose-county/9.summary: Commissioners put a Montrose and Ouray county line discussion on the Oct. 26 work session agenda. The documents give no details.

montrose/0.title: Charter amendments for the November ballot (Ordinances 2727-2730)
montrose/0.summary: Council took up four proposed charter amendments: moving municipal elections to November (2727), an 8-year lifetime term limit for the at-large seat (2728), and council approval over hiring and firing the police chief (2729) and city clerk (2730). Residents spoke both for and against, and Ordinances 2727 and 2728 were heard on second reading Sept. 1.

montrose/1.title: City manager separation and interim manager
montrose/1.summary: After closed-door sessions about a confidential memo and possible independent counsel, Council approved a mutual separation agreement with City Manager Bill Bell. It then appointed Ann Morgenthaler as interim city manager and Montrose Urban Renewal Authority executive director, and ratified those decisions on Sept. 15 to cure notice problems. The interim agreement is open-ended during recruitment of a new manager.

montrose/2.title: Council vacancies: District IV and At-Large seats
montrose/2.summary: The District IV seat was vacated Sept. 7, and the charter requires an appointment within 30 days. Council agreed to appoint Adam Woodden to District IV, which opened the At-Large seat, with applications due Oct. 21. John Brown, Danielle Godt and Cindee Williams were slated for the At-Large appointment on Nov. 2.

montrose/3.title: Call for a data center moratorium
montrose/3.summary: A resident asked Council to enact a moratorium on new data centers until regulations are in place. The documents show no Council action on the request.

montrose/4.title: Locust Road annexation and R-2 zoning
montrose/4.summary: The Planning Commission recommended R-2 Low Density zoning for the Locust Road Addition at 1815 Locust Road and discussed pedestrian improvements and rebuilding Locust Road. Council considered Ordinance 2731 annexing the 4.2 acres on second reading Oct. 6.

montrose/5.title: New subdivisions and annexations before Planning Commission
montrose/5.summary: The commission reviewed several projects: Star Court Lot 8 townhomes (739-749 East Star Court), Chelsi Lane amended PD plan (24 units reduced to 23), Spruce Point amended preliminary plat, Chipeta Lake 2 annexation zoning (1.14 acres, "P" Public), and the El Chapin sketch plan for 45 lots on 6600 Road. One resident spoke on Spruce Point boundaries.
montrose/5.where: East Star Court, Chelsi Lane, Sanctuary Drive, Chipeta Road, 6600 Road

montrose/6.title: Comprehensive plan update and state growth mandates
montrose/6.summary: Staff and consultants are doing a five-year update of the Envision 2040 plan, adding state-required housing needs assessment, housing action plan, water supply and growth elements. The goal is approval by year end. Residents asked that growth pay its own way and that plan standards be upheld.

montrose/7.title: Affordable housing commitment and homeless shelter funding
montrose/7.summary: Council considered a Proposition 123 affordable housing commitment; the city approved 221 units against a requirement of 162. It also weighed $28,597 in lodging-tax funds for startup costs of The Shepherd's Hand seasonal homeless shelter.

montrose/8.title: Rotary Park pump house replacement
montrose/8.summary: Council considered a $514,011 contract with FCI Constructors to replace the 1980s irrigation pump house. This is $14,011 above the $500,000 budget, to be covered by other Public Works savings.

montrose/9.title: Student parking and speed sign requests
montrose/9.summary: Residents asked for permit-only parking on streets near the high school and more police presence. Others asked for an electronic speed sign on Miami Road near Cedar Creek.
montrose/9.where: Streets near the high school; Miami Road at Cedar Creek

montrose/10.title: 2027 fee schedule and landfill agreement extension
montrose/10.summary: Council's Nov. 2 agenda included Resolution 2026-18 adopting the 2027 fee schedule and a one-year extension of the landfill agreement with Bruin Waste Management.

montrose/11.title: Montrose Post Office alteration hearing
montrose/11.summary: The Historic Preservation Commission held a hearing on an application to alter the designated Montrose Post Office.

monument/0.title: Monument 2040 Comprehensive Plan and Downtown Master Plan
monument/0.summary: The Planning Commission heard the draft 2040 Comprehensive Plan and Downtown Master Plan on Sept. 9 and again Oct. 14, after nearly two years of outreach. Residents worried that conceptual downtown redevelopment renderings don't fit Monument's historic small-town character. Town Council was scheduled to hold a public hearing on Resolution 78-2026 adopting the plan on Nov. 2.

monument/1.title: 2027 budget and use tax ballot proposals
monument/1.summary: The Citizens Service Levels Advisory Committee reviewed the preliminary 2027 budget, including impact fee funds, new police positions and park funding. The committee also discussed use tax ballot measures, including a possible $2.2M construction use tax gain and raising the motor vehicle use tax to 3.5 for about $500K more. Council was to see the proposed 2027 draft budget Nov. 2.

monument/2.title: Jackson Creek Parkway and traffic concerns
monument/2.summary: Committee members asked about Jackson Creek Parkway expansion, and whether traffic impact fees could fund it, as new development like Target and apartments near Walmart arrives. Council was to get a Jackson Creek Parkway improvements update Nov. 2, and a resident raised traffic concerns on Old Denver Road.
monument/2.where: Jackson Creek Parkway and Old Denver Road

monument/3.title: Native Sun Construction PUD amendment at 15010 Woodcarver Road
monument/3.summary: The Planning Commission recommended approval of a major PUD amendment for Native Sun Construction, including relocating the shop building, a deceleration lane on Wood Carver Road, and 66 new trees. Council took up Ordinance 24-2026 on Sept. 8.

monument/4.title: 7 Brew Drive Thru Coffee final PUD plan
monument/4.summary: The final PUD plan for a 7 Brew drive-thru coffee shop went to the Planning Commission and then to Council as Ordinance 23-2026.

monument/5.title: Karl Malone Powersports and Conexus Lot 1 PUDs
monument/5.summary: The Planning Commission recommended approval of the final PUD for a 30,000-square-foot RV sales and service facility for Karl Malone Powersports. It also took up the Conexus Lot 1 Filing 2 final PUD, which involves 312 apartment units.

monument/6.title: Falcon Commerce Center Phase 2 PUD amendment
monument/6.summary: Council re-introduced Ordinance 15-2026, a preliminary PUD major amendment for the south 43 acres of Falcon Commerce Center, continued from Aug. 3, and staff gave a timeline of events.

monument/7.title: Police handgun purchase and fee schedule
monument/7.summary: Council's consent agenda included Resolution 63-2026 to buy Shadow Systems handguns for officers' on-duty use. Council also approved revisions to the police services fee schedule effective Oct. 1 (Resolution 72-2026).

monument/8.title: Water attorney and water workshop
monument/8.summary: Council appointed Nazarenus Stack & Wombacher LLC as the town's water attorney (Resolution 71-2026). A councilmember also said she would like a water workshop with outside experts. The council also considered a new tap for two properties.

monument/9.title: Silver Key funding request and Ordinance 25-2026
monument/9.summary: Silver Key's CEO asked Council to consider a $25,000 contribution for senior services. Council also approved Ordinance 25-2026 on prohibited conduct, with educational components, and Ordinance 27-2026 amending Title 3 Section 3.09.

monument/10.title: Small Business Development Center funding proposal
monument/10.summary: The advisory committee discussed a funding request from the Small Business Development Center Network, alongside the chamber groups. Members questioned its impact and the $250 consulting fee.

morgan-county/0.title: Data center zoning regulations
morgan-county/0.summary: The county commissioners have been working on new data center rules for the Zoning Regulations, with a Planning Commission hearing on April 21, 2026 and a commissioner hearing opened May 5 and continued repeatedly through August 4. Drafts define edge, large and accessory data centers, allow only closed-loop cooling, and are still debating setbacks and decommissioning requirements. Zoning amendments were again on the September 15 agenda.

morgan-county/1.title: Fortress solar and battery project road work enforcement
morgan-county/1.summary: The county issued a Notice of Intent to Take Enforcement Action and Order to Show Cause against Fortress over road improvements on County Roads Q and R tied to its 2024 solar and battery special use permits. Fortress says paving began without county observation of proof rolling and has chosen to crush and rebuild the road. A hearing was set for October 23, 2026.

morgan-county/2.title: County jail expansion and capital planning
morgan-county/2.summary: The 2025 annual financial report notes commissioners are reviewing the capital improvement plan and targeting a County Jail expansion. An Energy Impact Assistance Fund grant helps, and the county may ask other municipalities to help fund it. A security fence project for the Justice Center and East Point Building was also up for bid award on October 20.
morgan-county/2.where: Morgan County Jail and Justice Center, Fort Morgan

morgan-county/3.title: 2027 preliminary budget and county finances
morgan-county/3.summary: The Finance Director presented the proposed preliminary 2027 budget on November 5. The treasurer's report showed tax collections of about $64.97 million, 98.66% of taxes levied. The 2025 annual comprehensive financial report was presented in August.

morgan-county/4.title: Home Rule Charter and special election
morgan-county/4.summary: A charter commissioner presented on a Home Rule Charter for Morgan County on September 1, alongside a resolution (2026 BCC 38) calling a special election.

morgan-county/5.title: Zoning code changes and planning fee increases
morgan-county/5.summary: Commissioners considered new planning and building inspection fees, a revised 2026 fee schedule, and zoning amendments on enforcement processes. A November 5 hearing covers variances, storage units, campgrounds and RV parks, school dedications, wells and replats.

morgan-county/6.title: Junk and rubbish ordinance
morgan-county/6.summary: Ordinance No. 2, Series 2026, restricts accumulation of junk and refuse in unincorporated areas, citing rodents, fire hazards and pollution. Existing operating junk yards are exempt. It had first reading on September 15 and second reading on November 5.

morgan-county/7.title: Fort Morgan wastewater plant road use and solar lease
morgan-county/7.summary: Commissioners considered a road use agreement with Glacier Construction for the City of Fort Morgan's wastewater treatment plant expansion, plus a second amendment to a solar energy system lease and easement on about 17 acres and a related release and waiver.

morgan-county/8.title: Mission Goldwing Solar Project comments
morgan-county/8.summary: The county was asked to comment on the Mission Goldwing Solar Project in Adams County near the Morgan County line.

morgan-county/9.title: Prairie dogs on state-owned land
morgan-county/9.summary: The commissioners planned to submit comments to Colorado Parks and Wildlife about prairie dogs on state-owned land.

mountain-view/0.title: R3 and R4 Zoning District Update
mountain-view/0.summary: The Environmental Planning Commission is set to consider recommending adoption of the R3 Zoning District Update. It would update R3 and R4 zoning, amend the General Plan land use map, and rezone areas into new R3-A, R3-B, R3-C and R4 districts, including 14 R4 change areas.

mountain-view/1.title: Rowhouse project at 924-940 San Rafael Avenue
mountain-view/1.summary: A gatekeeper project would replace two industrial buildings with a 36-unit rowhouse development using state density bonus law. It needs a rezoning from MM (General Industrial) to R3-2, a General Plan amendment, a vesting tentative map and removal of two heritage trees on 1.80 acres.

mountain-view/2.title: LinkedIn development agreement amendment
mountain-view/2.summary: Council held a public hearing and introduced an ordinance amending the development agreement for LinkedIn's sites on East Middlefield Road and Maude Avenue. The adoption agenda would put a $1.6 million public benefit fee into the Affordable Housing Fund.
mountain-view/2.where: 700-810 East Middlefield Road and 1100-1200 Maude Avenue

mountain-view/3.title: Historic Preservation Ordinance and Historic Register update
mountain-view/3.summary: The Environmental Planning Commission held a public hearing on amendments to the zoning code for designating and preserving historic resources, plus a zoning map amendment. Council then took up the second reading on October 13. Public comments were included in the materials.

mountain-view/4.title: Heritage tree removal appeals and ordinance update
mountain-view/4.summary: The Urban Forestry Board heard appeals on heritage tree removals. It denied the appeals at 961 Eichler Drive and 1473 Tyler Park Way, and granted the appeal for one tree at 777 San Carrizo Way. Commissioners also asked staff to resolve permitting conflicts and gave input on the upcoming Heritage Tree Ordinance update.
mountain-view/4.where: 961 Eichler Drive, 777 San Carrizo Way, 1473 Tyler Park Way

sources.body: Parks and Recreation Commission and Urban Forestry Board
Parks and Recreation Commission and Urban Forestry Board

mountain-view/5.title: Rengstorff Complete Streets Study and Active Transportation Plan
mountain-view/5.summary: The Bicycle/Pedestrian Advisory Committee reviewed the Rengstorff Complete Streets Study and recommended the final Active Transportation Plan 5-0. The Council Transportation Committee was also to review both items.

mountain-view/6.title: Interim Pedestrian Mall Improvements at Castro and California Streets
mountain-view/6.summary: Staff presented the concept intersection layout for Project 23-49 to the Bicycle/Pedestrian Advisory Committee for feedback. The Council Transportation Committee was to recommend a design concept to Council. The Downtown Committee also tracks Castro Street updates.

mountain-view/7.title: State Route 237 and Middlefield Road interchange design concept
mountain-view/7.summary: Council was asked to approve the design concept for Project 19-65, as recommended by the Council Transportation Committee.

mountain-view/8.title: Affordable housing funding: PLHA funds and bond financing
mountain-view/8.summary: Council took up a resolution accepting $388,515 in state Permanent Local Housing Allocation funds. The money would go to the 96 West El Camino Real affordable housing project and a homeownership assistance pilot. Council also considered tax-exempt bond financing for 96 West El Camino Real and for 334 San Antonio Road.
mountain-view/8.where: 96 West El Camino Real; 334 San Antonio Road

mountain-view/9.title: Rent stabilization appeals
mountain-view/9.summary: The Rental Housing Committee heard a landlord appeal against a tenant (Petition C25260029) and approved the tentative decision in full. It also had another appeal (Petition C25260032) on its October 22 agenda, and worked on the one-time utility adjustment petition process.

mountain-view/10.title: Public Safety Building construction and public art
mountain-view/10.summary: Council was asked to authorize pre-qualification of responsible bidders and critical-trade subcontractors for Package 2 of Project 20-49. The Visual Arts Committee also discussed public art for the building.

mountain-view/11.title: Shoreline athletic fields renovation and Google environmental reimbursement
mountain-view/11.summary: Acting as the Shoreline Regional Park Community board, Council considered an $880,000 professional services agreement with Tetra Tech for the athletic fields. It also considered appropriating $4,968,700 under reimbursement agreements with Google for past and ongoing environmental work.

mountain-view/12.title: Ambulance billing and user fees
mountain-view/12.summary: Council considered a resolution adopting revised ambulance billing and user fees for the Fire Department, to be reflected in the Master Fee Schedule.

mountain-view/13.title: Pathways to Housing homeless response progress report
mountain-view/13.summary: Council considered accepting the first annual progress report on the 2026 Pathways to Housing Homeless Response Strategy Implementation and Expenditure Plan.

mountain-view/14.title: All-electric construction zoning exceptions
mountain-view/14.summary: The Environmental Planning Commission was to hold a hearing on zoning amendments allowing exceptions to development standards in R1 and R2 districts for single-family and duplex homes that voluntarily build all-electric.

nederland/0.title: Rezoning 242 & 252 E 5th St from General Commercial to Medium Density Residential
nederland/0.summary: LandShark Investments LLC wants to rezone two vacant lots from General Commercial to Medium Density Residential to build two roughly 2,100 sq ft A-frame homes. The Planning Commission held a hearing on Oct 21; a neighbor worried about losing GC flexibility and spot zoning, while another resident supported it. The commission recommended approval of Ordinance 895.

nederland/1.title: Temporary use permits (Ordinance 893)
nederland/1.summary: Draft Ordinance 893 would create administratively reviewed temporary-use permits, generally limited to 90 days, that staff could suspend or revoke. A fee would be set by resolution, and staff could require neighbor notification case by case. A resident submitted public comment.

nederland/2.title: Outdoor sales, eating and drinking use group amendment (Ordinance 894)
nederland/2.summary: The Planning Commission reviewed changes to the Use Group Table to allow outdoor sales, eating and drinking, with safety standards for activities near roadways. A resident spoke in support, and the commission moved to recommend approval of Ordinance 894.

nederland/3.title: Moving Board of Zoning Adjustment duties to the Planning Commission (Ordinance 896)
nederland/3.summary: Ordinance 896 would dissolve the separate Board of Zoning Adjustment and give its function to the Planning Commission. Discussion cited few variance applications and difficulty keeping a separate volunteer board, and noted Colorado law allows this for a statutory town.

nederland/4.title: Flex zoning for housing and redevelopment
nederland/4.summary: The Planning Commission began discussing a 'flex zoning' concept from the Comprehensive Plan that could broaden housing types and mixed uses and add affordable-housing incentives. The Wolf Tongue industrial area and General Commercial parcels near East Street Garage and Mountain Auto were discussed as candidates.
nederland/4.where: Wolf Tongue industrial area; East Street Garage and Mountain Auto area

nederland/5.title: Eldora spending resolution (Resolution 2026-31)
nederland/5.summary: The Board of Trustees took up Resolution 2026-31 on Eldora spending as an action item on Nov 9. Several residents, including Dallas Masters and Karen Blakemore, submitted public comment. The documents do not state the outcome.

nederland/6.title: Fiscal Year 2027 budget
nederland/6.summary: The Board of Trustees held a discussion of the FY27 budget on Nov 9.

nederland/7.title: Interim Town Manager agreement amendment
nederland/7.summary: Trustees considered Resolution 2026-30, a first amendment to the Interim Town Manager employment agreement with Gordon.

nederland/8.title: Town property purchase for recreation (executive session)
nederland/8.summary: The Board of Trustees scheduled an executive session on Oct 29 about purchasing property and operations for recreational activities.

nederland/9.title: Chipeta Park playground replacement and PROST update
nederland/9.summary: The parks advisory board continued discussing the playground vision, grant opportunities and priorities for replacing the Chipeta Park playground. It also worked on final revisions to the PROST plan update and a timeline for returning it to the Board.

sources.body: PROSAB - Nederland Parks, Recreation, and Open Space Advisory Board

new-castle/0.title: Data center general information discussion
new-castle/0.summary: Town Council scheduled a discussion of general data center information at its November 3, 2026 meeting. The documents give no detail on a specific proposal.

norwood/0.title: Town-wide 15 mph speed limit
norwood/0.summary: The board discussed lowering the speed limit in the spring and summer, then considered an ordinance in July setting a 15 mph limit on all town streets unless otherwise posted. A further ordinance was on the August 12 agenda, but the documents do not state the outcome.

norwood/1.title: Moratorium on medium and large-scale development and land use code rewrite
norwood/1.summary: The board considered extending the emergency temporary moratorium on medium and large-scale development (Ordinance 0813, 2025). It also contracted KLJ for a land use code update and a master plan, and a Land Use Code amendment ordinance was scheduled for October. A joint work session covered the master plan and annexation.

norwood/2.title: Norwood Public School property purchase and rezone
norwood/2.summary: The town tracked its purchase of the Norwood Public School property. A public hearing and ordinance were scheduled on May 13 to rezone 2028 Maverick Way from Agriculture to a Public zoning district.

norwood/3.title: Short-term rental rules
norwood/3.summary: Short-term rentals were a recurring discussion item from July through October. The documents do not give specifics of any proposed rules.

norwood/4.title: Employee compensation and retention incentives
norwood/4.summary: The board considered a resolution and ordinance authorizing additional compensation and retention incentives for employees, with legal review of compensation in May. A second ordinance on the subject came up in July.

norwood/5.title: Water treatment plant land, raw water and water commission
norwood/5.summary: The board and Water Commission met about State Land Board property for the water treatment plant. They also worked on raw water board rules, grant authority for the Water Commission, commission appointments and terms, and a drainage study and system design by SGM.

norwood/6.title: Pocket park construction and dedication
norwood/6.summary: The town took a bid from RMC Builders for the pocket park at 1575 Grand Ave. Signage and an update followed, and a dedication was set for September.

norwood/7.title: Sidewalks, school traffic and CDOT projects
