norwood/7.summary: The town approved job bids for the CDOT Safer Sidewalks to School project and an MOU with CDOT. It later discussed school traffic and the sidewalk project, and heard about upcoming CDOT projects.

norwood/8.title: Removal for cause hearing
norwood/8.summary: The board adopted a resolution in August setting a public hearing to consider removing an official for cause, and amended it in September. The October 15 hearing was cancelled. The documents do not name the person or give the reason.

norwood/9.title: Wildlife and wildfire ordinances, fireworks
norwood/9.summary: The board discussed wildlife and wildfire ordinances in January and February. Fireworks, including a Noel Night or New Year's Eve show and 2026 plans, came up several times.

norwood/10.title: 2027 draft budget
norwood/10.summary: The 2027 draft budget was taken up in October and again on November 4.

norwood/11.title: EV charging, streetlights and dark sky rules
norwood/11.summary: The board discussed EV charging station rates and install budget, streetlight dark sky compliance, and updated Dark Sky Coalition rules.

nunn/0.title: North Weld Water Services Agreement and Master Water Plan
nunn/0.summary: The Town attorney has been reviewing and amending the water services agreement with North Weld County Water District, with a final version to go to the Board before approval. The Town also awarded a Master Water Plan grant, chose an engineer bid in August 2026, and is working on a grant to find water loss.

nunn/1.title: Water taps, excess water use ordinance and 2027 water rates
nunn/1.summary: In fall 2026 the Board took up water tap approvals with water share and tap fees, an excessive water use ordinance for properties over their water unit, and 2027 water rates and fees. Water loss and added meters were earlier concerns, as were hydrant locks and a bulk fill station.

nunn/2.title: Clayton Homes and Blue Spruce developments, 4th Street lot line variance
nunn/2.summary: Clayton Homes wants to build 18 homes. The Board has discussed plant investments and tap fees for large developments, approved permits for lots 2 and 3 of the RLD subdivision, and held a September 2026 hearing on a variance at 1467 4th Street after a house at 1457 4th Street was placed too close to the lot line. A development agreement with Blue Spruce Development on 4th Street is under review, and they must provide water shares.

nunn/3.title: CDBG Senior Center/Community Center grant and Town Hall improvements
nunn/3.summary: The Town got a CDBG grant of $206,739.34 for the senior and community center, and asbestos abatement bids ranged from $56,000 to $161,000. The Board voted on how to complete the work, including interior painting and a trophy case, and on a project manager.

nunn/4.title: Wildfire resiliency code and 2024 building code adoption
nunn/4.summary: The Board adopted Ordinance 329 for the 2024 International Building Code in April 2026. It is working on adopting the Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code, which the fire district must review, and plans a hearing notice and draft ordinance.

nunn/5.title: Safer Streets grant, speed study and Master Drainage Plan
nunn/5.summary: The Town chose an engineering firm for the Safer Streets grant, ran a speed study, and gathered resident input through an interactive map and outreach events. The Safer Streets plan and Master Drainage Plan are to be posted online for 30 days for public comment. Weld County road help on CR 31 is also under discussion.

nunn/6.title: Sunrise Solar project at CR 29.5
nunn/6.summary: The Board reviewed a permit application for a 20-acre solar project at 49600 CR 29.5, with a 10-foot fence. It asked for written plans on dust mitigation, construction truck routes and an eco plan, and expects 50% plans in mid-August. Chalk Bluffs Energy Project also presented in January 2026.

nunn/7.title: 2027 budget, mill levy and police funding
nunn/7.summary: The 2026 mill levy and budget were adopted in December 2025. The 2027 budget draft was reviewed in October 2026. The police department sought less-lethal pepper ball guns at $969 each, tasers, vehicle upgrades or lease, and a Byrne JAG grant with a match of up to $5,000.

nunn/8.title: RV and ADU ordinance
nunn/8.summary: The Board began reviewing an ordinance on RVs and accessory dwelling units in fall 2026.

nunn/9.title: Marijuana license renewals and new manufacturing application
nunn/9.summary: The Board handled several marijuana cultivation and manufacturing license renewals. It also reviewed a new manufacturing application, which still needs state approval and then a local license vote.

nunn/10.title: Bus stop shelter on Highway 85
nunn/10.summary: The Board discussed and voted on an additional bus stop shelter on the east side of Highway 85.

nunn/11.title: Preliminary concept plan for 20 acres, former Antelope Run
nunn/11.summary: The Board was to review a preliminary concept plan from Robert Kearny for 20 acres of the former Antelope Run property.

oak-creek/0.title: New 2% sales tax chapter for capital improvements (Ordinance No. 678)
oak-creek/0.summary: The Town Board discussed an ordinance adopting a new Chapter 3.02 of the municipal code covering the town's 2.0% sales tax, to be used for construction and rehabilitation of capital improvements. It was discussed in August and September and Ordinance No. 678 was up for approval on October 8, 2026.

oak-creek/1.title: Lot 15, Sierra View Subdivision development agreement with MACOGA, LLC
oak-creek/1.summary: The board was asked to approve a development agreement for Lot 15, Sierra View Subdivision on October 8, and on October 22 it held a legal-advice session and considered a Development Improvement Agreement with MACOGA, LLC. The new agreement would terminate and replace an April 2025 improvements agreement, and requires a $5,000 deposit from the developer.

oak-creek/2.title: Sheriff Dam enlargement and reservoir project
oak-creek/2.summary: The board considered a Special Use Permit for the enlargement and rehabilitation of Sheriff Dam, as approved by the state Division of Water Resources, along with an agent authorization form for the Sheriff Dam Reservoir Project.

oak-creek/3.title: Law enforcement agreements with Routt County Sheriff's Office
oak-creek/3.summary: The August 13 meeting included a hearing on two draft law enforcement service agreements with Routt County and an off-duty overtime reimbursement agreement with the Routt County Sheriff's Office.

oak-creek/4.title: 2027 budget first draft
oak-creek/4.summary: The board reviewed the first draft of the town's 2027 annual budget on October 8, 2026.

oak-creek/5.title: Bulk water dispensing station upgrades
oak-creek/5.summary: The board discussed upgrades to the bulk water dispensing station, then took up buying a new control panel and a proposal to build a new shell for the station.

oak-creek/6.title: Trash hauling rate increases from Apex Twin Enviro
oak-creek/6.summary: Apex Twin Enviro was scheduled to discuss with the board its trash hauling rate increases beginning in November 2026.

oak-creek/7.title: Dog park proposal and flow trail grant
oak-creek/7.summary: The SOROCO Youth Action Council sought a letter of support for a grant and presented a proposed dog park in town. Separately, the board considered a resolution to apply for a $125,000 Colorado Parks and Wildlife trail grant to complete a downhill flow trail in Oak Creek Mountain Park.

oak-creek/8.title: South Routt Medical Center health service plan expansion
oak-creek/8.summary: The Planning Commission and Town Board held public hearings on an application to add 880 square feet of institutional space to the existing South Routt Medical Center facility.

oak-creek/9.title: Street and drainage projects: Sharp Avenue, Oak Ridge, Bell Avenue
oak-creek/9.summary: The board considered an asphalt patching project on Sharp Avenue and Oak Ridge and a bid for the Bell Avenue drainage improvement project. It also considered buying a $135,364 sewer jetter.
oak-creek/9.where: Sharp Avenue, Oak Ridge, Bell Avenue

oak-creek/10.title: South Routt Housing Authority funding request
oak-creek/10.summary: The South Routt Housing Authority asked the town for $13,000 in operations funding.

oak-creek/11.title: School running track condition and nuisance abatement
oak-creek/11.summary: The board planned to discuss the condition of the running track with the South Routt school district, and later discussed nuisance abatement actions in town.

ophir/0.title: Ban on short-term rentals (Ordinance 2026-7)
ophir/0.summary: The Planning and Zoning Commission recommended 3-0 an ordinance amending Section 303.1 of the Land Use Code to make leasing short-term rentals unlawful, citing impacts on town services, neighbors and the town's limited housing stock. P&Z also discussed what minimum rental length should count, with one member suggesting anything under 63 days, and was to review a full draft from the Town.

ophir/1.title: Wildfire Resiliency Code and new exterior material rules
ophir/1.summary: Ophir must adopt the 2025 Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code under state law (deadline noted as May). P&Z has reviewed wildfire-resistant siding, such as wood-styled cement board, and in October considered new exterior material requirements for siding, garage doors, decking and fences that comply with the code.

ophir/2.title: Revegetation ordinance for soil disturbance
ophir/2.summary: A draft ordinance would require a revegetation plan before any soil disturbance, including construction, septic, utility and road work, to protect native plants and pollinators, with penalties for non-compliance. P&Z recommended approval 5-0 in March, with the construction fencing requirement removed, after discussing an approved seed list.

ophir/3.title: Dark Sky and lighting ordinance
ophir/3.summary: A draft Dark Sky/Lighting Ordinance was reviewed by P&Z, which recommended approval 5-0 in March 2026.

ophir/4.title: Variance for side setbacks and 2/12 roof pitch on Aurum Street
ophir/4.summary: An applicant requested a variance to cut required side yard setbacks from 15 feet to 10 feet and to allow a 2/12 roof pitch for new construction on Lots 1 and 2, Block 2 on Aurum Street. The applicant presented the request to P&Z in March 2026, and approval would also involve the General Assembly.

ophir/5.title: Fence rules and the Bobtail Street fence
ophir/5.summary: P&Z considered whether a fence on Lots 5 and 6, Block 4 is a permitted accessory use to the residence on Lots 7 and 8, and decided new fencing needed neither a variance nor a Special Use Permit. It then took up fencing materials for a new fence at 112 Bobtail Street, and earlier discussed whether neighbor permission should be required for fences.

ophir/6.title: Residential building plan reviews
ophir/6.summary: P&Z reviewed building plans for the Aplin and Kondracki home on Bobtail Street, the Croke residence on Granite Street (recommended 4-0) and the Cooper residence on Aurum Street. Reviews check setbacks, parking, exterior materials and fire safety.

ophir/7.title: Low Energy and Carbon Code presentation
ophir/7.summary: EcoAction Partners was scheduled to give P&Z a 30-minute presentation on a Low Energy & Carbon Code in June 2026.

ophir/8.title: Wood stove permits and parking rules
ophir/8.summary: P&Z discussed requiring permits for replacement wood stoves, with free application and review. It also discussed parking spaces placed where roofs shed snow, and limiting parking of vehicles and boats to spaces or town rights-of-way.

ordway/0.title: Addies Restaurant annexation at 17484 Highway 96
ordway/0.summary: Trustees took up an annexation petition filed by Toni Evans (Addies Restaurant) in August, and Planning and Zoning recommended annexation. Ordinances 673 and 674 on annexation and zoning had a second reading on Oct. 5, but were repealed Oct. 21. Council then set a Nov. 30, 2026 public hearing on the annexation.

ordway/1.title: Water moratorium, restrictions and water supply
ordway/1.summary: Council denied a water restrictions resolution (2026-06) in April, then approved Resolution 2026-07 in June, a moratorium on additional water services. Water reports and a town resident water restructuring discussion also came up, along with the SE Colorado Water Conservancy allocation of 64.75 AF.

ordway/2.title: Town attorney contract loss and CIRSA insurance claim
ordway/2.summary: Documents include a CIRSA coverage letter and a settlement agreement tied to a former town attorney's amendment of a water rate contract, with losses beginning in 2022. The Town's losses and the malpractice claim are described, but the outcome is not clear from the documents.

ordway/3.title: 428 E. 3rd Street town property sale and foreclosure
ordway/3.summary: Council authorized sale of town-owned property in March, including 428 East 3rd Street, then discussed the property in executive session in May. In June it discussed restarting foreclosure on the property.

ordway/4.title: Historic preservation and Certified Local Government
ordway/4.summary: Council moved to establish a Certified Local Government and a Historic Preservation Advisory Authority (Ordinances 668, 669, 671) and gave updates on the CLG process. A further historic ordinance (675) had a first reading in October.

ordway/5.title: Affordable housing development agreement and tax certificate purchases
ordway/5.summary: In October the Town considered an agreement with a development company on future affordable housing. It also approved negotiating tax certificates for properties at 305, 317 and 319 Arkansas and 326 Idaho, and approved a demolition application at 318 E 3rd.

ordway/6.title: Mobile park holding negotiations ended
ordway/6.summary: Council discussed a sewer tap for a mobile park in June and in October moved to discontinue negotiations with Mobile Park Holding LLC.

ordway/7.title: Cemetery board and cemetery grant
ordway/7.summary: Council passed an ordinance (672) creating a Cemetery Board for Ordway Cemetery and gave an update on moving ahead with a cemetery grant.

ordway/8.title: Fire department county invoices and funding
ordway/8.summary: Council discussed an invoice from the county to the Fire Department in June. The Fire Department will pay past-due invoices with a subsidy. Workers' compensation and Air Med Care membership also came up.

ordway/9.title: Community Library agreement
ordway/9.summary: Council discussed the library in April and approved a revised Community Library IGA in September.

pagosa-springs/0.title: Data center moratorium (Ordinance 1037)
pagosa-springs/0.summary: Town Council held the second reading of Ordinance 1037, which pauses acceptance and processing of permit and land development applications that include a data center. Staff said the Land Use Development Code has no data center use classification and the pause lets them monitor development nationally and in Colorado while codifying one.

pagosa-springs/1.title: Ponderosa Mountain planned development (Ordinance 1042)
pagosa-springs/1.summary: Modern Community Builders LLC seeks a planned development overlay, agreement and zoning change for a 70-acre project near Hwy 160 and Goldmine Drive, with commercial lodging, housing and deed-restricted workforce housing (90%-130% AMI) in three phases. It was continued from October 6 to a first reading on October 20, with a second reading as amended on the November 3 agenda; a resident asked for a development moratorium over infrastructure needs.

pagosa-springs/2.title: Sanitation district sewer and wastewater plant projects
pagosa-springs/2.summary: The Sanitation General Improvement District is replacing broken sewer lines (McCabe Creek, Rosita Street), buying pumps and surge tanks, and moving ahead with a new wastewater treatment facility, with interviews of firms Oct 28-29. A $3 million loan for the 1st Street lift station was approved and a $900,000 grant was sought. Evolve Infrastructure Group was the only bidder for pump and surge tank installation.
pagosa-springs/2.where: Townwide sewer system, 1st Street lift station

pagosa-springs/3.title: 2027 town and sanitation district budgets
pagosa-springs/3.summary: Council adopted a 2027 budget with a 1.561 mill levy raising $173,145, a fee schedule and a 5-year capital plan including the community center roof, vehicles and park improvements. The sanitation district adopted a $6.06M budget with higher commercial sewer and connection fees and a .904 mill levy. Town sales tax receipts have come in below projections.

pagosa-springs/4.title: G&I Sanitation trash franchise and rates
pagosa-springs/4.summary: Council approved a five-year franchise for G&I Sanitation Services to run refuse collection using town streets and alleys, on first reading Sept 15 and second reading Oct 6. A public hearing on the company's proposed rates was also held, as the charter requires.

pagosa-springs/5.title: Talisman Drive area rezoning to Multi-unit Town Center (Ordinance 1040)
pagosa-springs/5.summary: Council rezoned properties on Talisman, Eaton and Village Drives, including Cornerstone Lofts and Talisman Pointe units, to Multi-unit Town Center. Planning Commission recommended approval Aug 25, and Council passed first and second readings.
pagosa-springs/5.where: Talisman Drive, Eaton Drive, Village Drive

pagosa-springs/6.title: Housing Action Plan and Proposition 123 credits
pagosa-springs/6.summary: Town and County held joint work sessions on the Housing Action Plan, and Council approved an intergovernmental agreement on Proposition 123 shared affordable housing credits. The housing coordinator said the plan addresses community housing needs.

pagosa-springs/7.title: Dark Sky Lighting Management Plan
pagosa-springs/7.summary: The Dark Sky Steering Committee is drafting a Lighting Management Plan stricter than Land Use Code Article 6.11, with limits on pole height, illumination at property lines, lights-out times and no lighting of trails. A work session was held Oct 1 ahead of committee review.

pagosa-springs/8.title: Kids Camp ending and parks plans
pagosa-springs/8.summary: The Town will stop operating Kids Camp, which carried an annual subsidy of about $40,000, while talks continue with PCI about a summer program; families were notified. Parks staff are also working on the Parks and Recreation Master Plan, Yamaguchi South Bike Park, and tree planting grants.

pagosa-springs/9.title: San Juan River Park naming at 1040 E US 160
pagosa-springs/9.summary: Council named the former Bob's LP/Basin Coop property, bought in May 2025, San Juan River Park after considering Gateway River Park. Staff may add Native names later.

pagosa-springs/10.title: Cancelled July 4 fireworks rescheduled
pagosa-springs/10.summary: The July 4 show was cancelled for extreme fire risk, but the Acme contract means the town forfeits $32,000 unless it holds a show in 2026. Council voted to shoot the fireworks during Old Fashion Christmas.

pagosa-springs/11.title: Apache Street speeding and traffic complaints
pagosa-springs/11.summary: Residents asked Council for speed bumps at 6th Street and a deer crossing sign on Apache Street, citing traffic from Yamaguchi Park, pickleball and school. Another resident said the jake brake ordinance is not enforced and complained about overnight parking.

palisade/0.title: Draft 2027 Town of Palisade budget
palisade/0.summary: Staff presented the draft 2027 budget to the Board of Trustees as required by state law. The board was asked to set the public hearing to adopt the final budget for November 10, 2026.

palisade/1.title: 2027 special event calendar and blackout dates (Resolution 2026-17)
palisade/1.summary: The Board of Trustees was to consider Resolution 2026-17, approving the 2027 special event calendar and blackout dates.

palisade/2.title: Watershed wildfire mitigation presentation from Colorado State Forest Service
palisade/2.summary: The Colorado State Forest Service was scheduled to present on watershed wildfire mitigation and coordination with the town.

palisade/3.title: Tourism Advisory Commission interviews and appointment
palisade/3.summary: The board was to interview candidates and appoint a commissioner to the Tourism Advisory Commission by roll call vote.

palisade/4.title: Fall Town Cleanup Day and Trick-or-Treat Street events
palisade/4.summary: Fall Town Cleanup Day is Saturday, October 17 from 8 am to noon at the Riverbend Park parking lot, or until dumpsters are full. Trick-or-Treat Street and Touch a Truck is Friday, October 30.

palmer-lake/0.title: Temporary data center moratorium (Resolution 31-2026)
palmer-lake/0.summary: The Board of Trustees had Resolution 31-2026 on its September 10 agenda for a temporary moratorium on data centers. The documents do not state the outcome.

palmer-lake/1.title: Town-wide bear-proof trash rules and bear mitigation ordinance
palmer-lake/1.summary: The Planning Commission discussed a mandatory town-wide bear-proof container ordinance, certified receptacles and CPW grants. A resident asked for strict enforcement. The Trustees later had Ordinance 6-2026 on Bear Mitigation and Enforcement on their October 22 agenda.

palmer-lake/2.title: Water emergency and watering restrictions
palmer-lake/2.summary: The town remains under a stage one water emergency. An outdoor watering ban and seasonal changes cut demand by 25% and allowed a shift to the Denver well. Monument Creek is too low to be a production source and there is no firm end date for the water call. A resident criticized how the town communicated the restrictions. The Shady Lane water main project is under way.

palmer-lake/3.title: 2027 town budget and spending freeze
palmer-lake/3.summary: The Town Administrator started the 2027 budget projections and froze non-essential spending and new capital projects. Trustees held budget workshops and reviewed department budgets, the 2026 amended budget and the draft 2027 budget. The Parks Commission ranked its own budget requests. The Master Fee Schedule for 2026 was also amended by Resolution 34-2026.

palmer-lake/4.title: Buc-ee's annexation request withdrawn; negotiations with landowner
palmer-lake/4.summary: An executive session on September 10 covered discussions and negotiations with the landowner's counsel and Buc-ee's following withdrawal of the annexation request.

palmer-lake/5.title: Lease with option to purchase town property
palmer-lake/5.summary: The Trustees went into executive session on a proposed lease with option to purchase of town property. They took up legal advice and negotiation strategy on September 10 and October 22.

palmer-lake/6.title: Lakeview conservation easement and donation of about 140 lots
palmer-lake/6.summary: The Board's September 24 agenda included a conservation easement and donation of about 140 platted lots in Lakeview.

palmer-lake/7.title: Fire protection ballot measure and department consolidation
palmer-lake/7.summary: The Town Administrator is researching a possible ballot measure on fire protection involving the Palmer Lake Fire Department and Monument Fire. Because it involves taxation, a special election may not be permitted. He also proposed consolidating the Water, Roads/Streets and Parks departments.

palmer-lake/8.title: Hearing process involving Trustee Roger Moseley and board policies
palmer-lake/8.summary: The Town has retained a hearing officer and is finalizing an agreement with a presenting officer for hearings concerning Trustee Roger Moseley. Trustees also discussed CORA request procedures, legal costs and Trustee-staff communications. New agenda-setting, social media and snow removal policies were up for adoption on October 22.

palmer-lake/9.title: Parks projects: Centennial Park, Elephant Rock Pavilion, Glen Park weeds
palmer-lake/9.summary: The Parks and Trails Commission decided against no-fishing zones at Centennial Park Lake. It held off Columbine Park plantings until spring because of water restrictions. It is working on poison hemlock control in Glen Park, Elephant Rock Pavilion renovation, pickleball court flooding and curbing, the playground inspection, a pocket park and motorized vehicles on trails. Creek Week cleanups run September 26 to October 4.
palmer-lake/9.where: Centennial Park, Glen Park, Elephant Rock

palmer-lake/10.title: Planning Commission land use items: Fowler Branch, plat amendment, Calverts sign
palmer-lake/10.summary: On September 16 the Planning Commission had the Fowler Branch land use item, a plat amendment adjusting Lot 8 to be larger, and a sign application for Calverts. The applicant requested a continuance on one item.

palmer-lake/11.title: EcoSpa Annex at 350 Highway 105
palmer-lake/11.summary: The EcoSpa Annex at 350 Highway 105 was on a Board of Trustees agenda for September 19 as a gathering where Trustees may be present. No formal action was to be taken.

paonia/0.title: Short-term rental rules and the draft Common Ground Ordinance
paonia/0.summary: An ad hoc committee has met repeatedly since August to go through the proposed Common Ground Ordinance on short-term rentals, line by line. It has leaned toward registration with no fee for owner-occupied rentals, a fee limited to administrative cost for whole-home rentals, self-certified safety, tax compliance, and a saturation threshold (the draft says 8% of housing stock) that would pause new registrations. The Board of Trustees would set final fees and requirements. Survey respondents mostly raised housing, noise, parking and tax concerns.

paonia/1.title: Stage 2 water restrictions and water supply concerns
paonia/1.summary: After unusually high water use dropped the tank level about four feet over a weekend, the Board considered Resolution 19-26 for Stage 2 restrictions. Edits allowed hand or drip watering of gardens, and residents commented on fire risk from dried lawns and on watering schedules. Staff reported the stored supply would last about eight days without production, and the Board asked for regular tank-level updates. Resolution 22-26 rescinding the restrictions was later on the October 27 agenda. The Planning Commission is also discussing water moratorium planning and tap availability, and the Board went into executive session on water rights.

paonia/2.title: Raw Water Monitoring Project engineering amendment
paonia/2.summary: The Board considered Amendment #2 to the RESPEC agreement for pre-construction award and construction engineering services on the Raw Water Monitoring Project. It covers verifying plans and meeting state and federal funding requirements, including installing meters to better track water production. It is funded within the project budget, and a resident asked for clarification.

paonia/3.title: Estate zoning density and Table 16-2 changes
paonia/3.summary: Staff found an inconsistency in the estate zoning table and recommended allowing 1.5 to two acres per dwelling to support the Comprehensive Plan's housing-density goals. The Board discussed water and access limits and sent the item for a work session and a revised ordinance. A rezoning application from David Warren also had a continued public hearing.

paonia/4.title: Accessory dwelling units, sidewalks and subdivision rules
paonia/4.summary: The Planning Commission is discussing adding ADU rules to Chapter 16 because the 2025 Comprehensive Plan lists ADUs as a key way to create housing. Questions include where ADUs are allowed, utilities, parking, owner occupancy, fees and separate sale. It is also discussing sidewalk requirements in new subdivisions by lot size.

paonia/5.title: New police chief appointment
paonia/5.summary: The Board appointed Sergeant Henderson as the new Chief of Police. Residents spoke in support of Henderson during public comment.

paonia/6.title: 2027 budget and Town Administrator search
paonia/6.summary: The Board held budget work sessions in October and November on the 2027 budget, and asked for weekly sessions separate from other work sessions. A solid waste enterprise was also discussed. The Board considered an executive search firm profile for a Town Administrator, and employee insurance benefits were on an agenda.

paonia/7.title: Comprehensive Safety Action Plan (Safe Streets for All)
paonia/7.summary: Consor Engineering is collecting data and presenting updates on the town's Comprehensive Safety Action Plan. Findings show crash rates fell between 2018 and 2023, and reported concerns include speeds on Samuel Wade Road and damaged roads and sidewalks on 2nd Street, 3rd Street and Grand Avenue. The plan positions the town for future funding.

paonia/8.title: West Fourth Street overlay and Town Hall projects
paonia/8.summary: Public Works proposed an agreement with Delta County for a two-inch asphalt overlay on West Fourth Street, limited by the County's roughly $25,000 project cap. The Board also considered a Town Hall roof replacement bid and removing the solar panels, with an Empower presentation on upgrading them.

paonia/9.title: Solid waste, recycling and tobacco ordinances
paonia/9.summary: The Board considered Ordinance 01-26 on solid waste disposal rules and a proposal from Recyclops for free recycling service under Colorado's Extended Producer Responsibility program. The Board also acted on Ordinance 06-26 on the sale of cigarettes and tobacco.

paonia/10.title: Sewer tap fee waiver and sewer line inspection
paonia/10.summary: Ordinance 02-26 would waive sewer tap fees on certain properties and was reconsidered as an emergency waiver. Work on the trailer court utilities and a bid for sewer pipe CCTV scoping were also on agendas.

paonia/11.title: Town Board meeting rules, meeting time and rejected citizen initiatives
paonia/11.summary: The Board adopted Ordinance 07-26 amending meeting procedures and Resolution 23-26 moving regular meetings to a 5:30 start. It also discussed ordinances arising from rejected citizen initiative petitions.

paonia/12.title: Street lights, dark skies and liquor license distance rules
paonia/12.summary: The Board discussed removing street lights, dark skies and trail lights, and eliminating liquor license distance requirements for certain license classes.

parachute/0.title: Data center regulations (Ordinance 838-2026)
parachute/0.summary: Town Council is set to consider Ordinance No. 838-2026, which would amend Title 15 of the municipal code to regulate data centers and technology facilities. It was on the October 15, 2026 agenda with a cover memo; the documents do not state an outcome.

parachute/1.title: Prop 123 expedited review for affordable housing (Ordinance 837-2026)
parachute/1.summary: The Council is considering a Title 15 amendment adding Section 15.02.214 to create expedited review for affordable housing under Prop 123 and updating the land use review procedures chart. The Planning Commission recommended approval. In July the council also heard a regional housing needs assessment from an Aspen analyst.

parachute/2.title: 2026 and 2027 town budget
parachute/2.summary: Council held a 2026 budget workshop in late 2025, including an employee benefits package assessment. A 2027 budget kickoff took place in September 2026, and the draft 2027 budget with a 2027-2031 capital improvement plan was presented October 15. Council also discussed sales tax ballot initiative options in February.

parachute/3.title: Highway 6 and 1st Street "Parachute Moves" reconstruction project
parachute/3.summary: Council backed multiple grant applications for the Highway 6 and 1st Street mobility, revitalization, reconstruction and safety project, including a USDOT BUILD grant, congressionally directed spending, and HUD funding. The town was later noted as recipient of a $600,000 CDBG grant for the 1st Street project, and committed local match dollars to a federal grant in October.

parachute/4.title: Water system: raw water tank, loan refinance and Stage 2 restrictions
parachute/4.summary: Council supported a DOLA grant for the raw water tank replacement and approved a loan amendment on the water enterprise loan with Alpine Bank (Ordinance 833-2026). Stage 2 water restrictions remained in place in May 2026. Council also celebrated the Shoshone instream flow agreement and later considered a resolution on the Glenwood Hot Springs Protection Act with a water consultant report.

parachute/5.title: Town purchase of 147 1st Street from Qwest/Lumen
parachute/5.summary: Council considered Ordinance 834-2026 approving a contract to buy the property at 147 1st Street from Qwest Corporation. By May 2026 the town reported the purchase had closed and it was town-owned.

parachute/6.title: Parachute Area Transit System and bus service
parachute/6.summary: Council approved a services agreement with Glenwood Downtowner for public transit operations and a license agreement with Flix Bus for a bus stop. It also supported a state transit grant application and a regional transit planning grant in June 2026. Riders can use the ridepats.com app.

parachute/7.title: Community center and Senior Center future use
parachute/7.summary: The Valley Senior Center president asked Council in February to make the Senior Center more of a community center and noted the need for funding. In July 2026 Council reviewed a draft Community Center Management Plan with a rental agreement and liability waiver.
parachute/7.where: Parachute Community Center / Valley Senior Center

parachute/8.title: Wildland Urban Interface fire code and landscaping turf rules
parachute/8.summary: Council took up Ordinance 836-2026 revising and adopting the Wildland Urban Interface Fire Code in Title 15. Earlier, Ordinance 835-2026 added restrictions on nonfunctional artificial turf and invasive plant species in development projects.

parachute/9.title: Household pet limits ordinance (831-2025)
parachute/9.summary: Council approved Ordinance 831-2025 on animal rules and impound fines, amended to remove any household pet limits.

parachute/10.title: 6670 Transmission Line rebuild and Xcel easement
parachute/10.summary: Council held a special use review hearing for reconstruction of a public utility transmission line (6670 Transmission Line). In July it also considered a temporary construction easement for Xcel Energy. A solar project expansion of 50 acres at Straight Bottom Ranch was also noted.

parachute/11.title: Fun House Kids special use review at 201 East 1st Street
parachute/11.summary: Council scheduled a public hearing on Resolution 2026-39, a special use review for Fun House Kids LLC at 201 East 1st Street.

parker/0.title: Axon drone-as-first-responder and license plate reader program
parker/0.summary: Police are proposing to join the Axon Countywide Drone as First Responder and License Plate Reader programs, which would raise the Axon contract by about $175,000 a year. Council discussed transparency, accountability and video retention. A resident also asked the Town to remove Flock cameras around Parker.

parker/1.title: Nine-month moratorium on drone delivery facilities
parker/1.summary: Council passed an emergency ordinance on July 20, 2026 pausing applications for land use approvals or building permits for commercial drone dispatch and delivery facilities for nine months. On August 17 it affirmed the pause on second reading, with no public comment.

parker/2.title: Salisbury Regional Park Phase 2 expansion
parker/2.summary: The Planning Commission and Council approved a site plan amendment for Phase 2 of the 91-acre park. It adds tennis, pickleball and basketball courts, an inclusive playground and spray ground, a bike park and parking. Council also approved a water pipeline easement with Parker Water and Sanitation District. A resident asked about parking.
parker/2.where: East side of Motsenbocker Road, north of Hess Road

parker/3.title: 2027 Town budget, property tax levy and special funds
parker/3.summary: Staff presented the proposed 2027 budget at an October 2 workshop and published it on October 13, with adoption set for November 16. Ordinances introduced November 2 would levy 2026 property taxes, revise the 2026 budget and create special funds for risk management and the My Mainstreet General Improvement District. Staff are also redesigning property and liability insurance with a reserve.

parker/4.title: Parker 2050 Comprehensive Plan and Three-Mile Area Plan
parker/4.summary: After a Planning Commission hearing, Council adopted the Town of Parker 2050 Comprehensive Plan by Resolution 26-060 on September 21. The Planning Commission also took up adoption of the 2026 Three-Mile Area Plan on October 22.
parker/4.where: Townwide and three-mile radius around town

parker/5.title: School resource officers for American Academy
parker/5.summary: Council discussed American Academy's request for a School Resource Officer in a work session, then approved an amended and restated agreement for SRO services for the 2026-27 school year.

parker/6.title: Speeding, drag racing and Mainstreet safety
parker/6.summary: Residents complained of teens speeding and drag racing at O'Brien Park, Victorian Drive and Longs Way, and asked for more enforcement. Another resident asked for a traffic study on Mainstreet between Jordan Road and Twenty Mile Road. Others urged making Mainstreet pedestrian-only.
parker/6.where: O'Brien Park, Victorian Drive, Longs Way, Mainstreet

parker/7.title: Road projects: Twenty Mile Road, Parker/Hilltop and resurfacing
parker/7.summary: Council introduced an ordinance on its intent to acquire property interests to build and improve Twenty Mile Road. It awarded a $1,339,679.75 contract to Denver Dirt Works for Parker Road and Hilltop Road intersection improvements. It also added $607,070.35 to the 2026 townwide resurfacing contract.
parker/7.where: Twenty Mile Road, Parker Road at Hilltop Road

parker/8.title: Security guard, massage facility and merchant patrol licensing updates
parker/8.summary: The Town is rewriting its 1994 security guard (merchant patrol) ordinance, last amended in 2004, with new fees and an updated investigation process. Council also repealed and readopted the massage facility licensing chapter and set license fees for it.

parker/9.title: Parker Heritage Center interpretive plan and tribal history
parker/9.summary: Council reviewed an interpretive plan to reimagine the Heritage Center with Douglas County and Parker History. The 2026 budget has $100,000 for it plus a $7,500 grant, and a first IGA amendment was introduced November 2. Council also heard a presentation on honoring Parker's tribal history.

parker/10.title: Parker Senior Center update and feasibility study
parker/10.summary: Staff updated Council on a feasibility study and needed repairs at the Senior Center, including drainage, flooring and parking lot work. No funding or formal action was requested.

parker/11.title: Business improvement districts and nursery deer-fencing rule
parker/11.summary: The Downtown Parker and Chambers Commercial Center BIDs presented 2027 operating plans and budgets, with approval resolutions planned for October 19. Staff also weighed amending the code to allow 8-foot deer exclusion fencing for plant nurseries.

phillips-county/0.title: Wind, solar, battery storage and data center regulations
phillips-county/0.summary: The county commissioners had an agenda item on regulations for wind energy, solar, battery energy storage and data center facilities on Aug. 20. A Land Use Code public hearing was cancelled that day. The documents do not say what was decided.

phillips-county/1.title: 2027 county budget work sessions
phillips-county/1.summary: Commissioners scheduled 2027 budget work sessions after their meetings from September through November. A 2027 sales tax MOU for control of confidential data also came up on Sept. 29.

phillips-county/2.title: Floodplain ordinance
phillips-county/2.summary: A floodplain ordinance had its first reading on Oct. 19 and its second reading on Oct. 30. The documents do not give its contents.

phillips-county/3.title: Housing needs assessment and Proposition 123 recertification
phillips-county/3.summary: The county sought qualifications from firms for a Housing Needs Assessment and Water Supply Element on Oct. 9. On Oct. 30 it took up Proposition 123 recertification, which relates to affordable housing commitments.

phillips-county/4.title: Landfill equipment purchase and rates
phillips-county/4.summary: The landfill manager presented an equipment purchase on Aug. 20. Landfill rates were on the Aug. 31 agenda.

phillips-county/5.title: Viaero roadway occupancy agreements
phillips-county/5.summary: Roadway occupancy agreements with Viaero were on the Aug. 31 and Oct. 9 agendas. Such agreements cover the company's use of county road right-of-way.

phillips-county/6.title: Brightwater Cattle Co. on County Road 38 and minor land use change
phillips-county/6.summary: The commissioners heard a Brightwater Cattle Co. item on County Road 38 on Oct. 30. A public hearing on a minor land use change for Jason Roberts was held Sept. 21.

phillips-county/7.title: Road and Bridge propane contracts and equipment
phillips-county/7.summary: Road and Bridge brought a CHS propane contract and a cutting edges equipment purchase on Sept. 29. Propane contracts returned Oct. 9.

phillips-county/8.title: Fairgrounds entrance asphalt replacement
phillips-county/8.summary: The commissioners considered a project payment for replacing asphalt at the fairgrounds entrance on Oct. 19.

pitkin/0.title: 2026 Zoning Code rewrite, RV parks and Planned Development
pitkin/0.summary: The Board went through the zoning code update page by page in November, held a public hearing in January, and took up adoption of the 2026 Zoning Code in February. Residents debated an RV park use and the Planned Development wording, and the Board agreed to strike the RV Park section and the "mixed uses" language. In April the Zoning Board was set to review more code wording on May 4.

pitkin/1.title: Western Slope Towers radio tower lease with Gunnison Met Rec
pitkin/1.summary: The Board has been negotiating a lease for the town's tower site, where Western Slope wants 18 months at no charge. The mayor thought the proposed amount was too low, and the lease lists 2,500 square feet at the site. Residents commented, and the Board wanted a clause requiring site cleanup if no tenant remains. The agreement was discussed again in February, and the contract came up again in April.

pitkin/2.title: 2025 budget amendment, 2026 budget and mill levy
pitkin/2.summary: The Board held a public hearing on the 2025 budget amendment (street maintenance raised by $7,000) and the 2026 budget, then waited on county mill levy figures. On Dec. 11 it adopted Resolution 7 (amended 2025 and 2026 budgets) and Resolution 8 (levying 2026 property taxes). April financials showed a large increase in sales tax.

pitkin/3.title: Pay for town officials and board members
pitkin/3.summary: Trustees discussed paying the Environmental Health Agent about $550 for classes, the Streets/Ditches Commissioner $300 a month, and Zoning Board members $50 per meeting (about $3,000 a year for a full board). Resolution 6 on coverage with CIRSA was also passed, and Ramon Reed was paid for his time as Trustee.

pitkin/4.title: Onsite wastewater (OWTS) regulations update
pitkin/4.summary: After a public hearing on Nov. 19, the Board adopted Ordinance 1 of 2025 updating on-site wastewater treatment system regulations, as required by state Regulation 43. Josh Ackerman was appointed the town's Environmental Health Agent.

pitkin/5.title: Wildfire resiliency, energy and building codes
pitkin/5.summary: The town held a work session on a Wildfire Resiliency Code in October and planned public hearings on the Zoning, Wildfire, Energy and Building codes starting in January 2026. A wildfire mitigation seminar was noted in April.

pitkin/6.title: Fire/irrigation ditch cleaning and pond maintenance agreement with CPW
pitkin/6.summary: The Board took bids to clean and dig about 600 feet of fire and irrigation ditches. It also considered a 5-year operations and maintenance agreement with Colorado Parks and Wildlife for a pond. The mayor heard concerns that the pond could be drained into the ditch.

pitkin/7.title: Two open Board seats and Zoning Board vacancy
pitkin/7.summary: Resolution 4 of 2026 declared two Board member positions open, and the Board posted an open Zoning Board seat since the mayor's term there expires at the end of April. Cory Nasso was named Mayor Pro Tem and the Town Clerk and Attorney were reappointed.

pitkin/8.title: Fence permit at 428 State Street
pitkin/8.summary: The Board reviewed a previously denied fence permit request for 428 State Street and approved it in April.

platteville/0.title: Housing needs assessment, expedited affordable housing review and Proposition 123 commitment
platteville/0.summary: The Oct. 20, 2026 agenda lists three housing items: Resolution 2026-20 adopting a Housing Needs Assessment (with a public hearing), Resolution 2026-21 on expedited review policies for affordable housing projects, and Resolution 2026-22 on the town's Proposition 123 commitment for 2027-2029. The documents do not state the outcome.

pueblo-county/0.title: Aspen Acres Fire disaster declaration and flood recovery
pueblo-county/0.summary: The commissioners renewed the local disaster emergency for the Aspen Acres Fire almost every week. The fire began June 29, 2026 and affected over 101,965 acres. The county took a USDA watershed grant (about $18.3 million) for burn-scar flood protection, hired Wilson and Company ($300,000) and Rocksol for engineering design, and approved a $500,000 mitigation agreement. FEMA also leased office space at 201 W. 8th Street.

pueblo-county/1.title: Draft zoning standards for data centers
pueblo-county/1.summary: The Planning Commission held work sessions on Aug 19 and Sept 16 on draft use-specific standards for data centers, which are currently a special use in the county code. The draft adds requirements for decommissioning within 12 months, road use agreements, and developers showing they will pay their fair share of utility infrastructure. Staff aim to send a code amendment to the Planning Commission and then the commissioners.

pueblo-county/2.title: County budget cuts, layoffs and 2027 budget
pueblo-county/2.summary: The county is in a budget squeeze, and executive sessions repeatedly cover personnel and operating cuts for 2026 and 2027, including the Assessor, DA, Treasurer, Sheriff and Clerk offices. A resolution eliminates the BOCC receptionist positions, with the separation date moved to Dec 19, 2026. The commissioners also heard 2027 budget presentations, declared no outside funding requests will be accepted for 2027, and amended the 2026 budget.

pueblo-county/3.title: Certificates of participation, lease-purchase financing and TABOR reserve
pueblo-county/3.summary: The county worked on lease-purchase financing involving certificates of participation, including collateral questions and amendments to Resolution 26-188. It also redesignated county-owned property (DHS building at 2631 E. Fourth St. and 414 W. Ninth St.) for its TABOR emergency reserve. The Capital Construction Corporation board was changed, and property at West 11th Street was deeded to the county.
pueblo-county/3.where: Countywide; 2631 E. Fourth St. and 414 W. Ninth St.

pueblo-county/4.title: Runyon Sports Complex lease
pueblo-county/4.summary: The county negotiated a lease with the Runyon Sports Complex Commission and discussed contracts for bleachers and artificial turf. The commissioners approved the lease agreement on Oct 22.

pueblo-county/5.title: Solar and energy projects: Honors Energy permit and solar agreements
pueblo-county/5.summary: Honors Energy, LLC asked for a second 24-month extension of its House Bill 1041 permit for a project on about 1,390 acres. Another 1041 permit request came from 3 Corners Connector LLC. The county also discussed agreements with Solon Solar and AES Solar and signed stormwater maintenance agreements for Highland Solar I and Thunder Wolf II.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Land Use

pueblo-county/6.title: New county jail construction contract and jail health services
pueblo-county/6.summary: The commissioners discussed the jail construction contract with JE Dunn in executive session. They also approved the inmate health services agreement, a Sheriff's Office collective bargaining agreement, and a community corrections contract renewal.

pueblo-county/7.title: Pueblo West roads sales tax and road maintenance
pueblo-county/7.summary: The county and Pueblo West Metropolitan District are handling the 1% temporary sales tax (Ballot Question 6C) for Pueblo West roads. The commissioners met with the district about the 2023 IGA and appointed members to the oversight committee.

pueblo-county/8.title: Land use cases: rezonings, permit rescissions and zoning violations
pueblo-county/8.summary: Land use hearings covered a 0.55-acre rezoning, a 0.53-acre rezoning to SR2 to vacate interior lot lines, rescission of a cell tower permit at 4800 North Creek Road in Beulah, abandonment of three special use permits, and a vehicle sales special use permit for Toby and Rose Miller. The county also pursued legal action over zoning violations, including one at 46911 Fields Road, Avondale. The Planning Commission reviewed the Fremont Paving gravel and asphalt permit on 1,030 acres.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Land Use
Board of County Commissioners Land Use

pueblo-county/9.title: County revitalization authority and economic development campaign
pueblo-county/9.summary: The CAO presented on tax increment financing through a county revitalization authority and an economic development campaign. The commissioners also named the CAO to the PEDCO board and considered private activity bonds and a revenue bond declaration.

pueblo-county/10.title: Regional transportation planning: PACOG projects and Bustang
pueblo-county/10.summary: The Pueblo Area Council of Governments worked on the 2027 budget, transportation improvement program amendments (including $618,750 in highway safety funds, signal work on CO96A, and the Medal of Honor Blvd. trail), a bicycle and pedestrian master plan, and Bustang expansion.

pueblo-county/11.title: Fulton Heights playground and Rye Mountain Park forest thinning
pueblo-county/11.summary: The county approved a Playcore/GameTime playground agreement for the Fulton Heights Community Center (up to $102,466.47) and a Summit Logging contract for forest thinning and fuels reduction at Rye Mountain Park. A fire hydrant for Pueblo Rural Fire Station 2 also drew impact fee disbursement.
pueblo-county/11.where: Fulton Heights Community Center; Rye Mountain Park

pueblo/0.title: Speed safety camera (automated enforcement) program
pueblo/0.summary: Police Traffic Division presented a plan for speed cameras on residential streets, park frontages and designated traffic safety corridors. Estimates run $302,400 to $504,000 in monthly citations, depending on the pay rate. On Oct. 13 Council took up an ordinance amending the 2026 police staffing ordinance for automated enforcement.

pueblo/1.title: 2027 city budget, property tax levies and sales tax
pueblo/1.summary: Departments presented 2027 budgets (police, fire, public works, IT, law, finance, parks). The recommended total is $117,785,907, with a 3.7% city sales tax rate. A public hearing was set for Oct. 26, and the mill levies and budget appropriation ordinances came up Nov. 9.

pueblo/2.title: Opposition to Black Hills Colorado Electric rate increase
pueblo/2.summary: Council reviewed Black Hills Colorado Electric's 2026 rate case and took up a resolution opposing the proposed electric rate increase and the cost impacts of its Electric Resource Plan and Clean Energy Plan (Proceeding 26A-0333E). Certified copies would go to the Colorado PUC.

pueblo/3.title: Leonardo da Vinci Museum funding and RTA sales tax
pueblo/3.summary: Council discussed the museum's funding request from the half-cent sales tax fund, which has already approved $14.4 million for the project and replaced the Professional Bull Riders University. A closed-door economic development agreement discussion on the museum was also scheduled.

pueblo/4.title: St. Charles Industrial Park and Lime Road improvements
pueblo/4.summary: Council reviewed Lime Road, the only route into the industrial park, a 1.4-mile unreinforced concrete road. Estimated costs are about $20M for reinforced concrete versus $5M for asphalt, and a traffic study is required. $8M was previously transferred for park infrastructure. Closed sessions covered projects in the park, including Project Manta.
pueblo/4.where: Lime Road / St. Charles Industrial Park

pueblo/5.title: Annexations and zoning: Pueblo Masterplan Communities and Jackson Ranch
pueblo/5.summary: Council found the petition to annex the 89.93-acre Pueblo Masterplan Communities valid and sent it to Planning and Zoning. Ordinances to zone parts of the Jackson Ranch annexation area (250.1, 65.70 and 225.66 acres) came up for first presentation Sept. 14.
pueblo/5.where: Pueblo Masterplan Communities and Jackson Ranch annexation areas

pueblo/6.title: Airport: policy advisory board, aviation asset defense funds and lawsuit
pueblo/6.summary: Council established an Airport Policy Advisory board and took up an airline operating agreement. It approved a $300,000 transfer for an Aviation Asset Defense project, then scheduled a motion to reconsider it Oct. 5, alongside a closed session on City of Pueblo v. Airport litigation.

pueblo/7.title: Regional Transportation Authority (RTA) steering committee
pueblo/7.summary: Council reviewed a draft proposal for a broad voting steering committee to build an RTA, with working groups on governance, projects, finance and outreach, and CDOT and legal staff as non-voting advisors.

pueblo/8.title: Pueblo Mountain Park next steps and city parks
pueblo/8.summary: Council scheduled a Pueblo Mountain Park next-steps discussion on Aug. 31. A resident spoke Oct. 13 about city parks and Mountain Park.

pueblo/9.title: Economic development partner RFP and purchasing policy changes
pueblo/9.summary: Council held several work sessions on selecting an economic development partner through an RFP, plus a purchasing policy amendment and a procurement process overview. Closed sessions covered projects Tortuga and Falcon, and a PEDCO lawsuit.

pueblo/10.title: Library funding: no new tax or rate increase
pueblo/10.summary: The library foundation presented that its funding continues under the 2019 voter-approved mill levy and is not a new tax or rate increase.

pueblo/11.title: Moratorium ordinance and 125 E. 7th Street demolition costs
pueblo/11.summary: Council passed an ordinance assessing demolition costs for dangerous buildings at 125 E. 7th Street, raising interest from 7% to 10%. A 24-month moratorium on accepting applications for new licenses also came up for first presentation Sept. 14; the minutes do not say what kind.

pueblo/12.title: Smelter cleanup and Benedict Park
pueblo/12.summary: An EPA project manager briefed Council on the Eilers and Bessemer smelter cleanup. Public comment closed Oct. 15 and a responsiveness summary is being prepared. Benedict Park revitalization is also underway.
pueblo/12.where: Eilers and Bessemer neighborhoods; Benedict Park

rangely/0.title: Geothermal energy campus and proposed data center
rangely/0.summary: Council repeatedly took up the Energy Campus Development & Municipal Participation Study (stage 2 of Rangely geothermal development). Residents including Tanner Nielsen and Camille raised concerns about a possible data center, water use, noise, NDAs and transparency, and Nielsen suggested a moratorium and a solar partnership with CNCC. A proposal was raised to bar officials from signing NDAs for economic development.

rangely/1.title: Water shortage, Stage 3 restrictions and White River water supply
rangely/1.summary: The Town went into Stage 3 water restrictions as river flow dropped, with the water conservancy district releasing 10 cfs from Kenney Reservoir; it later returned to Stage 1. Council took up Resolution 2026-07 declaring a municipal water urgency and authorizing negotiation, but not signing, of a conditional storage agreement for the White River Regional Water Supply Project. Council also dealt with bulk water customers under Emergency Ordinance 707.

rangely/2.title: Water and wastewater plant repairs
rangely/2.summary: Staff reported the wastewater pond liner needs replacement, with other lagoon liners also needing work and grants being sought. The water plant has structural problems including corrosion, and the middle zone water tank re-coating project was proposed for delay. Repairs to chlorine pumps and the water softener were also reported.

rangely/3.title: 2027 budget and capital projects
rangely/3.summary: Council held budget and capital project work sessions, including a possible Main Street beautification project. On Oct 13 it considered approving the draft 2027 budget as presented, and revised the Housing Assistance Fund budget.

rangely/4.title: Town Manager's outside employment and oversight
rangely/4.summary: A resident, Jack Richens, raised concerns about the Town Manager, and council discussed Jonah's employment outside the Town in a conversation reported at the Sept 22 meeting. The documents do not state an outcome.

rangely/5.title: Independent hearing officers for employee grievances
rangely/5.summary: A virtual special meeting on Oct 29 considered Resolution 2026-08, creating two to three independent hearing officers to hear grievances over discipline and terminations by the Town Manager, and amending personnel rules. The Town Council would no longer sit as the hearing body.

rangely/6.title: Police leadership and services
rangely/6.summary: Interim Chief of Police Joseph McGuire was sworn in, with two police openings reported earlier. Council also amended the 2026 fee schedule for certified VIN inspections, and an SRO change was noted.

rangely/7.title: Bell Street crosswalk and no-parking changes
rangely/7.summary: Residents and council discussed the Bell Street crosswalk sign and a no-parking area extended 50 ft at the park. Council member Tim Webber worried about the effect on parking during events.

rangely/8.title: Asbestos abatement on Birch Street
rangely/8.summary: An asbestos project on Birch is starting, and additional asbestos was found. The grant is expected to cover it.

rico/0.title: Letter of support for Montelores Bridge restoration trail grant
rico/0.summary: The Dolores Ranger District asked the Town of Rico for a letter of support for its 2027 Colorado Parks and Wildlife Non-Motorized Trail Grant application, seeking about $80,000 to repair the Montelores Bridge. The Forest Service wants letters by September 15, 2026, and the Town's support would be limited to endorsing the project. The Council was set to consider approving the letter on September 2, 2026.

ridgway/0.title: Beaver Creek Diversion Restoration and infiltration gallery
ridgway/0.summary: The Town amended its RESPEC engineering contract to $657,312 in January 2026 to redesign the infiltration gallery. The project is funded by NRCS grants and a CWCB loan of up to $8,080,000, with total cost near $4 million. In June 2026 Council awarded the gallery work to Meridian Contracting for no more than $641,386.

ridgway/1.title: Wastewater Treatment Plant renovation and siting
ridgway/1.summary: Council reviewed the needs assessment for renovating the wastewater treatment plant in May 2026. Siting and treatment options were slated for discussion at the September agenda and the October 31 budget retreat. A resident asked that the new plant be built to last 50 to 60 years.

ridgway/2.title: Housing Action Plan and regional affordable housing services
ridgway/2.summary: The Town is preparing a Housing Action Plan required under state law (SB 24-174) with five goal areas, including ADUs, land banking and workforce housing. A resolution adopting it was on the October 14 agenda, along with Proposition 123 participation and the Home Trust of Ouray County's housing services work. The Home Trust also gave the Council a right-of-first-refusal decision on a home at 683 Frederick St.

ridgway/3.title: 2026 and 2027 budgets, sales tax decline and capital plans
ridgway/3.summary: The 2026 budget was adopted in December 2025 after workshops. Staff noted sales tax receipts were down 22.64% from 2024, with 2.4% pay movements proposed. The draft 2027 budget was presented in October with a budget retreat on October 31 covering pay, capital projects and funding requests from the Home Trust and EcoAction Partners.

ridgway/4.title: Lodge converted to workforce housing and tourism strategy
ridgway/4.summary: The Town's move of a lodge to workforce housing cut lodging tax revenue by about $40,000 and reduced sales tax. The Council received a tourism strategy report and a destination marketing plan, and signed a visitor and business engagement agreement.

ridgway/5.title: Water supply planning and drought restrictions
ridgway/5.summary: Council reviewed the Draft Water Supply Element of the Master Plan amendment. It considered rescinding Stage 2 mandatory water restrictions and fire restrictions, and a modified Water Conservation and Management Plan. A resident asked how growth is being planned against water supply.

ridgway/6.title: Lawsuit over land use code
ridgway/6.summary: In March 2026 Council considered filing a Complaint for Declaratory and Injunctive Relief, discussing the importance of defending the land use code and not setting a precedent.

ridgway/7.title: Wildfire Resiliency Code and building code update
ridgway/7.summary: Council introduced Ordinance 03-2026 adopting the 2025 Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code and other codes by reference, with 25 of 26 staff amendments forwarded by the Planning Commission.

ridgway/8.title: Vehicle idling ordinance
ridgway/8.summary: An ordinance to limit vehicle idling was presented for adoption in December 2025. In July 2026 a resident asked Council to reconsider addressing the proposed idling ordinance.

ridgway/9.title: Street closures for events and Council meeting procedures
ridgway/9.summary: Council weighed closures of Clinton Street and other streets for events, and a business owner complained of insufficient notice. Council also discussed adopting rules of procedure and decorum, including time limits on comment.

ridgway/10.title: Athletic Park Bike Park and development applications
ridgway/10.summary: The Athletic Park Coalition asked for Town funds for design of a bike park. Council also had a site plan for Riverbend Townhomes on Liddell Drive and plat applications.

rifle/0.title: Data center / bulk resource consumer permit rules
rifle/0.summary: Community Development drafted a Conditional Use Permit framework for data centers and other bulk resource consumers, limited to industrial districts. It would require utility, water, noise, fiscal, emergency response, thermal, housing and decommissioning analyses, and let the city deny projects that can't show net public benefit. Planning Commission and Council discussed it, and Ordinance No. 21 was set for first reading on Nov. 4.

rifle/1.title: 2026 Comprehensive Plan update
rifle/1.summary: A draft update of the 2019 comprehensive plan was reviewed by the Planning Commission on Oct. 27 and by City Council on Nov. 4. It projects demand for roughly 1,800 to 2,200 more housing units over 20 years. The state-required strategic growth and water supply elements are still being prepared.

rifle/2.title: Rifle Municipal Code text amendments: ADUs, warehouses, site plans
rifle/2.summary: Staff proposed multiple Chapter 16 code changes, including ADU size requirements, height, lot line amendments and variance application rules. They would split warehouse into Local and Regional categories for industrial zones. The ADU ordinance (No. 20) was on the Nov. 4 Council agenda.

rifle/3.title: GRIT façade grants and downtown improvements funded by lodging tax
rifle/3.summary: The GRIT board approved four grants totaling $22,200 and considered façade grants for 126 W. 4th Street, ProMex Bakery (233 Railroad Ave) and the Rifle CoWork. Council took up the ProMex and CoWork awards on Nov. 4. The board also reviewed the 2027 GRIT budget, a participatory budgeting pilot, wayfinding consultant selection, and a Third Street shade structure estimated at $20,000 to $30,000.
rifle/3.where: Downtown Rifle, 233 Railroad Ave and 126 W. 4th St

sources.body: Greater Rifle Improvement Team (GRIT) Advisory Board
Greater Rifle Improvement Team (GRIT) Advisory Board
Greater Rifle Improvement Team (GRIT) Advisory Board

rifle/4.title: Centennial Park riparian restoration and RESTORE grant
rifle/4.summary: The city is partnering with the Middle Colorado Watershed Council on a federal, no-match RESTORE grant request of $130,000 for construction documents for Centennial Park creek restoration. The Parks board gave unanimous support, and Council considered applying on Nov. 4. The parks board also heard about Rifle Creek habitat restoration and Raynard Ditch invasive removal and fire mitigation.

rifle/5.title: Rifle Community Foundation restructuring
rifle/5.summary: After the president's resignation, the foundation discussed simplifying operations to focus on grant review and awards, and recommended to Council a possible move under city administration. It also reviewed a dozen grant requests, including $30,000 from Discovery Cafe, and planned to fill a board vacancy.

rifle/6.title: Skate park concerns and Rifle Mountain Park plaque
rifle/6.summary: Residents raised skate park concerns, including one by email, at Parks board meetings. The board also considered a request to place a recognition plaque by an apple tree near the ice caves in Rifle Mountain Park under the naming policy, and heard about bike racks installed by the Rifle Climbing Coalition.

rifle/7.title: Roan Plateau gas leasing update and water rights report
rifle/7.summary: Council scheduled an update from Wilderness Workshop on Roan Plateau natural gas leasing, and a water rights report.

rifle/8.title: Railroad rehabilitation project DOLA grant and rezone
rifle/8.summary: The Parks board considered a letter of support for a DOLA EIAF grant for the Railroad Rehabilitation Project. The Planning Commission also scheduled a rezone (PLN 2026-023) from Tourist, plus hearings on a conditional use permit at 799 Buckhorn, a variance at 758 Railroad Ave and a minor subdivision at 1317 E 17th St.

rye/0.title: Water treatment plant, water tanks and sewer main replacement
rye/0.summary: Council's November and December agendas carry updates on Water Tanks #1, #2 and #3, the Sewer Main Line Replacement capital project, and brainstorming on removing silt and reeds from the inlet. The documents are agendas only and do not state any decisions.

rye/1.title: 2026 budget and supplemental appropriation
rye/1.summary: Council prepared the 2026 budget in November. The December agenda lists Ordinance 2025-7, a supplemental budget and appropriation, and 2025-8, adopting the 2026 budget.

rye/2.title: Road maintenance and satellite office agreements with Pueblo County
rye/2.summary: Council is reviewing an intergovernmental agreement with Pueblo County on road maintenance. It is also reviewing a three-party agreement with Pueblo County and Colorado City Metro for a satellite office. Both appeared on the November and December agendas.

rye/3.title: Safer Routes to School grant
rye/3.summary: Council received a grant update on the Safer Routes to School program in November. No details of the project were given in the agenda.

rye/4.title: Wildlife protection refuse ordinance and animal control review
rye/4.summary: Council reviewed Ordinance 2020-11, which protects wildlife through refuse disposal rules, including an update on Account #87. It also planned to review the Pueblo County Animal Control Ordinance.

rye/5.title: Lien for unpaid ordinance violation fees (Account #69)
rye/5.summary: Council considered placing a lien on Account #69 for nonpayment of 2022 ordinance violation fees. It appeared on both the November and December agendas.

rye/6.title: Dumpster right-of-way service fees
rye/6.summary: The December agenda includes a discussion of service fees for dumpsters placed in the right-of-way.

rye/7.title: EV charging stations and CERT program presentation
rye/7.summary: Matt Akers was scheduled to present on EV charging stations and the Community Emergency Response Team (CERT) program at the November meeting.

salida/0.title: 1st & D Space-to-Create affordable workforce housing project
salida/0.summary: Council approved an MOU with Trellis Housing Partners, LLC for an affordable workforce rental project at 233 E. First Street and 102 D Street. A November 2 agenda lists a resolution authorizing sale of the city property at those addresses, subject to an upcoming ordinance, plus an MOU with the Chaffee Housing Authority.
salida/0.where: 233 E. First Street and 102 D Street

salida/1.title: Regional housing needs assessment and Proposition 123 collaboration
salida/1.summary: Council reviewed preliminary housing needs assessment results in August, and the November 2 agenda lists approval of the regional assessment and final findings. On October 6 Council also approved a Proposition 123 affordable housing MOU with Buena Vista, Poncha Springs, Chaffee County and the Chaffee Housing Authority. Council also approved a Chaffee Housing Trust fee transfer for 8 deed-restricted units in the Two Rivers development.

salida/2.title: Short-term rental license rules
salida/2.summary: Council held a second reading of Ordinance 2026-22 on September 1. Paula Givan and Nancy Wallace spoke about the active use requirement. Council approved the residency requirement amendment and removed the amendment on the active use requirement.

salida/3.title: Energy code adoption (Ordinance 2026-23)
salida/3.summary: Ordinance 2026-23 amends the city's adoption of the 2021 International Energy Conservation Code amendments. It passed first reading on August 18, and a September 15 public hearing drew Madelyne Felsch, Felicia Houston, Craig Nielson, Alex Buck and Ken Fogle.

salida/4.title: Mountain Mail building renovation at 121-129 E. 2nd Street
salida/4.summary: The Historic Preservation Commission considered a Major Certificate of Approval for Shavano Holding Co. LLC to renovate the old Mountain Mail building. The plan includes a rooftop patio, two upper-floor residences, ground-floor retail, new egress windows and demolition of a deteriorated rear structure. The upper-story facade and windows are to be retained.

salida/5.title: Land Use Code amendments and follow-up work
salida/5.summary: Council adopted Ordinance 2026-21 amending Chapter 16 (Land Use Code) after a public hearing with no comments. The Planning Commission began a work session on remaining issues such as separate rules for cottage housing and co-housing. Council also moved to allow up to two alternate Historic Preservation Commission members.

salida/6.title: 2027 budget and community budget survey
salida/6.summary: Council discussed a community budget survey on August 31, then held preliminary 2027 budget discussions on October 6 and November 2.

salida/7.title: Comprehensive Plan update and water supply element
salida/7.summary: Council supported a Local Planning Capacity grant application for the 2027 Comprehensive Plan update. The Planning Commission was to discuss Comprehensive Plan amendments for a Water Supply Element and a Strategic Growth Element on October 26.

salida/8.title: Mesa Tank water project award
salida/8.summary: Council pulled the Mesa Tank Project award from the consent agenda for separate consideration on October 6. Final settlements were also approved for the CR105 Bridge Area River Restoration Project and the 2026 Utility Replacement Project.

salida/9.title: Regional sustainability project and waste policy
salida/9.summary: Staff updated Council on the grant-funded regional sustainability contractor. Work covers energy code training, EV readiness and a greenhouse gas inventory. Upcoming policy proposals include recycling and landfill space requirements for multifamily housing and waste hauler licensing.

salida/10.title: 5-H LLC R-2 zoning question on November ballot
salida/10.summary: On October 6 Council adopted Resolution 2026-29 expressing support for the 5-H LLC R-2 zoning question on the November 3, 2026 ballot.

salida/11.title: CDOT intersection improvements letter
salida/11.summary: Council approved a letter to CDOT about intersection improvements.

salida/12.title: 610 Walnut Street dangerous building
salida/12.summary: Council went into executive session about contracts tied to the Chaffee County Building Safety Department's Notice to Vacate and Notice of Demolition of a dangerous building at 610 Walnut Street.

san-juan-county/0.title: Stage Two fire ban (Resolution 2026-07)
san-juan-county/0.summary: The council agenda for June 29, 2026 includes Resolution 2026-07 to put a Stage Two fire ban in place. The agenda gives no further detail on the restrictions or the outcome.

san-miguel-county/0.title: Natural Resources code rewrite: forestry, oil & gas, and deep geothermal
san-miguel-county/0.summary: The county is adding a new Article 6 on Natural Resources to the Land Use Code, covering forestry practices (including streamlined review of wildfire mitigation logging), oil and gas operations, and deep geothermal. The Planning Commission took these up in September and October, and the Commissioners scheduled public hearings on Resolutions 2026-40 through 2026-43 for October 21.

san-miguel-county/1.title: Housing Code Update and affordable housing code changes
san-miguel-county/1.summary: Funded by a Proposition 123 planning grant, the county is reworking its Land Use Code to make affordable and workforce housing easier to build in unincorporated areas. Stakeholder roundtables have discussed a community housing zone, density bonuses tied to deed-restricted workforce housing, ADU barriers and streamlined review, and the Planning Commission held a work session on October 8. A shared inter-jurisdictional Prop 123 housing presentation was set for November 9.

san-miguel-county/2.title: Land Use Code amendments: affordable housing qualified developer, nonconforming lots, natural medicine
san-miguel-county/2.summary: The Planning Commission reviewed amendments to let the county define a qualified affordable housing developer, to allow uses and special use permits on nonconforming lots, and to set rules (including a 1,000-foot buffer from daycares) for where natural medicine businesses can operate. Attorneys and consultants spoke on the nonconforming lots item; no one commented on natural medicine.

san-miguel-county/3.title: Employee Housing Impact Mitigation Fee review
san-miguel-county/3.summary: Commissioners discussed the county's Employee Housing Impact Mitigation Fee, adopted in 2022 and amended in 2023, which applies to new construction and additions in the unincorporated Telluride R-1 school district area. The county uses the payments to buy housing units, partner on community housing like Sunnyside, and purchase land. Staff compared it with Telluride's and Mountain Village's fees.
san-miguel-county/3.where: Unincorporated county in the Telluride R-1 school district

san-miguel-county/4.title: Mountain Village Ilium affordable housing setback variance
san-miguel-county/4.summary: The Town of Mountain Village asked the Board of Adjustment to cut the setback from County Road 63L from 20 feet to 7 feet on a 56.34-acre Community Housing parcel. The town says this keeps homes farther from the riparian corridor and wetlands, and staff recommended a five-year approval.

san-miguel-county/5.title: Bridal Veil Falls water flow and nesting black swifts
san-miguel-county/5.summary: Residents raised concern that diversion by the town dropped flow at Bridal Veil Falls to about 1 cfs versus the 6.5 cfs required, threatening nesting black swifts. The Open Space Commission noted no management prescriptions exist for minimum water, that the Forest Service and US Fish & Wildlife are the appropriate leads, and considered the matter resolved for now as the birds migrate.

san-miguel-county/6.title: Open Space Commission work plan, new Parks and Open Space manager, and park projects
san-miguel-county/6.summary: J.D. Wise was introduced as the new Parks and Open Space Manager, and commissioners are choosing 3-5 priority projects and cuts ahead of the November 9 budget deadline. Galloping Goose Park is targeted for completion by October 29, and the commission wants Gunnison sage-grouse work kept on the plan, plus a short management plan and fire mitigation for an under-used property.
san-miguel-county/6.where: Galloping Goose Park, Mill Creek Park and county open space

san-miguel-county/7.title: Noxious weed program, grants and enforcement
san-miguel-county/7.summary: The Noxious Weed Advisory Board is weighing how to allocate a $5,800 state Noxious Weed Fund grant and whether to enforce weed rules on landowners. The county also set the 2027 Vegetation Control and Management fee schedule (Resolution 2026-44), and a tamarisk removal project in Dry Creek Basin covered about 3 miles.

san-miguel-county/8.title: San Miguel Basin Fair Board budget shortfall and possible separation from the county
san-miguel-county/8.summary: The Fair Board reported a $13,000 unfavorable budget position, pursued grants, and deferred equipment purchases until the budget is balanced. The county manager floated separating the Fair Board from the county as a nonprofit, with updated bylaws and a dissolution agreement, and the board discussed 2027 livestock sale rule changes.

san-miguel-county/9.title: Telluride Pines water system CDBG grant
san-miguel-county/9.summary: Commissioners considered co-sponsoring a Colorado Community Development Block Grant application for Telluride Pines HOA to restore safe and reliable water.

san-miguel-county/10.title: Placerville and Sawpit transportation and fire station updates
san-miguel-county/10.summary: Down-valley residents asked for multimodal improvements with CDOT in Sawpit and Placerville, signage for Juniper Village Road, and planning for Highway 145 work around the 2027 Norwood Hill rockfall project. The Telluride Fire Protection District gave an update on the Placerville Station 3 project, and the county planned an RFP for the Down Valley Master Plan.

san-miguel-county/11.title: 2027 community support funding and gondola agreement
san-miguel-county/11.summary: Commissioners considered 2027 Community Support Funding requests (including the Telluride Historical Museum, West End Family Link at $12,000 and the Norwood Community Garden) and approved the 2027 Gondola IGA supplement, which shares the gondola replacement planning budget among five entities.

severance/0.title: Annexation petitions: Berrado Holding, Buffalo Creek and Ridgegate
severance/0.summary: On Oct. 27 the Town Council was asked to find substantial compliance and start annexation proceedings for three properties: Berrado Holding, Buffalo Creek and Ridgegate. Each resolution also sets a public hearing under the Municipal Annexation Act of 1965.

severance/1.title: 2027 budget, rates and fee schedule
