severance/1.summary: The Council took up the 2027 proposed rates, fee schedule and budget on Oct. 27, after a Town Projects and Budget town hall on Oct. 13. Only 2027 capital projects are appropriated in the 2027 budget.

severance/2.title: 2027 Capital Improvement Program
severance/2.summary: Council reviewed the final draft 10-year capital plan on Sept. 22. Updates include a new 2036 Police Department addition, more money for the 2027 Water Acquisition Program, and added funds for a restroom in the Town Park improvement program.

severance/3.title: Oil and gas setbacks aligned with Weld County
severance/3.summary: Planning Commission took up a Land Use Code amendment to align the town's oil and gas setbacks with Weld County regulations. Council then had Ordinance 2026-14 on its Oct. 27 agenda amending section 16.8.80.

severance/4.title: Metropolitan district service plans: Bower North and Northgate Lakes
severance/4.summary: Council held public hearings on Sept. 22 on consolidated service plans for Bower North Metropolitan District (Ordinance 2026-11) and Northgate Lakes Metropolitan District (Ordinance 2026-12). On Oct. 27 a consent resolution confirmed the effectiveness of the Northgate Lakes approval.
severance/4.where: Bower North and Northgate Lakes areas

severance/5.title: Land use code changes: setbacks, time-sensitive amendments, suspended applications, early grading
severance/5.summary: Planning Commission handled a package of code changes. These include fixing setbacks in Town Core and Development Node zones, letting Council adopt time-sensitive code amendments without prior Planning Commission recommendation, procedures for suspending applications at an applicant's request, and early grading permit rules. Council had the early grading ordinance (2026-13) and a setback ordinance (2026-15) on its Oct. 27 agenda.

severance/6.title: Electric service infrastructure requirements for new development
severance/6.summary: Planning Commission approved Resolution PC 2026-06R amending the Municipal Code on electric service infrastructure for new development, with all commissioners present voting yes.

severance/7.title: Comprehensive Plan update
severance/7.summary: The Comprehensive Plan Advisory Committee reviewed draft chapters, a sample design and an engagement plan and schedule. Feedback themes include small-town and agricultural feel, economic development and more housing diversity.

severance/8.title: Interim town attorney appointment
severance/8.summary: Council considered a resolution appointing an interim town attorney and amending the engagement agreement on Sept. 22.

severance/9.title: Severance High School After Prom community grant
severance/9.summary: The Citizen Advisory Board approved a $2,000 community grant request for the 2027 After Prom, up from $1,000 awarded in February 2026. It went to Council on the Oct. 27 consent calendar.
severance/9.where: Severance High School, 1200 Hidden Valley Parkway

silver-plume/0.title: 2025 Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code and Ordinance 359
silver-plume/0.summary: The Town Board continued discussing adoption of the 2025 Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code and Ordinance 359. A public hearing on second and final reading was set for the September 14 meeting.

silver-plume/1.title: Ordinance regulating camping within town limits
silver-plume/1.summary: A public hearing on second and final reading of an ordinance regulating camping within Silver Plume town limits was scheduled for September 14.

silver-plume/2.title: 2027 budget and 2026 third-quarter review
silver-plume/2.summary: The Budget Committee met in September and October to compare 2026 general ledger spending against the budget. It also worked through the preliminary 2027 budget line by line, flagged areas of concern and proposed a 2027 budget.

silver-plume/3.title: 2027 utility rate increase proposal
silver-plume/3.summary: The Town Board was scheduled on November 9 to discuss and decide on a proposed 2027 utility rate increase from the Budget Committee.

silver-plume/4.title: Taylor Kennedy land purchase wrap-up
silver-plume/4.summary: The November 9 agenda included a wrap-up of the Taylor Kennedy land purchase, with guest Cindy Neely.

silver-plume/5.title: CCFA intergovernmental agreement amendment
silver-plume/5.summary: The Town Board was to consider an amendment to its intergovernmental agreement with CCFA on November 9.

snowmass-village/0.title: Ritz Carlton / Viewline redevelopment sketch plan
snowmass-village/0.summary: Elevate Snowmass's proposal would redevelop the Viewline/Wildwood area with a lodge (167 units in the mix discussed), about 125 workforce housing units and a 252-space subgrade parking garage. It needs a Major PUD amendment and rezoning. The Planning Commission reviewed it in segments from August and adopted Resolution No. 4 with conditions on Oct. 7, recommending approval. Town Council site visit and review run through Nov. 2026 to Jan. 2027. A resident raised height, massing, traffic and delivery concerns on Fall Lane, and advisory boards worried about scale.
snowmass-village/0.where: Viewline/Wildwood, Snowmass Mall and Fall Lane

snowmass-village/1.title: Housing mitigation nexus study and rate increase
snowmass-village/1.summary: After raising the housing mitigation rate from 60% to 100%, the Council is updating employee generation rates and fee-in-lieu with consultant EPS. Proposals include covering residential remodels and a fee based on $945/SF for a 750 sf unit at 1.75 employees per unit. Council asked for more data and continued discussion.

snowmass-village/2.title: Draw Site workforce housing project
snowmass-village/2.summary: Council reviewed next steps as owner for the Draw Site workforce housing project. The 2027 budget lists about $76.1 million for construction.

snowmass-village/3.title: 2027 Town budget and tourism funding
snowmass-village/3.summary: Staff call the 2027 budget exceptionally tight after a low-snow 2026 season. The budget includes $107.96 million in capital projects. The Financial Advisory Board and Tourism Board reviewed it, with tourism revenue (marketing and lodging taxes) projected around $14.8 million. Council reviewed it in October, with adoption by resolution scheduled Nov. 4, along with a 2027 Road Maintenance Mill Levy hearing.

snowmass-village/4.title: Transit center / 'grand entrance' project at Snowmass Mall
snowmass-village/4.summary: A proposed transit center with RFTA improvements is estimated at $42M to $60M. The Part-Time Resident Advisory Board agreed some improvement is needed but questioned the scale, cost sharing and timing given the pending Ritz redevelopment. It prepared a letter calling for an alternative plan. A separate entryway roundabout project was also presented to an advisory board.

snowmass-village/5.title: Cavern Springs mobile home park funding
snowmass-village/5.summary: Council took up Ordinance No. 15 appropriating funds for the Cavern Springs Mobile Home Park, plus Resolution No. 23 on an IGA, housing covenants and grant agreement. Second readings were scheduled for Oct. 5.

snowmass-village/6.title: Wildfire mitigation MOU with Roaring Fork Fire Rescue
snowmass-village/6.summary: Council reviewed and considered adopting an MOU with the Fire Authority on wildfire mitigation. The town offers a $1,000 fire mitigation rebate, which the RFV Wildfire Collaborative will administer.

snowmass-village/7.title: SHOP final plan and PUD amendment
snowmass-village/7.summary: Council considered the SHOP Final Plan and PUD Amendment through Ordinance No. 14, with first reading Sept. 8 and second reading Oct. 5.

snowmass-village/8.title: Pesticide use and noxious weed spraying on trails
snowmass-village/8.summary: Council discussed pesticide application and the Environmental Advisory Board noted a lack of signage about trail spraying. Staff were asked for a more detailed noxious weed plan, and an Integrated Pest Management Plan draft was up for review.

sources.body: Parks, Open Space, Trails & Recreation Board

snowmass-village/9.title: Workforce housing hours regulation and advisory board
snowmass-village/9.summary: Council considered Ordinance No. 16 creating a Workforce Housing Advisory Board and Ordinance No. 17 on workforce housing hours regulations. It also took up the reasonable-accommodation housing rules and a housing committee process.

snowmass-village/10.title: Playground renovation at Town Park
snowmass-village/10.summary: The Parks board discussed the capital playground renovation, including asking the vendor about theming such as the Mt Daly stripe and nature motifs.

sources.body: Parks, Open Space, Trails & Recreation Board
Parks, Open Space, Trails & Recreation Board
Parks, Open Space, Trails & Recreation Board

snowmass-village/11.title: Il Poggio and other show cause hearings over unpaid sales tax
snowmass-village/11.summary: The Liquor Authority scheduled show cause hearings for licensees, including Il Poggio, alleged to be delinquent on town sales tax. Licenses could be suspended or revoked.

sources.body: Liquor Authority Hearing & Local Marijuana Licensing Authority Hearing

starkville/0.title: Crypto currency data center on Industrial Park Road (SE 26-08)
starkville/0.summary: The Planning and Zoning Commission held a public hearing on a special exception to allow a "Data Center - Crypto Currency Generation Facility" on the east side of Industrial Park Road, about 350 feet south of Miley Road, in an industrial zone. The documents do not state the outcome.
starkville/0.where: Industrial Park Road, about 350 ft south of Miley Road

starkville/1.title: 2027 city budget, 34-mill rate and pay and staffing changes
starkville/1.summary: At a special meeting on Aug. 25 the Board of Aldermen approved a resolution setting the FY2027 millage rate at 34 mills. It also approved general fund pay adjustments, Parks and Recreation non-utility increases, police fleet additions, and new police positions (a sergeant, code enforcement, an additional officer and part-time parking enforcement). Contributions to the SMART system, library, JL King Center, community theater and the humane society spay/neuter vouchers were also approved. Budgets for outside agencies were on the Aug. 18 agenda.

starkville/2.title: Electric rate increase and capital plan
starkville/2.summary: Starkville Utilities proposed a 2% electric rate increase across all rate classes, starting November 2026 and continuing in later years. It would raise about $650,000 a year and is the first increase since October 2016. The plan funds replacement of 856 wood poles, LED street lighting, and a grid resiliency grant project with a $454,000 match. The proposed FY26-27 budget has a $375,000 shortfall.

starkville/3.title: Pat Station Road and Highway 12 East multi-dwelling development
starkville/3.summary: A proposed multi-dwelling residential development near Pat Station Road and Highway 12 East needs a building height variance (VA 26-07) and a special exception (SE 26-11). It went to the Board of Adjustments on Sept. 23 and the Planning Commission on Oct. 13, and was on the Nov. 3 Board of Aldermen agenda.
starkville/3.where: Pat Station Road and Highway 12 East

starkville/4.title: Jackson 128 mixed-use development downtown
starkville/4.summary: A mixed-use development at 128 South Jackson Street in the T-5D downtown district requested five special exceptions, including a fifth story. A resident, Steve Langston, spoke in favor at the June hearing.

starkville/5.title: Sterling Ridge phased preliminary plat
starkville/5.summary: The phased preliminary plat for Sterling Ridge, at the southwest corner of Mockingbird Road and MS Highway 182, went to the Planning Commission in August and then to the Board of Aldermen on Aug. 18.

starkville/6.title: Proposed hotel on Mill Street and other special exceptions
starkville/6.summary: On Oct. 13 the Planning Commission heard a special exception to reduce minimum parking for a proposed hotel on the east side of Mill Street near Cotton Mill Road. It also heard a Bluefield Road request in an RN district and another in an SD-6 district.
starkville/6.where: Mill Street at Cotton Mill Road

starkville/7.title: Airport runway extension and hangar grants
starkville/7.summary: The Board accepted MDOT's 2.5% matching grant offers for FAA projects, including extending the runway, taxiway and lighting. In October it took up change orders and grant applications for Corporate Hangar #3 and Phase III of the runway and taxiway extension.

starkville/8.title: Pafford Emergency Services contract renewal
starkville/8.summary: Pafford Emergency Services representatives presented on renewing their contract with the city during the Aug. 28 work session.

starkville/9.title: Humane Society facility and spay/neuter clinic
starkville/9.summary: The Oktibbeha County Humane Society gave the Board an update on its projects, the facility, budget and spay/neuter clinic. The city later approved a spay/neuter voucher contribution in the 2027 budget.

starkville/10.title: Highway 12 and Garrard Road roundabout and road projects
starkville/10.summary: The Board approved Neel-Schaffer for design and inspection on the Safe Streets for All Highway 12 and Garrard Road roundabout project. It also approved a rail spur crossing easement for Southwire's connection to CC Clark Road.
starkville/10.where: Highway 12 and Garrard Road; CC Clark Road

starkville/11.title: Zoning ordinance for maintenance uses in C and CN districts
starkville/11.summary: A public hearing was set for Nov. 3 on an ordinance establishing rules for maintenance uses in the C and CN zoning districts.

starkville/12.title: Henderson Road and Sand Road sewer project
starkville/12.summary: The Board was to hear from Golden Triangle Planning and Development about a CDBG project to provide sewer for the Henderson Road and Sand Road area. Memoranda of understanding tied to a sewer and lagoon project were on the Oct. 20 agenda.

steamboat-springs/0.title: 2027 city budget and Redevelopment Authority budget
steamboat-springs/0.summary: City Council held a budget retreat on Oct. 6 to review the 2027 proposed budget, including General Fund operations and the capital improvement plan. On Oct. 20 the ordinance adopting the 2027 budget had first reading, along with an eighth 2026 supplemental appropriation and a resolution adopting the Redevelopment Authority budget.

steamboat-springs/1.title: Slate Creek / Brown Ranch development roadmap
steamboat-springs/1.summary: The Slate Creek Steering Committee met in October and November on the development roadmap, including scope, budget and a draft roadmap budget. Agendas tie the work to the Brown Ranch plan and annexation proposal, with the City, County and Yampa Valley Housing Authority involved.

steamboat-springs/2.title: Base area redevelopment and Gondola Transit Center agreement
steamboat-springs/2.summary: The Redevelopment Authority reviewed its 2026 project activity plan and preliminary 2027 budget. It also scheduled an executive session on negotiations over the Gondola Transit Center and public improvements with Steamboat Ski & Resort Corporation. The advisory committee reviewed Complete Streets Segment 4B Phase II and Mount Werner Road/Circle projects.
steamboat-springs/2.where: Mountain base area, Mount Werner Road

steamboat-springs/3.title: The Forge at Burgess Creek preliminary plat
steamboat-springs/3.summary: Planning Commission considered a preliminary plat and major variance for 2.32 acres of unplatted land in the 1900 block of Burgess Creek Road. Council then had a resolution approving the plat and variance on its Oct. 20 consent calendar.

steamboat-springs/4.title: Child care centers in commercial zones
steamboat-springs/4.summary: A Community Development Code text amendment would allow large and small child care centers in commercial zones. Planning Commission heard it Oct. 8 and an ordinance had first reading at Council Oct. 20.

steamboat-springs/5.title: Yampa Valley regional transportation sales tax ballot question
steamboat-springs/5.summary: Council considered a resolution supporting the Yampa Valley Regional Transportation Authority ballot question for a one-half percent sales tax.

steamboat-springs/6.title: Overlook Triplexes development plan
steamboat-springs/6.summary: Planning Commission held a public hearing on a development plan and conditional use for the Overlook Triplexes project (PL20250368).

steamboat-springs/7.title: Crowell-Marshall House permanent placement
steamboat-springs/7.summary: Council considered directing staff to approve a building permit for the permanent placement of the Crowell-Marshall House, tied to Ordinance No. 3036 that waived code provisions for its temporary storage. The Historic Preservation Commission also reviewed a demolition and a Rodeo Grounds sales tax exemption certification.

steamboat-springs/8.title: Water supply element and downtown plan text amendment
steamboat-springs/8.summary: The Planning Commission policy work session was to hear a presentation of the Water Supply Element and a Downtown Plan implementation text amendment.

steamboat-springs/9.title: Easement vacations and Yampa River riprap easement
steamboat-springs/9.summary: Council took up several ordinances vacating easements, including a water and sewer line and fire hydrant easement, and on Oct. 20 a Yampa River riprap easement agreement and a purchase contract amendment for parcels including 140-R.

steamboat-springs/10.title: Golf course rates and overhead
steamboat-springs/10.summary: The Golf Management Committee planned to discuss allocated overhead and 2027 golf rates.

sterling/0.title: Proposed street improvement sales tax for November 3, 2026 ballot
sterling/0.summary: Council took up a resolution to refer a 1% sales and use tax to voters on November 3, 2026. At the September 8 meeting, residents John Tyson and Lee Roth asked for more information, questions about exemptions, the sunset clause and the time since the last tax increase, and asked that the $400,000 budgeted for street repair be combined with any new tax money.

sterling/1.title: Veterinary clinics as a conditional use (Ordinance No. 8)
sterling/1.summary: Council amended the zoning code to allow veterinary clinics as a conditional use in a district, with a first reading August 11 and a public hearing on second reading September 8. Mayor Fuller said Council discussed the change and chose the conditional use application route.

sterling/2.title: Rezoning 917 Hamilton Street from R-3 to Community Business
sterling/2.summary: Ordinance No. 10 would rezone the property at 917 Hamilton Street from High Density Residential (R-3) to Community Business (CB). It had a first reading August 25 and a second-reading public hearing on October 13, where no one spoke.

sources.url: http://www.sterlingcolo.com/City Council/Agenda, Packet, Minutes/2026/09-22-2026 Agenda Amended.pdf?t=202609211636560

sterling/3.title: Proposed 2027 city budget
sterling/3.summary: A tentative budget workshop was set for September 25, and a public hearing on the proposed 2027 budget was scheduled for the October 27 meeting.

sources.url: http://www.sterlingcolo.com/City Council/Agenda, Packet, Minutes/2026/10-27-2026 Agenda Amended.pdf?t=202610261608010

sterling/4.title: Waterline replacement projects
sterling/4.summary: Council accepted a bid from Hard Rock Civil, LLC for the 2026 Waterline Replacement Project #26-001. It also considered a change order with Hard Rock Civil for the North 10th Avenue waterline project and a change order for the 2025 Waterline Replacement Project #25-006 with Concrete Specialties and Utilities Construction.

sources.url: http://www.sterlingcolo.com/City Council/Agenda, Packet, Minutes/2026/10-27-2026 Agenda Amended.pdf?t=202610261608010

sterling/5.title: Shipping container rules and community business zoning
sterling/5.summary: Ordinance No. 9 amends a section of City Code Chapter 3. Resident Richard Bedford told Council the new shipping container updates cause unintended problems and do not properly address community business zoning.

sources.url: http://www.sterlingcolo.com/City Council/Agenda, Packet, Minutes/2026/9-22-2026 Packet Amended.pdf?t=202609211637320

sterling/6.title: Chicken permitting process
sterling/6.summary: Residents including Lisa LeFevre asked Council to revisit the chicken code and clarify the building permit process tied to the chicken permit.

sterling/7.title: Police Department Armory renovation and expansion
sterling/7.summary: Council considered Resolution 9-3-26 approving a professional engineering design services agreement for renovating and expanding the Police Department Armory.

sources.url: http://www.sterlingcolo.com/City Council/Agenda, Packet, Minutes/2026/09-22-2026 Agenda Amended.pdf?t=202609211636560

sterling/8.title: Master Plan update and DOLA grant
sterling/8.summary: Council authorized a funding request to the Colorado Department of Local Affairs Local Planning Capacity Grant Program to update the city's Master Plan.

sources.url: http://www.sterlingcolo.com/City Council/Agenda, Packet, Minutes/2026/09-22-2026 Agenda Amended.pdf?t=202609211636560

sterling/9.title: Hotel Tax Fund spending: downtown holiday garland and promotion
sterling/9.summary: On the Citizen's Advisory Board's recommendation, Council considered spending up to $45,000 from the Hotel Tax Fund on holiday lighted garland wraps and storage for West Main Street. A separate item sought up to $10,000 from the fund for an update.

sources.url: http://www.sterlingcolo.com/City Council/Agenda, Packet, Minutes/2026/10-27-2026 Agenda Amended.pdf?t=202610261608010
http://www.sterlingcolo.com/City Council/Agenda, Packet, Minutes/2026/09-22-2026 Agenda Amended.pdf?t=202609211636560

sterling/10.title: Speeding near Pioneer Park
sterling/10.summary: Resident Rudy Owen said traffic on the road by Pioneer Park is too fast, making it hard to cross the street and enjoy the park. Another resident reported loud mufflers early and late; the City Manager will pass it to police.

sterling/11.title: Sober living conditional use and garage conversion on McKinley
sterling/11.summary: The Planning Commission agenda included a conditional use request from Milestone Community Wellness to operate a sober living facility and a variance request from Jesse Mull to convert a garage to a home at 728 McKinley Street.

summit-county/0.title: Quikrete concrete and asphalt batch plant appeal on Highway 9
summit-county/0.summary: The commissioners held a public hearing on an appeal of the Lower Blue Planning Commission's decision on PLN26-004, a Class 4 conditional use permit for milling and concrete and asphalt batch plant operations. The site is a 151-acre portion of a 605-acre A-1 parcel. The packet includes public comments, a stormwater plan and a landscape plan. The documents do not state the outcome.

summit-county/1.title: 2027 county budget
summit-county/1.summary: A draft 2027 budget was presented on Oct. 13, with a public hearing and public comment on the proposed budget on Oct. 27. Work sessions covered capital projects, road and bridge, lodging tax, the coroner, human services (BOSS) and a District Attorney budget amendment.

summit-county/2.title: SCRAP fee analysis and rate study
summit-county/2.summary: Commissioners reviewed a rate study and fee analysis for SCRAP on Oct. 20. A follow-up rate study Q&A and a comparison of other agencies' rate factors were on the Oct. 27 work session.

summit-county/3.title: Proposition 123 housing credits for Soda Creek project in Keystone
summit-county/3.summary: The county was asked to approve an intergovernmental agreement with the Town of Keystone on allocating Proposition 123 housing credits (units) for the Soda Creek project.

summit-county/4.title: Summit Gulch claims option agreement in Upper Blue Basin
summit-county/4.summary: Commissioners were asked to approve exercising an option agreement to acquire the Summit Gulch claims in the Upper Blue Basin.

summit-county/5.title: County Road 506 full maintenance consideration
summit-county/5.summary: Commissioners considered a resolution on whether the county should provide full maintenance on CR 506.

summit-county/6.title: Background checks for massage facility personnel
summit-county/6.summary: Commissioners considered a proposed resolution requiring background checks for massage facility personnel.

summit-county/7.title: Community Services Block Grant needs assessment and Head Start grant
summit-county/7.summary: Commissioners were asked to authorize the chair to approve the 3-year CSBG Community Needs Assessment and the 2027-2029 Community Action Plan. They were also asked to approve a Head Start supplemental grant application.

superior/0.title: Marshall Fire Remembrance Project and 5-year anniversary event
superior/0.summary: The Town is designing a Marshall Fire Remembrance with a place to gather, pet remembrance and dispersed components. Colorado Gives will act as fiscal sponsor, Make Philanthropy Work was hired as fundraising advisor, and Louisville is committing $25,000. A kickoff fundraising and Resilience Celebration is planned for Dec. 18, 6-8pm at the Community Center.

sources.body: Cultural Arts and Public Spaces Advisory Committee (CAPS)

superior/1.title: 2027 Town budget, fee schedule and property tax levy
superior/1.summary: Council reviewed the 2027 budget and 2027-2031 financial plan in several sessions, then on Oct. 12 adopted the budget, fee schedule and property tax levy. Metro district and urban renewal authority budgets were adopted too. Mid-year figures showed vehicle use tax down 17.1%, permit revenue down and sales tax roughly flat.

superior/2.title: Zaharias property amendment to Rock Creek Ranch PUD
superior/2.summary: Planning Commission heard the Twenty-Fifth Amendment to the Planned Development Plan for the Zaharias property, applied for by Garrett Companies. A resident spoke on it and the commission recommended approval. Council then held a public hearing on the ordinance.

superior/3.title: Water conservation, turf reduction and water supply
superior/3.summary: The Town drafted a water conservation plan with a survey and a turf plan. Council adopted the Waterwise Landscape Transformation Roadmap and turf reduction prioritization tool and approved a Northern Water Southern Water Supply Project allotment amendment. Water use was up 17.4% in 2026 including a 9.5% rate increase.

superior/4.title: Park herbicide spraying and Vargas landscape maintenance contract
superior/4.summary: A resident raised concerns at ACES about spraying in a park near a pond, and spraying was said to be limited to 20 feet from the water. At the Oct. 26 Council meeting speakers backed the Vargas landscape maintenance contract.

superior/5.title: Coyote Ridge trails, prairie dog and wildlife management plans
superior/5.summary: Pointe Strategies drafted Coyote Ridge trail recommendations that staff must approve before cost estimates are made, and OSAC was to recommend Town acceptance. OSAC is also working on a Prairie Dog Management Plan, a Town Wildlife Management Plan, and wildfire mitigation and habitat work.

superior/6.title: 88th Street bike/ped improvements and McCaslin trail grant
superior/6.summary: Council approved an intergovernmental agreement with CDOT for the 88th Street Bicycle and Pedestrian Improvements Project. It later approved a Colorado Parks and Wildlife trail grant submission, supported by PARC, for the McCaslin multi-use trail.

superior/7.title: Pirate Park playground and community pool construction
superior/7.summary: PARC and Council received updates on the Pirate Park playground project. Council also got construction updates on Rock Creek Parkway, the Community Center and the north and south pools.
superior/7.where: Pirate Park; Community Center and pools

superior/8.title: Boulder County child care mill levy measure
superior/8.summary: Council discussed the Boulder County Child Care Investment Initiative and passed a resolution supporting the county's Early Childhood Care and Education mill levy increase ballot measure.

superior/9.title: ARTery public art and Circle Park benches
superior/9.summary: CAPS is expanding the ARTery through Circle Park and behind Safeway, with utility box art and swing benches. A purchase recommendation of roughly $12,000 for art and two benches at $12,000 each went to Council.

sources.body: Cultural Arts and Public Spaces Advisory Committee (CAPS)
Cultural Arts and Public Spaces Advisory Committee (CAPS)
Cultural Arts and Public Spaces Advisory Committee (CAPS)

superior/10.title: 2024 International Fire Code adoption
superior/10.summary: Council adopted the 2024 International Fire Code by reference as Ordinance 80 on second reading, after Chief Webb spoke on the ordinance continued from an earlier meeting.

superior/11.title: Proposition 123 housing agreement and affordable housing
superior/11.summary: Council approved an intergovernmental agreement with Boulder County for housing development to implement Proposition 123. The Town also received $1M from Boulder County for affordable and attainable housing.

teller-county/0.title: Short-term rental regulation (Ordinance #23) and tax administration
teller-county/0.summary: The commissioners were set to hold a second reading of Ordinance #23 on Sept. 10, regulating short-term rentals in unincorporated Teller County. On Sept. 24 they were to ratify an agreement with Neumo Group, LLC for short-term rental tax and license administration.

teller-county/1.title: Quantum Tech compliance agreement for 10180 West property
teller-county/1.summary: The county Planning Commission revoked a 1995 conditional use permit for a construction storage yard on May 12, 2026, and the Board of Adjustment took up the matter July 9. A compliance agreement gives Quantum Tech, LLC 90 days to remove non-permitted operations while keeping office use. Any future permit would require a new application. Commissioners were to ratify the agreement Sept. 10.

teller-county/2.title: Cripple Creek & Victor mine Amendment 14
teller-county/2.summary: Commissioners were to discuss on Oct. 27 a Mining Development Plan modification, Amendment 14, for the CC&V gold mine. It includes a proposed employee parking lot along County Road 821 and a temporary access road in Grassy Valley. Staff recommends approval with conditions. The state approved it Oct. 1, 2025 with a condition tied to a process water event investigation. County approval is still required and public comments are in the packet.
teller-county/2.where: Cripple Creek Mining Overlay District, County Road 821 and Grassy Valley

teller-county/3.title: 2026 budget amendments and 2027 proposed budget
teller-county/3.summary: Commissioners held budget work sessions in August, September and November, including capital planning and strategic planning. They were to hear the 2027 proposed budget on Oct. 8. They also moved to amend the 2026 General, Jail, Road and Bridge, and Social Services fund budgets, including on Oct. 22.

teller-county/4.title: Building code and contractor licensing changes
teller-county/4.summary: A work session on Aug. 25 covered proposed changes to the Teller County building code and contractor licensing. Proposals include license categories and fees for septic (OWTS) installers, cleaners and maintenance contractors, with annual fees of $50 to $150.

teller-county/5.title: Fire ban lowered from Stage II to Stage I
teller-county/5.summary: Commissioners considered a resolution on Sept. 2 to move from a Stage II to a Stage I fire ban. It was up for ratification Sept. 10. Earlier notes said the Stage II ban remained needed amid dry conditions and low river flows.

teller-county/6.title: Jail underground repair contract increase
teller-county/6.summary: A change order with Mid Colorado Construction LLP for jail underground repair and investigation raises the contract cap from $40,000 to $100,000 and extends it to June 30, 2027. Commissioners were to ratify it on Oct. 8.

teller-county/7.title: Pollock-Kenyon amended final plat, Highland Meadows
teller-county/7.summary: Commissioners reviewed an amended final plat adjusting the lot line between Lots 3 and 4 in Highland Meadows Filing 1, creating Lots 3R and 4R. This resolves encroachments of a residence onto the neighboring lot. Staff recommends approval.
teller-county/7.where: 100 Floresta Drive and 10 Floresta Place, Highland Meadows

teller-county/8.title: Pinestone Ranch project and Halchak zoning variance
teller-county/8.summary: Palmer Land Trust was scheduled to discuss the Pinestone Ranch project with commissioners on Oct. 13. On Oct. 27 commissioners were to take up the Halchak zoning variance. The documents give no details of either.

teller-county/9.title: Public health items: rural health grant, oxygen program, address signs
teller-county/9.summary: A board of health meeting covered a rise in suicides among men aged 45 to 65, the Rural Health Transformation Grant, and a non-emergent oxygen program. It also covered childcare facility permits and grant-funded reflective address signs to speed emergency response.

telluride/0.title: Carhenge Redevelopment Project review
telluride/0.summary: HARC has three Preliminary Large-Scale applications for the Carhenge Redevelopment (Buildings A–C, D1–D2, E1–E3) on Lots 34 and 34B, Backman Village. The applications were continued from July and August and were on the Sept. 30 agenda. On Oct. 27 Town Council considered a resolution affirming the July 23 P&Z decision on a preliminary large-scale subdivision consolidating the two lots.

telluride/1.title: Telluride Housing Authority waitlist and rental policies
telluride/1.summary: The Housing Authority and its subcommittee are working on waitlist management (§105) and leasing procedures under the Employee Rental Housing Policies, following a recent suspension of the waitlist. They also took up a policy statement on partial 2027 rental rate increases and an interpretation of primary residency for children of multiple custodial parents, adopted with amendments (20% custodial cutoff, age through 18).

telluride/2.title: Deed restriction changes for Town-built Fino units
telluride/2.summary: The Housing Authority considered a resolution to amend deed restrictions on Town-constructed affordable units at 215 East Colorado Avenue (Units 1A and others). Staff described it as a contract amendment, not an exception, and a last resort after extensive Council discussion.

telluride/3.title: Affordable housing exceptions and guidelines (multi-bed units, lending)
telluride/3.summary: The subcommittee heard exception requests on capital improvement limits, household size, and lender rules. It held worksessions on households that own multi-bedroom units, bedroom size standards, nonconventional lending for mixed-use structures, and a property ownership standard. It also discussed the Spruce House H lottery timeline.

telluride/4.title: 2027 budget: real estate transfer tax suspension and fees
telluride/4.summary: Town Council had first reading of an ordinance suspending a Telluride real estate transfer tax-related item for the 2027 budget year. The Open Space Commission discussed the 2027 budget with the Town Manager. The Parks commission reviewed 2027 campground fee increases (about 5% revenue growth to $203,304) and shower fees (to $62,500 revenue).

telluride/5.title: Gondola replacement project funding
telluride/5.summary: Town Council and the San Miguel Authority for Regional Transportation took up the 2027 Gondola Project Development budget, including the fourth supplement to the cost-sharing IGA and a FY27 amendment to the Gondola Project Development IGA.

sources.body: San Miguel Authority for Regional Transportation

telluride/6.title: Ethics complaint and a Code of Conduct for Council
telluride/6.summary: The Ethics Commission considered a complaint against a councilmember's conduct at a public meeting. It discussed recommending a Code of Conduct to Town Council, either integrated into the ethics code or as a stand-alone policy, with penalties like removal from liaison roles.

telluride/7.title: Proposed ban on fuel-burning landscape equipment
telluride/7.summary: The Ecology Commission discussed a draft ordinance banning combustion lawn and garden equipment, as called for in the 2022 Climate Action Plan. Staff will consult Town departments that use such equipment before recommendations go to Council. The commission is also updating the 2027 Climate Action Plan.

telluride/8.title: Town Park Oval improvements and proposed two-night concert
telluride/8.summary: The Parks & Recreation Commission discussed Town Park Oval goals, design options and facility uses with public input. Town Council discussed a proposed two-night concert in Town Park and reviewed 2026 special events on Town property.

telluride/9.title: Valley Floor goat grazing pilot and winter use plan
telluride/9.summary: A resident, Ramona Gaylord, wrote asking for results, costs and future of the Valley Floor goat grazing pilot. The Open Space Commission also reviewed the 2026/27 Valley Floor winter use plan covering grooming, trails and dog signage.

telluride/10.title: Comprehensive Plan update
telluride/10.summary: Planning & Zoning held special sessions with the consultant team to give input and wrap up a week of community Comprehensive Plan events; a later session was rescheduled.

telluride/11.title: Historic review of Shandoka, Tomboy Road and Columbia Avenue projects
telluride/11.summary: HARC continued the Shandoka Lot Redevelopment and 448 Tomboy Road applications to later meetings. It also took up payment-in-lieu of parking at 510 W Columbia/129 N Townsend, and P&Z reviewed a minor subdivision merging lots there.
telluride/11.where: 510 W Columbia Ave; 448 Tomboy Road; Shandoka lot

thornton/0.title: Data center moratorium discussion
thornton/0.summary: City Council took up a possible data center moratorium at its Aug. 25 update session and continued the discussion at the Sept. 1 planning session, with staff presentations on data centers. The documents do not state an outcome.

thornton/1.title: Creekside Gardens Annexation and zoning
thornton/1.summary: Council held a public hearing on Aug. 25 on annexing about 26 acres at the southwest corner of East 140th Avenue and Washington Street into Ward 4, with zoning, an overall development plan and a conceptual site plan. Second readings of the annexation and zoning ordinances were on the Sept. 8 agenda.
thornton/1.where: Southwest corner of East 140th Avenue and Washington Street

thornton/2.title: Bellflower Annexation, zoning and site plan
thornton/2.summary: The Planning Commission was scheduled on Oct. 20 to hold hearings on annexing about 39 acres near East 120th/140th Avenue and Holly Street. The hearings cover annexation, a zoning amendment with a development plan, and a conceptual site plan for a residential development on about 38 acres.
thornton/2.where: East of Holly Street, near East 120th and East 140th Avenues

thornton/3.title: Welby Station zoning amendment
thornton/3.summary: The Planning Commission considered a zoning amendment for about 55 acres at the northeast and northwest corners of East 88th Avenue and Welby Road (Case PLZ202600342) on Sept. 15. Council held a public hearing on the zoning ordinance on Oct. 13.

thornton/4.title: 2027 city budget, pay plans and tax levy
thornton/4.summary: Council reviewed the preliminary 2027 budget in September planning sessions. On Oct. 27 it held a public hearing on adopting the 2027 budget, pay plans, appropriations and the property tax levy (first reading). Related boards also took up 2027 budgets, including the 136th Avenue GID, TDA and TASHCO.

thornton/5.title: 2027 water, sewer and stormwater rates and Water Enterprise bonds
thornton/5.summary: Council reviewed proposed 2027 utility rate and fee adjustments for water, sewer and stormwater, effective Jan. 1, 2027. An ordinance authorizing Series 2026 Water Enterprise Revenue Bonds was also on the Aug. 11 agenda.

thornton/6.title: Interim City Attorney hiring and personnel matters
thornton/6.summary: Council held several executive sessions on the Interim City Attorney position, including interviewing internal candidates and a potential employment agreement. In October it also discussed a vendor for the City Attorney recruitment and the performance of the Municipal Judge, Interim City Attorney and City Manager.

thornton/7.title: City Code changes to align with Colorado Supreme Court ruling
thornton/7.summary: Council discussed and took up on first reading an ordinance amending Thornton City Code Sections 1-8, 38-175, 38-176 and 38-177 to align with state law following a Colorado Supreme Court ruling.

thornton/8.title: Parks and Recreation Master Plan and Arts and Culture Master Plan
thornton/8.summary: Council reviewed the 2026 Parks, Recreation & Community Programs Master Plan and the Arts and Culture Master Plan 2026-2030 on Sept. 8. A resolution adopting the Parks and Recreation Master Plan was on the Sept. 22 agenda.

thornton/9.title: Parterre subdivision legal strategy
thornton/9.summary: Council met in executive session on Sept. 8 to receive legal advice and give instructions to negotiators about strategies for developing the Parterre subdivision.

thornton/10.title: Small-lot housing and residential design standards
thornton/10.summary: Council discussed residential housing and design standards, including small-lot housing, on Oct. 20. The Planning Commission also had Chapter 18 development code housekeeping amendments on Oct. 6.

thornton/11.title: Marijuana licensing code amendments
thornton/11.summary: Council reviewed potential amendments to the city's marijuana licensing code on Oct. 27, with draft amendments prepared.

thornton/12.title: Station area plans, Thornton Parkway path and transit-area redevelopment
thornton/12.summary: Council discussed visioning for the York at 144th and North Thornton at CO 7 station areas. The TDA moved to convey property to the city for the Thornton Parkway Multimodal Path from I-25 to Grant Street. Council also held executive sessions on responses to a Request for Qualifications for a redevelopment project.
thornton/12.where: Thornton Parkway, I-25 to Grant Street; York/144th and CO 7 station areas

thornton/13.title: Municipal Annexation Act plan for Adams and Weld County land
thornton/13.summary: Council considered a resolution on Oct. 13 designating a plan under the Municipal Annexation Act for land in Adams and Weld Counties.

thornton/14.title: Security and speaker rules at public hearings
thornton/14.summary: Council held an executive session on Oct. 13 to receive legal advice on speakers' constitutional rights and maintaining order during public hearings, and to discuss security arrangements.

timnath/0.title: 2027 Town budget and five-year capital plan
timnath/0.summary: Town Council held budget work sessions on the 2027 draft budget, which includes a five-year capital improvement plan and cash-flow projections. Budget allocations are tied to the Strategic Plan, and capital projects include a parks maintenance facility, police department upgrades and security cameras at Timnath Community Park. A compensation study is also to be folded into the budget.

timnath/1.title: Peanut Park (Timnath Ranch North Park) master plan
timnath/1.summary: The PROST Committee reviewed the master planning process for Peanut Park, including a resident poll on amenities, drainage challenges and the park's size. The five-year capital plan includes $6 million for the park next year, but funding is not guaranteed until the budget is approved, so improvements will likely be phased.
timnath/1.where: Peanut Park / Timnath Ranch North Park

timnath/2.title: Timnath Landing GID bond issuance (Series 2026A and 2026B)
timnath/2.summary: The Timnath Landing General Improvement District Board took up an ordinance authorizing limited tax general obligation bonds, Series 2026A and subordinate Series 2026B. The bonds would fund public improvements approved by district voters, reimburse the developer and the Town, and cover issuance costs. The ordinance was re-authorized because the earlier December 2025 approval was delayed; first reading was Oct. 13 with a public hearing Oct. 27.

sources.body: Timnath Landing General Improvement District Board
Timnath Landing General Improvement District Board

timnath/3.title: Costco fuel facility expansion
timnath/3.summary: The Planning Commission reviewed a site plan to expand the Costco fuel canopy at 4665 Weitzel Street from about 3,884 to 10,216 square feet and increase fueling positions from 16 to 32. Discussion focused on traffic circulation and a median extension to remove an unsafe southbound movement; staff recommended approval.

timnath/4.title: Rec Center design and park projects
timnath/4.summary: The Rec Center project has finished schematic design, and the Town is working with Adolfson & Peterson Construction and a third-party architect to confirm costs before moving into design development. The Timnath Community Park entrance project is nearly complete, with flood irrigation removed to save water.

timnath/5.title: Land Use Code amendments and Comprehensive Plan draft
timnath/5.summary: The Planning Commission reviewed Council's decisions on code changes covering a wastewater and graywater prohibition, Larimer County flood insurance rate maps, neighborhood meeting notices, subdivision procedures, administrative plats and fencing materials. It also looked at the working draft of the Comprehensive Plan.

washington-county/0.title: Washington County landfill resolution
washington-county/0.summary: The county commissioners took up a landfill resolution at a 2:30 item on Aug. 18 and again as Resolution 34-2026 on Sept. 1. The agendas give no details on what it does. A landfill capital purchase was also on the Aug. 25 agenda.

washington-county/1.title: RAISE grant bids and SEH presentation
washington-county/1.summary: The county drafted an RFP for a RAISE grant in August and September. It opened and discussed bids on Oct. 6 and Oct. 20, and SEH presented on the RAISE grant bid on Nov. 3. The agendas do not say what project the grant would fund.

washington-county/2.title: County comprehensive plan RFP
washington-county/2.summary: The commissioners reviewed a draft request for proposals for a new county comprehensive plan from August through September. Proposals were opened and discussed on Oct. 27, with further discussion on Nov. 3.

washington-county/3.title: Clinic roof and clinic bids
washington-county/3.summary: The commissioners approved an agreement with APEX for the clinic roof on Aug. 25. They opened and discussed clinic bids on Oct. 6 and Oct. 20, and discussed them again on Oct. 27 and Nov. 3.

washington-county/4.title: Wind moratorium extension
washington-county/4.summary: The commissioners considered Resolution 49-2026 on Sept. 29 to extend the county's moratorium on wind energy development.

washington-county/5.title: PILT agreement and conflict waiver
washington-county/5.summary: The commissioners discussed a conflict waiver and a PILT (payment in lieu of taxes) agreement on Oct. 13. They returned to the PILT agreement on Oct. 20 and Nov. 3.

washington-county/6.title: 2027 county health benefits and health pool rates
washington-county/6.summary: The commissioners reviewed 2027 health pool rates on Sept. 22. Resolution 50-2026 on 2027 health benefits appeared on agendas from Sept. 29 through Oct. 27.

washington-county/7.title: Courthouse and EMS building surveillance system
washington-county/7.summary: The commissioners considered proposals for a surveillance system for the courthouse and EMS building on Aug. 18, with a decision on the agenda. A CamNet service contract followed on Sept. 8.

washington-county/8.title: Fiber and telecom utility accommodation agreements
washington-county/8.summary: On Oct. 20 the commissioners took up Resolution 52-2026 for Level 3 Communications and Resolution 53-2026 for Williams Communications, both utility accommodation agreements.

washington-county/9.title: Nursing home and housing authority board vacancies
washington-county/9.summary: The commissioners discussed letters of interest for the Nursing Home Board and Housing Authority Board on Oct. 13 and Oct. 20. Separately, the nursing home had several capital purchases.

washington-county/10.title: 2027 budget review
washington-county/10.summary: The commissioners held budget review sessions on Nov. 3, at 11:00 and 3:00.

washington-county/11.title: Planning and zoning fee schedule
washington-county/11.summary: The commissioners took up Resolution 48-2026, the Washington County fee schedule for planning and zoning, on Sept. 1.

weld-county/0.title: Justice Center project (Block 66) construction and parking garage
weld-county/0.summary: The county picked a construction manager/general contractor (Bid #B2600077) for the Weld County Justice Center and later approved a contract with J.E. Dunn Construction Group for Block 66. Related items include an interim stormwater agreement with the City, third-party plan review for the parking garage, and a temporary parking lot on Trophy Block North.

weld-county/1.title: Rule Farm Metropolitan District Nos. 1-3 service plan
weld-county/1.summary: The board accepted the filing of a service plan for the proposed Rule Farm Metropolitan District Nos. 1-3, then held a hearing on September 23 and approved the service plan (MET26-0001). The district is north of County Road 2 and east of County Road 21.
weld-county/1.where: North of County Road 2, east of County Road 21

weld-county/2.title: 2027 county budget and annual fee changes
weld-county/2.summary: On November 9 the board held first reading of Ordinance #263 adopting the county budget. It also read Code Ordinance #2026-09 on annual fees, and an emergency ordinance (#264) authorizing a ground lease and lease-purchase financing. Liquor code, dance license and fee updates (#2026-19) moved through readings as well.

weld-county/3.title: Dissolving the Department of Oil and Gas Energy and 1041 oil and gas permits
weld-county/3.summary: The board considered dissolving the Weld County Department of Oil and Gas and approved road maintenance agreements with Noble Energy for 1041 WOGLA permits. It also hired a backup hearing officer for oil and gas location assessments, and reviewed large-tract oil and gas lease auctions, leases and extensions.

weld-county/4.title: Voluntary transfer of Housing Choice Voucher program to Greeley Housing Authority
weld-county/4.summary: The board considered and approved transferring the county's Housing Choice Voucher program to the Housing Authority of the City of Greeley under PIH Notice 2018-12. Related items include a private activity bond declaration for residential facilities and bond volume cap assignments for the Prairie Rose Rehab and University Plaza projects.

weld-county/5.title: Code changes: cistern permits, right-of-way use permits, and land-use code rewrite
weld-county/5.summary: Ordinance #2026-12 (cistern usage permit criteria) and #2026-13 (right-of-way use permit) passed first, second and final readings in late September and October. Earlier, Ordinance #2026-04 rewrote zoning, areas of state interest and administration chapters, and #2026-11 revised the administration chapter.

weld-county/6.title: Solar energy permits and related land use hearings
weld-county/6.summary: The board heard Use by Special Review permits for solar facilities on County Road 35 near AA Street (Chickadee Solar) and east of County Road 31 on County Road 46. It also dealt with a decommissioning plan and collateral for Dixie Water, a quit claim deed for Latham Solar Farm annexations, and show cause hearings on gravel, mineral and recreation permits.

weld-county/7.title: Road and intersection projects: roundabouts, signals and bridges
weld-county/7.summary: The county moved on roundabouts at County Roads 31/74 and 13/50, a traffic signal at State Highway 52 and CR 37, improvements at SH 392 and CR 35, and bridge replacements (19/46.5A and 76.5/21A). It also approved easement purchases, utility relocations, street lights and an Xcel Energy gas pipeline agreement for High Plains Boulevard, along with many temporary road closures.

weld-county/8.title: Dispatch services agreements with towns and Greeley
weld-county/8.summary: The board approved public safety communications dispatch agreements with Eaton, Greeley, Johnstown, Mead and Windsor, after pulling them from one agenda and reconsidering on September 14. Similar agreements were made with Ault police and the Briggsdale and Fort Lupton fire districts.

weld-county/9.title: Weld County Jail renovations and contracts
weld-county/9.summary: The county awarded bids for jail work including shower replacements in Jail 1 West, pod renovations, North Jail lighting, makeup air units, inmate commissary and food services. It also signed on to state opioid response grants for jail-based behavioral services.

weld-county/10.title: November 2026 election arrangements and Amendment 83 resolution
weld-county/10.summary: The board approved coordinated election agreements such as with the Town of Firestone, facility usage agreements for the November 3 election, and a voting system equipment amendment. It also considered a resolution to support Amendment 83 and a fiscal agent for state election grant funds.

weld-county/11.title: Latham/West Lowell annexation deeds and Pawnee Grasslands grant
weld-county/11.summary: The county approved quit claim deeds tied to Latham Solar Farm annexations and a portion of Poudre River Trail resulting from the West Lowell Annexation. It also considered an annexation petition covering portions of County Roads 18 and a FLAP grant for Pawnee Grasslands.
weld-county/11.where: Latham area, West Lowell, Pawnee Grasslands

wellington/0.title: Flock license plate reader cameras and Sheriff's Office contract
wellington/0.summary: Larimer County Sheriff's Office presented on Flock automated license plate readers at five Wellington locations, including Highway 1/County Road 9 and 6th Street/Cleveland Avenue. The Town set aside $17,000 after a grant was not awarded. By October 13 the Board had asked to remove ALPRs from the 2027 LCSO budget, and a resident thanked them for it.

wellington/1.title: FY2027 budget and sewer fund interfund loan
wellington/1.summary: The Board worked through the 2027 budget in a workday on October 2 and a public presentation on October 13, including department reductions and delayed capital projects. A $2,000,000 loan from the General Fund to the Sewer Fund, through 2040, would delay a sewer rate adjustment and was set for a resolution vote on October 27.

sources.body: Parks, Recreation, Open Space, and Trails Advisory Board

wellington/2.title: Cleveland Avenue downtown construction project
wellington/2.summary: The signature downtown project adds street and sidewalk lighting, more on-street parking and a new storm drain in Cleveland Avenue and 5th Street. It relies on grants including $1.8 million Revitalizing Main Street and $1.35 million MMOF money that must be spent by 12/31/2026. Coulson Excavating is the contractor, and crews have dealt with waterline and sewer service conflicts.

wellington/3.title: Water supply agreements, water master plan and utility fees
wellington/3.summary: On October 27 the Board was to consider a water supply agreement with North Poudre, a storage and carriage operations agreement, and the 2025-2026 Water Distribution System Master Plan. It also had new town fees and capital investment (tap) fees for water and wastewater connections on the agenda. A resident asked the Board in August to look at water options beyond reliance on Lake 3.

wellington/4.title: Economic development incentive policy
wellington/4.summary: The Board gave direction in August on a framework for incentives aimed at commercial development, with public benefit matching the incentive and caution about waiving tap fees. Resolution 36-2026 adopting the policy was considered August 25 and discussed affordable housing gains.

wellington/5.title: Metropolitan district model service plan and review policy
wellington/5.summary: The Board held work sessions on a model service plan and review criteria for metro district proposals. Topics included what counts as sufficient public benefit, single versus multi-district plans, and mill levy limits such as a 60-mill combined cap.

wellington/6.title: Housing needs assessment and affordable housing
wellington/6.summary: The Planning Commission reviewed a technical memorandum updating the Housing Needs & Affordability Assessment with new data, ahead of a Housing Action Plan expected in 2027. The NoCo Foundation also briefed the Board on regional housing needs and down payment assistance.

wellington/7.title: Parks master plan, community center and park improvements
wellington/7.summary: The Parks board toured east-side parks, worked on implementing the PROST Master Plan and community center feasibility study, and discussed signage and fundraising. A Girl Scout proposed an accessible playground at Sunrise Park or Park Meadows.
wellington/7.where: Sunrise Park, Park Meadows, Wellville Park, Harvest Park

sources.body: Parks, Recreation, Open Space, and Trails Advisory Board
Parks, Recreation, Open Space, and Trails Advisory Board
Parks, Recreation, Open Space, and Trails Advisory Board

wellington/8.title: Floodplain code amendments
wellington/8.summary: The Planning Commission recommended and the Board adopted Ordinance 13-2026 updating the floodplain rules in Chapter 15 to align with FEMA model standards. The changes affect properties newly mapped into the floodplain and the flood insurance program.

wellington/9.title: 2024 building and fire code adoption
wellington/9.summary: Ordinance 11-2026 updates the Town's building, residential and fire codes, with local amendments to align with the Wellington Fire Protection District's 2024 Fire Code. It includes electric-ready and solar-ready provisions, which prepare buildings for future solar rather than requiring panels.

wellington/10.title: Xcel power shutoffs and wildfire mitigation
wellington/10.summary: Xcel Energy briefed the Board on Public Safety Power Shutoffs and wildfire risk mapping, with undergrounding planned. The Town's water and wastewater plants are treated as critical facilities.

westcliffe/0.title: Data center moratorium (Ordinance 2-2026)
westcliffe/0.summary: After a June discussion of data centers straining the electrical grid and water supply, the Town drafted a moratorium. First reading was July 21, and the Council approved Ordinance 2-2026 on Aug. 18 as an emergency ordinance, effective immediately. No one spoke at the public hearing.

westcliffe/1.title: Main Street parking, safety and crosswalk
westcliffe/1.summary: The Mayor raised closing Main Street between 2nd and 3rd in summers because of over-length vehicles and people crossing outside crosswalks. A workshop is planned. The Town bought two signs (up to $1,000) for the Rosita Street lot and approved a temporary painted crosswalk near 104 Main St. A permanent crosswalk is to be budgeted next year. A stop sign at Main and Adams Blvd is also on the October agenda.
westcliffe/1.where: Main Street between 2nd and 3rd Streets; Rosita lot; Main St. and Adams Blvd

westcliffe/2.title: Prop 123 affordable housing, Housing Needs Assessment and IGA with Silver Cliff
westcliffe/2.summary: The Town considered the final Housing Needs Assessment. It approved an intergovernmental agreement with Silver Cliff on Prop 123 so Westcliffe can count some of Silver Cliff's affordable housing numbers, since it missed the three-year requirement. Residents asked numerous questions about the Prop 123 grant in September, and a Custer County workforce housing report is on the October agenda.

westcliffe/3.title: Water/sewer expansion south of town and reservoir project
westcliffe/3.summary: The Council approved a public statement for trustees and staff to use when residents ask about the water/sewer expansion south of town. It says the project improves the chance private lots get built on. In August the reservoir project was awarded to Mountain Valley Excavation, starting in September with completion hoped by May. The wastewater pilot study was 70% complete.

westcliffe/4.title: Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code rejected and wildfire plan adopted
westcliffe/4.summary: The Council adopted the Custer County Community Wildfire Protection Plan in January, replacing a 2007 plan. In March it denied Ordinance 1-2026 adopting the state Wildfire Resiliency Code. The Fire Department, Silver Cliff and the County had not adopted it, and the attorney noted possible insurance and permitting risks.

westcliffe/5.title: Park shade structures instead of tree planting amid drought
westcliffe/5.summary: Because of drought and water shortage concerns, the Council dropped 2026 tree planting. It approved up to $40,000 for shade structures of about $3,000-$4,000 each. Bids for Memorial Park structures were moving forward in August.

westcliffe/6.title: Overnight camping ordinance update
westcliffe/6.summary: A trustee wants to revamp the Town camping ordinance to match Silver Cliff's, citing more overnight camping linked to rising homelessness. The current ordinance refers only to parks.

westcliffe/7.title: Tourism funding: Highway 69 welcome signs and holiday decor
westcliffe/7.summary: The Council gave $5,000 for Highway 69 welcome signs to get travelers to stop in town, with Mr. Shy opposed and approval contingent on the auditor. It also gave $3,500 for the holiday wreath contest and business holiday decor. The attorney said a statutory town cannot donate to the Altitude Fitness pool resurfacing and it must go through the grant process.

westcliffe/8.title: 2026 budget and mill levy
westcliffe/8.summary: After a public hearing with no comment, the Council approved the 2026 budget, appropriation and mill levy ordinances (5, 6 and 7-2025) in one motion on Dec. 9. A 2027 budget workshop was set for Aug. 28.

westcliffe/9.title: Façade Grant program
westcliffe/9.summary: The Council approved 2026 Façade Grant awards, cutting the Wildflower Hotel's award to $3,542. It rewrote application rules: reimbursement only, in-town business license, brick-and-mortar, and signs capped at $1,000. It also let a 2025 recipient finish work past the deadline.

westcliffe/10.title: Street sweeper purchase and town truck replacement
westcliffe/10.summary: The Council approved buying a street sweeper after a trial period, with discussion of renting it to businesses. Earlier the public works lead sought to buy a truck to replace aging Town trucks.

westcliffe/11.title: Farmer's Market at Jess Price Park and Bluff Park observatory hours
westcliffe/11.summary: The Council approved Resolution 4-2025 supporting the Farmer's Market on Town land at Jess Price Park, drafted as a resolution to avoid creating a leasehold. It also approved an MOU for extended Bluff Park hours at the Smokey Jack Observatory.

westminster/0.title: Data center land use and neighboring-jurisdiction proposals
westminster/0.summary: After Resolution No. 20 (July 27, 2026) supported a zoning interpretation treating data centers as a prohibited use in Westminster, Council asked for a study session on data centers proposed just outside city limits, with concerns about water use and extraterritorial utility service. Staff also plans stronger data center language in the Unified Development Code.

westminster/1.title: Automated license plate readers (Flock cameras) discontinued
westminster/1.summary: Police presented on automated license plate readers on Oct. 5, and the Oct. 26 agenda includes Resolution No. 46 on discontinuing the technology. Residents spoke against Flock cameras, raising data retention, cybersecurity and privacy concerns.

westminster/2.title: 2027 budget adoption
westminster/2.summary: The proposed 2027 budget went through a Sept. 14 public hearing, a Sept. 21 study session for Council feedback, and second reading on Oct. 26. The charter requires adoption by Oct. 26. Related WEDA and General Improvement District 2027 budgets were heard Oct. 12.

westminster/3.title: Affordable housing definition, density bonus and down payment assistance
westminster/3.summary: Council took up bills amending the 2040 Comprehensive Plan and code to redefine affordable housing, add a density bonus and set a parking provision (first reading Sept. 14, second Sept. 28). Staff is also finalizing a contractor for a Down Payment Assistance program that would cover up to 20 percent of purchase price. Council adopted Proposition 123 expedited review policies for affordable projects (Resolution No. 45) and got updates on Housing LIFT agreements and right-of-first-refusal agreements with regional housing authorities.

westminster/4.title: Event center moratorium and new regulations
westminster/4.summary: Council imposed a six-month moratorium on new event centers in multi-tenant commercial areas or within 300 feet of residential uses, citing impacts on public safety, utilities, parking and neighboring businesses. Staff presented revised recommendations for Councillor's Bill No. 19 on Oct. 5.

westminster/5.title: Water rates and stormwater fee changes for 2027-2028
westminster/5.summary: Council followed up on 2027 and 2028 single-family water rates, held a hearing on stormwater fee changes, and moved bills implementing water, sewer and reclaimed water rates and stormwater fees through readings in September and October.

westminster/6.title: Regional homelessness agreements and Navigation Center
westminster/6.summary: Council considered intergovernmental agreements with Jefferson County and several cities on homelessness, including a Navigation Center in Lakewood. A resident urged Council to consider a navigation center closer to Westminster. Staff also gave a homelessness prevention and response update.

westminster/7.title: Kaiser North redevelopment plan amendment
westminster/7.summary: Council held a hearing and first reading on a Comprehensive Plan amendment and preliminary development plan amendment for the Kaiser North redevelopment. Other development items followed on Oct. 12, including a preliminary development plan hearing and a street right-of-way vacation.

westminster/8.title: Business tax filing moves online
westminster/8.summary: Staff proposed an ordinance requiring online filing and payment of business tax returns starting Jan. 1, 2027, with an exception for those without internet. About 94 percent of the 77,424 returns filed in 2025 were already online. It does not affect resident taxpayers or tax revenue.

westminster/9.title: Childcare market study and property tax rebate for providers
westminster/9.summary: A market study found a need for licensed childcare spaces for 3,695 children, with affordability a major barrier. Council considered a Child Care Provider Property Tax Rebate Program (Councillor's Bill No. 51).

westminster/10.title: Waste, recycling and composting code updates
westminster/10.summary: Council reviewed options to amend hauler licensing, adopt a Skip the Stuff ordinance, and create a construction and deconstruction waste program, building on a CU Boulder capstone study and state producer responsibility funding.

westminster/11.title: Renter concerns about rising rents and housing conditions
westminster/11.summary: A Westminster renter told Council about rising rents and mold in a previous apartment, and urged action on healthy housing. Council also reviewed a residential property maintenance code update.

windsor/0.title: Crossroads/Colorado Blvd. roundabout construction closure request
windsor/0.summary: Contractor AB Underground asked the Town to fully close Crossroads Boulevard east of Colorado Boulevard during Phase 2, saying two-way traffic is too constrained in the work area. It says the change could speed the project and allow the NISP water casing to be installed in one operation. The Town Board took up the phasing plan at a Sept. 21 work session.

windsor/1.title: 2027 budget, staffing and shrinking property tax revenue
windsor/1.summary: Staff are building the 2027 budget with lower projected revenue, including falling property taxes, and have not recommended positions such as a Deputy Police Chief, Deputy Town Attorney and Transportation Planner/Engineer. The Board reviewed staffing requests, capital projects and the operating budget, with sales tax split 67% general fund and 33% capital. The Board backed $1.2M for LaBue Park design and a wrap-up of revisions in November.

windsor/2.title: 2027 water, sewer and stormwater rate increases
windsor/2.summary: Stantec's 2027 rate study proposes a 20% sewer increase in 2027 and 12.5% annual water increases through 2028, driven by the NISP water project and the new wastewater treatment plant (about $154M Windsor share). The Water and Sewer Board was asked to recommend the rates to the Town Board, which took them up Oct. 26.

windsor/3.title: Sign code rewrite
windsor/3.summary: The Town is replacing its sign regulations (Chapter 15, Article 17) as called for in the 2024 Comprehensive Plan. The Planning Commission recommended approval of the final draft on Oct. 21, and it went to the Town Board for first reading Oct. 26 and was on the Nov. 9 agenda as Ordinance 2026-1753.

windsor/4.title: Data center discussions
windsor/4.summary: Town and board members reported ongoing talks about proposed data centers in unincorporated Weld County, with concerns about electricity and water use and a joint board work session. Annexation had not been requested.

windsor/5.title: Hollister Lake Metropolitan District service plan and Windsor Lake Road
windsor/5.summary: The Town Board reviewed the service plan and an intergovernmental agreement for the Hollister Lake Metropolitan District (Ordinance 2026-1754). Separately, the Board accepted right-of-way for the Weld County Road 70 extension (Windsor Lake Road) connecting Hollister Lake Road to SH 257.

windsor/6.title: Housing: Prop 123, housing action plan and down payment assistance
windsor/6.summary: The Board considered a resolution of intent to commit to Proposition 123 affordable housing, a draft Housing Action Plan, and findings on a possible down payment assistance program that may be funded if DOLA or NoCo Foundation grants come through.

windsor/7.title: Glade Inlet Canal Diversion grant (NISP)
windsor/7.summary: The NISP Enterprise is applying for a $3,000,000 Bureau of Reclamation grant for the Glade Inlet Canal Diversion. Windsor holds about 15% of the project, so a grant could save the Town roughly $450,000.

windsor/8.title: Open space purchase near sewer plant and Kodak open space
windsor/8.summary: The Town is under contract for open space land with water, ditch water and four historic structures near the sewer plant, for $6.2M total ($3M water, $3.2M land). It will be funded from the Park Improvement Fund and reimbursed from open space sales tax.
windsor/8.where: South of Kodak open space near the wastewater plant

windsor/9.title: Police shooting range proposal
windsor/9.summary: The Board's budget follow-up memo says it supports limited funding of $37,000 in 2027 for the police shooting range and no more. Staff will hold a work session in early 2027 on location and design, noting the floodplain issue. A local range would meet all firearms training locally.

windsor/10.title: Wireless tower at Timberline Church
windsor/10.summary: A 50-foot stealth silo wireless tower and conditional use permit were proposed at 29918 County Road 17, with staff recommending approval. The Town Board hearing was set for Nov. 9.

windsor/11.title: Downtown parking management
windsor/11.summary: Under the 2025 Downtown Parking Management Plan, the Board reviewed data collection and code updates. Studies show occupancy stays below 85%, with demand peaking near Main and Walnut.

windsor/12.title: American Legion request for ADA funding
windsor/12.summary: American Legion Post 109 asked the Town for financial help with ADA improvements at its building at 624 Ash Street, whose main floor sits about five feet above grade.

windsor/13.title: Greeley litigation and logistics facilities code
windsor/13.summary: The Town Board agenda lists legal matters including The City of Greeley v. Town of Windsor, and direction on the Multimodal Transportation Logistics Facilities Code and a conditional use permit extension.

winter-park/0.title: 2027 Town of Winter Park budget
winter-park/0.summary: Town Council holds a public hearing on Resolution 2355 to adopt the 2027 budget and make appropriations. It is on the Nov. 3 agenda; the documents do not state the outcome.

winter-park/1.title: Urban Renewal Authority tax increment deals with Fire District and Cooper Creek Village
winter-park/1.summary: The URA board considered a tax increment revenue agreement with the East Grand County Fire Protection District No. 4 (Resolution 25) and a financial services agreement with Northland Securities (Resolution 26). It also planned a closed session on negotiating tax increment sharing with the Cooper Creek Village Metro Districts.

winter-park/2.title: Wheeler Road housing purchases by Housing Authority
winter-park/2.summary: Council, acting as the Winter Park Housing Authority, considered resolutions authorizing purchase and sale agreements for 34 Wheeler Road and 56 Wheeler Road. A closed session on buying, selling or leasing Town-owned property was also scheduled.

winter-park/3.title: Sojourn development agreement amendment and ADU deed restrictions
winter-park/3.summary: Council considered Resolution 2356, a second amendment to the Development Improvement Agreement for Sojourn that would also release accessory dwelling unit deed restrictions.

winter-park/4.title: Thermal energy network design contract
winter-park/4.summary: Council considered Resolution 2354 to award GreyEdge Group a contract for 10 percent design of a Town thermal energy network.

winter-park/5.title: Downtown ATS aerial transit portal and transit budget
winter-park/5.summary: The URA saw a design presentation on the downtown portal for the Aerial Transit System (ATS). The Transit Advisory Committee reviewed the 2027 transit operating budget.

winter-park/6.title: Downtown Design Guidelines draft
winter-park/6.summary: The Planning Commission reviewed the 75% draft of the Winter Park Downtown Design Guidelines and its 2026 priorities list. It also discussed the Arrow at Winter Park master sign program.

winter-park/7.title: 47 Village Drive preliminary plat and Rendezvous Filing 2C final plat
winter-park/7.summary: The Planning Commission held public hearings on the preliminary plat for 47 Village Drive and the final plat for Rendezvous at Winter Park Filing No. 2C.
winter-park/7.where: 47 Village Drive; Rendezvous at Winter Park

winter-park/8.title: ROAM Neighborhood Park
winter-park/8.summary: The Planning Commission put the ROAM Neighborhood Park on its Aug. 25 agenda.

winter-park/9.title: Site plan and variance reviews
winter-park/9.summary: Planning bodies reviewed minor site plans at 373 Bear Trail, 405 Lupine Lane, 40 Ski Idlewild Road and 100 Trademark Drive, and a setback variance at 23 Maple Road. They also reviewed a subdivision exemption plat at 215 Dreamcatcher South.

woodland-park/0.title: Temporary moratorium on residential development applications
woodland-park/0.summary: City Council took up Ordinance No. 1541 on initial posting, which would temporarily halt submission, acceptance, processing and approval of development, zoning and land use applications for residential development in the city. A public hearing was set for November 19, 2026.

woodland-park/1.title: Eagle Fire Lodge rezoning and multi-household permit at 777 E. US Highway 24
woodland-park/1.summary: Cedarwood Development requested rezoning of Lot 3R, Block 3, C.D. Weaver #1A Subdivision from PUD to Multiple Dwelling Urban Residential, plus a conditional use permit for multi-household attached dwellings. The Planning Commission held a hearing on Oct. 8, and Council saw Ordinances 1539 and 1540 on initial posting with hearings set for Nov. 19, 2026.

woodland-park/2.title: Appeal of dangerous building order at 209 E. Midland Avenue
woodland-park/2.summary: Owner Andrew Nguyen appealed a Notice and Order and Notice to Vacate for the long-vacant building. His representatives said the 60-day permit deadline is unworkable, citing a contractor bankruptcy and plan review and construction timelines. The building has also been recommended for Local Historic Landmark designation.

woodland-park/3.title: Historic landmark designation for 116 W. Lake Avenue
woodland-park/3.summary: The Historical Preservation Committee scheduled a Sept. 1 public hearing on a request by Steve Plutt and Murray WP Cabin, LLC to designate the property a Local Historic Landmark. The City Council hearing is set for Oct. 1, 2026.

woodland-park/4.title: Unified Development Code change for Public Safety Facilities
woodland-park/4.summary: The city is amending the Unified Development Code to add Public Safety Facilities as a use under the Special Use Permit process and define the term. The Planning Commission considered it in September and October, and Council had Ordinance No. 1536 up for a public hearing on Nov. 5.

woodland-park/5.title: Downtown Development Authority 2027 budget and micro-grants
woodland-park/5.summary: The DDA reviewed its 2027 budget, including $275,000 for TIF agreements (increased for the TAVA TIF agreement), $200,000 for micro-grants and $50,000 for beautification. It also reviewed micro-grant final reports: about $48,337 paid so far, $175,000 expected by year-end, and a move to one grant per applicant going forward.

woodland-park/6.title: City 2027 budget
woodland-park/6.summary: The 2027 budget was on the Nov. 5 City Council agenda, with public comment allowed.

woodland-park/7.title: Historic preservation projects: Junction House, Templeton Cemetery, Bergstrom Park
woodland-park/7.summary: The Historical Preservation Committee tracks the Junction House/Roberts House grant (Brownfields funding was discussed), the Templeton Cemetery restoration plan, a preservation plan and the Bergstrom Park Reimagined project. It also reviewed its 2027 work plan and proposed budget.

woodland-park/8.title: Main Street programs and grants
woodland-park/8.summary: The Main Street board discussed seeking a $2,500 AARP grant and DOLA mini-grants, and Oktoberfest and parade planning. Council also scheduled a State of Main Street presentation for Nov. 5.

yuma-county/0.title: Moratorium on data centers through 2026
yuma-county/0.summary: On March 17, 2026 the commissioners approved a resolution placing a moratorium on data centers in the county until 12/31/2026, along with a companion resolution adopting rules. The documents give no further detail on the rules.

yuma-county/1.title: County Road 39 repaving project
yuma-county/1.summary: The commissioners approved Simon Construction's proposal for repairs on County Road 39 in March. Work was expected to start in late July 2026; by mid-August paving was done from County Road G to M, with grinding next from Highway 59 to County Road G.

yuma-county/2.title: County Road M railroad approach and asphalt repairs
